Participant updates : Track group member responses via onInviteeAccepted: and onInviteeRejected: , updating active member rosters accordingly see Handle call events /sdk/ios/calling/managing calls/handle call events .

title: Accept a call
description: Accept a call invitation with the OpenIM iOS SDK.
keywords: sdk ios v4 sdk ios calling managing-calls accept-call
content: Accept an incoming audio or video call invitation using signalingAccept:onSuccess:onFailure: , passing the exact OIMSignalingInfo received from the incoming invitation event. Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | signalingInfo | OIMSignalingInfo | Yes | The complete signaling information object delivered by the onReceiveNewInvitation: callback. | Code example OIMManager manager signalingAccept:signalingInfo onSuccess:^ OIMInvitationResultInfo Nullable credentials if credentials = nil self joinMediaRoom:credentials ; onFailure:^ NSInteger code, NSString Nullable message self showCallError:code message:message ?: @"Failed to accept invitation" ; ; Pass the unaltered OIMSignalingInfo instance received from the incoming event; never synthesize a new object or modify roomID . Return value The onSuccess callback returns an OIMInvitationResultInfo instance containing the call roomID , authentication token , and streaming liveURL . Join the RTC media room only after receiving these valid credentials. State changes after the call Local state merge : Merge call state by roomID and correlate participant states with userID . Remote event notification : The caller and connected participants receive the acceptance notification via onInviteeAccepted: in OIMSignalingListener see Handle call events /sdk/ios/calling/managing calls/handle call events . Multi device sync : Other devices logged in under the same account receive onInviteeAcceptedByOtherDevice: to synchronize UI state.

title: Reject a call
description: Reject a call invitation with the OpenIM iOS SDK.
keywords: sdk ios v4 sdk ios calling managing-calls reject-call
content: Decline an incoming audio or video call invitation using signalingReject:onSuccess:onFailure: , passing the exact OIMSignalingInfo received from the incoming invitation notification. Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | signalingInfo | OIMSignalingInfo | Yes | The complete signaling information object delivered by onReceiveNewInvitation: . | Code example OIMManager manager signalingReject:signalingInfo onSuccess:^ self closeIncomingCall ; onFailure:^ NSInteger code, NSString Nullable message self showCallError:code message:message ?: @"Failed to reject call" ; ; Dismiss the incoming call presentation and release local audio/ringing resources upon rejection. Return value The onSuccess callback signifies that OpenIMServer processed the rejection signal and notified the caller. State changes after the call Local state merge : Merge call session state by roomID and correlate participant states with userID . Remote event notification : The caller receives the rejection notification via onInviteeRejected: in OIMSignalingListener see Handle call events /sdk/ios/calling/managing calls/handle call events . Multi device sync : Other devices logged in under the same account receive onInviteeRejectedByOtherDevice: to dismiss incoming call notifications synchronously.

title: Cancel a call invitation
description: Cancel an unanswered call invitation with the OpenIM iOS SDK.
keywords: sdk ios v4 sdk ios calling managing-calls cancel-call
content: Cancel an outgoing audio or video call invitation before the callee answers by invoking signalingCancel:onSuccess:onFailure: . Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | signalingInfo | OIMSignalingInfo | Yes | The complete signaling information object preserved when the call was initiated. | Code example OIMManager manager signalingCancel:signalingInfo onSuccess:^ self releaseCallResources ; onFailure:^ NSInteger code, NSString Nullable message self showCallError:code message:message ?: @"Failed to cancel invitation" ; ; Provide the unaltered OIMSignalingInfo instance saved during the initial signalingInvite:... or signalingInviteInGroup:... call. Return value The onSuccess callback signifies that OpenIMServer processed the cancellation command and broadcasted it to all invitees. State changes after the call Local state teardown : Exit the ringing wait state, dismiss the outgoing call screen, and release audio ringing resources. Remote event notification : Invitees receive cancellation notifications via onInvitationCancelled: in OIMSignalingListener , triggering automatic dismissal of their incoming call screens see Handle call events /sdk/ios/calling/managing calls/handle call events . State merge key : Call sessions merge state by roomID , combining with userID for participant state.

title: Hang up a call
description: Hang up an established call with the OpenIM iOS SDK.
keywords: sdk ios v4 sdk ios calling managing-calls hang-up-call
content: Terminate an active audio or video call using signalingHungUp:onSuccess:onFailure: . Any connected participant can invoke this method using the active OIMSignalingInfo object associated with the room. Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | signalingInfo | OIMSignalingInfo | Yes | The active signaling information object for the ongoing call session. | Code example OIMManager manager signalingHungUp:signalingInfo onSuccess:^ self releaseCallResources ; onFailure:^ NSInteger code, NSString Nullable message self showCallError:code message:message ?: @"Failed to hang up call" ; ; Return value The onSuccess callback confirms that the hang up signaling command was accepted by OpenIMServer. State changes after the call Local resource teardown : Stop audio and video capture pipelines, disconnect from the RTC media room, deactivate AVAudioSession , and release camera/microphone devices idempotently by roomID . Remote event notification : Remaining participants receive a hang up notification via onInvitationTimeout: or room termination callbacks in OIMSignalingListener see Handle call events /sdk/ios/calling/managing calls/handle call events . State merge key : Call sessions merge state by roomID and correlate individual participant statuses with userID .

title: Handle call events
description: Add and remove the OpenIM iOS SDK call signaling delegate in one place.
keywords: sdk ios v4 sdk ios calling managing-calls handle-call-events
content: Implement the OIMSignalingListener protocol in your call state controller to observe incoming call invitations, participant acceptance or rejection, timeouts, and stream updates. Register and unregister the listener using the same retained instance via OIMManager callbacker . Code example @interface CallStore @end @implementation CallStore void startListening OIMManager callbacker addSignalingListener:self ; void stopListening OIMManager callbacker removeSignalingListener:self ; void onReceiveNewInvitation: OIMSignalingInfo info self upsertCall:info state:@"ringing" ; void onInviteeAccepted: OIMSignalingInfo info self mergeCall:info state:@"accepted" ; void onInviteeRejected: OIMSignalingInfo info self mergeCall:info state:@"rejected" ; void onInvitationCancelled: OIMSignalingInfo info self finishCall:info.invitation.roomID ; void onInvitationTimeout: OIMSignalingInfo info self finishCall:info.invitation.roomID ; void onInviteeAcceptedByOtherDevice: OIMSignalingInfo info self stopRinging:info.invitation.roomID ; void onInviteeRejectedByOtherDevice: OIMSignalingInfo info self stopRinging:info.invitation.roomID ; void onHunguUp: OIMSignalingInfo info self finishCall:info.invitation.roomID ; void onRoomParticipantConnected: OIMParticipantConnectedInfo info self mergeParticipants:info roomID:info.roomID ; void onRoomParticipantDisconnected: OIMParticipantConnectedInfo info self removeParticipants:info roomID:info.roomID ; void onStreamChange: OIMMeetingStreamEvent event self updateStream:event roomID:event.roomID ; @end State changes after the call State merge key : Merge all incoming signaling events using roomID as the primary key. For participant rosters within multi party calls, combine roomID and userID . Lifecycle management : When logging out, switching user accounts, or tearing down the call controller, invoke removeSignalingListener: with the exact listener instance registered earlier to avoid memory leaks or cross account event collisions.

title: Restore a pending invitation
description: Restore an unresolved call invitation received before app startup with the OpenIM iOS SDK.
keywords: sdk ios v4 sdk ios calling retrieving-call-information restore-pending-invitation
content: Recover pending, unanswered call invitations after an iOS cold app launch using getSignalingInvitationInfoStartAppWithOnSuccess:onFailure: . This method requires no input parameters. Code example OIMManager manager getSignalingInvitationInfoStartAppWithOnSuccess:^ OIMSignalingInfo Nullable info if info.invitation.roomID.length 0 self restoreIncomingCall:info ; onFailure:^ NSInteger code, NSString Nullable message self showCallError:code message:message ?: @"Failed to restore call invitation" ; ; Return value The onSuccess callback delivers an OIMSignalingInfo object representing the invitation pending at application launch. If no invitation is pending, the callback returns nil . Always verify that both info and info.invitation.roomID are non empty before presenting the incoming call UI. State changes after the call Snapshot restoration : This query restores an instantaneous snapshot of the unresolved invitation. Asynchronous event tracking : After rendering the incoming call screen, observe ongoing state updates such as cancellation, timeout, remote acceptance, or hangup via OIMSignalingListener delegate callbacks see Handle call events /sdk/ios/calling/managing calls/handle call events .

title: Retrieve a group call room
description: Retrieve an active call room by group ID with the OpenIM iOS SDK.
keywords: sdk ios v4 sdk ios calling retrieving-call-information get-room-by-group-id
content: Query the active audio or video call room and connected participants for a specified group using signalingGetRoomByGroupID:onSuccess:onFailure: . Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | groupID | NSString | Yes | Target group identifier. Pass the group ID, not an application defined room ID. | Code example OIMManager manager signalingGetRoomByGroupID:groupID onSuccess:^ OIMParticipantConnectedInfo Nullable room if room.roomID.length 0 self renderParticipants:room.participant roomID:room.roomID ; onFailure:^ NSInteger code, NSString Nullable message self handleMissingGroupCall:code message:message ; ; Return value The onSuccess callback delivers an OIMParticipantConnectedInfo object describing current room metadata, linked invitation details, and the list of active connected participants. If no call is currently active in the group, treat the result as having no ongoing call and refrain from using stale credentials.

title: Retrieve room credentials
description: Retrieve credentials for joining a room by room ID with the OpenIM iOS SDK.
keywords: sdk ios v4 sdk ios calling retrieving-call-information get-token-by-room-id
content: Retrieve the credentials required to enter a call room by room ID using signalingGetTokenByRoomID:onSuccess:onFailure: . Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | roomID | NSString | Yes | Target call room identifier. Certain SDK headers denote this selector argument as groupID , but pass the actual room ID . | Code example OIMManager manager signalingGetTokenByRoomID:roomID onSuccess:^ OIMInvitationResultInfo Nullable credentials if credentials.roomID.length 0 self joinMediaRoom:credentials ; onFailure:^ NSInteger code, NSString Nullable message self showCallError:code message:message ?: @"Failed to retrieve room credentials" ; ; Return value The onSuccess callback delivers an OIMInvitationResultInfo instance containing the room identifier roomID , RTC room access token token , and live media URL liveURL . Connect to your media engine once valid credentials arrive. When media credentials expire or during connection recovery, invoke this method again to refresh credentials.

title: Send a custom signal
description: Send and receive custom signals in a call room with the OpenIM iOS SDK.
keywords: sdk ios v4 sdk ios calling sending-custom-signals send-a-custom-signal
content: Transmit lightweight coordination data within an ongoing call room using signalingSendCustomSignal:customInfo:onSuccess:onFailure: . Use custom signaling for events like raising hands, requesting layout changes, or syncing transient presentation flags. Custom signaling is distinct from chat messages and does not substitute for media engine data channels. Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | roomID | NSString | Yes | Target call room identifier matching the active call session. | | customInfo | NSString | Yes | Application defined string payload. When serializing JSON, include a schema version and an idempotency event ID. | Code example NSDictionary signal = @ @"version": @1, @"eventID": NSUUID.UUID.UUIDString.lowercaseString, @"type": @"hand raised", @"userID": currentUserID, @"sentAt": @ NSInteger64 NSDate.date.timeIntervalSince1970 1000 , ; NSData data = NSJSONSerialization dataWithJSONObject:signal options:0 error:nil ; NSString customInfo = NSString alloc initWithData:data encoding:NSUTF8StringEncoding ; OIMManager manager signalingSendCustomSignal:roomID customInfo:customInfo onSuccess:^ self markSignalSubmitted:signal @"eventID" ; onFailure:^ NSInteger code, NSString Nullable message self showCallError:code message:message ?: @"Failed to send custom signal" ; ; Return value The onSuccess callback indicates that OpenIMServer accepted the signaling payload and dispatched it to room participants. It does not signify that other participants have processed or rendered the payload. Custom signaling is designed for lightweight, ephemeral coordination; do not transmit large binaries, message histories, or persistent records over this channel. Receive custom signals Implement onReceiveCustomSignal: from the OIMSignalingListener protocol to intercept incoming custom signals. The delegate provides the raw JSON string; parse and validate the payload according to your agreed client schema: @interface CallSignalStore @end @implementation CallSignalStore void startListening OIMManager callbacker addSignalingListener:self ; void stopListening OIMManager callbacker removeSignalingListener:self ; void onReceiveCustomSignal: NSString rawSignal NSDictionary signal = self parseAndValidateCallSignal:rawSignal ; if signal == nil return; if signal @"roomID" isEqualToString:self.activeRoomID return; if self hasAppliedSignal:signal @"eventID" return; self applySignal:signal ; @end Retain the listener instance strongly and remove it using removeSignalingListener: upon account logout or when exiting the call session. Because the incoming delegate method delivers only the raw string without a dedicated top level room field, embed roomID inside your custom JSON dictionary and verify it matches the current room before executing UI changes. Deduplicate signals using eventID to handle potential out of order deliveries. Signals and durable state Custom signals operate purely as transient real time broadcasts rather than queryable server state. Devices that were offline, views that initialize after broadcast, or listeners registered late will miss earlier signals. Store persistent state in backend application databases or standard chat messages. To synchronize active call room membership, query current snapshots via Retrieve a group call room /sdk/ios/calling/retrieving call information/get room by group id .

title: Events overview
description: Register OpenIM iOS SDK listeners and synchronize connection and data state with the application lifecycle.
keywords: sdk ios v4 sdk ios events overview-events
content: The OpenIM iOS SDK defines listener protocols segmented by functional domain. Add and remove listeners through OIMManager callbacker . Retain a strong reference to each listener instance within your application state management layer, as OIMCallbacker maintains only weak references to registered delegates. Registration lifecycle | Event scope | Protocol | Related documentation | | | | | | Connection and token | Connection callbacks passed during initialization | Authenticate and manage the session /sdk/ios/getting started/authenticate and manage session | | User, friend, and blacklist | OIMUserListener , OIMFriendshipListener | User overview /sdk/ios/user/overview user | | Conversations and synchronization | OIMConversationListener | Retrieve the conversation list /sdk/ios/conversation/retrieving conversations/retrieve conversation list | | Conversation groups | Open im sdk callbackOnConversationGroupListener | Conversation groups overview /sdk/ios/conversation/managing conversation groups/overview conversation groups | | Groups and group members | OIMGroupListener | Group overview /sdk/ios/group/overview group | | Messages | OIMAdvancedMsgListener | Receive messages /sdk/ios/message/receiving messages/receive messages | | Custom business notifications | OIMCustomBusinessListener | Receive custom business messages /sdk/ios/message/receiving messages/custom business listener | | Audio and video calls | OIMSignalingListener | Handle call events /sdk/ios/calling/managing calls/handle call events | Register application level listeners after initSDKWithConfig:... succeeds and prior to initiating login:token:... . Avoid re registering listeners on view transition or rendering cycles. When logging out, switching user accounts, or tearing down the state controller, invoke the matching remove...Listener: method with the retained listener instance. Conversation group events follow a dedicated mechanism: OpenIMCore configures a single Open im sdk callbackOnConversationGroupListener via Open im sdkSetConversationGroupListener . It bypasses OIMManager callbacker and cannot be registered incrementally. Retain this callback object within the conversation manager for the duration of the session and configure it once during startup. Refer to Conversation groups overview /sdk/ios/conversation/managing conversation groups/overview conversation groups for detailed JSON payloads and callback contracts. Listen for initial synchronization Data synchronization lifecycle callbacks reside within the OIMConversationListener protocol. Implement the four core synchronization methods to track server state synchronization: Code example @interface SDKSyncStore @end @implementation SDKSyncStore void startListening OIMManager callbacker addConversationListener:self ; void stopListening OIMManager callbacker removeConversationListener:self ; void onSyncServerStart: BOOL reInstall self setSyncingWithProgress:0 reInstall:reInstall ; void onSyncServerProgress: NSInteger progress self setSyncingWithProgress:progress reInstall:self.reInstallSync ; void onSyncServerFinish: BOOL reInstall self setSyncReadyWithReInstall:reInstall ; self reloadVisibleSnapshots ; void onSyncServerFailed: BOOL reInstall self setSyncFailedWithReInstall:reInstall ; @end When reInstall evaluates to YES , synchronization follows a local database rebuild, indicating that complete state restoration is underway. Track synchronization progress with onSyncServerProgress: . Once synchronization finishes, re query initial data snapshots required by visible views, and subsequently process incremental updates dispatched by domain listeners. Synchronization events operate independently of query API callbacks and carry no business entity merge keys. Process synchronization completion, query snapshot fetching, and subsequent real time event merges as distinct operational phases, scoping data strictly by user account.

title: Logging
description: Configure OpenIM iOS SDK logs, write application diagnostics, and upload logs.
keywords: sdk ios v4 sdk ios logger
content: OpenIM iOS SDK logging aids in diagnosing initialization, connection, and business API invocation issues. Configure initialization settings to adjust log levels, standard output forwarding, and log storage directories. Configure logging during initialization Configure logging options on OIMInitConfig before initializing the SDK: Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | logLevel | NSInteger | No | SDK log severity level. Defaults to 6 . | | isLogStandardOutput | BOOL | No | Whether to print SDK core logs to standard output. | | logFilePath | NSString | No | Custom directory path for log file storage. Must be writable by the application sandbox. | | systemType | NSString | No | System type identifier recorded in log headers e.g., @"ios" . | Higher log verbosity generates larger log volumes. Ensure logFilePath references a valid sandbox directory with write permissions. Code example OIMInitConfig config = OIMInitConfig new ; config.platform = iPhone; config.apiAddr = apiAddress; config.wsAddr = websocketAddress; config.dataDir = dataDirectory; config.logLevel = 4; config.isLogStandardOutput = YES; config.logFilePath = logDirectory; config.systemType = @"ios"; Write application diagnostic logs Inject application specific business context into SDK log streams by calling logs:line:msgs:err:keyAndValues:logLevel: : OIMManager manager logs: NSString stringWithUTF8String: FILE .lastPathComponent line: LINE msgs:@"send message failed" err:errorMessage keyAndValues:@ @"conversationID", conversationID, @"clientMsgID", clientMsgID logLevel:2 ; Pass keyAndValues as alternating key and value pairs to attach diagnostic metadata such as conversationID and clientMsgID . Upload logs Upload SDK logs to the remote server for remote troubleshooting: OIMManager manager uploadLogsWithProgress:^ NSInteger saveBytes, NSInteger currentBytes, NSInteger totalBytes self updateLogUploadCurrentBytes:currentBytes totalBytes:totalBytes ; line:2000 ex:@"support ticket 42" onSuccess:^ NSString Nullable data self showLogUploadCompleted ; onFailure:^ NSInteger code, NSString message self showLogUploadError:code message:message ; ; The progress closure sequentially delivers saved bytes, currently processed bytes, and total bytes. Return value The onSuccess callback indicates that the log upload request completed successfully. If the upload encounters an error, inspect code and message in onFailure to diagnose the failure.

title: OpenIM Android SDK overview
description: Integrate real-time chat, users, conversations, groups, messages, signaling, and events into native Android applications with OpenIM Android SDK.
keywords: sdk android v4 sdk android overview
content: The OpenIM Android SDK provides real time instant messaging capabilities for native Android applications. Built for Java and Kotlin, the SDK exposes the unified OpenIMClient entry point and domain specific managers to manage conversations, messages, groups, relationships, and signaling. title: Before you start
description: Prepare your OpenIMServer, credentials, and Android project environment before initializing, authenticating, or sending messages.
keywords: sdk android v4 sdk android getting-started before-you-start
content: Before integrating the OpenIM Android SDK into a native Android app, verify that you have an accessible OpenIMServer deployment, valid user authentication credentials, and an Android project configured to meet SDK build requirements. These prerequisites apply to both Authenticate and manage a session /sdk/android/getting started/authenticate and manage session and Send your first message /sdk/android/getting started/send first message . Prepare OpenIMServer If you have not deployed an OpenIMServer instance yet, follow the Docker deployment guide /docs/guides/deployment/docker compose . Ensure that both physical Android devices and emulators can reach the following server endpoints: | Endpoint | Description | | | | | apiAddr | OpenIMServer HTTP API endpoint used for authentication, data synchronization, and resource requests. | | wsAddr | OpenIMServer WebSocket endpoint used for persistent connections and real time events. | Do not verify endpoints only on your development workstation. In the Android emulator, localhost points to the virtual device itself, not your host computer. When running OpenIMServer locally on your development machine, forward the HTTP and WebSocket ports to the emulator using adb : adb reverse tcp:10002 tcp:10002 adb reverse tcp:10001 tcp:10001 Once forwarded, the app inside the emulator can use http://127.0.0.1:10002 as apiAddr and ws://127.0.0.1:10001 as wsAddr . Replace port numbers with the actual listening ports configured on your machine, and confirm that adb is connected to your target emulator before executing the commands. For production environments, use HTTPS and WSS endpoints, and verify DNS resolution, TLS certificates, firewalls, reverse proxies, and WebSocket upgrade handshakes on physical devices. Prepare users and tokens A userID uniquely identifies a user in OpenIM, while a token authenticates that user session. Your business backend is responsible for creating or binding users and issuing matching userID and token pairs to the Android client. Before integrating OpenIMServer REST APIs into your backend service, refer to Preparation /platform api/prepare to use api and Get a user token /platform api/auth/tokens/get user token . The Android SDK login requires the following values: | Field | Description | | | | | userID | The OpenIM user ID of the signing in user. | | token | The authentication token corresponding to the user ID. | | apiAddr | The OpenIMServer HTTP API URL. | | wsAddr | The OpenIMServer WebSocket URL. | The userID must match the token subject; otherwise, authentication fails. Prepare the Android project Before integrating the SDK, verify that your Android project meets the following requirements: Set minSdk to 21 or higher, enable Java 8 language desugaring/compilation options, and configure compileSdk to 36 or higher. Declare android.permission.INTERNET in your AndroidManifest.xml and grant permissions to access network states. Prepare a dedicated, persistent directory in private app storage such as a subfolder in context.filesDir ; never place SDK local SQLite databases in cache or shared external storage. Ensure physical devices can resolve and connect to apiAddr , wsAddr , and media storage domains. Verify that your app release packaging includes the native ABIs required by your target architectures. Ensure your app gracefully handles lifecycle events, including network reconnection, foreground/background switching, token expiration, forced logout kicked offline , and multi device synchronization. For dependency declarations and manifest configuration, see Integrate for Android /sdk/android/getting started/environment specific implementation . For SDK initialization and login flows, see Authenticate and manage a session /sdk/android/getting started/authenticate and manage session . Next steps After completing your preparations, proceed to Authenticate and manage a session /sdk/android/getting started/authenticate and manage session . After confirming that authentication succeeds and receiving the connection established callback OnConnListener.onConnectSuccess , verify message delivery with Send your first message /sdk/android/getting started/send first message .

title: Integrate for Android
description: Add OpenIM Android SDK dependencies and network permissions to your Android project.
keywords: sdk android v4 sdk android getting-started environment-specific-implementation
content: Before integrating the OpenIM Android SDK into a native Android project, declare the core dependencies in your Gradle build scripts and request the required network permissions in the application manifest. After configuring your build environment, proceed to Authenticate and manage a session /sdk/android/getting started/authenticate and manage session to initialize the SDK and complete authentication. Add SDK dependencies Add the following dependencies to your application module's build.gradle : dependencies implementation 'io.openim:android sdk: @aar' implementation 'io.openim:core sdk: @aar' implementation 'com.google.code.gson:gson: ' Replace the placeholders with matching dependency versions from the official SDK release notes. Do not mix Android SDK wrapper layers with Core AAR binaries from different release tags. For team projects, commit your resolved dependency locks to avoid version drift. Configure the manifest Declare network permissions in AndroidManifest.xml : Next steps Authenticate and manage a session /sdk/android/getting started/authenticate and manage session Send your first message /sdk/android/getting started/send first message

title: Authenticate and manage a session
description: Initialize the OpenIM Android SDK, log in, monitor connection status, handle session lifecycle callbacks, and log out.
keywords: sdk android v4 sdk android getting-started authenticate-and-manage-session
content: The OpenIM Android SDK initializes the local runtime environment and establishes a user session to connect to instant messaging services. Before starting authentication, verify that you completed the server, user credentials, and token preparations listed in Before you start /sdk/android/getting started/before you start , and configured dependencies and permissions according to Integrate for Android /sdk/android/getting started/environment specific implementation . The complete session flow is as follows: 1. Create a stable connection listener OnConnListener within an application scoped session component. 2. Initialize the SDK runtime environment and confirm that initialization succeeds. 3. Configure domain specific event listeners centrally before authenticating. 4. Retrieve the userID and authentication token from your business backend and call login . 5. Wait for both the login callback to succeed and the persistent connection callback onConnectSuccess to fire before executing operations that require connectivity. 6. Log out when switching accounts or signing out, and clean up application level state after the callback completes. The apiAddr , wsAddr , userID , and token parameters referenced below are provided by your application configuration or business backend. Initialize and handle connection lifecycle Create the local data directory, initialize the SDK, and register the connection listener within your Application lifecycle: import android.app.Application; import java.io.File; import io.openim.android.sdk.OpenIMClient; import io.openim.android.sdk.enums.LogLevel; import io.openim.android.sdk.listener.OnConnListener; import io.openim.android.sdk.models.InitConfig; File dataDirectory = new File application.getFilesDir , "openim" ; if dataDirectory.exists && dataDirectory.mkdirs throw new IllegalStateException "Cannot create the OpenIM data directory." ; InitConfig config = new InitConfig apiAddr, wsAddr, dataDirectory.getAbsolutePath ; config.logLevel = LogLevel.Info; config.isLogStandardOutput = false; OnConnListener connectionListener = new OnConnListener @Override public void onConnecting // Connection establishment is in progress. @Override public void onConnectSuccess // The connection is ready. Resume operations that depend on connectivity. @Override public void onConnectFailed long code, String error // Handle connection failure using code and error. @Override public void onKickedOffline // Clean up current session state and prompt the user to re authenticate. @Override public void onUserTokenExpired // Acquire a new token from your backend and re authenticate. @Override public void onUserTokenInvalid String reason // Clean up current session state and prompt the user to re authenticate. ; boolean initialized = OpenIMClient.getInstance .initSDK application, config, connectionListener ; if initialized throw new IllegalStateException "OpenIMClientSDK initialization failed." ; The initSDK method returns true when the local SDK runtime initializes successfully. Connection callbacks on OnConnListener begin reporting persistent connection state after you call login . | Field | Type | Description | | | | | | application | Application | The application level Context holding the SDK lifecycle. | | apiAddr | String | The OpenIMServer HTTP API URL. | | wsAddr | String | The OpenIMServer WebSocket URL. | | dataDirectory | File | The persistent private app directory used for SDK SQLite databases and logs. | | config.logLevel | int | Sets the logging verbosity using LogLevel constants. | | isLogStandardOutput | boolean | Determines whether the SDK prints logs to standard output. | Initialize the SDK once in your Application class or an application scoped session manager. The Android SDK wrapper automatically manages app foreground/background transitions and network connectivity changes. Register listeners before logging in SDK listener registration methods follow setter semantics, where each call replaces the previous listener. Create long lived listeners in an application level event manager, and then dispatch events to your presentation layers. For listener registration patterns, lifecycle rules, and listener replacement behaviors, see Event overview /sdk/android/events/overview events . The SDK does not expose remove or unset methods. When signing out or switching accounts, stop dispatching callbacks to views belonging to the previous account, and register new listeners for the incoming user account before calling login . Sign in the current user Authenticate the user using login : OpenIMClient.getInstance .login new OnBase @Override public void onError int code, String error // Handle login failure using code and error. @Override public void onSuccess String data // The authentication request succeeded. , userID, token ; A successful onSuccess callback indicates that the authentication request succeeded on the server. The onConnectSuccess callback indicates that the persistent WebSocket connection has been established. Although authentication is typically followed immediately by connection establishment, do not launch concurrent login attempts, and do not assume that authentication alone means real time data synchronization has completed. Query login status Check the local login status and retrieve the active user ID: int loginStatus = OpenIMClient.getInstance .getLoginStatus ; if loginStatus == LoginStatus.Logged String currentUserID = OpenIMClient.getInstance .getLoginUserID ; // currentUserID is the authenticated user ID. | Status | Description | | | | | LoginStatus.Logout | The SDK is currently logged out. | | LoginStatus.Logging | Authentication is currently in progress. Avoid triggering concurrent login calls. | | LoginStatus.Logged | The SDK is logged in. Monitor OnConnListener for real time network connectivity. | getLoginStatus and getLoginUserID read cached session state stored locally in the SDK and do not trigger network requests or connection callbacks. When switching users, log out of the existing session first rather than calling login directly with new credentials. Handle token expiration and kick offline events When onUserTokenExpired or onUserTokenInvalid fires, request a fresh authentication token from your business backend and re authenticate. The onKickedOffline callback indicates that another client session or an administrative action revoked the active session, which is distinct from an explicit client logout. These callbacks are scoped to the active session. When switching accounts, cancel background tasks and UI subscriptions associated with the previous user before proceeding. Log out and release SDK resources Terminate the active session: OpenIMClient.getInstance .logout new OnBase @Override public void onError int code, String error // Handle logout failure using code and error. @Override public void onSuccess String data // The session has terminated successfully. ; A successful logout callback confirms that the local session has ended and the server connection is closed. Clean up application level user state after onSuccess fires. When switching users, wait for logout completion before initiating login for the new account. When the application terminates or no longer requires the SDK, release the runtime environment: OpenIMClient.getInstance .unInit ; unInit tears down the SDK runtime environment. Do not use it as a substitute for logging out, and do not call it when destroying individual activities or fragments. Next steps Before you start /sdk/android/getting started/before you start Integrate for Android /sdk/android/getting started/environment specific implementation Send your first message /sdk/android/getting started/send first message

title: Send your first message
description: Send and verify your first direct text message in a native Android application.
keywords: sdk android v4 sdk android getting-started send-first-message
content: Sending a single direct text message verifies that SDK initialization, connection establishment, and message delivery pipelines are functioning properly. Before proceeding, complete SDK initialization and user login as described in Authenticate and manage a session /sdk/android/getting started/authenticate and manage session . Prerequisites Prepare two test user accounts: one for the sender and one for the recipient. Initialize the SDK on both accounts following Authenticate and manage a session /sdk/android/getting started/authenticate and manage session ; the recipient must register the application message listener prior to logging in. Replace user b in the examples below with the actual recipient's userID . Step 1: Listen for incoming messages on the recipient client The recipient client registers the message listener before logging in and updates the chat interface when onRecvNewMessage Message message fires. For complete listener registration details, event payloads, and dispatch architecture, see Receive messages /sdk/android/message/receiving messages/receive messages . Do not duplicate message listener registrations inside individual chat screens. Step 2: Confirm connection readiness Once both users log in and the sender's client receives onConnectSuccess from OnConnListener , the client is ready to send messages. Ensure the recipient maintains an active connection to receive messages immediately. If disconnected, wait for reconnection rather than repeating login calls. Step 3: Send a text message Send a direct chat text message Construct the message entity first, then dispatch it. Pass the recipient userID as the target, leaving the group ID parameter as an empty string. Message message = OpenIMClient.getInstance .messageManager .createTextMessage "Hello, OpenIM" ; OnMsgSendCallback sendCallback = new OnMsgSendCallback @Override public void onProgress long progress // Text messages typically do not report upload progress. @Override public void onError int code, String error // Notify the user of failure and enable retry. @Override public void onSuccess Message sentMessage // Update the sender UI with the delivered sentMessage. ; OpenIMClient.getInstance .messageManager.sendMessage sendCallback, message, "user b", "", new OfflinePushInfo ; OfflinePushInfo configures push notification behavior. Pass a default empty instance for initial verification, then populate title, summary, and custom payload fields as required. When onSuccess triggers on the sender client, the message has been delivered to the server. When onRecvNewMessage fires on the recipient client, the message has arrived on the remote device. When both callbacks fire with matching content, your end to end messaging pipeline is verified. Send a group chat text message To send a group message, set recvUid to an empty string and pass the destination groupID : Message groupMessage = OpenIMClient.getInstance .messageManager .createTextMessage "Hello everyone, OpenIM" ; OpenIMClient.getInstance .messageManager.sendMessage sendCallback, groupMessage, "", "group 123", new OfflinePushInfo ; Supply either recvUid or groupID in a single invocation, leaving the other as an empty string. Verify delivery The sender receives a successful onSuccess callback via OnMsgSendCallback . The recipient receives onRecvNewMessage via OnAdvancedMsgListener and renders the text message content. Next steps Authenticate and manage a session /sdk/android/getting started/authenticate and manage session OpenIM Android SDK overview /sdk/android/overview

title: User overview
description: Understand current user profiles, public profiles, account settings, and presence management in the OpenIM Android SDK.
keywords: sdk android v4 sdk android user overview-user
content: The OpenIM Android SDK identifies users through unique userID values. User APIs read and update the current user's profile, retrieve public user information, and subscribe to real time online presence states. Friend relationships, friend applications, and blocklists belong to relationship management; for their associated data types, APIs, and state updates, see Relationship overview /sdk/android/user/overview relationships . User data models The Android SDK uses distinct data models tailored to different application contexts: | Class | Application scenario | Primary operations | | | | | | LocalUser | The authenticated user's profile, settings screens, avatar, nickname, and account preferences. | Get current user profile /sdk/android/user/user profile/get self local user info , Update the current user profile /sdk/android/user/user profile/set self info | | PublicUserInfo | Querying application users and presenting public profile cards. | Get user profiles /sdk/android/user/user profile/get users info | | UsersOnlineStatus | Online presence, connection status, and active platform lists. | Subscribe to user status /sdk/android/user/online status/subscribe users online status , Refresh subscribed user status /sdk/android/user/online status/get subscribe online users status , Unsubscribe from user status /sdk/android/user/online status/unsubscribe users online status | LocalUser represents the authenticated user, whereas PublicUserInfo models queryable public contact profiles. Group member profiles, in group nicknames, and member moderation belong to group capabilities. Navigation by task | Task | Documentation page | | | | | Query public profiles by userID to display contact cards | Get user profiles /sdk/android/user/user profile/get users info | | Retrieve or update the current user's nickname, avatar, and custom extensions | Get current user profile /sdk/android/user/user profile/get self local user info , Update the current user profile /sdk/android/user/user profile/set self info | | Set account level message reception and notification rules | Set global message reception /sdk/android/user/user profile/set global message reception | | Configure how incoming friend requests are evaluated | Set friend request permissions /sdk/android/user/user profile/set friend add permission | | Subscribe to, query, and cancel user online presence | Subscribe to user status /sdk/android/user/online status/subscribe users online status , Refresh subscribed user status /sdk/android/user/online status/get subscribe online users status , Unsubscribe from user status /sdk/android/user/online status/unsubscribe users online status | | Manage friends, applications, or blocklists | Relationship overview /sdk/android/user/overview relationships | State updates The Android SDK's UserInfoManager retains a single listener instance. Register OnUserListener centrally within an application event manager, and merge local cached user state using userID as the unique key before dispatching updates to UI observers: Current user profile changes: see Update the current user profile /sdk/android/user/user profile/set self info . Online presence changes: see Subscribe to user status /sdk/android/user/online status/subscribe users online status . Friend relationships, requests, and blocklist updates: see Relationship overview /sdk/android/user/overview relationships .

title: Get user profiles
description: Batch query public user profile cards by a list of user IDs using getUsersInfo().
keywords: sdk android v4 sdk android user user-profile get-users-info
content: Batch query public basic profiles for application users by their user IDs. This is suitable for contact search, stranger profile cards, and user candidate presentations. Query public profiles Pass a list of target user IDs to retrieve public profile snapshots in batches. Filter empty strings and duplicate IDs before calling, and keep batch sizes reasonable. Code example List userIDs = Arrays.asList "user a", "user b" ; OpenIMClient.getInstance .userInfoManager.getUsersInfo new OnBase @Override public void onSuccess List users // Render user profiles with users @Override public void onError int code, String error // Handle error , userIDs ; Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | base | OnBase | Yes | Callback delivering the asynchronous operation result. | | userIDs | List | Yes | List of target user IDs to query. Remove duplicate or empty entries before calling. | Return value The successful callback returns a List containing the matched public user records: | Field | Description | | | | | userID | Unique global user ID. | | nickname | Public display nickname. | | faceURL | Public avatar URL. | | ex | Custom public extension string. | | createTime | Account registration Unix timestamp. | Cache and merge returned public profiles using userID as the unique key. To modify the authenticated user's own profile and extension data, see Update the current user profile /sdk/android/user/user profile/set self info . Search and add friends When your application obtains candidate userID values, query and display their public profile cards first. After user confirmation, initiate a friend request using Send a friend application /sdk/android/user/friend applications/add friend . This method performs exact queries by userID . Fuzzy searching by nickname or phone number requires dedicated backend business API support. Select profile models by context A single userID resolves to different profile models depending on context: | Context | Model class | | | | | User search, candidate lists, stranger cards | PublicUserInfo | | Friend lists, contact screens, friend remarks | FriendInfo | | Group member lists, in group nicknames, group roles | GroupMembersInfo | For friend profiles, see Get friend profiles /sdk/android/user/friends/get friends info . For group member profiles, see Get the group member list /sdk/android/group/retrieving group members/get group member list . Next steps Get the friend list /sdk/android/user/friends/get friend list page Get friend profiles /sdk/android/user/friends/get friends info Get received friend applications /sdk/android/user/friend applications/get recv friend application list

title: Get current user profile
description: Retrieve the cached profile for the authenticated user from local storage using getSelfLocalUserInfo().
keywords: sdk android v4 sdk android user user-profile get-self-local-user-info
content: Retrieve a snapshot of the authenticated account's complete profile directly from local storage. This snapshot includes nickname, avatar, custom extension fields, and account wide preferences. This method reads from local storage without executing network requests. Code example OpenIMClient.getInstance .userInfoManager.getSelfLocalUserInfo new OnBase @Override public void onSuccess LocalUser user // Update current user profile using user @Override public void onError int code, String error // Handle error ; Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | base | OnBase | Yes | Callback delivering the asynchronous operation result. | Return value The successful callback returns the LocalUser entity representing the authenticated user: | Field | Description | | | | | userID | Unique global user ID of the authenticated account. | | nickname | Current display nickname. | | faceURL | Current avatar URL. | | ex | Custom business extension string. | | attachedInfo Enterprise | Supplementary business metadata defined by the application. | | globalRecvMsgOpt | Global message reception mode: 0 for normal reception, 1 for rejecting messages, 2 for silent reception without notifications. | | addFriendPermission Enterprise | Friend request verification mode; for detailed values, see Set friend request permissions /sdk/android/user/user profile/set friend add permission . | If the user updates profile attributes from another client or via server side APIs, the SDK delivers the changes via OnUserListener.onSelfInfoUpdated . Update local cache records using userID as the primary key. For profile mutation APIs and listener registration, see Update the current user profile /sdk/android/user/user profile/set self info .

title: Update the current user profile
description: Update the nickname, avatar, or custom extensions for the authenticated user using setSelfInfo().
keywords: sdk android v4 sdk android user user-profile set-self-info
content: Update basic profile attributes for the authenticated user, including nickname, avatar URL, and custom business extension strings. Populate only the fields that require modification. Code example UserInfoReq request = new UserInfoReq ; request.setNickname displayName.trim ; request.setFaceURL avatarURL ; request.setEx extra ; OpenIMClient.getInstance .userInfoManager.setSelfInfo new OnBase @Override public void onSuccess String data // Profile updated successfully @Override public void onError int code, String error // Handle error , request ; Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | base | OnBase | Yes | Callback delivering the asynchronous operation result. | | request | UserInfoReq | Yes | Request payload holding fields to update. | Profile attributes | Field | Type | Description | | | | | | nickname | String | New display nickname to set. | | faceURL | String | New avatar image URL. | | ex | String | Custom business metadata string formatted according to application specifications. | Friend request permissions and account wide DND rules are managed independently; see Set friend request permissions /sdk/android/user/user profile/set friend add permission and Set global message reception /sdk/android/user/user profile/set global message reception . Return value The successful callback indicates that the server persisted the profile updates. The changes synchronize across all devices authenticated with the user account. State changes after the call After updating the profile, the SDK dispatches the update via OnUserListener . Locate the cached profile by userID , merge modified properties, and refresh the UI: @Override public void onSelfInfoUpdated UserInfo info // Current user profile updated; merge local cache and refresh the UI

title: Set global message reception
description: Configure account-level message reception and notification rules across all conversations.
keywords: sdk android v4 sdk android user user-profile set-global-message-reception
content: Configure account wide message reception and do not disturb DND policies that apply universally across all direct and group conversations. Set the global option integer code in the user configuration request, then submit it via Update the current user profile /sdk/android/user/user profile/set self info : Code example UserInfoReq request = new UserInfoReq ; request.setGlobalRecvMsgOpt 2 ; OpenIMClient.getInstance .userInfoManager.setSelfInfo new OnBase @Override public void onSuccess String data // Global message reception option configured successfully @Override public void onError int code, String error // Handle error , request ; Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | base | OnBase | Yes | Callback delivering the asynchronous operation result. | | request | UserInfoReq | Yes | User profile request payload containing the global reception mode integer code. | Message reception modes | Enum constant | Value | Description | | | | | | ReceiveMessageOpt.Normal | 0 | Receive messages normally with local alerts and push notifications. | | ReceiveMessageOpt.NotReceive | 1 | Block incoming messages entirely across all chats. | | ReceiveMessageOpt.NotNotify | 2 | Receive messages silently without sound, vibration, or push notifications global DND . | Return value Upon success, data in onSuccess returns a confirmation message. State changes after the call 1. Callback confirmation : The onSuccess callback indicates that the server recorded the global reception setting. If your application exposes a simple "Mute all notifications" toggle, switch between 0 and 2 ; mode 1 rejects incoming messages entirely and should be treated as a distinct privacy option. 2. Asynchronous event delivery : The current account receives the OnUserListener.onSelfInfoUpdated event containing the updated user profile with the new global message reception option. 3. Re query calibration : To verify or reload current account settings, call Get current user profile /sdk/android/user/user profile/get self local user info . For per conversation message reception overrides, see Set conversation message reception /sdk/android/conversation/managing conversations/set message receive option .

title: Set friend request permissions
description: Configure verification rules for incoming friend requests targeting the authenticated account.
keywords: sdk android v4 sdk android user user-profile set-friend-add-permission
content: Configure how the server handles incoming friend applications sent by other users such as requiring manual approval, auto accepting, or rejecting all incoming requests . This capability belongs to the Commercial Edition. Set the permission enum code in the user configuration request, then submit it via Update the current user profile /sdk/android/user/user profile/set self info : Code example UserInfoReq request = new UserInfoReq ; request.setAddFriendPermission AddFriendPermission.Allow.getValue ; OpenIMClient.getInstance .userInfoManager.setSelfInfo new OnBase @Override public void onSuccess String data // Friend request permissions updated successfully @Override public void onError int code, String error // Handle error , request ; Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | base | OnBase | Yes | Callback delivering the asynchronous operation result. | | request | UserInfoReq | Yes | User profile request payload containing the friend permission enum value. | Permission modes | Enum constant | Value | Description | | | | | | AddFriendPermission.Allow | 0 | Allows users to send friend requests, requiring manual review and approval by the recipient. | | AddFriendPermission.AllowNoReview | 1 | Automatically accepts incoming friend requests without manual approval. | | AddFriendPermission.Deny | 2 | Disallows any incoming friend requests to the account. | Return value Upon success, data in onSuccess returns a confirmation message. State changes after the call 1. Callback confirmation : The onSuccess callback indicates that the server recorded the updated friend request permission. 2. Scope of effect : This setting applies strictly to incoming friend requests initiated after the update. It does not alter existing friendships or auto resolve pending friend applications. 3. Asynchronous event delivery : The current account receives OnUserListener.onSelfInfoUpdated reflecting the updated user profile configuration. 4. Re query calibration : To review pending friend applications, see Get received friend applications /sdk/android/user/friend applications/get recv friend application list .

title: Subscribe to user status
description: Subscribe to the online presence and multi-platform login state of specified users.
keywords: sdk android v4 sdk android user online-status subscribe-users-online-status
content: Subscribe to real time online status and multi platform connection state for specified users. When subscription succeeds, the SDK delivers a snapshot of their current presence immediately and publishes incremental event updates whenever target users log in, disconnect, or change active platforms. Code example List userIDs = Arrays.asList "user a", "user b" ; OpenIMClient.getInstance .userInfoManager.subscribeUsersOnlineStatus new OnBase @Override public void onSuccess List states // Render online presence indicators using states @Override public void onError int code, String error // Handle error , userIDs ; Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | base | OnBase | Yes | Callback delivering the asynchronous operation result. | | userIDs | List | Yes | List of target user IDs to subscribe to. Subscribe on demand when entering a chat or list view. | Return value The successful callback returns an initial presence snapshot as List . Maintain your presence cache using userID as the unique key: | Field | Description | | | | | userID | Target user ID. | | status | Presence status 1 for online, 0 for offline . | | platformIDs | List of active client platforms such as Android, iOS, or Web platform codes . | State changes after the call Subsequent presence transitions for subscribed users arrive via OnUserListener : @Override public void onUserStatusChanged UsersOnlineStatus status // Received status update; update the UI matching status.getUserID When navigating away from a chat screen or when presence tracking is no longer needed, call Unsubscribe from user status /sdk/android/user/online status/unsubscribe users online status to conserve bandwidth and avoid unnecessary presence broadcasts.

title: Refresh subscribed user status
description: Retrieve current presence states and active platforms for all subscribed users.
keywords: sdk android v4 sdk android user online-status get-subscribe-online-users-status
content: Retrieve a current presence snapshot for all users currently subscribed by this client. This is used to refresh screen states or calibrate presence data on demand. Code example OpenIMClient.getInstance .userInfoManager.getSubscribeOnlineUsersStatus new OnBase @Override public void onSuccess List states // Render presence indicators using states @Override public void onError int code, String error // Handle error ; Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | base | OnBase | Yes | Callback delivering the asynchronous operation result. | Return value The successful callback returns the presence snapshot as List . Maintain your local cache using userID as the unique key: | Field | Description | | | | | userID | Target user ID. | | status | Presence status 1 for online, 0 for offline . | | platformIDs | List of active client platforms such as Android, iOS, or Web platform codes . | To subscribe to additional users or terminate existing subscriptions, see Subscribe to user status /sdk/android/user/online status/subscribe users online status and Unsubscribe from user status /sdk/android/user/online status/unsubscribe users online status .

title: Unsubscribe from user status
description: Cancel presence subscriptions for specified users to stop receiving real-time status updates.
keywords: sdk android v4 sdk android user online-status unsubscribe-users-online-status
content: Cancel active presence subscriptions when users scroll out of view, screens are destroyed, or accounts switch. This avoids processing extraneous status broadcast events. Code example List userIDs = Arrays.asList "user a", "user b" ; OpenIMClient.getInstance .userInfoManager.unsubscribeOnlineUsersStatus new OnBase @Override public void onSuccess String data // Unsubscription confirmed @Override public void onError int code, String error // Handle error , userIDs ; Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | base | OnBase | Yes | Callback delivering the asynchronous operation result. | | userIDs | List | Yes | List of target user IDs to unsubscribe from. Remove empty strings and duplicates before calling. | Return value Upon success, data in onSuccess returns a confirmation message. State changes after the call 1. Callback confirmation : The onSuccess callback confirms that the server has stopped broadcasting status transitions for the specified users to this client session. 2. Local cache management : Clear corresponding userID entries from your local presence cache according to your application requirements. 3. Resubscription : To resume receiving real time presence events, call Subscribe to user status /sdk/android/user/online status/subscribe users online status .

title: Relationship overview
description: Understand friend management, friend applications, and blocklist APIs in the OpenIM Android SDK.
keywords: sdk android v4 sdk android user overview-relationships
content: Relationship capabilities track friend connections, incoming/outgoing friend applications, and blocklists for the authenticated account. User profile details, account settings, and presence tracking belong to user capabilities; see User overview /sdk/android/user/overview user . Relationship models The Android SDK uses distinct models across relationship operations: | Class | Application scenario | Primary operations | | | | | | UserInfo | Comprehensive user profile and relationship details in friend lists, profile lookups, and blocklists | Get the friend list /sdk/android/user/friends/get friend list page , Get friend profiles /sdk/android/user/friends/get friends info , Get the blacklist /sdk/android/user/blacklist/get blacklist | | FriendInfo | Friend metadata, remarks, and custom relationship extension fields | Accessed via UserInfo.friendInfo , Search friends /sdk/android/user/friends/search friends | | FriendshipInfo | Check bilateral friendship state between the current user and a target | Check friendship status /sdk/android/user/friends/check friend | | FriendApplicationInfo | Incoming and outgoing friend applications along with their review states | Get received friend applications /sdk/android/user/friend applications/get recv friend application list , Get sent friend applications /sdk/android/user/friend applications/get send friend application list | | BlacklistInfo | Blocklist entry information | Accessed via UserInfo.blackInfo , Get the blacklist /sdk/android/user/blacklist/get blacklist | UserInfo contains comprehensive relation snapshots; access FriendInfo through the friendInfo property and BlacklistInfo through the blackInfo property. Navigation by task | Task | Documentation page | | | | | Paginate, search, or query specific friend profiles | Get the friend list /sdk/android/user/friends/get friend list page , Search friends /sdk/android/user/friends/search friends , Get friend profiles /sdk/android/user/friends/get friends info | | Check friendship status with a target user | Check friendship status /sdk/android/user/friends/check friend | | Update friend remarks or delete a friendship | Update friend information /sdk/android/user/friends/update friends , Delete a friend /sdk/android/user/friends/delete friend | | Send, query, accept, or reject friend applications | Send a friend application /sdk/android/user/friend applications/add friend , Get received friend applications /sdk/android/user/friend applications/get recv friend application list , Get sent friend applications /sdk/android/user/friend applications/get send friend application list , Accept a friend application /sdk/android/user/friend applications/accept friend application , Refuse a friend application /sdk/android/user/friend applications/refuse friend application | | View and manage the blocklist | Get the blacklist /sdk/android/user/blacklist/get blacklist , Block a user /sdk/android/user/blacklist/add blacklist , Unblock a user /sdk/android/user/blacklist/remove blacklist | State updates Relationship events are broadcast in real time through OnFriendshipListener . Deduplicate and incrementally merge friend records, friend applications, and blocklist entries using userID as the unique primary key: OpenIMClient client = OpenIMClient.getInstance ; client.friendshipManager.setOnFriendshipListener new OnFriendshipListener @Override public void onFriendApplicationAdded FriendApplicationInfo application // Handle new friend application @Override public void onFriendApplicationAccepted FriendApplicationInfo application // Handle friend application accepted @Override public void onFriendApplicationRejected FriendApplicationInfo application // Handle friend application rejected @Override public void onFriendApplicationDeleted FriendApplicationInfo application // Handle friend application deleted @Override public void onFriendAdded FriendInfo friend // Handle new friend added @Override public void onFriendInfoChanged FriendInfo friend // Handle friend profile or remark changed @Override public void onFriendDeleted FriendInfo friend // Handle friend removed @Override public void onBlacklistAdded BlacklistInfo user // Handle user added to blocklist @Override public void onBlacklistDeleted BlacklistInfo user // Handle user removed from blocklist ; Friend application updates: see Get received friend applications /sdk/android/user/friend applications/get recv friend application list . Friend relationships and profile updates: see Get the friend list /sdk/android/user/friends/get friend list page . Blocklist updates: see Get the blacklist /sdk/android/user/blacklist/get blacklist .

title: Get the friend list
description: Paginate the friend list for the authenticated user and synchronize friendship events in real time.
keywords: sdk android v4 sdk android user friends get-friend-list-page
content: Paginate the friend list for the authenticated account to prevent excessive memory and network overhead. Each record contains basic user profile information alongside friend specific attributes like remarks and source details. Code example OpenIMClient.getInstance .friendshipManager.getFriendListPage new OnBase @Override public void onSuccess List friends // Update friend list UI using friends @Override public void onError int code, String error // Handle error , 0, 40, true ; Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | base | OnBase | Yes | Callback delivering the asynchronous operation result. | | offset | int | Yes | Zero based paging offset; pass 0 for the initial page. | | count | int | Yes | Number of friend records to return in this page. | | filterBlack | boolean | Yes | When true , automatically filters out blocked users; when false , includes them. | Return value The successful callback returns the current page as List . Deduplicate and merge items into your local cache using userID as the unique key. When the returned item count is less than count , the end of the list has been reached. Commonly used fields within the friend records include: | Field | Description | | | | | userID | Global user ID of the friend. | | nickname | Public display nickname of the friend. | | faceURL | Avatar URL of the friend. | | remark | Private remark alias set by the authenticated user. | | ex | Custom relationship extension metadata. | | addSource | Channel or source through which friendship was established. | | operatorUserID | User ID of the operator who initiated or approved the relationship. | | createTime | Unix timestamp when friendship was established. | State changes after the call When friends are added, modified, or removed, the SDK dispatches real time events via OnFriendshipListener . Use userID as the primary key to merge updates or delete entries: @Override public void onFriendAdded FriendInfo friend // New friend added; insert into the list or refresh UI @Override public void onFriendInfoChanged FriendInfo friend // Nickname, remark, or avatar updated; refresh the item matching friend.getUserID @Override public void onFriendDeleted FriendInfo friend // Friendship terminated; remove the entry matching friend.getUserID from local cache

title: Search friends
description: Search friends locally by keywords matching user ID, nickname, and remark alias.
keywords: sdk android v4 sdk android user friends search-friends
content: Perform local fuzzy searches across the authenticated account's friend database, matching by user ID, nickname, and remark name. Code example OpenIMClient.getInstance .friendshipManager.searchFriends new OnBase @Override public void onSuccess List results // Display search results using results @Override public void onError int code, String error // Handle error , Collections.singletonList keyword.trim , true, true, true ; Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | base | OnBase | Yes | Callback delivering the asynchronous operation result. | | keywordList | List | Yes | List of search keywords, typically containing a single non empty query string. | | isSearchUserID | boolean | Yes | Whether to search against user IDs. | | isSearchNickname | boolean | Yes | Whether to search against nicknames. | | isSearchRemark | boolean | Yes | Whether to search against remark names. | At least one search toggle must be set to true . Return value The successful callback returns matching records as List . Deduplicate and render results using userID as the primary key. If no matching friends are found, an empty list is returned.

title: Get friend profiles
description: Batch query detailed friend relationships, remarks, and user profiles by user IDs.
keywords: sdk android v4 sdk android user friends get-friends-info
content: Batch query friend relationship details using a list of user IDs. Retrieved items include friend remarks, custom relation extensions, and basic user profile information. Code example OpenIMClient.getInstance .friendshipManager.getFriendsInfo new OnBase @Override public void onSuccess List friends for UserInfo friend : friends // Update friend profiles using friends @Override public void onError int code, String error // Handle error , Arrays.asList "user a", "user b" , true ; Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | base | OnBase | Yes | Callback delivering the asynchronous operation result. | | userIDs | List | Yes | List of target friend user IDs. Filter empty strings and duplicate entries before calling. | | filterBlack | boolean | Yes | When true , automatically filters out blocked users; when false , includes blocked friends. | Return value The successful callback returns a List containing matched friend entries. Merge the records into your local friend cache using userID as the primary key. If a specified user is not a friend or was excluded due to filterBlack == true , that user is omitted from the returned list. To display public profile cards for non friends, call Get user profiles /sdk/android/user/user profile/get users info ; to verify bilateral relationship state without fetching full profiles, see Check friendship status /sdk/android/user/friends/check friend .

title: Check friendship status
description: Batch verify friendship relationships between specified users and the authenticated account using checkFriend().
keywords: sdk android v4 sdk android user friends check-friend
content: Batch verify whether specified users have active friendship relationships with the authenticated account. This is typically used on user profile screens to toggle between "Add friend" and "Send message" actions. Code example OpenIMClient.getInstance .friendshipManager.checkFriend new OnBase @Override public void onSuccess List relations // Update relationship UI using relations @Override public void onError int code, String error // Handle error , Arrays.asList "user a", "user b" ; Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | base | OnBase | Yes | Callback delivering the asynchronous operation result. | | userIDs | List | Yes | List of user IDs to check. | Return value The successful callback returns a List . Match records using userID as the primary key: | Field | Description | | | | | userID | Target user ID. | | result | Friendship status code: 1 indicates the user is an active friend and not blocked; 0 indicates no friendship exists. | To retrieve detailed profiles including nicknames, avatars, and remarks, see Get friend profiles /sdk/android/user/friends/get friends info .

title: Update friend information
description: Update remarks, pinned status, or custom extensions for specified friends using updateFriendsReq().
keywords: sdk android v4 sdk android user friends update-friends
content: Modify friend relationship attributes, including setting remark aliases, pinning friends in the contacts list, and updating custom extension fields. Code example UpdateFriendsReq request = new UpdateFriendsReq ; request.setFriendUserIDs new String friendUserID ; request.setRemark remark.trim ; OpenIMClient.getInstance .friendshipManager.updateFriendsReq new OnBase @Override public void onSuccess String data // Friend information updated successfully @Override public void onError int code, String error // Handle error , request ; Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | base | OnBase | Yes | Callback delivering the asynchronous operation result. | | request | UpdateFriendsReq | Yes | Request payload containing updated friend attributes. | Request attributes | Field | Type | Description | | | | | | friendUserIDs | String | Array of target friend user IDs. When providing multiple IDs, specified field values overwrite existing values across all targets. | | remark | String | Remark alias set by the authenticated user for the friend. | | isPinned | boolean | Whether to pin the friend at the top of the contacts list. | | ex | String | Custom friend relationship metadata. | Return value The successful callback indicates that the server persisted the updated friend information. State changes after the call Once the updates take effect, the SDK dispatches the onFriendInfoChanged FriendInfo friend event via OnFriendshipListener . Locate the cached friend record using userID and update its modified properties. For complete listener registration details, see Get the friend list /sdk/android/user/friends/get friend list page .

title: Delete a friend
description: Terminate friendship with a specified user using deleteFriend().
keywords: sdk android v4 sdk android user friends delete-friend
content: Terminate the bilateral friendship between the authenticated user and a target user. Code example OpenIMClient.getInstance .friendshipManager.deleteFriend new OnBase @Override public void onSuccess String data // Friend deleted successfully @Override public void onError int code, String error // Handle error , friendUserID ; Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | base | OnBase | Yes | Callback delivering the asynchronous operation result. | | friendUserID | String | Yes | Target user ID to unfriend. | Return value The successful callback indicates that the server terminated the friendship. State changes after the call Once the friendship is dissolved, the SDK triggers the onFriendDeleted FriendInfo friend event via OnFriendshipListener . Locate and remove the friend record matching friend.getUserID from your local cache and update the UI. For complete listener registration details, see Get the friend list /sdk/android/user/friends/get friend list page . Deleting a friend does not purge conversation entries or chat history; to delete conversation history as well, see Delete a conversation and its messages /sdk/android/conversation/managing conversations/delete conversation with messages .

title: Send a friend application
description: Initiate a friend request to a target user with an optional verification message using addFriend().
keywords: sdk android v4 sdk android user friend-applications add-friend
content: Send a friend request to a specified user along with an optional verification greeting. Code example OpenIMClient.getInstance .friendshipManager.addFriend new OnBase @Override public void onSuccess String data // Friend request sent successfully @Override public void onError int code, String error // Handle error , "user b", "Hello, I am Alex" ; Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | base | OnBase | Yes | Callback delivering the asynchronous operation result. | | userID | String | Yes | Target user ID of the application recipient. | | reqMsg | String | No | Optional greeting or verification note attached to the application. | Return value Upon success, data in onSuccess returns a confirmation message. State changes after the call 1. Callback confirmation : The onSuccess callback indicates that the server recorded and dispatched the friend application; it does not indicate that the recipient has accepted it. If the recipient configured automatic approval without verification, friendship establishes immediately. 2. Asynchronous event delivery : The recipient receives OnFriendshipListener.onFriendApplicationAdded , delivering the new application info to merge using userID . If auto accepted, both sides receive onFriendAdded . 3. Re query calibration : The sender can inspect pending outgoing requests using Get sent friend applications /sdk/android/user/friend applications/get send friend application list . Track friend application updates across screens using userID as the unique identifier.

title: Get received friend applications
description: Paginate friend requests received by the authenticated account using getRecvFriendApplicationList().
keywords: sdk android v4 sdk android user friend-applications get-recv-friend-application-list
content: Paginate friend requests received by the authenticated account along with their approval states. This is typically used to render the "New Friends" view in a contacts screen. Code example GetFriendApplicationListAsRecipientReq request = new GetFriendApplicationListAsRecipientReq 0, 20 ; OpenIMClient.getInstance .friendshipManager.getRecvFriendApplicationList new OnBase @Override public void onSuccess List applications // Update received friend requests UI using applications @Override public void onError int code, String error // Handle error , request ; Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | base | OnBase | Yes | Callback delivering the asynchronous operation result. | | request | GetFriendApplicationListAsRecipientReq | Yes | Request payload holding paging parameters offset and count . | Paging request attributes | Field | Type | Description | | | | | | offset | int | Zero based paging offset; pass 0 for the first page. | | count | int | Number of application items requested for this page. | Return value The successful callback returns the current page as List . Deduplicate and merge entries into your local list using the applicant's user ID fromUserID as the primary key.
