The Android SDK delivers the event data as a JSON payload: @Override public void onConversationUserInputStatusChanged String payload InputStatesChangedData state = JsonUtil.toObj payload, InputStatesChangedData.class ; if state == null || state.getConversationID == null return; // state.getConversationID identifies the target conversation // state.getUserID identifies the typing user // state.getPlatformIDs contains platform IDs where the user is typing Merge and display typing indicators using state.getConversationID and state.getUserID . 3. Re query calibration : Typing indicators are ephemeral and expire automatically after a timeout. To actively query whether a user is currently typing, see Retrieve typing status /sdk/android/message/composing messages/get typing status .

title: Retrieve typing status
description: Use getInputState to retrieve a specified user’s current typing status in a conversation.
keywords: sdk android v4 sdk android message composing-messages get-typing-status
content: Query whether a specific user is currently typing in a conversation. The SDK returns a list of platform IDs where the user is actively typing, allowing you to calibrate the typing indicator when entering a chat or recovering from a network disconnection. Code example String conversationID = "si user a user b"; String userID = "user b"; OpenIMClient.getInstance .conversationManager.getInputState new OnBase @Override public void onSuccess List platformIDs boolean isTyping = platformIDs = null && platformIDs.isEmpty ; // isTyping indicates whether the user is actively typing @Override public void onError int code, String error // Failed to query typing status , conversationID, userID ; Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | base | OnBase | Yes | Callback handler for the asynchronous request. | | conversationID | String | Yes | Globally unique ID of the target conversation. | | userID | String | Yes | User ID of the target user to check. | Return value Upon success, onSuccess returns a list of platform IDs List where the user is currently typing. A non empty list indicates the user is actively typing on at least one client device. An empty or null list indicates the user is not actively typing. For real time typing indicators and listeners, see Update typing status /sdk/android/message/composing messages/update typing status .

title: Delete a local message
description: Use deleteMessageFromLocalStorage to delete only the message copy on the current device.
keywords: sdk android v4 sdk android message managing-messages delete-local-message
content: Delete a single message record exclusively from the local SQLite storage on the current device. This operation does not issue a network request to the server, does not alter cloud roaming history, and does not synchronize to other client devices logged into the same account or to chat peers. Code example String conversationID = "si user a user b"; String clientMsgID = "msg 001"; OpenIMClient.getInstance .messageManager.deleteMessageFromLocalStorage conversationID, clientMsgID, new OnBase @Override public void onSuccess String data // Local deletion succeeded, remove message from UI timeline @Override public void onError int code, String error // Failed to delete message from local storage ; Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | conversationID | String | Yes | Globally unique ID of the target conversation. | | clientMsgID | String | Yes | Client message ID of the message to delete. | | base | OnBase | Yes | Callback handler for the asynchronous request. | Return value Upon success, data in onSuccess returns a confirmation message. State changes after the call 1. Callback confirmation : The onSuccess callback confirms that the record was removed from the local database on this device. 2. Local scope : This is a local only operation that does not trigger network events or synchronization listeners. 3. Re query behavior : If the conversation history is later refetched from the server via Load older messages /sdk/android/message/retrieving messages/load older messages , the message may reappear because it remains in cloud storage. To delete messages from both local storage and the server across all devices, call Delete messages in a batch /sdk/android/message/managing messages/delete saved messages .

title: Delete messages in a batch
description: Delete multiple messages from one conversation for the current account with the Android SDK.
keywords: sdk android v4 sdk android message managing-messages delete-saved-messages
content: Batch delete message records within a designated conversation for the current account. You can configure whether the deletion synchronizes to other devices logged into the same account. This deletion applies only to the current user's mailbox and does not affect message copies retained by other participants. Code example String conversationID = "si user a user b"; String selectedClientMsgIDs = new String "msg 001", "msg 002" ; boolean isSync = true; // true: sync deletion to all devices; false: delete only locally and on current device's server view DeleteMessagesReq request = new DeleteMessagesReq isSync, conversationID, selectedClientMsgIDs ; OpenIMClient.getInstance .messageManager.deleteMessages request, new OnBase @Override public void onSuccess String data // Batch deletion succeeded @Override public void onError int code, String error // Failed to delete messages ; Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | request | DeleteMessagesReq | Yes | Batch deletion request object containing conversationID , an array of clientMsgIDs to delete, and the isSync synchronization flag. | | base | OnBase | Yes | Callback handler for the asynchronous request. | Return value Upon success, data in onSuccess returns a confirmation message. State changes after the call 1. Callback confirmation : The onSuccess callback indicates that the messages were deleted from local storage and the server. Remove the deleted items from the active UI list using clientMsgID . 2. Asynchronous event delivery : When isSync = true , other client devices logged into the same account receive deletion notifications through OnAdvanceMsgListener.onMsgDeleted . Clients should remove matching messages using clientMsgID . 3. Re query calibration : If message lists diverge, reload messages via Load older messages /sdk/android/message/retrieving messages/load older messages . For complete listener registration and lifecycle management, see Receive messages /sdk/android/message/receiving messages/receive messages .

title: Delete all messages from a user in a group chat
description: Delete every message sent by a specified user in a group chat with the Android SDK.
keywords: sdk android v4 sdk android message managing-messages delete-user-messages
content: Group owners and administrators can clear every historical message sent by a designated member in a group chat. This is commonly used to remove spam, moderate rule violations, or ban abusive accounts across a group conversation. Code example String conversationID = "g group 123"; String targetUserID = "user spammer"; OpenIMClient.getInstance .messageManager.deleteUserAllMessagesInConv conversationID, targetUserID, new OnBase @Override public void onSuccess String data // Deletion request processed successfully @Override public void onError int code, String error // Failed to delete user messages e.g. insufficient permissions ; Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | conversationID | String | Yes | Globally unique ID of the target group conversation. Group conversations only. | | targetUserID | String | Yes | User ID of the member whose messages should be cleared. | | base | OnBase | Yes | Callback handler for the asynchronous request. | Return value Upon success, data in onSuccess returns a confirmation message. State changes after the call 1. Callback confirmation : The onSuccess callback indicates that the server has executed the purge across the specified group conversation. 2. Asynchronous event delivery : All online group members receive an event via OnAdvanceMsgListener.onDeleteUserAllMsgsInConv : @Override public void onDeleteUserAllMsgsInConv DeleteUserAllMsgsListenerMsg event // Filter by event.getConversationID and event.getUserID // Remove all messages sent by this user from the local timeline Group members filter messages by conversationID and sendID == targetUserID , removing all matching bubbles from their active UI timeline. 3. Re query calibration : If UI state diverges after reconnecting, reload the message history using Load older messages /sdk/android/message/retrieving messages/load older messages . For complete listener registration and lifecycle management, see Receive messages /sdk/android/message/receiving messages/receive messages .

title: Revoke a message
description: Revoke a sent message and handle revocation notifications received by other clients.
keywords: sdk android v4 sdk android message managing-messages revoke-a-message
content: Recall a previously sent message within the allowed revocation time window. Upon successful invocation, the message in the conversation is marked as revoked, and peer clients receive an asynchronous event to replace the original message body with a revocation notice. Code example String conversationID = "si user a user b"; String clientMsgID = "msg 001"; OpenIMClient.getInstance .messageManager.revokeMessageV2 new OnBase @Override public void onSuccess String data // Revocation request processed successfully @Override public void onError int code, String error // Failed to revoke message e.g. exceeded allowed time limit , conversationID, clientMsgID ; Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | base | OnBase | Yes | Callback handler for the asynchronous request. | | conversationID | String | Yes | Globally unique ID of the conversation containing the message. | | clientMsgID | String | Yes | Client message ID of the message to revoke. | Return value Upon success, data in onSuccess returns a confirmation message. Handling message revocation events Clients across the conversation receive revocation notices through OnAdvanceMsgListener.onRecvMessageRevokedV2 : @Override public void onRecvMessageRevokedV2 RevokedInfo info // Find the original message using info.getClientMsgID // Update its state to revoked and display revoker name info.getRevokerNickname When receiving onRecvMessageRevokedV2 , match the targeted message using clientMsgID and render a revocation placeholder e.g., "Alex revoked a message" rather than deleting the message row from the list. State changes after the call 1. Callback confirmation : The onSuccess callback indicates that the server processed the revocation. 2. Asynchronous event delivery : Receiving clients receive onRecvMessageRevokedV2 with RevokedInfo . Update message state in place using clientMsgID . 3. Re query calibration : If message states fall out of sync, reload message history via Load older messages /sdk/android/message/retrieving messages/load older messages . For complete listener registration and lifecycle management, see Receive messages /sdk/android/message/receiving messages/receive messages .

title: Modify a message
description: Modify supported message content and handle modification events received by other clients.
keywords: sdk android v4 sdk android message managing-messages modify-a-message
content: Edit and update the content of an already sent message online. Typically, you clone the original Message object, modify editable fields such as text content in textElem , and submit the updated object while retaining all original identifiers clientMsgID , serverMsgID . Code example // Clone or copy original message and update text content Message modifiedMessage = originalMessage; modifiedMessage.getTextElem .setContent "This is the updated message content." ; OpenIMClient.getInstance .messageManager.modifyMessage new OnBase @Override public void onSuccess String data // Message modified successfully @Override public void onError int code, String error // Failed to modify message , modifiedMessage ; Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | base | OnBase | Yes | Callback handler for the asynchronous request. | | message | Message | Yes | The updated Message object. Must retain original identifiers including clientMsgID , serverMsgID , and conversation bindings. | Return value Upon success, data in onSuccess returns a confirmation message. Handling message modification events After a message is modified, other online clients in the conversation receive the updated Message through OnAdvanceMsgListener.onMessageModified : @Override public void onMessageModified Message message // message contains updated content; refresh UI by message.getClientMsgID Upon receiving onMessageModified , match the message by clientMsgID to refresh the text bubble in place and display an "edited" status indicator. State changes after the call 1. Callback confirmation : The onSuccess callback indicates that the modification was saved on the server. Update the local UI model with the new content. 2. Asynchronous event delivery : Peer clients receive onMessageModified with the complete updated Message . Merge in place using clientMsgID . 3. Re query calibration : If message content falls out of sync, reload via Load older messages /sdk/android/message/retrieving messages/load older messages . For complete listener registration and lifecycle management, see Receive messages /sdk/android/message/receiving messages/receive messages .

title: View pinned messages
description: Use getConversationPinnedMsgs to retrieve pinned messages in a conversation.
keywords: sdk android v4 sdk android message managing-messages get-pinned-messages
content: Query the list of messages currently pinned in a designated conversation. This method is typically invoked when entering a chat window to render the persistent pinned message banner at the top of the interface. Code example String conversationID = "g group 123"; OpenIMClient.getInstance .messageManager.getConversationPinnedMsgs new OnBase @Override public void onSuccess List messages // messages contains all pinned messages in the current conversation @Override public void onError int code, String error // Handle query failure , conversationID ; Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | base | OnBase | Yes | Callback handler for the asynchronous request. | | conversationID | String | Yes | Globally unique ID of the target conversation. | Return value Upon success, messages in onSuccess returns the list of pinned messages List for the designated conversation. State changes after the call 1. Callback confirmation : The onSuccess callback returns a snapshot list of pinned messages. Clients should render pinned banner items using clientMsgID as the distinct item identifier. 2. Asynchronous event delivery : This is a read only query and does not trigger state change events. Real time pin and unpin actions performed across participants are delivered through OnAdvanceMsgListener.onChangedPinnedMsg . 3. Re query calibration : If the pinned message header falls out of sync with client state, re run getConversationPinnedMsgs to calibrate against local database state. To change the pinned status of a message, see Pin or unpin a message /sdk/android/message/managing messages/set message pinned .

title: Pin or unpin a message
description: Change a conversation message’s pinned state and handle pinned-message change events.
keywords: sdk android v4 sdk android message managing-messages set-message-pinned
content: Pin an important message to the top of a conversation or unpin a previously pinned message. Pinned status is a shared conversation attribute. In group chats, pinning is typically restricted to group owners and administrators. Once pinned, member devices display the message prominently in a pinned banner at the top of the chat screen. Code example String conversationID = "g group 123"; String clientMsgID = "msg 001"; boolean isPinned = true; // true: pin the message; false: unpin the message OpenIMClient.getInstance .messageManager.setConversationPinnedMsg new OnBase @Override public void onSuccess String data // Pinned status updated successfully @Override public void onError int code, String error // Handle update failure , conversationID, clientMsgID, isPinned ; Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | base | OnBase | Yes | Callback handler for the asynchronous request. | | conversationID | String | Yes | Globally unique ID of the target conversation. | | clientMsgID | String | Yes | Client message ID of the target message to pin or unpin. | | isPinned | boolean | Yes | Pin status flag: true to pin the message, false to unpin it. | Return value Upon success, data in onSuccess returns a confirmation message. State changes after the call 1. Callback confirmation : The onSuccess callback indicates that the pinned state change was saved on the server. 2. Asynchronous event delivery : Conversation members receive the change event through OnAdvanceMsgListener.onChangedPinnedMsg : @Override public void onChangedPinnedMsg ChangedPinnedMsg event // event.getConversationID identifies the target conversation // event.getMsgs returns the updated list of pinned messages Clients should merge the new list of pinned items using event.getConversationID and clientMsgID . 3. Re query calibration : To retrieve the complete current list of pinned messages directly from storage, see View pinned messages /sdk/android/message/managing messages/get pinned messages . For complete listener registration and lifecycle management, see Receive messages /sdk/android/message/receiving messages/receive messages .

title: Insert a local direct message
description: Use insertSingleMessageToLocalStorage to insert a one-to-one message visible only on the current device.
keywords: sdk android v4 sdk android message managing-messages insert-local-single-message
content: Write a pre constructed message directly into the local SQLite database of the current device for a one to one conversation. This operation does not issue a network request to the server, does not deliver the message to the peer user, and does not synchronize to other devices logged into the same account. It is commonly used for inserting local security prompts, client side assistant messages, or migrating offline records. To send an actual message across the network, call Send a message /sdk/android/message/sending messages/send message . Code example String receiverUserID = "user b"; String senderUserID = "user a"; OpenIMClient.getInstance .messageManager.insertSingleMessageToLocalStorage new OnBase @Override public void onSuccess String data // Message written to local storage, refresh direct chat UI @Override public void onError int code, String error // Handle insertion failure , message, receiverUserID, senderUserID ; Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | base | OnBase | Yes | Callback handler for the asynchronous request. | | message | Message | Yes | Pre constructed message object typically created via one of the create Message APIs . | | receiver | String | Yes | User ID of the direct chat recipient. | | sender | String | Yes | User ID of the direct chat sender. These two fields determine message direction and must not be inverted. | Return value Upon success, data in onSuccess returns a confirmation message. State changes after the call 1. Callback confirmation : The onSuccess callback confirms that the message was saved to local storage on this device. Insert the item into your conversation timeline using clientMsgID as the distinct key. 2. Local scope : This is a local only operation that does not trigger network requests or dispatch OnAdvanceMsgListener.onRecvNewMessage events. 3. Re query calibration : The inserted message exists only in the local database on this device. It will not synchronize to cloud roaming history or appear on other devices logged into the same account.

title: Insert a local group message
description: Use insertGroupMessageToLocalStorage to insert a group message visible only on the current device.
keywords: sdk android v4 sdk android message managing-messages insert-local-group-message
content: Write a pre constructed message directly into the local SQLite database of the current device for a group conversation. This operation does not issue a network request to the server, does not dispatch messages to other group members, and does not persist to cloud storage. It is suitable for displaying group join safety notices, local event announcements, or device specific system logs. To send an actual message to all group members across the network, call Send a message /sdk/android/message/sending messages/send message . Code example String groupID = "group 123"; String senderUserID = "user a"; OpenIMClient.getInstance .messageManager.insertGroupMessageToLocalStorage new OnBase @Override public void onSuccess String data // Message written to local storage, refresh group chat UI @Override public void onError int code, String error // Handle insertion failure , message, groupID, senderUserID ; Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | base | OnBase | Yes | Callback handler for the asynchronous request. | | message | Message | Yes | Pre constructed message object typically created via one of the create Message APIs . | | groupID | String | Yes | Globally unique ID of the target group. | | sender | String | Yes | User ID designated as the sender of the message. | Return value Upon success, data in onSuccess returns a confirmation message. State changes after the call 1. Callback confirmation : The onSuccess callback confirms that the message record was written to the local database. Insert the message into your group chat UI timeline using clientMsgID . 2. Local scope : This is a local only operation that does not persist to the server, does not dispatch to other group members, and does not fire OnAdvanceMsgListener.onRecvNewMessage events. 3. Re query calibration : The message exists only on the current device. It will not synchronize across devices logged into the same account or appear in cloud roaming history.

title: Clear all local messages
description: Use deleteAllMsgFromLocal to clear all messages stored on the current device.
keywords: sdk android v4 sdk android message managing-messages clear-all-local-messages
content: Clear all historical message records stored in the local database on the current device for the logged in account. This operation does not issue a network request, does not alter cloud roaming history, and does not affect message records on other devices or peer accounts. It is recommended to display a confirmation prompt to the user before executing this action. Code example OpenIMClient.getInstance .messageManager.deleteAllMsgFromLocal new OnBase @Override public void onSuccess String data // Local messages cleared, reset active conversation timelines @Override public void onError int code, String error // Handle clearing failure ; Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | base | OnBase | Yes | Callback handler for the asynchronous request. | Return value Upon success, data in onSuccess returns a confirmation message. State changes after the call 1. Callback confirmation : The onSuccess callback confirms that all local message data has been cleared from SQLite storage on this device. Clear active message timeline displays across all conversations. 2. Local scope : This is a local only operation that does not trigger network requests or broadcast events to other devices. 3. Re query calibration : Because server records remain intact, subsequent roaming history queries may retrieve previous messages from cloud storage. To delete messages from both local storage and the server across all devices, see Clear all saved messages /sdk/android/message/managing messages/clear all messages .

title: Clear all saved messages
description: Use deleteAllMsgFromLocalAndSvr to clear local and server-side messages.
keywords: sdk android v4 sdk android message managing-messages clear-all-messages
content: Clear all message records stored both in the local SQLite database and on the remote server for the logged in account. This operation is permanent and irreversible; once executed, historical message data for the current account cannot be restored. This operation clears only the caller's message mailbox and does not delete message copies retained by other participants or alter friend and group relationships. Code example OpenIMClient.getInstance .messageManager.deleteAllMsgFromLocalAndSvr new OnBase @Override public void onSuccess String data // Local and server messages cleared successfully @Override public void onError int code, String error // Handle clearing failure ; Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | base | OnBase | Yes | Callback handler for the asynchronous request. | Return value Upon success, data in onSuccess returns a confirmation message. State changes after the call 1. Callback confirmation : The onSuccess callback indicates that message records across all conversations were purged from both local storage and the server for this account. Clear open chat message views. 2. Conversation summary update : The last message preview latestMsg on conversations is cleared or refreshed to reflect the empty state. 3. Re query calibration : To delete only the local offline cache on this device while retaining cloud roaming history, call Clear all local messages /sdk/android/message/managing messages/clear all local messages .

title: Set local message extensions
description: Use setMessageLocalEx to store message data used only on the current device.
keywords: sdk android v4 sdk android message managing-messages set-message-local-ex
content: Save device specific custom extension data localEx for a designated message on the current device. This is suitable for caching local file download states, media playback timestamps, audio transcription text caches, or custom UI display attributes. The stored data remains strictly local and is never synchronized to the server or other client devices. Code example String conversationID = "si user a user b"; String clientMsgID = "msg 001"; String localExJson = " \"downloadStatus\":2,\"localPath\":\"/storage/emulated/0/...\" "; OpenIMClient.getInstance .messageManager.setMessageLocalEx new OnBase @Override public void onSuccess String data // Local extension saved successfully @Override public void onError int code, String error // Handle save failure , conversationID, clientMsgID, localExJson ; Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | base | OnBase | Yes | Callback handler for the asynchronous request. | | conversationID | String | Yes | Globally unique ID of the conversation containing the message. | | clientMsgID | String | Yes | Client message ID of the target message. | | localEx | String | Yes | Custom extension string typically formatted as JSON . | Return value Upon success, data in onSuccess returns a confirmation message. State changes after the call 1. Callback confirmation : The onSuccess callback confirms that localEx was updated in the local database. Update the localEx property on the in memory message instance using clientMsgID and refresh the UI item. 2. Local scope : This operation writes strictly to local storage. It does not alter message body content on the server and does not trigger real time events on other clients. 3. Re query calibration : The extension persists only in local storage on this device and will not be present if the message is re fetched from cloud roaming history on another device.

title: Report group messages as read
description: Report group-message read receipts with the Android SDK.
keywords: sdk android v4 sdk android message managing-read-status send-group-read-receipts
content: Report read receipts for group messages that the current user has viewed. As the conversation timeline scrolls or messages enter the visible viewport, pass the list of visible client message IDs to the server. This allows group message senders to track read and unread member counts in real time. Code example String conversationID = "g group 123"; List visibleClientMsgIDs = Arrays.asList "msg 001", "msg 002" ; OpenIMClient.getInstance .messageManager.sendGroupMessageReadReceipt conversationID, visibleClientMsgIDs, new OnBase @Override public void onSuccess String data // Read receipts reported successfully @Override public void onError int code, String error // Handle reporting failure ; Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | conversationID | String | Yes | Globally unique ID of the target group conversation. | | clientMsgIDs | List | Yes | List of client message IDs in the visible viewport to mark as read. All messages must belong to the specified conversation. | | base | OnBase | Yes | Callback handler for the asynchronous request. | Return value Upon success, data in onSuccess returns a confirmation message. State changes after the call 1. Callback confirmation : The onSuccess callback indicates that the server accepted the read receipts. 2. Asynchronous event delivery : Group message senders and participants receive incremental read receipt events through OnAdvanceMsgListener.onRecvGroupMessageReadReceipt : @Override public void onRecvGroupMessageReadReceipt GroupMessageReceipt receipt // Update read count and read status for messages matched by clientMsgID 3. Aggregate unread count separation : Group message read receipts update message level reader counts. To clear the aggregate unread badge count for the conversation locally and on the server, call Mark a conversation as read /sdk/android/conversation/managing conversations/mark conversation read . 4. Member detail query : To view the full list of members who have or have not read a specific group message, see Get members who read a group message /sdk/android/message/managing read status/get group message readers . For complete listener registration and lifecycle management, see Receive messages /sdk/android/message/receiving messages/receive messages .

title: Get members who read a group message
description: Retrieve members who have or have not read a group message using pagination.
keywords: sdk android v4 sdk android message managing-read-status get-group-message-readers
content: Retrieve the list of group members who have or have not read a designated group message using pagination. A filter condition separates read from unread members, making this method ideal for rendering read receipt lists on message detail screens. Code example String conversationID = "g group 123"; String clientMsgID = "msg 001"; int filter = 0; // 0: query members who read; 1: query members who have not read int offset = 0; int count = 50; OpenIMClient.getInstance .messageManager.getGroupMessageReaderList conversationID, clientMsgID, filter, offset, count, new OnBase @Override public void onSuccess List members // members contains member profile information @Override public void onError int code, String error // Handle query failure ; Filter options | Filter value | Description | | | | | 0 | Query group members who have read the message. | | 1 | Query group members who have not yet read the message. | Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | conversationID | String | Yes | Globally unique ID of the target group conversation. | | clientMsgID | String | Yes | Client message ID of the target message to query. | | filter | int | Yes | Read status filter: 0 for read members, 1 for unread members. | | offset | int | Yes | Starting pagination offset index 0 for the initial request . | | count | int | Yes | Maximum number of records to retrieve in this page. | | base | OnBase | Yes | Callback handler for the asynchronous request. | Return value Upon success, members in onSuccess returns List . Each entry contains group member details including nickname , faceURL , roleLevel , and userID . For property definitions, see Get group members /sdk/android/group/retrieving group members/get group member list . State changes after the call 1. Callback confirmation : The onSuccess callback returns a snapshot of group member records matching the filter. Render or append the member list using userID as the unique identifier. 2. Asynchronous event delivery : This query does not trigger state change events. New read receipts from other members arrive through OnAdvanceMsgListener.onRecvGroupMessageReadReceipt . For details, see Report group messages as read /sdk/android/message/managing read status/send group read receipts . 3. Pagination continuation : If the returned list size matches count , increment offset by count to fetch the next page. A return count less than count indicates the end of the list.

title: Upload a file
description: Upload files directly to object storage and retrieve their remote URLs using the OpenIM Android SDK.
keywords: sdk android v4 sdk android file-uploads upload-file
content: The standalone file upload API uploads user avatars, group avatars, profile attachments, or other business assets directly to object storage. This upload operation is decoupled from the message lifecycle and does not create messages or update user profiles automatically. Code example File file = new File localPath ; PutArgs args = new PutArgs file.getAbsolutePath ; args.name = file.getName ; args.cuase = "user avatar"; OpenIMClient.getInstance .uploadFile new OnBase @Override public void onSuccess String result // result is the final JSON string result of the upload request. @Override public void onError int code, String error // code and error describe the failure. , new OnPutFileListener @Override public void open long size // size is the total byte size of the file to upload. @Override public void uploadID String id // id is the server assigned upload task identifier. @Override public void uploadComplete long fileSize, long streamSize, long storageSize // File byte transfer is complete. @Override public void complete long size, String url, long type // url is the accessible remote resource URL. , args ; Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | base | OnBase | Yes | Callback delivering the final success or error response of the upload request. | | listener | OnPutFileListener | Yes | Listener tracking file chunks, hashing progress, upload status, and completion. | | putArgs.filepath | String | Yes | Local absolute file path accessible to the Android application. | | putArgs.name | String | Yes | Upload file name. Defaults to the input path; customize as needed. | | putArgs.cuase | String | No | Business upload reason tag. Matches the exact cuase field declared in the Android SDK's PutArgs . | Return value The onSuccess callback receives the raw completion string, while the complete long size, String url, long type callback on OnPutFileListener delivers the final remote URL, total file size, and content type. Use the returned URL in subsequent API calls to update user avatars, configure group avatars, attach media to messages, or link attachments. Uploading writes binary data to object storage but does not update domain profiles or dispatch chat messages automatically. Progress and lifecycle callbacks OnPutFileListener provides real time chunk and transmission lifecycle events: | Callback | Parameters | Description | | | | | | open | size | File stream opened; reports total file size in bytes. | | partSize | partSize , num | Chunking configuration reporting individual chunk size and total chunk count. | | hashPartProgress | index , size , partHash | Checksum calculation completed for a single chunk. | | hashPartComplete | partsHash , fileHash | Complete checksum calculation finished across all chunks. | | uploadID | uploadID | Server upload session ID assigned. | | uploadPartComplete | index , partSize , partHash | Chunk upload confirmed by the storage service. | | uploadComplete | fileSize , streamSize , storageSize | Data transmission finished, delivering final file, stream, and storage sizes. | | complete | size , url , type | Full upload pipeline finished; delivers the remote resource URL. |

title: Calling overview
description: Understand audio and video calling signaling, room models, and event lifecycles in the OpenIM Android SDK.
keywords: sdk android v4 sdk android calling overview-calling
content: The OpenIM Android SDK's SignalingManager provides the signaling pipeline required to initiate, accept, reject, cancel, and hang up calls, query room states, and synchronize call participants. It orchestrates call metadata, participant rosters, and call lifecycles, but does not capture camera frames, process audio streams, or render video views. Pass the roomID , token , and liveURL returned by the SDK to your chosen WebRTC or LiveKit media engine. Your application handles Android runtime permissions, audio routing, media tracks, network adaptation, and calling UI state. Calling lifecycle 1. The caller initiates a call using Start a single call /sdk/android/calling/managing calls/start single call or Start a group call /sdk/android/calling/managing calls/start group call . 2. The callee receives an incoming invitation event and accepts or rejects the call. 3. The answering party calls Accept a call /sdk/android/calling/managing calls/accept call , and both sides connect to LiveKit or WebRTC using room credentials returned by the server. 4. Active screens render participant lists, published tracks, and custom business signals during the call. 5. Before connection, the caller can Cancel a call invitation /sdk/android/calling/managing calls/cancel call ; after connection, any participant can Hang up a call /sdk/android/calling/managing calls/hang up call . Core data structures | Structure | Description | | | | | SignalingInvitationInfo | Inviter, invitees, group ID, room ID, media type, timeout, session type, and custom extension payload. | | SignalingInfo | Current operator, complete invitation data received in events, participant profiles, and optional offline push details. | | SignalingCertificate | roomID , token , liveURL , and busy user lists returned by OpenIMServer. | | RoomCallingInfo | Room details, active invitation, participant roster, group metadata, and access credentials queried by group ID. | Use customData and custom signaling to exchange lightweight, transient session negotiation data. Do not use signaling channels for bulk file transfers or persistent database storage. State updates and event ownership Distinguish clearly between asynchronous API callbacks and real time signaling events. An API success callback indicates that the server accepted the signaling request; participant state transitions are delivered asynchronously through event listeners. For the centralized listener handling invitation lifecycles, room entries, exits, hang ups, and stream updates, see Handle call events /sdk/android/calling/managing calls/handle call events . For application specific signals, see Send a custom signal /sdk/android/calling/sending custom signals/send a custom signal . The global primary key for call state is roomID ; individual participant state is keyed by roomID combined with userID . When recovering after app restarts or network disconnections, query room APIs to calibrate local state. Navigation by task | Task | Documentation page | | | | | Initiate a direct or group call | Start a single call /sdk/android/calling/managing calls/start single call , Start a group call /sdk/android/calling/managing calls/start group call | | Accept or decline an invitation | Accept a call /sdk/android/calling/managing calls/accept call , Reject a call /sdk/android/calling/managing calls/reject call | | Cancel an invitation or terminate a call | Cancel a call invitation /sdk/android/calling/managing calls/cancel call , Hang up a call /sdk/android/calling/managing calls/hang up call | | Recover room state or pending invitations | Query group call room /sdk/android/calling/retrieving call information/get room by group id , Get call room token /sdk/android/calling/retrieving call information/get token by room id , Restore pending invitation received before launch /sdk/android/calling/retrieving call information/restore pending invitation | | Handle signaling events and custom messages | Handle call events /sdk/android/calling/managing calls/handle call events , Send a custom signal /sdk/android/calling/sending custom signals/send a custom signal |

title: Start a single call
description: Initiate a direct audio or video call and acquire room credentials using signalingInvite().
keywords: sdk android v4 sdk android calling managing-calls start-single-call
content: Initiate a direct audio or video call. The OpenIM Android SDK handles signaling negotiation and room state synchronization; once room credentials are returned, connect to your real time audio/video media engine. Code example SignalingInvitationInfo invitation = new SignalingInvitationInfo ; invitation.setInviterUserID currentUserID ; invitation.setInviteeUserIDList Collections.singletonList peerUserID ; invitation.setGroupID "" ; invitation.setRoomID roomID ; invitation.setTimeout 30 ; invitation.setMediaType "video" ; invitation.setSessionType ConversationType.SINGLE CHAT ; invitation.setPlatformID Platform.ANDROID ; invitation.setCustomData " \"source\":\"contact card\" " ; SignalingInfo info = new SignalingInfo ; info.setInvitation invitation ; info.setOfflinePushInfo offlinePushInfo ; OpenIMClient.getInstance .signalingManager.signalingInvite new OnBase @Override public void onSuccess SignalingCertificate credentials // credentials provides roomID, token, and liveURL to join the media room. @Override public void onError int code, String error // code and error describe the failure. , info ; Parameters Calling method: signalingInvite OnBase callback, SignalingInfo info The parameters below represent public properties on Android's SignalingInfo and its nested objects. When initiating a call, populate invitation and optional offlinePushInfo ; participant and top level userID are typically populated in incoming event payloads rather than outgoing invitations. | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | invitation | SignalingInvitationInfo | Yes | Call invitation payload. | | invitation.inviterUserID | String | Yes | Inviter user ID; pass the authenticated user ID. | | invitation.inviteeUserIDList | List | Yes | Callee user list; contains exactly one peer user ID in direct calls. | | invitation.groupID | String | Yes | Target group ID; pass an empty string "" for direct calls. | | invitation.roomID | String | Yes | Unique room identifier used to track and merge call state. | | invitation.timeout | long | Yes | Invitation timeout interval in seconds. | | invitation.mediaType | String | Yes | Media stream type, conventionally "audio" or "video" . | | invitation.sessionType | int | Yes | Set ConversationType.SINGLE CHAT for direct calls, or ConversationType.SUPER GROUP CHAT for group calls. | | invitation.platformID | int | Yes | Current client platform identifier; pass Platform.ANDROID . | | invitation.customData | String | No | Custom business metadata string attached to the invitation. | | invitation.initiateTime | long | No | Timestamp when the invitation was initiated. Managed automatically by the signaling layer. | | offlinePushInfo | OfflinePushInfo | No | Push notification payload delivered when invitees are offline. | | offlinePushInfo.title | String | Conditional | Notification title; required when offlinePushInfo is provided. | | offlinePushInfo.desc | String | Conditional | Notification body text; required when offlinePushInfo is provided. | | offlinePushInfo.ex | String | Conditional | Extension string attached to push payload; pass "" if not needed. | | offlinePushInfo.iOSPushSound | String | Conditional | Sound resource for iOS push notifications; required when providing push info. | | offlinePushInfo.iOSBadgeCount | boolean | Conditional | Whether to badge iOS app icons; required when providing push info. | | participant | ParticipantMeta | No | Participant profile metadata; omit when sending invitations. | | userID | String | No | User ID associated with the operation; omit when sending invitations. | Return value Upon success, credentials in onSuccess returns a SignalingCertificate object containing: roomID : Unique global identifier of the call room. token : Authentication token used to join the media room. liveURL : Media server endpoint URL. busyLineUserIDList : List of busy user IDs if the target is already engaged in another call. State changes after the call 1. Callback confirmation : The onSuccess callback confirms that the signaling request succeeded and room credentials were acquired. It does not indicate that the remote peer has answered or joined media streams. 2. Asynchronous event delivery : Both caller and callee track subsequent call events such as answer, reject, cancel, or timeout through OnSignalingListener . Track the overall call using roomID and monitor participant transitions using roomID:userID . 3. Media connection : Connect to the real time audio/video engine only after obtaining a valid token and roomID . For real time updates regarding participant entries and stream states, see Handle call events /sdk/android/calling/managing calls/handle call events .

title: Start a group call
description: Initiate a group audio or video call and acquire room credentials using signalingInviteInGroup().
keywords: sdk android v4 sdk android calling managing-calls start-group-call
content: Initiate a group audio or video call within a group conversation. The parameter models match those of Start a single call /sdk/android/calling/managing calls/start single call , except invitation.groupID requires a valid group ID and invitation.sessionType is set to ConversationType.GROUP CHAT . Only group members explicitly specified in inviteeUserIDList receive invitations; providing a groupID does not automatically ring all members of the group. Exclude the current user ID, empty values, and duplicates from inviteeUserIDList . In the example below, the group ID is reused as the room ID; if you generate custom roomID values, ensure all participants join the same identifier. Code example SignalingInvitationInfo invitation = new SignalingInvitationInfo ; invitation.setInviterUserID currentUserID ; invitation.setInviteeUserIDList selectedGroupMemberIDs ; invitation.setGroupID groupID ; invitation.setRoomID groupID ; invitation.setTimeout 30 ; invitation.setMediaType "video" ; invitation.setSessionType ConversationType.GROUP CHAT ; invitation.setPlatformID Platform.ANDROID ; invitation.setCustomData " \"source\":\"group call\" " ; SignalingInfo info = new SignalingInfo ; info.setInvitation invitation ; info.setOfflinePushInfo offlinePushInfo ; OpenIMClient.getInstance .signalingManager.signalingInviteInGroup new OnBase @Override public void onSuccess SignalingCertificate credentials // credentials contains room token and liveURL to join the media room. @Override public void onError int code, String error // code and error describe the failure. , info ; Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | base | OnBase | Yes | Callback delivering room credentials needed to connect to the media engine. | | info | SignalingInfo | Yes | Complete signaling payload containing group ID, invitee list, room ID, and media type. | Invitation attributes | Field | Type | Description | | | | | | inviterUserID | String | Initiator user ID authenticated user . | | inviteeUserIDList | List | List of invited member user IDs, excluding the caller and deduplicated. Populating groupID does not automatically invite all group members. | | groupID | String | Target group ID for the group call. | | roomID | String | Call room identifier, such as the groupID or a random UUID. | | timeout | int | Invitation timeout in seconds. | | mediaType | String | Media type string, such as "audio" or "video" . | | sessionType | int | Session type; set to ConversationType.GROUP CHAT for group calls. | Return value Upon success, credentials in onSuccess returns a SignalingCertificate object containing: roomID : Unique global identifier of the call room. token : Authentication token used to join the media room. liveURL : Media server endpoint URL. busyLineUserIDList : List of invited members currently engaged in another call. State changes after the call 1. Callback confirmation : The onSuccess callback confirms that the signaling request succeeded and room credentials were acquired. It does not indicate that invited group members have answered or connected to the media engine. 2. Asynchronous event delivery : The initiator and invited members track subsequent call events through OnSignalingListener . Track the group call room state using roomID and track individual member response and connectivity states using roomID:userID . 3. Media connection : Connect to the real time audio/video engine using the returned token and roomID . For real time event updates, see Handle call events /sdk/android/calling/managing calls/handle call events .

title: Accept a call
description: Accept an incoming call invitation and acquire room credentials using signalingAccept().
keywords: sdk android v4 sdk android calling managing-calls accept-call
content: After receiving an incoming call invitation event, accept the invitation and acquire credentials to connect to the audio/video media room: Code example OpenIMClient.getInstance .signalingManager.signalingAccept new OnBase @Override public void onSuccess SignalingCertificate credentials // credentials provides roomID, token, and liveURL to join the media room. @Override public void onError int code, String error // code and error describe the failure. , receivedInfo ; Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | base | OnBase | Yes | Callback delivering room credentials to enter the media room. | | signalingInfo | SignalingInfo | Yes | Complete signaling payload received in the invitation event. Maintain the original roomID , inviter, invitees, and session type without passing an incomplete object. | Return value The successful callback returns a SignalingCertificate containing roomID , token , and liveURL . Use these credentials to establish a connection to your real time media engine. State changes after the call A successful callback indicates that the acceptance signal was submitted to the server, not that audio/video media streams have connected. Track the call using roomID and monitor individual participant lifecycles using roomID:userID . For real time updates regarding participant entries and stream states, see Handle call events /sdk/android/calling/managing calls/handle call events .

title: Reject a call
description: Decline an incoming call invitation using signalingReject().
keywords: sdk android v4 sdk android calling managing-calls reject-call
content: When the user declines an incoming call, pass the unmodified SignalingInfo object received in the invitation event to signalingReject : Code example OpenIMClient.getInstance .signalingManager.signalingReject new OnBase @Override public void onSuccess String result // Rejection request completed. @Override public void onError int code, String error // code and error describe the failure. , signalingInfo ; Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | base | OnBase | Yes | Callback delivering the asynchronous operation result. | | signalingInfo | SignalingInfo | Yes | Complete signaling payload received in the invitation event, preserving the original roomID , inviter, and invitees. | Return value The successful callback indicates that the server recorded the call rejection. Dismiss the incoming call ringing screen and cancel notification alerts on the callee client. State changes after the call The caller and other room members receive notification events indicating that the invitation was rejected. Update member statuses in active calling screens using roomID:userID . For complete listener registration details, see Handle call events /sdk/android/calling/managing calls/handle call events .

title: Cancel a call invitation
description: Cancel an unanswered call invitation using signalingCancel().
keywords: sdk android v4 sdk android calling managing-calls cancel-call
content: Before an invitation is answered, the initiator can cancel the pending call invitation: Code example OpenIMClient.getInstance .signalingManager.signalingCancel new OnBase @Override public void onSuccess String result // Cancel request completed. @Override public void onError int code, String error // code and error describe the failure. , activeInfo ; Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | base | OnBase | Yes | Callback delivering the asynchronous operation result. | | signalingInfo | SignalingInfo | Yes | Complete signaling payload stored when the call was initiated, preserving the original roomID , inviter, and invitees. | Return value The successful callback indicates that the server accepted the cancellation request. Dismiss the outgoing calling screen and release local media resources on the caller device. State changes after the call Invitees and other associated devices receive notification events indicating that the invitation was cancelled. Update the active call state using roomID . For complete listener registration details, see Handle call events /sdk/android/calling/managing calls/handle call events .

title: Hang up a call
description: Terminate an established call session using signalingHungUp().
keywords: sdk android v4 sdk android calling managing-calls hang-up-call
content: Once a call is connected, any participant can hang up to terminate their session. Pass the active SignalingInfo object, ensuring roomID matches the ongoing media room. Code example OpenIMClient.getInstance .signalingManager.signalingHungUp new OnBase @Override public void onSuccess String result // Hangup request completed. @Override public void onError int code, String error // code and error describe the failure. , signalingInfo ; Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | base | OnBase | Yes | Callback delivering the asynchronous operation result. | | signalingInfo | SignalingInfo | Yes | Active call signaling object, where roomID matches the ongoing call room. | Return value The successful callback indicates that the server processed the hangup signal. The client that initiated the hangup should dismiss the calling screen, disconnect from the media room, and release camera and microphone hardware resources. State changes after the call Other participants in the room receive hangup or participant disconnected events. Update active rosters or terminate the call screen using roomID or roomID:userID . For event handling details, see Handle call events /sdk/android/calling/managing calls/handle call events .

title: Handle call events
description: Register the centralized Android SDK listener for call invitations, participants, and media stream state transitions.
keywords: sdk android v4 sdk android calling managing-calls handle-call-events
content: Register OnSignalingListener centrally in your application wide call coordinator. The SDK uses these callbacks to notify you of incoming calls, acceptances, rejections, cancellations, timeouts, hang ups, and participant entries or exits; your application updates UI states and local media connections accordingly. SignalingManager holds at most one listener instance; registering a new listener overwrites any previously configured listener. When logging out or switching accounts, cease processing callbacks for the previous user before registering a new listener instance. Code example OpenIMClient.getInstance .signalingManager.setSignalingListener new OnSignalingListener @Override public void onReceiveNewInvitation SignalingInfo info // info contains the incoming call invitation payload. @Override public void onInviteeAccepted SignalingInfo info // info indicates the call was accepted. @Override public void onInviteeRejected SignalingInfo info // info indicates the call was rejected. @Override public void onInvitationCancelled SignalingInfo info // info indicates the invitation was cancelled. @Override public void onInvitationTimeout SignalingInfo info // info indicates the invitation timed out. @Override public void onInviteeAcceptedByOtherDevice SignalingInfo info // info indicates another device accepted the call. @Override public void onInviteeRejectedByOtherDevice SignalingInfo info // info indicates another device rejected the call. @Override public void onHangup SignalingInfo info // info indicates the call has hung up. @Override public void onRoomParticipantConnected RoomCallingInfo room // room contains updated participant lists after entry. @Override public void onRoomParticipantDisconnected RoomCallingInfo room // room contains updated participant lists after exit. @Override public void onStreamChange String streamInfo // streamInfo contains media stream changes. ; Callback events reference | Callback | Trigger condition | Handling guidance | | | | | | onReceiveNewInvitation | A new calling invitation arrives. | Persist the SignalingInfo object, launch the incoming call interface, and await user action. | | onInviteeAccepted , onInviteeRejected | An invitee accepts or declines the invitation. | Update the participant's status in the UI; in group calls, update that specific participant node without disrupting other members. | | onInvitationCancelled , onInvitationTimeout , onHangup | The invitation was cancelled, expired, or terminated by either party. | Dismiss calling screens, disconnect from media rooms, and release local hardware audio/video tracks. | | onInviteeAcceptedByOtherDevice , onInviteeRejectedByOtherDevice | Another active device logged into the same account handled the call. | Terminate ringing and dismiss the response UI on this device to avoid multi device conflicts. | | onRoomParticipantConnected , onRoomParticipantDisconnected | A member enters or leaves the media room. | Refresh active member lists and composite video grids in group calls. | | onStreamChange | The server broadcasts a media stream state change. | Parse stream descriptors according to server protocols and adjust local track renderers dynamically. | State reconciliation and lifecycle Global call identifier : Use roomID accessible via SignalingInfo.invitation.roomID or RoomCallingInfo.roomID to uniquely identify a call session for UI routing and lifecycle handling. Participant identifier : Combine roomID:userID to merge acceptance, rejection, room presence, and stream states without cross polluting concurrent group member updates. Listener cleanup : SignalingManager retains a single listener. When logging out or resetting session components, pass null or unbind callbacks to prevent memory leaks and guard against obsolete UI dispatches.

title: Restore pending invitation received before launch
description: Retrieve pending, unhandled call invitations during application startup using getSignalingInvitationInfoStartApp().
keywords: sdk android v4 sdk android calling retrieving-call-information restore-pending-invitation
content: Retrieve pending call invitations that arrived before or during application startup. This is commonly used to restore incoming call screens after cold launching from an offline push notification. Code example OpenIMClient.getInstance .signalingManager.getSignalingInvitationInfoStartApp new OnBase @Override public void onSuccess SignalingInfo info // Verify whether info contains a valid invitation and roomID before using. @Override public void onError int code, String error // code and error describe the failure. ; Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | base | OnBase | Yes | Callback delivering the asynchronous operation result. | Return value The successful callback returns the pending call invitation payload as SignalingInfo . This method does not answer or modify the call automatically. Verify whether info has a non null invitation and a valid roomID . If an active invitation exists, present the incoming call UI to let the user Accept a call /sdk/android/calling/managing calls/accept call or Reject a call /sdk/android/calling/managing calls/reject call . For subsequent cancellation or timeout events, see Handle call events /sdk/android/calling/managing calls/handle call events .

title: Query group call room
description: Look up an ongoing call room for a specific group using signalingGetRoomByGroupID().
keywords: sdk android v4 sdk android calling retrieving-call-information get-room-by-group-id
content: Look up an ongoing call room by group ID. Supply the groupID parameter even if a custom roomID was assigned to the call. Code example OpenIMClient.getInstance .signalingManager.signalingGetRoomByGroupID new OnBase @Override public void onSuccess RoomCallingInfo room // room contains room ID, original invitation, and current participant list. @Override public void onError int code, String error // code and error describe the failure. , groupID ; Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | base | OnBase | Yes | Callback delivering the asynchronous operation result. | | groupID | String | Yes | Target group ID to query. | Return value The successful callback returns a RoomCallingInfo snapshot of the active group call: roomID : Call room identifier. invitation : Original invitation payload configured at initiation. participant : Roster and status of members currently in the room. groupID : Target group ID. token : Media token required to join the session. liveURL : Media server endpoint URL. If roomID in the returned object is empty, no ongoing audio/video call exists in this group. This query delivers a point in time snapshot; track subsequent call transitions via Handle call events /sdk/android/calling/managing calls/handle call events .

title: Get call room token
description: Retrieve or refresh access credentials for an active calling room by room ID using signalingGetTokenByRoomID().
keywords: sdk android v4 sdk android calling retrieving-call-information get-token-by-room-id
content: When the client knows the roomID but needs to acquire or refresh media room access tokens, fetch updated credentials using signalingGetTokenByRoomID : Code example OpenIMClient.getInstance .signalingManager.signalingGetTokenByRoomID new OnBase @Override public void onSuccess SignalingCertificate credentials // credentials provides roomID, token, and liveURL to connect to the media room. @Override public void onError int code, String error // code and error describe the failure. , roomID ; Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | base | OnBase | Yes | Callback delivering the asynchronous operation result. | | roomID | String | Yes | Target call room identifier. | Return value The successful callback returns a SignalingCertificate object containing: roomID : Unique global identifier of the call room. token : Authentication token used to join the media room. liveURL : Media server endpoint URL. busyLineUserIDList : List of busy users. Once valid credentials are received, connect to your media engine. If credentials expire during reconnection or extended waiting, call this method again to refresh them.

title: Send a custom signal
description: Exchange custom, transient signaling messages within an active calling room using signalingSendCustomSignal().
keywords: sdk android v4 sdk android calling sending-custom-signals send-a-custom-signal
content: Send lightweight, transient call related messages within an active calling room, such as hand raising notifications, layout switch prompts, or temporary status synchronization. This mechanism is designed for transient room coordination, not persistent chat messages or file transfers. Code example Both roomID and customInfo are required strings. When transmitting structured payloads, serialize them to JSON: JSONObject signal = new JSONObject ; signal.put "version", 1 ; signal.put "eventID", eventID ; signal.put "type", "hand raised" ; signal.put "userID", currentUserID ; signal.put "sentAt", System.currentTimeMillis ; OpenIMClient.getInstance .signalingManager.signalingSendCustomSignal new OnBase @Override public void onSuccess String result // Custom signal dispatched successfully. @Override public void onError int code, String error // code and error describe the failure. , roomID, signal.toString ; Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | base | OnBase | Yes | Callback delivering the asynchronous operation result. | | roomID | String | Yes | Target call room identifier. | | customInfo | String | Yes | Custom signal payload string, recommended to be structured JSON. | Return value Upon success, result in onSuccess returns a confirmation message. State changes after the call 1. Callback confirmation : The onSuccess callback indicates that the server accepted and routed the custom signal; it does not guarantee that the remote peer has processed it. 2. Asynchronous event delivery : Room participants receive custom signals via OnSignalingListener.onReceiveCustomSignal : @Override public void onReceiveCustomSignal CustomSignalingInfo info // Check info.getRoomID before parsing info.getCustomInfo Include a protocol version and unique eventID in the payload so recipients can deduplicate incoming signals. Do not rely on delivery sequence to represent state machine transitions. Register this callback within your centralized listener in Handle call events /sdk/android/calling/managing calls/handle call events . 3. Re query calibration : Custom signals are transient and not replayed on reconnection. To reconcile room state after network recovery, re query the room snapshot.

title: Events overview
description: Register OpenIM Android SDK listeners centrally and dispatch connection, synchronization, and domain data events.
keywords: sdk android v4 sdk android events overview-events
content: The OpenIM Android SDK notifies applications of connection, synchronization, user, friendship, conversation, group, message, and call events via listeners. Each manager holds at most one listener instance; registering a new listener overwrites any previously registered listener. Manage listeners centrally within an application scoped event coordinator and register them once before logging in, rather than inside activities, fragments, or Compose screens. The core server connection lifecycle is handled by OnConnListener . Rather than configuring it through a domain manager, supply it during SDK initialization; for the full connection lifecycle implementation, see Authenticate and manage a session /sdk/android/getting started/authenticate and manage session . Centralized listener registration The following example registers domain specific listeners at an application wide event center. Each listener handles callbacks strictly within its respective domain: public final class OpenIMEventCenter private final OpenIMClient client = OpenIMClient.getInstance ; private final OnUserListener userListener = new OnUserListener // Handle user profile and presence updates ; private final OnFriendshipListener friendshipListener = new OnFriendshipListener // Handle relationships, friend applications, and blocklist events ; private final OnConversationListener conversationListener = new OnConversationListener // Handle conversations, unread counters, typing status, and data sync ; private final OnGroupListener groupListener = new OnGroupListener // Handle group profiles, members, and group applications ; private final OnAdvanceMsgListener messageListener = new OnAdvanceMsgListener // Handle new messages, revocations, deletions, edits, and read receipts ; private final OnCustomBusinessListener businessListener = new OnCustomBusinessListener // Handle custom business messages ; private final OnSignalingListener signalingListener = new OnSignalingListener // Handle calling invitations, participant state, and custom signaling ; public void registerBeforeLogin client.userInfoManager.setOnUserListener userListener ; client.friendshipManager.setOnFriendshipListener friendshipListener ; client.conversationManager.setOnConversationListener conversationListener ; client.groupManager.setOnGroupListener groupListener ; client.messageManager.setAdvancedMsgListener messageListener ; client.messageManager.setCustomBusinessListener businessListener ; client.signalingManager.setSignalingListener signalingListener ; The Android SDK does not provide an unset or remove listener API. When logging out, switching accounts, or tearing down screens, stop propagating callbacks to stale UI controllers or former user state. Before logging in with a new account, re register complete listener instances configured for the new session. Event domain ownership | Scope | Listener | Documentation page | | | | | | Connection, token expiration, and kick offline | OnConnListener | Authenticate and manage a session /sdk/android/getting started/authenticate and manage session | | Current user profile | OnUserListener | Update the current user profile /sdk/android/user/user profile/set self info | | Online presence | OnUserListener | Subscribe to user online status /sdk/android/user/online status/subscribe users online status | | Friendship status and profiles | OnFriendshipListener | Get the friend list /sdk/android/user/friends/get friend list page | | Friend applications | OnFriendshipListener | Get received friend applications /sdk/android/user/friend applications/get recv friend application list | | Blocklist | OnFriendshipListener | Block a user /sdk/android/user/blacklist/add blacklist , Unblock a user /sdk/android/user/blacklist/remove blacklist | | Conversation list | OnConversationListener | Get the conversation list /sdk/android/conversation/retrieving conversations/retrieve conversation list | | Total unread count | OnConversationListener | Get the total unread message count /sdk/android/conversation/managing conversations/get total unread count | | Typing status | OnConversationListener | Report typing status /sdk/android/message/composing messages/update typing status | | Group profiles, members, and applications | OnGroupListener | Group overview /sdk/android/group/overview group | | New messages, offline messages, and online sync | OnAdvanceMsgListener | Receive messages /sdk/android/message/receiving messages/receive messages | | Message revocation | OnAdvanceMsgListener | Revoke a message /sdk/android/message/managing messages/revoke a message | | Message deletion | OnAdvanceMsgListener | Batch delete messages /sdk/android/message/managing messages/delete saved messages | | Message modification | OnAdvanceMsgListener | Modify a message /sdk/android/message/managing messages/modify a message | | Pinned messages | OnAdvanceMsgListener | Pin or unpin a message /sdk/android/message/managing messages/set message pinned | | Direct chat read receipts | OnAdvanceMsgListener | Mark a conversation as read /sdk/android/conversation/managing conversations/mark conversation read | | Custom business messages | OnCustomBusinessListener | Receive custom business messages /sdk/android/message/receiving messages/receive custom business messages | | Calling sessions | OnSignalingListener | Handle calling events /sdk/android/calling/managing calls/handle call events | | Calling custom signaling | OnSignalingListener | Send custom signaling /sdk/android/calling/sending custom signals/send a custom signal | | SDK data synchronization | OnConversationListener | Listen for initialization synchronization listen for initialization synchronization | Listen for initialization synchronization Data synchronization events belong to OnConversationListener , which also handles conversation list, unread count, and typing indicators. The following snippet illustrates the synchronization callbacks: private final OnConversationListener conversationListener = new OnConversationListener @Override public void onSyncServerStart boolean reinstall // Synchronization started: update sync status and display a loading indicator if appropriate @Override public void onSyncServerProgress long progress // Synchronization in progress: update progress indicators @Override public void onSyncServerFinish boolean reinstall // Synchronization finished: refresh UI components that depend on complete local datasets @Override public void onSyncServerFailed boolean reinstall // Synchronization failed: update error state and wait for retry or network reconnection // Implement other conversation callbacks as needed... ; The reinstall flag indicates whether synchronization is performing a full rebuild after local cache eviction: true indicates a fresh sync following app re installation or cleared app storage, where local cached records do not exist; false indicates standard incremental synchronization on regular logins. The onSyncServerProgress callback provides completion percentage. When synchronization completes, query fresh data snapshots to populate active screens; on failure, reflect error status and wait for automatic retry or connection recovery.

title: Logging
description: Configure OpenIM Android SDK logging, record application diagnostic events, and upload logs for debugging.
keywords: sdk android v4 sdk android logger
content: OpenIM Android SDK logging helps diagnose initialization issues, connection drops, and API failures. You can customize the log level, standard output redirection, and log directory within your initialization configuration. Configure logging on initialization Configure logging options when initializing the SDK: File dataDirectory = new File application.getFilesDir , "openim" ; File logDirectory = new File application.getFilesDir , "openim logs" ; InitConfig config = new InitConfig apiAddr, wsAddr, dataDirectory.getAbsolutePath ; config.logLevel = BuildConfig.DEBUG ? LogLevel.Debug : LogLevel.Warn; config.isLogStandardOutput = BuildConfig.DEBUG; config.logFilePath = logDirectory.getAbsolutePath ; boolean initialized = OpenIMClient.getInstance .initSDK application, config, connectionListener ; | Field | Description | | | | | logLevel | Uses LogLevel constants to control verbosity. Options include DebugWithSQL , Debug , Info , Warn , Error , Panic , and Fatal . | | isLogStandardOutput | Determines whether the SDK prints log output to Android logcat. | | logFilePath | Optional log storage directory, which must reside within writable application storage. | DebugWithSQL captures raw SQLite execution details, whereas Debug , Info , Warn , and Error successively reduce output volume. Select an appropriate logging level according to your troubleshooting requirements. Write application logs When you need to persist application level diagnostics alongside SDK events in local log files, call logs : OpenIMClient.getInstance .logs LogLevel.Error, ChatRepository.class.getSimpleName , 184, "send message failed", errorMessage, "conversationID", conversationID, "clientMsgID", clientMsgID ; currentClassName and currentLineNum locate the call site, msgStr provides an action description, and errStr contains the failure details. Levels Warn , Error , Panic , and Fatal require a non empty errStr . Key value attributes at the end are passed in trailing alternating pairs. Legacy overloads that accepted callback listeners or Map parameters are deprecated; use the varargs signature above. Upload logs When users report unexpected behavior or customer support requests diagnostics, upload client log files to the server: String cancelID = UUID.randomUUID .toString ; OpenIMClient.getInstance .uploadLogs new OnBase @Override public void onSuccess String data // Log upload request completed successfully. @Override public void onError int code, String error // code and error describe the failure. , new ArrayList< , 2000, // line cancelID, "support ticket 42", // ex new UploadLogProgress @Override public void onProgress long current, long total // current and total report upload progress. ; Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | base | OnBase | Yes | Callback delivering the final upload status. | | params | List | No | Legacy parameter unused by the current SDK; pass an empty list, such as new ArrayList< . | | line | int | Yes | Number of log lines to extract and upload. | | cancelID | String | Yes | Unique task identifier for this upload session, such as a random UUID. | | ex | String | No | Business metadata attached to the upload task, such as a support ticket ID. | | UploadLogProgress | UploadLogProgress | No | Progress listener reporting uploaded and total byte counters. | Return value The successful callback indicates that the log package has been uploaded to the server. You can cross reference the upload with timestamps, operation names, and identifiers such as conversationID , clientMsgID , groupID , or roomID to trace issues. Related guides Integrate for Android /sdk/android/getting started/environment specific implementation Authenticate and manage a session /sdk/android/getting started/authenticate and manage session Send a message /sdk/android/message/sending messages/send message

title: OpenIM Flutter SDK overview
description: Integrate user, conversation, group, message, calling, and event capabilities into your Flutter app with the OpenIM Flutter SDK.
keywords: sdk flutter v4 sdk flutter overview
content: The OpenIM Flutter SDK delivers native instant messaging capabilities for cross platform Flutter applications. The package is published on pub.dev as flutter openim sdk . Access all core capabilities—including initialization, user profiles, relationship chains, conversations, groups, messages, and audio/video calling signaling—globally through OpenIM.iMManager . The OpenIM Flutter SDK provides a comprehensive set of Dart APIs, strongly typed data models, and listener callbacks tailored for Flutter applications. Always use the paginated APIs when retrieving friend and conversation lists. Integration workflow 1. Add the flutter openim sdk dependency from pub.dev. 2. Retrieve the current user's userID , token, and OpenIMServer endpoints from your business backend. 3. Initialize the SDK and monitor connection, token expiration, and kick out states via OnConnectListener . 4. Once login succeeds and the connection is established, invoke user, friend, conversation, group, message, and call signaling APIs. 5. Merge incremental changes received from listeners into application state using stable entity identifiers.
