When switching accounts, clear state from the previous account. import 'package:flutter openim sdk/flutter openim sdk.dart'; final openIM = OpenIM.iMManager; Documentation structure | Domain | Description | | | | | Environment specific implementation /sdk/flutter/getting started/environment specific implementation | Platform setup, authentication, connection lifecycle, and sending your first message. | | Users overview /sdk/flutter/user/overview user | User profiles, relationship chains, friend applications, blocklists, and online presence. | | Conversations overview /sdk/flutter/conversation/overview conversation | Conversation queries, configurations, conversation groups, drafts, unread counts, hiding, and deletion. | | Groups overview /sdk/flutter/group/overview group | Group profiles, member management, join applications, role permissions, and group events. | | Messages overview /sdk/flutter/message/overview message | Creating, sending, receiving, querying, searching, modifying, pinning, transcribing, revoking, and read receipts. | | Audio & video calls overview /sdk/flutter/calling/overview calling | Call signaling, room credentials, custom signals, and call events. | | Events overview /sdk/flutter/events/overview events | Manager listeners, lifecycle events, and initial synchronization. | Key data boundaries When sending single chat messages, supply userID . When sending group chat messages, supply groupID . Never provide both targets simultaneously. ConversationInfo stores conversation display data, unread counts, drafts, and notification receive settings. GroupInfo and GroupMembersInfo manage group metadata and member relations. Listeners notify subsequent incremental changes. When entering a screen for the first time, proactively query the initial snapshot, then merge subsequent updates using userID , conversationID , groupID , or clientMsgID . Pure query Futures return the snapshot required by the screen at invocation time and do not trigger shared events. Treat state changing method completion, listener events, and query recalibration as three distinct stages. References Authenticate and manage session /sdk/flutter/getting started/authenticate and manage session Send your first message /sdk/flutter/getting started/send first message Logger /sdk/flutter/logger

title: Before you start
description: Prepare your OpenIMServer instance, user credentials, and Flutter environment before authenticating or sending messages.
keywords: sdk flutter v4 sdk flutter getting-started before-you-start
content: Before integrating the OpenIM Flutter SDK into your Flutter app, prepare an accessible OpenIMServer deployment, valid user sign in credentials, and configured Android or iOS development environments. These prerequisites apply to both Authenticate and manage session /sdk/flutter/getting started/authenticate and manage session and Send your first message /sdk/flutter/getting started/send first message . Prepare OpenIMServer If you do not have an active OpenIMServer instance, deploy one via Docker deployment /docs/guides/deployment/docker compose . Ensure your target mobile devices can connect to the following endpoints: | Endpoint | Description | | | | | apiAddr | OpenIMServer HTTP API endpoint used for authentication, data synchronization, and media uploads. | | wsAddr | OpenIMServer WebSocket endpoint used for persistent bidirectional connections and real time events. | Do not verify endpoints solely on your development workstation. Verify DNS resolution, TLS certificates, firewall rules, reverse proxy settings, and WebSocket upgrade handshakes directly from physical devices or emulators. Production deployments must use HTTPS and WSS protocols. Prepare user credentials and token The userID uniquely identifies a user within OpenIM, and the token authenticates that user session. Your business backend creates or associates user accounts and supplies matching userID and token pairs to your Flutter client. Refer to API preparation /platform api/prepare to use api and Get user token /platform api/auth/tokens/get user token to integrate your backend with the OpenIMServer REST API. The Flutter SDK requires the following parameters at login: class OpenIMSDKSession const OpenIMSDKSession required this.userID, required this.token, required this.apiAddr, required this.wsAddr, ; final String userID; final String token; final String apiAddr; final String wsAddr; The userID must match the subject in the token ; otherwise, login fails. Prepare the Flutter project The Flutter SDK supports Android and iOS. Verify the following prerequisites: Flutter and Dart SDK versions satisfy the constraints declared in flutter openim sdk 's pubspec.yaml . Android and iOS project files include network permissions, meet minimum OS target versions, and conform to SDK build requirements. An application data directory is prepared. Use path provider to retrieve a persistent application documents directory; avoid temporary or shared cache paths. Physical devices can reach apiAddr , wsAddr , and object storage domains hosting message media. Your application handles foreground/background transitions, network reconnects, token expiration, and multi device kick out events. For platform initialization specifics, see Environment specific implementation /sdk/flutter/getting started/environment specific implementation . Next steps After completing environment setup, proceed to Authenticate and manage session /sdk/flutter/getting started/authenticate and manage session . Once login succeeds and OnConnectListener.onConnectSuccess fires, proceed to Send your first message /sdk/flutter/getting started/send first message to verify the messaging pipeline.

title: Environment-specific implementation
description: Initialize OpenIMClientSDK in Android and iOS Flutter apps and manage mobile runtime boundaries.
keywords: sdk flutter v4 sdk flutter getting-started environment-specific-implementation
content: Runtime selection The flutter openim sdk package targets Android and iOS Flutter applications. Both platforms share identical Dart managers, data models, and listener contracts, but require platform specific platform IDs, storage directories, permissions, background execution policies, and native build configurations. | Runtime | platformID | Primary considerations | | | | | | Android | IMPlatform.android | Network permissions, private storage directory, battery optimization rules, and notification push setup. | | iOS | IMPlatform.ios | App Transport Security ATS policies, app sandbox directories, background execution modes, and APNs integration. | For Web, desktop, and Mini Programs, use their respective dedicated SDKs. Do not assume Flutter support on those runtimes solely because other constants exist in the IMPlatform enum. Install dependencies Add the SDK along with path provider to access the application documents directory: flutter pub add flutter openim sdk path provider This command resolves the latest compatible versions and records them in pubspec.yaml . Commit your lockfile to source control. After upgrading dependencies, independently verify the initialization and connection lifecycles on both Android and iOS devices. Initialize the SDK Reuse a single instance of OpenIM.iMManager across your application process. Obtain a persistent writable documents directory, select the appropriate platform identifier, and provide the connection listener during initialization. Code example import 'dart:io'; import 'package:flutter openim sdk/flutter openim sdk.dart'; import 'package:path provider/path provider.dart'; Future initializeOpenIM required String apiAddr, required String wsAddr, async final directory = await getApplicationDocumentsDirectory ; final platformID = Platform.isIOS ? IMPlatform.ios : IMPlatform.android; final initialized = await OpenIM.iMManager.initSDK platformID: platformID, apiAddr: apiAddr, wsAddr: wsAddr, dataDir: directory.path, logLevel: 6, isLogStandardOutput: true, listener: OnConnectListener onConnecting: = updateConnectionState 'connecting' , onConnectSuccess: = updateConnectionState 'connected' , onConnectFailed: code, message updateConnectionState 'failed' ; logConnectionFailure code, message ; , onKickedOffline: handleKickedOffline, onUserTokenExpired: refreshSession, onUserTokenInvalid: redirectToSignIn, , ; return initialized == true; Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | platformID | int | Yes | Platform identifier. Pass IMPlatform.android for Android, and IMPlatform.ios for iOS. | | apiAddr | String | Yes | OpenIMServer HTTP API endpoint. | | wsAddr | String | Yes | OpenIMServer WebSocket endpoint. | | dataDir | String | Yes | App sandbox directory for local SQLite databases and logs. | | listener | OnConnectListener | Yes | Listener for connection state transitions, token expiration, and kick out events. | | logLevel | int | No | Numeric SDK logging level. Defaults to 6 . | | isNeedEncryption | bool | No | Whether to enable local database encryption. Defaults to false . | | isCompression | bool | No | Whether to compress network payloads. Defaults to false . | | isLogStandardOutput | bool | No | Whether to print SDK logs to standard output. | | logFilePath | String? | No | Custom log file path. When omitted, the SDK creates logs inside dataDir . | Return value A successful Future returns a boolean indicating whether the underlying native core was initialized. WebSocket readiness after login is signaled exclusively through the OnConnectListener.onConnectSuccess event. Android and iOS boundaries Android Ensure AndroidManifest.xml includes and store SDK data in internal app storage. When running on an Android emulator, do not use localhost to refer to the host workstation. Process retention and push message delivery depend on system battery policies and OEM specific background restrictions. iOS Store database and cache files strictly within the writable application sandbox; never attempt to write to the app bundle. Configure App Transport Security ATS exceptions if connecting to non HTTPS/WSS staging endpoints. Production deployments require valid TLS certificates. Physical devices, background fetch modes, and simulators exhibit different lifecycle characteristics; verify each independently. Lifecycle and teardown The Flutter SDK does not expose manual network status or foreground/background lifecycle reporting methods. When the app resumes, rely on OnConnectListener callbacks to determine connection status, and re query fresh snapshots for visible screens. When releasing SDK resources completely, invoke: OpenIM.iMManager.unInitSDK ; Uninitialization is not equivalent to signing out. When switching user accounts, await logout , clear user specific UI state, and then log in with the new credentials. Verification and troubleshooting Verify initialization, login, and onConnectSuccess on at least one physical Android and iOS device. Verify that HTTP, WebSocket, and media storage URLs are reachable from external networks. Test app process termination, backgrounding, and network disconnections to confirm automatic reconnection and screen recovery. Avoid re initializing the SDK or swapping the global listener across multiple Widgets. Next steps Authenticate and manage session /sdk/flutter/getting started/authenticate and manage session Send your first message /sdk/flutter/getting started/send first message

title: Authenticate and manage session
description: Initialize OpenIMClientSDK, log in, query login status, handle connection lifecycle events, and log out.
keywords: sdk flutter v4 sdk flutter getting-started authenticate-and-manage-session
content: The OpenIM Flutter SDK configures the local mobile environment through its initialization method, then establishes a persistent WebSocket connection session for the current user via the login API. Before starting authentication, verify that your server endpoints, user account, token, and mobile runtime are properly prepared as described in Before you start /sdk/flutter/getting started/before you start . The complete authentication lifecycle consists of the following steps: 1. Call initSDK and supply an OnConnectListener . 2. Retrieve the userID , token , apiAddr , and wsAddr from your business backend. 3. Call login , await Future completion, and wait for the onConnectSuccess callback. 4. Once the persistent connection is established, query users, friends, conversations, groups, and messages. 5. When the user logs out or switches accounts, invoke logout and reset local application state. Retrieve user credentials Obtain the current user's userID , token , and matching apiAddr and wsAddr from your backend service. See Before you start /sdk/flutter/getting started/before you start for data requirements. The userID is the unique user identifier within OpenIM and must match the subject signed into the token. The mobile client consumes credentials issued by the backend and does not issue tokens directly. Initialize and configure connection lifecycle Register the connection listener during SDK initialization so that you do not miss state transitions that occur during login. Code example final initialized = await OpenIM.iMManager.initSDK platformID: platformID, apiAddr: apiAddr, wsAddr: wsAddr, dataDir: dataDir, listener: OnConnectListener onConnecting: setConnectionState 'connecting' ; , onConnectSuccess: setConnectionState 'connected' ; , onConnectFailed: code, errorMsg setConnectionState 'failed' ; logConnectionFailure code, errorMsg ; , onKickedOffline: clearCurrentSession ; showSignedInElsewhereDialog ; , onUserTokenExpired: async await refreshSessionAndRelogin ; , onUserTokenInvalid: redirectToSignIn ; , , ; if initialized = true throw StateError 'OpenIMClientSDK initialization failed.' ; Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | platformID | int | Yes | Target client platform identifier. Must match the physical platform and server multi platform login policies. | | apiAddr | String | Yes | OpenIMServer HTTP API endpoint reachable from the mobile device. | | wsAddr | String | Yes | OpenIMServer WebSocket endpoint reachable from the mobile device. | | dataDir | String | Yes | Local storage directory for SDK SQLite databases and logs. Must reside in a private, writable application directory. | | listener | OnConnectListener | Yes | Callback listener for connection, token expiration, and kick out lifecycle events. | Return value A successful Future returning true indicates that the local SDK core was initialized. It does not indicate that the user has logged in or that the WebSocket connection is ready. Initialize the SDK once per application process; do not initialize separate instances inside individual Widgets. The OnConnectListener reference is held by initSDK . The SDK does not provide a separate listener removal method. Maintain a centralized listener service across your application to prevent re registration during Widget rebuilds. Log in the current user Invoke login with the user credentials: Code example final UserInfo currentUser = await OpenIM.iMManager.login userID: session.userID, token: session.token, ; setCurrentUser currentUser ; Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | userID | String | Yes | OpenIM user ID. Must match the token subject. | | token | String | Yes | Authentication token issued by your business backend. | | checkLoginStatus | bool | No | Whether to check existing login status first. Defaults to true . | | defaultValue | Future Function ? | No | Fallback callback invoked if fetching user profile fails. Usually left null to propagate real errors. | Return value A successful Future returns a UserInfo object representing the logged in user, indicating that authentication and local database initialization are complete. The onConnectSuccess callback indicates that the persistent WebSocket connection has been established. Treat Future completion and onConnectSuccess as distinct milestones; wait for connection readiness before initiating real time messaging workflows. Do not invoke login concurrently. Disable login buttons while the Future is pending or check the current login state before re invoking. Query login status Check whether the SDK is currently authenticated: Code example final status = await OpenIM.iMManager.getLoginStatus ; if status == LoginStatus.logged final currentUserID = await OpenIM.iMManager.getLoginUserID ; restoreSessionFor currentUserID ; | Status | Description | | | | | LoginStatus.logout | SDK is currently logged out. | | LoginStatus.logging | Login is currently in progress. Do not trigger parallel login requests. | | LoginStatus.logged | SDK is authenticated. Verify active network connectivity with OnConnectListener . | login returns the UserInfo cached during that session. To fetch updated profile information from the server, see Get self profile /sdk/flutter/user/retrieving and updating user information/get self profile . Querying the login status or current user ID returns the immediate cached state without triggering connection callbacks. Use getLoginUserID to verify that the active SDK account matches your application state, but do not treat it as a substitute for business backend token validation. When switching accounts, do not overwrite the session in place. Await logout on the existing account, clear local state, and then log in with the new credentials. Handle token expiration and kick outs When a token expires or becomes invalid, obtain a new token from your backend and re authenticate. The onKickedOffline event indicates that the current user was forced offline by another client login or administrative action, which is distinct from an explicit client logout. The Flutter SDK accepts an OpenIM token directly; it does not distinguish between client side access and session tokens. Token lifetime, renewal, and revocation policies are governed by your business backend and OpenIMServer configurations. These lifecycle callbacks do not contain entity merge keys. Isolate state per SDK session and user account. When switching accounts, clear state from pending asynchronous tasks to avoid writing stale data to new views. Log out End the active session by invoking logout : Code example await OpenIM.iMManager.logout ; clearCurrentSession ; Return value A successful Future indicates that the SDK session has terminated. When switching accounts, wait for logout to complete, purge the previous account's cache, and then invoke login . Future completion, connection callbacks, and view teardown represent distinct phases. Await logout before purging conversation lists, message views, unread counters, and cached state. Do not rely solely on connection state callbacks to conclude that logout succeeded. To release SDK resources entirely when closing the app, call unInitSDK . This method frees native runtime memory; it is not a substitute for logout and should not be invoked during normal page navigation. Next steps Before you start /sdk/flutter/getting started/before you start Send your first message /sdk/flutter/getting started/send first message Events overview /sdk/flutter/events/overview events Logger /sdk/flutter/logger

title: Send your first message
description: Verify the single-chat and group-chat message sending flow in a Flutter application.
keywords: sdk flutter v4 sdk flutter getting-started send-first-message
content: Install and initialize the OpenIM Flutter SDK, authenticate a user, and send your first text message in a single chat or group chat conversation. Before proceeding, complete the setup steps outlined in Before you start /sdk/flutter/getting started/before you start . For single chat conversations, supply the recipient's userID . For group chat conversations, supply the target groupID . Never specify both destinations simultaneously. Step 1: Install the SDK Add the dependency to your Flutter project: flutter pub add flutter openim sdk This command selects the latest compatible release from pub.dev and updates pubspec.yaml alongside your lockfile. Commit the lockfile to source control, and verify SDK initialization, login, and message delivery whenever you upgrade dependencies. Step 2: Initialize the SDK Follow Environment specific implementation /sdk/flutter/getting started/environment specific implementation to resolve your persistent app data directory and initialize the client. Provide an OnConnectListener to confirm network readiness before issuing messaging requests. import 'package:flutter openim sdk/flutter openim sdk.dart'; final initialized = await OpenIM.iMManager.initSDK platformID: platformID, apiAddr: session.apiAddr, wsAddr: session.wsAddr, dataDir: dataDir, listener: connectListener, ; Step 3: Log in Authenticate the user session: await OpenIM.iMManager.login userID: session.userID, token: session.token, ; HTTP login completion and WebSocket connection readiness are two distinct stages. Await the OnConnectListener.onConnectSuccess callback before sending messages. Step 4: Prepare the destination For a single chat conversation, specify an existing recipient's user ID: const targetUserID = 'user b'; For a group chat, specify a group ID in which the current user is a valid member permitted to send messages: const targetGroupID = 'group 123'; Step 5: Create and send a text message Create a local Message object first, then pass it to sendMessage . Creating a message does not transmit data over the network or trigger events on the recipient's client. final message = await OpenIM.iMManager.messageManager.createTextMessage text: 'Hello, OpenIM', ; final sentMessage = await OpenIM.iMManager.messageManager.sendMessage message: message, userID: targetUserID, offlinePushInfo: OfflinePushInfo title: 'New message', desc: 'You received a new message', , ; appendOutgoingMessage sentMessage ; When sending to a group chat, pass groupID instead of userID : final sentMessage = await OpenIM.iMManager.messageManager.sendMessage message: message, groupID: targetGroupID, offlinePushInfo: OfflinePushInfo title: 'New group message', desc: 'A new message was posted in the group', , ; Once the Future completes, the sender app can append the returned Message to the UI using clientMsgID as the deduplication and merge key. The recipient receives the incoming message through message listeners see Receive messages /sdk/flutter/message/receiving messages/receive messages for implementation details . Sender dispatch success and recipient delivery represent two distinct asynchronous phases; verify both during testing. Next steps Authenticate and manage session /sdk/flutter/getting started/authenticate and manage session Send messages /sdk/flutter/message/sending messages/send message Receive messages /sdk/flutter/message/receiving messages/receive messages

title: Users overview
description: Understand user profiles, friendship relations, blocklists, and presence status in OpenIMClientSDK.
keywords: sdk flutter v4 sdk flutter user overview-user
content: The OpenIM Flutter SDK identifies users by their userID . When implementing user profile cards, friend discovery, contact directories, or blocklists, differentiate between public user profiles, friend relationships maintained by the current account, and blocklist states. Group member rosters, in group nicknames, group roles, and membership administration belong to the group domain; see Retrieving group members overview /sdk/flutter/group/retrieving group members/overview retrieving group members . User data models OpenIM returns distinct user data structures depending on the operational context: | Model | Target Use Case | Associated Guides | | | | | | UserInfo | Currently logged in user profile, account settings, self avatar, nickname, and global message reception settings. | Get self profile /sdk/flutter/user/retrieving and updating user information/get self profile , Update self profile /sdk/flutter/user/retrieving and updating user information/update self profile | | PublicUserInfo | User search, friend discovery candidates, stranger profile cards. | Retrieve users /sdk/flutter/user/retrieving users/retrieve users | | FriendInfo | Friend list entries for the current user, friend remarks, and friendship custom extensions. Note: the Dart model does not contain isPinned . | Get friend list with pagination /sdk/flutter/user/friends/get friend list page , Get friends info /sdk/flutter/user/friends/get friends info | | BlacklistInfo | Users blocked by the current account. | Retrieve a list of blocked users /sdk/flutter/user/moderating a user/retrieve a list of blocked users , Block a user /sdk/flutter/user/moderating a user/block user , Unblock a user /sdk/flutter/user/moderating a user/unblock user | | UserStatusInfo | Real time presence status and active platform indicators. | Subscribe to user status /sdk/flutter/user/retrieving and updating user information/subscribe user status , Get subscribed user status /sdk/flutter/user/retrieving and updating user information/get subscribed user status | A single userID can exist simultaneously in public directories, the friend roster, the blocklist, and group rosters. Prioritize FriendInfo when rendering contacts; use PublicUserInfo when displaying stranger profiles; and use GroupMembersInfo in group contexts. For conversation list titles and chat headers, use ConversationInfo.showName . Functional directory | Requirement | Recommended Guide | | | | | Query public profiles by userID for friend discovery or profile cards | Retrieve users /sdk/flutter/user/retrieving users/retrieve users | | Paginate, search, or inspect friend relationships | Get friend list with pagination /sdk/flutter/user/friends/get friend list page | | Send, query, accept, or reject friend applications | Get friend application list as recipient /sdk/flutter/user/friend applications/get friend application list as recipient | | Modify friend remarks and relationship extensions | Update friends /sdk/flutter/user/friends/update friends | | Remove friend relationships | Delete a friend /sdk/flutter/user/friends/delete friend | | View and manage the blocklist | Retrieve a list of blocked users /sdk/flutter/user/moderating a user/retrieve a list of blocked users | | Read or update the current user's nickname, avatar, and extensions | Update self profile /sdk/flutter/user/retrieving and updating user information/update self profile | | Configure account wide message reception and DND rules | Set global message reception /sdk/flutter/user/retrieving and updating user information/set global message reception | | Subscribe to and inspect user presence | Subscribe to user status /sdk/flutter/user/retrieving and updating user information/subscribe user status | | Retrieve group member lists, member search, or specific member details | Retrieving group members overview /sdk/flutter/group/retrieving group members/overview retrieving group members | State management and listeners Listen to and merge user domain events within their respective capability handlers: Current user profile updates: see Update self profile /sdk/flutter/user/retrieving and updating user information/update self profile . Friend application changes: see Get friend application list as recipient /sdk/flutter/user/friend applications/get friend application list as recipient . Friendship additions, deletions, and updates: see Get friend list with pagination /sdk/flutter/user/friends/get friend list page . Blocklist modifications: see Block a user /sdk/flutter/user/moderating a user/block user . Presence status changes: see Subscribe to user status /sdk/flutter/user/retrieving and updating user information/subscribe user status . UserManager and FriendshipManager each maintain a single listener instance in the Flutter SDK. Assemble all required callbacks centrally in an application level state provider and register each listener once to prevent individual Widgets from overwriting one another.

title: Retrieve users
description: Batch query public user profiles (PublicUserInfo) by userID using the OpenIM Flutter SDK.
keywords: sdk flutter v4 sdk flutter user retrieving-users retrieve-users
content: Batch query public profiles of application users by userID , ideal for rendering friend candidates and stranger profile cards: When searching users by nickname, phone number, organization, or email, your business backend should first return matching userID values. Then call this method to retrieve their public profile details. Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | userIDList | List | Yes | List of user IDs to query for public information. Deduplicate entries and cap batch sizes before calling. | Code example final userIDList = 'user a', 'user b' .toList ; try final users = await OpenIM.iMManager.userManager.getUsersInfo userIDList: userIDList, ; final usersByID = for final user in users if user.userID = null user.userID : user, ; showUsers usersByID ; catch error logUserQueryFailure error, userIDList ; rethrow; Return value A successful Future returns a list of public user profiles List : | Field | Type | Description | | | | | | userID | String | Unique OpenIM user identifier. | | nickname | String? | Account level public display nickname. | | faceURL | String? | Account level public avatar URL. | | ex | String? | Account level extension string formatted per business conventions. | The returned ex is read only when viewing other accounts. The Flutter client cannot modify other users' profiles; to update the current user's profile, see Update self profile /sdk/flutter/user/retrieving and updating user information/update self profile . This query is a local read only operation and does not trigger user listener events. Re invoke this API to fetch fresh data when opening profile cards, pulling to refresh, reconnecting, or receiving business update notifications. Model selection by context The same userID may possess different display names and relationship data across contexts. Select the appropriate data model for each view: | Context | Recommended Model | | | | | User directory search, stranger profile cards | PublicUserInfo | | Friend lists, contact cards, friend remarks | FriendInfo | | Group rosters, in group nicknames, group roles | GroupMembersInfo | Friend remarks and group nicknames originate from friendship and group membership records; do not overwrite them with PublicUserInfo.nickname . For related queries, see Get friend list with pagination /sdk/flutter/user/friends/get friend list page , Get friends info /sdk/flutter/user/friends/get friends info , and Retrieving group members overview /sdk/flutter/group/retrieving group members/overview retrieving group members .

title: Get self profile
description: Retrieve the profile of the currently signed-in user using the OpenIM Flutter SDK.
keywords: sdk flutter v4 sdk flutter user retrieving-and-updating-user-information get-self-profile
content: Retrieve the full profile of the currently logged in user: Parameters This method accepts no parameters. Code example final user = await OpenIM.iMManager.userManager.getSelfUserInfo ; Return value A successful Future returns a UserInfo object representing the current user's profile. UserInfo contains core account properties: userID : Unique current user identifier. nickname : User's display nickname. faceURL : Avatar URL. gender : Gender enumeration value. ex : Custom business extension string. globalRecvMsgOpt : Global message reception and notification setting. This query is a read only operation and does not trigger profile change events. Use the returned object to initialize user profile pages, settings screens, or current user application state. Clear in memory profile state when logging out or switching accounts. To modify personal information, see Update self profile /sdk/flutter/user/retrieving and updating user information/update self profile . For profile event listening, see Events overview /sdk/flutter/events/overview events .

title: Update self profile
description: Update the nickname, avatar, and custom extensions of the currently logged-in user using the OpenIM Flutter SDK.
keywords: sdk flutter v4 sdk flutter user retrieving-and-updating-user-information update-self-profile
content: Modify the nickname, avatar URL, or custom business extensions of the currently logged in user: Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | nickname | String? | No | New user display nickname. Providing a trimmed non empty string is recommended. | | faceURL | String? | No | Full remote URL of the user's new avatar image. | | ex | String? | No | Custom business extension string. Passing a new value overwrites existing extension text without automatically merging JSON properties. | Supply only the fields that are being modified; omitted fields retain their existing values on the server. Code example await OpenIM.iMManager.userManager.setSelfInfo nickname: 'New Nickname', faceURL: 'https://example.com/avatar.png', ex: ' "customTheme":"dark" ', ; Return value A successful Future returns void , indicating that the profile update request was accepted and applied by the server. State changes after the call This method alters user profile state. Future completion represents request processing; it is distinct from event delivery across other client devices. While globalRecvMsgOpt belongs to the same user profile data structure, it controls account wide notification policies and should be managed via its dedicated method; see Set global message reception /sdk/flutter/user/retrieving and updating user information/set global message reception . Listen for self profile updates Handle profile modifications centrally. When the server completes the update, all active client sessions for this account receive onSelfInfoUpdated event notifications. Use userID as the key to update cached user profile state: void handleSelfInfoUpdated UserInfo info mergeSelfInfo info ; The Flutter SDK maintains a single OnUserListener instance inside UserManager . Configure this callback inside the consolidated application entry point described in Events overview /sdk/flutter/events/overview events . To fetch the full profile snapshot from scratch, see Get self profile /sdk/flutter/user/retrieving and updating user information/get self profile .

title: Set global message reception
description: Configure default message reception and notification behavior for the current account using the OpenIM Flutter SDK.
keywords: sdk flutter v4 sdk flutter user retrieving-and-updating-user-information set-global-message-reception
content: Configure default global message reception and offline push notification policies across all single chat and group chat conversations for the current account: Parameters Specify the globalRecvMsgOpt parameter in setSelfInfo to configure account level do not disturb DND behavior without altering other profile fields: | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | globalRecvMsgOpt | int | Yes | Global message reception option enumeration value. Typically toggles between normal delivery and do not disturb. | | Enum Option | Value | Behavior | | | | | | ReceiveMessageOpt.receive | 0 | Receive messages normally with offline push notifications enabled. | | ReceiveMessageOpt.notNotify | 2 | Receive messages silently without triggering offline push or system notification banners DND mode . | Code example await OpenIM.iMManager.userManager.setSelfInfo globalRecvMsgOpt: ReceiveMessageOpt.notNotify, ; Return value A successful Future returns void , indicating that the global message reception configuration was committed to the server. State changes after the call This method alters user state. Per conversation reception options take precedence over this global account default. To configure individual conversation rules, see Set conversation message receive option /sdk/flutter/conversation/managing conversations/set message receive option . When the update takes effect on the server, all active client sessions for this account receive onSelfInfoUpdated event notifications. Use userID as the merge key to update the current user's cached profile. For profile update listener implementation, see Update self profile /sdk/flutter/user/retrieving and updating user information/update self profile .

title: Subscribe to user status
description: Subscribe to real-time online presence status for specified users using the OpenIM Flutter SDK.
keywords: sdk flutter v4 sdk flutter user retrieving-and-updating-user-information subscribe-user-status
content: Subscribe to real time presence changes for specified target users and retrieve their initial presence snapshot: Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | userIDs | List | Yes | List of user IDs whose online status should be subscribed to. Deduplicate and filter out empty strings; subscribe only to users currently visible on screen. | Code example final states = await OpenIM.iMManager.userManager.subscribeUsersStatus 'user a', 'user b' , ; Return value A successful Future returns a list of presence status snapshots for the target users at the moment of subscription List . Core fields of each UserStatusInfo : userID : Unique user identifier; acts as the primary key for state lookup and merging. status : Integer representing presence state. detailPlatformStatus : List of platform presence details iOS, Android, Web, Desktop, etc. . Merge these snapshot records into your local presence cache using userID . Listen for presence status updates Handle presence transitions centrally. When a subscribed user's presence changes connecting, disconnecting, or changing active platforms , the SDK delivers updates through the onUserStatusChanged callback: void handleUserStatusChanged UserStatusInfo info mergePresence info ; The Flutter SDK maintains a single OnUserListener instance inside UserManager . Configure this callback inside the consolidated application entry point described in Events overview /sdk/flutter/events/overview events . When widgets are disposed or users scroll out of the visible viewport, invoke Unsubscribe from user status /sdk/flutter/user/retrieving and updating user information/unsubscribe user status to release subscription resources.

title: Get subscribed user status
description: Query the online presence status of subscribed users using the OpenIM Flutter SDK.
keywords: sdk flutter v4 sdk flutter user retrieving-and-updating-user-information get-subscribed-user-status
content: Retrieve an immediate presence snapshot for all users currently subscribed to by the signed in client: Parameters This method accepts no parameters. It automatically retrieves current presence data for all subscribed users. Code example final states = await OpenIM.iMManager.userManager.getSubscribeUsersStatus ; Return value A successful Future returns a list of presence status records List . Each UserStatusInfo item includes the target user's userID , numeric online status , and platform breakdown in detailPlatformStatus . When reconnecting or resuming from the background, invoke this method to pull a fresh presence snapshot and merge records into the local state store using userID as the key. OpenIM manages presence through persistent subscriptions; it does not offer ad hoc one off status queries for unsubscribed users. This query is a read only snapshot retrieval and does not modify active subscriptions or trigger presence listener events. To manage subscription targets, see Subscribe to user status /sdk/flutter/user/retrieving and updating user information/subscribe user status and Unsubscribe from user status /sdk/flutter/user/retrieving and updating user information/unsubscribe user status .

title: Unsubscribe from user status
description: Cancel presence status subscriptions for specified users using the OpenIM Flutter SDK.
keywords: sdk flutter v4 sdk flutter user retrieving-and-updating-user-information unsubscribe-user-status
content: Cancel online presence subscriptions for target users and release subscription capacity: Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | userIDs | List | Yes | List of user IDs to unsubscribe from presence tracking. | Code example await OpenIM.iMManager.userManager.unsubscribeUsersStatus 'user a', 'user b' , ; Return value A successful Future returns void , indicating that the cancellation request was accepted by the server. State changes after the call This method alters subscription state. After successfully unsubscribing, the SDK ceases receiving incremental presence updates for these users. Once the Future resolves, remove these entries from your local presence cache using userID as the key; if the request fails, retain active subscription records for subsequent retry. To subscribe to user presence, see Subscribe to user status /sdk/flutter/user/retrieving and updating user information/subscribe user status . To retrieve an immediate presence snapshot, see Get subscribed user status /sdk/flutter/user/retrieving and updating user information/get subscribed user status .

title: Get friend list with pagination
description: Retrieve the current user friend list using pagination in the OpenIM Flutter SDK.
keywords: sdk flutter v4 sdk flutter user friends get-friend-list-page
content: Retrieve the currently logged in user's friend list using pagination: Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | offset | int | Yes | Pagination offset index. Start at 0 for the first page. | | count | int | Yes | Maximum number of friend records to fetch per page. | | filterBlack | bool | No | Whether to exclude friends present on the blocklist. Pass true to filter out blocked users; pass false to include them. | Code example final friends = await OpenIM.iMManager.friendshipManager.getFriendListPage offset: 0, count: 40, filterBlack: true, ; Return value A successful Future returns a list of friend profiles for the requested page List . The client should deduplicate and append items to the local contacts list using userID as the primary key. When the returned list length is less than count , the end of the friend list has been reached. Always use paginated queries to retrieve friend data to avoid performance overhead on large contact rosters. This query returns a local database snapshot and does not emit friendship events. Listen for friend change events Friend additions, profile modifications, and deletions are handled centrally through listener callbacks. In your contact state store, use userID as the sole key for merging, updating, or deleting friend entries: void handleFriendChanged FriendInfo info mergeFriend info ; void handleFriendDeleted FriendInfo info final userID = info.userID; if userID = null removeFriend userID ; The Flutter SDK maintains a single OnFriendshipListener instance inside FriendshipManager . Integrate these handler functions into your application's contact store and register the listener centrally see Events overview /sdk/flutter/events/overview events rather than setting listeners inside individual Widget trees.

title: Search friends
description: Search friends in the local contact list using the OpenIM Flutter SDK.
keywords: sdk flutter v4 sdk flutter user friends search-friends
content: Perform local fuzzy searches across the current user's friend list matching specified keywords and field dimensions: Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | keywordList | List | Yes | List of search keywords. Providing a list with a single non empty keyword string is recommended. | | isSearchUserID | bool | No | Whether to match against the friend's user ID. | | isSearchNickname | bool | No | Whether to match against the friend's nickname. | | isSearchRemark | bool | No | Whether to match against the friend's remark. | Code example final results = await OpenIM.iMManager.friendshipManager.searchFriends keywordList: 'alice' , isSearchUserID: true, isSearchNickname: true, isSearchRemark: true, ; Return value A successful Future returns a list of matching friend search results List . Each SearchFriendsInfo object contains friend profile data alongside matched attributes. Search results should power temporary search views and must not replace the persistent global contact roster. When opening conversations or navigating from search results, use the candidate's userID as the unique entity key. This operation executes locally against the client database and does not trigger friend listener callbacks. To load the regular friend list, see Get friend list with pagination /sdk/flutter/user/friends/get friend list page .

title: Get friends info
description: Retrieve detailed friendship profiles for specified friends using the OpenIM Flutter SDK.
keywords: sdk flutter v4 sdk flutter user friends get-friends-info
content: Query detailed friendship profile cards for specified users in the currently signed in user's friend list: Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | userIDList | List | Yes | List of target user IDs to query for friend information. | | filterBlack | bool | No | Whether to filter out blocked users. Pass true to omit blocked friends; pass false to include them. | Code example final friends = await OpenIM.iMManager.friendshipManager.getFriendsInfo userIDList: 'user a', 'user b' , filterBlack: true, ; Return value A successful Future returns a list of matching friend profiles List . Each FriendInfo object contains comprehensive relationship data, including userID , nickname , faceURL , custom remark remark , and extension string ex . The client should validate the nullable userID and update its local contacts cache using userID as the key. If an ID is absent from the returned list, the user is either not a friend or was excluded by the blocklist filter. This query is a read only operation and does not emit friendship listener events. To verify relationship status without pulling full profile cards, see Check friendship /sdk/flutter/user/friends/check friend . To query public profiles for non friend users, see Retrieve users /sdk/flutter/user/retrieving users/retrieve users .

title: Check friendship
description: Verify friendship relationships with specified users using the OpenIM Flutter SDK.
keywords: sdk flutter v4 sdk flutter user friends check-friend
content: Check the friendship relationship status between the currently signed in user and a list of candidate user IDs: Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | userIDList | List | Yes | List of target user IDs to verify for friendship. | Code example final checks = await OpenIM.iMManager.friendshipManager.checkFriend userIDList: 'user a', 'user b' , ; Return value A successful Future returns a list of friendship check results List . Each FriendshipInfo item includes the target userID and an integer result : result == 1 indicates an active bilateral friendship, while other values indicate non friend status. This method performs a lightweight relation check; it does not return friend remarks, signatures, or custom extensions, nor does it emit listener events. To retrieve complete friend profile details, see Get friends info /sdk/flutter/user/friends/get friends info .

title: Update friends
description: Update remarks, pinned status, or custom extensions for specified friends using the OpenIM Flutter SDK.
keywords: sdk flutter v4 sdk flutter user friends update-friends
content: Update remarks, pin status, or custom business extensions for one or more friends: Parameters The UpdateFriendsReq object contains the following fields: | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | friendUserIDs | List | Yes | List of friend user IDs whose relationship details should be updated. | | remark | String? | No | Custom friend remark name. | | isPinned | bool? | No | Whether to pin this friend in contact views. | | ex | String? | No | Custom friendship extension string. Passing a new value overwrites existing extension data rather than merging keys incrementally. | Provide at least one property field to modify alongside friendUserIDs . If different friends require distinct remarks or extension attributes, invoke this API separately for each user. Code example await OpenIM.iMManager.friendshipManager.updateFriends UpdateFriendsReq friendUserIDs: 'user 123' , remark: 'Alice', isPinned: true, , ; Return value A successful Future returns void , indicating that the update request was accepted and processed by the server. State changes after the call This method alters relationship states. When the server successfully updates the friend details, connected clients receive onFriendInfoChanged event notifications. The client should update the corresponding friend item in the local contacts cache using userID as the merge key. For friend event listening and state management, see Get friend list with pagination /sdk/flutter/user/friends/get friend list page .

title: Delete a friend
description: Remove a specified user from the current user friend list using the OpenIM Flutter SDK.
keywords: sdk flutter v4 sdk flutter user friends delete-friend
content: Remove a user from the currently signed in user's friend list: Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | userID | String | Yes | Target user ID to remove from friends. | Code example await OpenIM.iMManager.friendshipManager.deleteFriend userID: 'user 123', ; Return value A successful Future returns void , indicating that the deletion request was processed by the server and friendship records were removed locally. State changes after the call This method alters relationship states. Upon successful deletion, the current client and other signed in sessions for this account receive onFriendDeleted events. The client should remove the corresponding entry from the local contacts cache using userID as the key. For friend event listening and state synchronization, see Get friend list with pagination /sdk/flutter/user/friends/get friend list page .

title: Add a friend
description: Send a friend application with a verification remark using the OpenIM Flutter SDK.
keywords: sdk flutter v4 sdk flutter user friend-applications add-friend
content: Send a friend request to a target user with an optional verification remark: Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | userID | String | Yes | Target user ID to add as a friend. | | reason | String | No | Optional verification remark message. | Code example await OpenIM.iMManager.friendshipManager.addFriend userID: 'user b', reason: 'Hi, I am Alex', ; Return value A successful Future indicates that the friend application was accepted and queued by the server. State changes after the call A successful call signifies only that the application has been transmitted; it does not establish a friendship immediately. Once the recipient approves the request, both users receive friend addition events via their listeners. To monitor the status of sent applications, see Get friend application list as applicant /sdk/flutter/user/friend applications/get friend application list as applicant .

title: Get friend application list as recipient
description: Query incoming friend applications received by the current user using pagination in Flutter.
keywords: sdk flutter v4 sdk flutter user friend-applications get-friend-application-list-as-recipient
content: Retrieve pending and processed incoming friend requests received by the currently logged in user using pagination: Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | offset | int | No | Pagination offset index. Start at 0 for the first page. | | count | int | No | Number of application records to fetch per page. | | handleResults | List ? | No | Filter records by resolution status: 0 for pending, 1 for approved, 1 for rejected. | Code example final items = await OpenIM.iMManager.friendshipManager .getFriendApplicationListAsRecipient req: GetFriendApplicationListAsRecipientReq offset: 0, count: 20 , ; Return value A successful Future returns a list of incoming friend application records for the requested page List . Query operations return an immediate data snapshot and do not emit listener events. For application handling actions, see Accept a friend application /sdk/flutter/user/friend applications/accept friend application and Refuse a friend application /sdk/flutter/user/friend applications/refuse friend application . Synchronize friend application events Listen to friend application events centrally and merge state incrementally using the composite key fromUserID:toUserID : void handleFriendApplicationChanged FriendApplicationInfo item mergeFriendApplication item ; void handleFriendApplicationDeleted FriendApplicationInfo item removeFriendApplication item.fromUserID, item.toUserID ; Within your single OnFriendshipListener , route onFriendApplicationAdded , onFriendApplicationAccepted , and onFriendApplicationRejected to handleFriendApplicationChanged , and route onFriendApplicationDeleted to handleFriendApplicationDeleted . See Events overview /sdk/flutter/events/overview events for the consolidated registration entry point. Distinguish incoming requests from outgoing requests by checking toUserID == currentUserID . The Flutter SDK does not expose a public method for deleting friend application history; do not simulate deletion by rejecting applications or deleting friends.

title: Get friend application list as applicant
description: Query outgoing friend applications sent by the current user using pagination in Flutter.
keywords: sdk flutter v4 sdk flutter user friend-applications get-friend-application-list-as-applicant
content: Retrieve outgoing friend applications initiated by the currently logged in user using pagination: Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | offset | int | No | Pagination offset index. Start at 0 for the first page. | | count | int | No | Number of application records to fetch per page. | Code example final items = await OpenIM.iMManager.friendshipManager .getFriendApplicationListAsApplicant req: GetFriendApplicationListAsApplicantReq offset: 0, count: 20 , ; Return value A successful Future returns a list of friend application records for the requested page List . Query operations return an immediate data snapshot and do not emit listener events. Deduplicate and merge application records using the composite identifier fromUserID:toUserID . To submit new requests, see Add a friend /sdk/flutter/user/friend applications/add friend .

title: Get unhandled friend application count
description: Retrieve the number of unhandled friend applications in Flutter.
keywords: sdk flutter v4 sdk flutter user friend-applications get-friend-application-unhandled-count
content: Query the count of unhandled friend applications created or updated after a given timestamp, typically used to display badge counts or red dot indicators on contacts tabs: Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | time | int | Yes | Epoch timestamp in seconds. Usually set to the timestamp when the user last viewed the application list; pass 0 to count all unhandled requests. | Code example final count = await OpenIM.iMManager.friendshipManager .getFriendApplicationUnhandledCount GetFriendApplicationUnhandledCountReq time: lastViewedAt , ; Return value A successful Future returns the unhandled friend application count as an int . This query returns an immediate numerical snapshot; it does not alter application states or trigger events. To inspect or resolve requests, see Get friend application list as recipient /sdk/flutter/user/friend applications/get friend application list as recipient .

title: Accept a friend application
description: Accept an incoming friend application and establish a friendship using the OpenIM Flutter SDK.
keywords: sdk flutter v4 sdk flutter user friend-applications accept-friend-application
content: Accept a friend application sent by another user to formally establish a bilateral friendship: Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | userID | String | Yes | User ID of the applicant who submitted the friend request. | | handleMsg | String | No | Optional remark message attached when approving the request. | Code example await OpenIM.iMManager.friendshipManager.acceptFriendApplication userID: applicantUserID, handleMsg: 'Approved', ; Return value A successful Future indicates that the server accepted the friend request and established the friendship. State changes after the call Upon success, update the applicant's record to approved using their userID as the key, and merge the new friend into the local contacts cache by userID . The SDK notifies connected clients of friend application updates and friend additions via listener callbacks. For application record handling, see Get friend application list as recipient /sdk/flutter/user/friend applications/get friend application list as recipient ; for friend list synchronization, see Get friend list with pagination /sdk/flutter/user/friends/get friend list page .

title: Refuse a friend application
description: Decline an incoming friend application using the OpenIM Flutter SDK.
keywords: sdk flutter v4 sdk flutter user friend-applications refuse-friend-application
content: Decline a friend application sent by another user with an optional refusal remark: Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | userID | String | Yes | User ID of the applicant who submitted the friend request. | | handleMsg | String | No | Optional remark explaining the reason for declining. | Code example await OpenIM.iMManager.friendshipManager.refuseFriendApplication userID: applicantUserID, handleMsg: 'Declined for now', ; Return value A successful Future indicates that the server has processed and recorded the application rejection. State changes after the call Upon success, update the applicant's record to rejected using their userID as the key. Connected devices receive friend application update events. For complete application status listening and state merging logic, see Get friend application list as recipient /sdk/flutter/user/friend applications/get friend application list as recipient .

title: Retrieve a list of blocked users
description: Retrieve the current user blocklist using the OpenIM Flutter SDK.
keywords: sdk flutter v4 sdk flutter user moderating-a-user retrieve-a-list-of-blocked-users
content: Retrieve the full blocklist maintained by the currently logged in user to build blocklist management views or verify relationship status in profile cards and conversation settings: Blocklists and group moderation are distinct features. Group mutes, kicking members, or altering group roles belong to group member management; this method queries only the user level blocklist maintained unilaterally by the current account. Parameters This method accepts no parameters. Code example final blockedUsers = await OpenIM.iMManager.friendshipManager.getBlacklist ; Profile views, conversation menus, and contact directories typically only need to determine whether a given userID is blocked. Construct a lookup Set for fast checks: final blockedUserIDs = blockedUsers .map user = user.userID .whereType .toSet ; bool isBlocked String userID = blockedUserIDs.contains userID ; Return value A successful Future returns a list of blocklist entries List . An empty list indicates no users are currently blocked. Each BlacklistInfo object contains the following fields: | Field | Type | Description | | | | | | userID | String | Blocked target user ID; use as the primary key for state deduplication and lookup. | | nickname | String? | Target user's nickname. | | faceURL | String? | Target user's avatar URL. | | ownerUserID | String | Owner of the blocklist relationship the currently logged in user . | | blockUserID | String | ID of the blocked user in the relation record; use userID for client merges. | | operatorUserID | String | User ID of the operator who executed the block. | | createTime | int | Unix timestamp in milliseconds when the block was created. | | addSource | int | Numeric origin source of the block record. | | gender | int | Gender enumeration value of the target user. | | ex | String? | Custom business extension string. | If the blocklist UI requires friend remarks or full user profiles, merge records using userID while preserving model boundaries. This query returns a local database snapshot and does not trigger blocklist addition or deletion events. When opening the blocklist screen or pulling to refresh, call this method to reload the full snapshot. For blocklist mutations, see Block a user /sdk/flutter/user/moderating a user/block user and Unblock a user /sdk/flutter/user/moderating a user/unblock user .

title: Block a user
description: Add a specified user to the current user blocklist using the OpenIM Flutter SDK.
keywords: sdk flutter v4 sdk flutter user moderating-a-user block-user
content: Add a specified user to the currently signed in user's blocklist: Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | userID | String | Yes | Target user ID to add to the blocklist. | | ex | String? | No | Custom extension string. Passing a new value overwrites existing extension text without automatically merging JSON properties. | Code example await OpenIM.iMManager.friendshipManager.addBlacklist userID: 'user 123', ex: ' "source":"profile menu" ', ; Return value A successful Future returns void , indicating that the block request was committed by the server and recorded locally. State changes after the call This method alters relationship states. Once the block takes effect, the blocked user cannot send single chat messages to the current user, though the current user can still dispatch messages to them; enforce mutual message suppression at the application layer if required. Listen for blocklist events Handle blocklist additions centrally. When the block takes effect, connected client devices receive onBlackAdded event notifications. Use userID as the key to merge records into the local blocklist state: void handleBlackAdded BlacklistInfo info mergeBlockedUser info ; The Flutter SDK maintains a single OnFriendshipListener instance inside FriendshipManager . Register this handler through the application wide entry point described in Events overview /sdk/flutter/events/overview events . To fetch the complete list of blocked users, see Retrieve a list of blocked users /sdk/flutter/user/moderating a user/retrieve a list of blocked users .

title: Unblock a user
description: Remove a specified user from the current user blocklist using the OpenIM Flutter SDK.
keywords: sdk flutter v4 sdk flutter user moderating-a-user unblock-user
content: Remove a specified user from the currently signed in user's blocklist: Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | userID | String | Yes | Target user ID to remove from the blocklist. | Code example await OpenIM.iMManager.friendshipManager.removeBlacklist userID: 'user 123', ; Return value A successful Future returns void , indicating that the unblock request was processed by the server and removed from local storage. State changes after the call This method alters relationship states. Once the unblock operation completes, the user regains the ability to send single chat messages to the current user. Listen for unblock events Handle unblock events centrally. When the removal is processed on the server, connected client sessions receive onBlackDeleted event notifications. Use userID as the key to remove the entry from local blocklist stores: void handleBlackDeleted BlacklistInfo info final userID = info.userID; if userID = null removeBlockedUser userID ; The Flutter SDK maintains a single OnFriendshipListener instance inside FriendshipManager . Register this handler through the application wide entry point described in Events overview /sdk/flutter/events/overview events . To recalibrate the full blocklist snapshot, see Retrieve a list of blocked users /sdk/flutter/user/moderating a user/retrieve a list of blocked users .

title: Conversations overview
description: Understand ConversationInfo, conversationID, conversation settings, and event responsibilities in the OpenIM Flutter SDK.
keywords: sdk flutter v4 sdk flutter conversation overview-conversation
content: In OpenIM, a Conversation encapsulates the chat state maintained locally by the client for a single chat or group chat channel. It is represented by a ConversationInfo record scoped to the currently signed in user. It holds list level state including unread counts, latest messages, pin status, drafts, notification reception options, and custom extensions. A conversation record is distinguished from chat destinations: conversationID identifies the conversation state of the active account, single chat targets use the counterparty's userID , and group chat targets use groupID . Both single chat and group chat channels project their list status onto conversation records; group metadata, membership relations, and permissions remain governed by Group APIs. A group chat view uses groupID to access group capabilities while using conversationID to manage conversation settings, unread counts, drafts, and message history. Conversation identifiers Single chat conversations use the counterparty user ID as sourceID with conversationType set to ConversationType.single ; group chat conversations use groupID as sourceID with conversationType set to ConversationType.superGroup . Call Get conversation ID /sdk/flutter/conversation/retrieving conversations/get conversation id to obtain a deterministic conversationID before invoking conversation settings, read receipts, hiding, or message deletion. | Identifier | Purpose | | | | | conversationID | Local conversation record ID of the active account. Used for settings, history queries, and unread states. | | userID | Counterparty user ID in a single chat conversation. | | groupID | Target group ID in a group chat conversation; also used for Group APIs. | | sourceID | Target ID passed when querying by session type: userID for single chat, groupID for group chat. | ConversationInfo Key fields in ConversationInfo : | Field | Description | | | | | conversationID | Conversation ID. | | conversationType | Conversation type. | | userID | Counterparty user ID in single chats. | | groupID | Target group ID in group chats. | | showName | Display name of the conversation. | | faceURL | Display avatar URL of the conversation. | | unreadCount | Unread message count of this conversation. | | latestMsg | The most recent message payload. | | latestMsgSendTime | Timestamp when the latest message was sent. | | recvMsgOpt | Message reception option for this conversation. | | groupAtType | Mention notification state in group chats. | | draftText | Local draft message content. | | draftTextTime | Timestamp when the draft was updated. | | isPinned | Whether the conversation is pinned to the top. | | isPrivateChat Enterprise | Whether private chat mode is enabled. | | isMsgDestruct Enterprise | Whether message auto destruction is enabled. | | burnDuration Enterprise | Self destruct countdown duration in seconds. | | msgDestructTime Enterprise | Message destruction time configuration. | | ex | Custom business extension string. | Queries and settings Get conversation by target /sdk/flutter/conversation/retrieving conversations/get conversation by target Get conversations by ID /sdk/flutter/conversation/retrieving conversations/get conversations by id Retrieve conversation list /sdk/flutter/conversation/retrieving conversations/retrieve conversation list Pin or unpin a conversation /sdk/flutter/conversation/managing conversations/pin conversation Set conversation message receive option /sdk/flutter/conversation/managing conversations/set message receive option Set private chat /sdk/flutter/conversation/managing conversations/set private chat Set message destruct /sdk/flutter/conversation/managing conversations/set message destruct Clear group mentions /sdk/flutter/conversation/managing conversations/clear group mentions Set conversation extension /sdk/flutter/conversation/managing conversations/set conversation extension Set conversation draft /sdk/flutter/conversation/managing conversations/set conversation draft Mark conversation as read /sdk/flutter/conversation/managing conversations/mark conversation read Get total unread count /sdk/flutter/conversation/managing conversations/get total unread count Conversation lifecycle Hide a conversation /sdk/flutter/conversation/managing conversations/hide a conversation Delete conversation with messages /sdk/flutter/conversation/managing conversations/delete conversation with messages Clear conversation messages /sdk/flutter/conversation/managing conversations/clear conversation messages Conversation groups Conversation groups overview /sdk/flutter/conversation/managing conversation groups/overview conversation groups covers organizing conversations into custom folders or tags. Group entries use conversationID , while the group itself uses conversationGroupID . It only reorganizes conversations for the current account; it does not create chat groups or alter groupID membership or permissions. The Flutter SDK provides this capability through ConversationGroupManager . Queries return folder hierarchies, group events update by conversationGroupID , and member events update by combining conversationGroupID with conversationID . The overview page provides data models, complete listener setup, and links to individual APIs. State synchronization Query methods load the initial snapshot required by the view, while events merge subsequent incremental changes: New conversations and conversation property changes are monitored centrally in Retrieve conversation list /sdk/flutter/conversation/retrieving conversations/retrieve conversation list . Account wide total unread changes are monitored centrally in Get total unread count /sdk/flutter/conversation/managing conversations/get total unread count . Register listeners centrally within dedicated capability modules rather than fragmenting listeners across Widget trees. Future completion, subsequent event arrivals, and query recalibrations represent distinct lifecycle phases; handle each explicitly rather than assuming immediate state transitions based on local user interactions.

title: Get conversation by target
description: Retrieve a conversation for a specific user or group using the OpenIM Flutter SDK.
keywords: sdk flutter v4 sdk flutter conversation retrieving-conversations get-conversation-by-target
content: When initiating a chat from contacts, user profiles, or group details, query the conversation object by target ID and session type. Even if no messages have been exchanged yet, the SDK automatically initializes and returns the corresponding conversation record, avoiding the need to mock data structures at the application layer: Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | sourceID | String | Yes | Target chat ID. Supply the counterparty's userID for single chat, or groupID for group chat. | | sessionType | int | Yes | Conversation type. Pass ConversationType.single for single chat, or ConversationType.superGroup for group chat. | Code example final conversation = await OpenIM.iMManager.conversationManager.getOneConversation sourceID: targetUserID, sessionType: ConversationType.single, ; openChatPage conversation: conversation ; Return value A successful Future returns the matching ConversationInfo object. This query returns an immediate data snapshot and does not emit event notifications. Subsequent conversation property changes are monitored and merged centrally in Retrieve conversation list /sdk/flutter/conversation/retrieving conversations/retrieve conversation list .

title: Get conversation ID
description: Compute a deterministic conversation ID by chat target using the OpenIM Flutter SDK.
keywords: sdk flutter v4 sdk flutter conversation retrieving-conversations get-conversation-id
content: When your application only needs a conversation identifier for routing or pre queries, call this method to compute a standard conversationID instead of concatenating strings manually: Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | sourceID | String | Yes | Target chat ID. Supply the counterparty's userID for single chat, or groupID for group chat. | | sessionType | int | Yes | Conversation type. Pass ConversationType.single for single chat, or ConversationType.superGroup for group chat. | Code example final conversationID = await OpenIM.iMManager.conversationManager .getConversationIDBySessionType sourceID: targetUserID, sessionType: ConversationType.single, ; Return value A successful Future returns the calculated standard conversationID string. This method computes the deterministic ID; it does not return the full ConversationInfo entity or emit conversation listener events.

title: Get conversations by ID
description: Batch query conversations by conversationID using the OpenIM Flutter SDK.
keywords: sdk flutter v4 sdk flutter conversation retrieving-conversations get-conversations-by-id
content: Retrieve full conversation details for a known collection of conversation IDs: Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | conversationIDList | List | Yes | List of target conversation IDs to query. | Code example final conversations = await OpenIM.iMManager.conversationManager .getMultipleConversation conversationIDList: conversationIDs ; final byID = for final item in conversations item.conversationID: item, ; Return value A successful Future returns a list of matching ConversationInfo objects List . If certain IDs do not exist locally, they will be omitted from the result list; do not assume a 1:1 positional correspondence between the input arguments and output items. This query returns an immediate data snapshot and does not emit event notifications. For subsequent real time updates, see Retrieve conversation list /sdk/flutter/conversation/retrieving conversations/retrieve conversation list .

title: Retrieve conversation list
description: Retrieve the current user conversation list using pagination in the OpenIM Flutter SDK.
keywords: sdk flutter v4 sdk flutter conversation retrieving-conversations retrieve-conversation-list
content: The conversation list belongs to the currently signed in user. Each ConversationInfo record encapsulates the conversation identifier, unread count, latest message, pin state, and draft text. Read the conversation list with pagination starting at offset: 0 for the first page: Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | offset | int | Yes | Zero based pagination offset index; reset to 0 when refreshing the list. | | count | int | Yes | Number of conversation items to fetch per page. | Code example const pageSize = 50; Future loadConversationPage int offset async final page = await OpenIM.iMManager.conversationManager .getConversationListSplit offset: offset, count: pageSize ; mergeConversations page ; return page; Return value A successful Future returns a list of conversations for the requested page List . For subsequent pages, increment offset by the number of retrieved items. The client deduplicates and merges entries using conversationID as the unique key. If the returned count is less than count , the end of the list has been reached. When performing a pull to refresh, reset offset back to 0 . Maintain real time synchronization Paginated queries fetch snapshot state at invocation time and do not emit listener events. Synchronize real time state transitions through the application's centralized OnConversationListener : void handleNewConversations List conversations mergeConversations conversations ; void handleConversationsChanged List conversations mergeConversations conversations ; Both onNewConversation and onConversationChanged deliver updated List arrays. Merge them into the active list using conversationID as the primary key. For centralized listener configuration, see Events overview /sdk/flutter/events/overview events . Do not substitute joined group lists for the conversation list. A user may join a group before a conversation record is instantiated, or retain historical conversation entries after leaving a group.

title: Pin or unpin a conversation
description: Set the pin state of a specified conversation in the conversation list using the OpenIM Flutter SDK.
keywords: sdk flutter v4 sdk flutter conversation managing-conversations pin-conversation
content: Pin a specified conversation to the top of the conversation list, or unpin it. This pin status takes effect only for the currently signed in user: Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | conversationID | String | Yes | Target conversation ID. | | req | ConversationReq | Yes | Conversation modification request object. Set isPinned to true to pin the conversation, or false to unpin it. | Code example await OpenIM.iMManager.conversationManager.setConversation conversationID, ConversationReq isPinned: true , ; Return value A successful Future indicates that the pin state has been saved on the server. The client uses conversationID as the merge key to update isPinned on the local conversation model and reorder the conversation list. State changes after the call Multi device synchronization or arriving changes trigger conversation change events. For complete event listening, see Retrieve conversation list /sdk/flutter/conversation/retrieving conversations/retrieve conversation list .

title: Set conversation extension
description: Configure custom business extension strings for a specified conversation using the OpenIM Flutter SDK.
keywords: sdk flutter v4 sdk flutter conversation managing-conversations set-conversation-extension
content: Attach custom business extension strings to a specified conversation. The ex field is a plain text string that overwrites existing content on update; if storing structured data like JSON, read existing values first, merge attributes in the application layer, and then persist the updated string: Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | conversationID | String | Yes | Target conversation ID. | | req | ConversationReq | Yes | Conversation modification request object. Pass the serialized extension string in ex . | Code example await OpenIM.iMManager.conversationManager.setConversation conversationID, ConversationReq ex: mergedExtensionJSON , ; Return value A successful Future indicates that the extension string has been updated on the server. State changes after the call Multi device synchronization and arriving changes trigger conversation change events. The client updates ex on the local conversation model using conversationID as the merge key. For complete listener integration, see Retrieve conversation list /sdk/flutter/conversation/retrieving conversations/retrieve conversation list .

title: Set conversation draft
description: Save or clear unsent message text drafts for a conversation using the OpenIM Flutter SDK.
keywords: sdk flutter v4 sdk flutter conversation managing-conversations set-conversation-draft
content: When a user leaves a chat screen, switches channels, or pauses typing, persist the unsent draft text for that conversation. Maintain editor state locally while typing, debounce persistence calls, and commit the latest text immediately before navigating away. Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | conversationID | String | Yes | Target conversation ID. | | draftText | String | Yes | Draft text content.
