Pass an empty string '' to clear the draft. | Code example await OpenIM.iMManager.conversationManager.setConversationDraft conversationID: conversationID, draftText: editorValue, ; Clear the draft by supplying an empty string: await OpenIM.iMManager.conversationManager.setConversationDraft conversationID: conversationID, draftText: '', ; Return value A successful Future indicates that the draft has been written to the local conversation database. State changes after the call Multi device synchronization and arriving changes trigger conversation change events. The client uses conversationID as the merge key to update draftText and draftTextTime on the local conversation model. title: Conversation groups overview
description: Understand the data models, group types, and listener lifecycles of conversation groups in the OpenIM Flutter SDK.
keywords: sdk flutter v4 sdk flutter conversation managing-conversation-groups overview-conversation-groups
content: Conversation groups allow the currently signed in user to organize conversations into custom folders or tags. They manage relations between conversationID and folder categories; they do not create chat groups, modify group rosters, or change message recipients. Conversation group types | Enum Option | Value | Behavior | | | : | | | ConversationGroupType.custom | 0 | Standard user created custom group folder. | | ConversationGroupType.preset | 1 | Preset folder managed by SDK or server side rules. | | ConversationGroupType.all | 2 | Filter used when querying all folder types. | Use custom for user defined folders. Preset group behavior depends on your OpenIMServer deployment. Key fields in ConversationGroupInfo include conversationGroupID , name , serial , version , ex , conversationGroupType , hidden , unreadCount , and conversationIDs . All fields are nullable in Dart. Available operations Create a conversation group /sdk/flutter/conversation/managing conversation groups/create conversation group Query conversation groups /sdk/flutter/conversation/managing conversation groups/get conversation groups Query conversations in group /sdk/flutter/conversation/managing conversation groups/get conversation group info with conversations Query conversation group IDs by conversation ID /sdk/flutter/conversation/managing conversation groups/get conversation group ids by conversation id Update a conversation group /sdk/flutter/conversation/managing conversation groups/update conversation group Set conversation group order /sdk/flutter/conversation/managing conversation groups/set conversation group order Add conversations to groups /sdk/flutter/conversation/managing conversation groups/add conversations to groups Remove conversations from groups /sdk/flutter/conversation/managing conversation groups/remove conversations from groups Delete a conversation group /sdk/flutter/conversation/managing conversation groups/delete conversation group Listen for conversation group events Future registerConversationGroupListener return OpenIM.iMManager.conversationGroupManager .setConversationGroupListener OnConversationGroupListener onConversationGroupAdded: mergeConversationGroups, onConversationGroupChanged: mergeConversationGroups, onConversationGroupDeleted: removeConversationGroups, onConversationGroupMemberAdded: mergeConversationGroupMembers, onConversationGroupMemberDeleted: removeConversationGroupMembers, , ; | Callback | Event Payload | Handling Strategy | | | | | | onConversationGroupAdded | List | Append or merge newly created groups. | | onConversationGroupChanged | List | Update existing groups by conversationGroupID . | | onConversationGroupDeleted | List | Remove deleted groups from local state. | | onConversationGroupMemberAdded | List | Merge group , conversationIDs , and conversations . | | onConversationGroupMemberDeleted | List | Remove corresponding associations. | Fields in member events may be null; always validate group?.conversationGroupID and conversation IDs before mutating state. Merge groups idempotently using conversationGroupID , and correlate members using conversationID . ConversationGroupManager stores only one listener instance, and the SDK does not provide a remove method. Register this listener once in your application state layer; when switching accounts, stop forwarding events to inactive views and re register the complete listener for the new account. Future completion, listener dispatch, and query recalibration are three separate stages.

title: Groups overview
description: Understand group profiles, members, join applications, roles, and group events in the OpenIM Flutter SDK.
keywords: sdk flutter v4 sdk flutter group overview-group
content: In OpenIM, multi user chat channels use Groups to govern shared metadata, member rosters, and permissions. The groupID uniquely identifies a group and is required for sending group messages, querying group details, managing member rosters, and handling join applications. In the current user's conversation list, the chat channel is identified and managed by conversationID ; do not conflate the two identifiers. Core data structures | Structure | Purpose | | | | | GroupInfo | Group name, avatar, announcement, owner, verification mode, member count, and extensions. | | GroupMembersInfo | A member's in group nickname, role, mute status, and join details. | | GroupApplicationInfo | Join application records and resolution statuses. | Group roles are defined in GroupRoleLevel : Ordinary members are 20 , administrators are 60 , and group owners are 100 . UI views can toggle actions based on these levels, but final authorization is verified by OpenIMServer. Group metadata and lifecycle Create a group /sdk/flutter/group/create group Update group profile /sdk/flutter/group/update group profile Set group announcement /sdk/flutter/group/set group announcement Set group join verification /sdk/flutter/group/set group join verification Set group member profile access /sdk/flutter/group/set group member profile access Set group member friend permission /sdk/flutter/group/set group member friend permission Set group extension /sdk/flutter/group/set group extension Join a group /sdk/flutter/group/join group Quit a group /sdk/flutter/group/quit group Dismiss a group /sdk/flutter/group/dismiss group Get specified groups info /sdk/flutter/group/retrieving groups/get specified groups info Group members and applications Group applications overview /sdk/flutter/group/group applications/overview group applications Retrieving group members overview /sdk/flutter/group/retrieving group members/overview retrieving group members Invite users to group /sdk/flutter/group/managing group members/invite user to group Group moderation Change group mute /sdk/flutter/group/change group mute Change group member mute /sdk/flutter/group/managing group members/change group member mute State synchronization Group related notifications encompass joining groups, leaving groups, group profile updates, and group dissolutions. Register callbacks centrally within the application's single OnGroupListener . Use groupID as the merge key to update local group stores. For member events, see Retrieving group members overview /sdk/flutter/group/retrieving group members/overview retrieving group members ; for application events, see Group applications overview /sdk/flutter/group/group applications/overview group applications . Future completion, event delivery, and query recalibration are distinct operational phases. The OpenIM Flutter SDK focuses on in group metadata, member rosters, and permissions. Public group discovery and large scale group capacity governance are coordinated between your business backend and OpenIMServer.

Merge updates idempotently using groupID:userID . Because events may be triggered by other users or background tasks, do not treat them as direct responses to a specific local method call. title: Message overview
description: Understand the Message model, message types, and message lifecycle in the OpenIM Flutter SDK.
keywords: sdk flutter v4 sdk flutter message overview-message
content: The OpenIM Flutter SDK organizes messaging capabilities around the Message model. Create ordinary messages or media messages backed by local paths or bytes using the corresponding factory method, then deliver them with Send a message /sdk/flutter/message/sending messages/send message . When media files have already been uploaded by your application server and a URL is available, construct the message using the corresponding URL based creation method and deliver it with Send a message without OSS /sdk/flutter/message/sending messages/send message not oss . Both delivery paths support one to one and group chats. Real time updates, recalls, deletions, read receipts, upload progress, and conversation shifts synchronize to application state via their respective listeners. The Flutter Message model does not include a conversationID field. The conversationID used for history retrieval, search, and conversation management is derived from the active conversation context. When a global listener receives a cross conversation message, determine the target from sessionType , groupID , sendID , recvID , and the current user ID, then obtain the conversation ID using the conversation ID helper. Message interfaces typically manage the following key identifiers: | Identifier | Purpose | | | | | clientMsgID | Stable client side message ID used for deduplication, state updates, queries, and pagination cursors. Never use an empty value as a merge key. | | conversationID | Unique ID of the conversation record used to load history, clear unread counts, and search. Obtained from the conversation context, not a field on Message . | | recvID | Recipient user ID for one to one messages. Omitted when sending group messages. | | groupID | Target group ID for group messages. Omitted when sending one to one messages. | Message types Construct each type of content with its dedicated factory method before sending. The sending layer provides a unified interface: pass the resulting Message instance to either Send a message /sdk/flutter/message/sending messages/send message or Send a message without OSS /sdk/flutter/message/sending messages/send message not oss . Message type comparison | Content type | Recommended guide | Content element | | | | | | Plain text | Create a text message /sdk/flutter/message/creating messages/create text message | textElem | | @ mention | Create an @ mention message /sdk/flutter/message/creating messages/create text at message | atTextElem | | Image | Create an image message /sdk/flutter/message/creating messages/create image message , Create an image message from full path /sdk/flutter/message/creating messages/create image message from full path , Create an image message by URL /sdk/flutter/message/creating messages/create image message by url | pictureElem | | Audio | Create an audio message /sdk/flutter/message/creating messages/create sound message , Create an audio message from full path /sdk/flutter/message/creating messages/create sound message from full path , Create an audio message by URL /sdk/flutter/message/creating messages/create sound message by url | soundElem | | Video | Create a video message /sdk/flutter/message/creating messages/create video message , Create a video message from full path /sdk/flutter/message/creating messages/create video message from full path , Create a video message by URL /sdk/flutter/message/creating messages/create video message by url | videoElem | | File | Create a file message /sdk/flutter/message/creating messages/create file message , Create a file message from full path /sdk/flutter/message/creating messages/create file message from full path , Create a file message by URL /sdk/flutter/message/creating messages/create file message by url | fileElem | | Custom | Create a custom message /sdk/flutter/message/creating messages/create custom message | customElem | | Quotes, merges, locations, cards, and faces | Create a quote message /sdk/flutter/message/creating messages/create quote message , Create a merged message /sdk/flutter/message/creating messages/create merger message , Create a location message /sdk/flutter/message/creating messages/create location message , Create a card message /sdk/flutter/message/creating messages/create card message , Create a face message /sdk/flutter/message/creating messages/create face message | quoteElem , mergeElem , locationElem , cardElem , faceElem | Media messages created from local paths or bytes are typically uploaded by the SDK and dispatched with Send a message /sdk/flutter/message/sending messages/send message . When media files have already been uploaded by external services and URLs are available, create the message using URL based factory methods and invoke Send a message without OSS /sdk/flutter/message/sending messages/send message not oss to bypass SDK upload pipelines. Attach business metadata intended for all recipients to message content or server side extension fields. Store client specific UI states intended only for the local device in localEx . Common Message fields | Field | Description | | | | | clientMsgID | Stable client side identifier used for delivery status tracking, queries, and event reconciliation. | | serverMsgID | Unique server assigned message identifier confirmed after receipt. | | sendID / recvID / groupID | Sender user ID, recipient user ID in direct chats, and destination group ID in group chats. | | sessionType | Conversation type: single or group chat; used to determine conversation routing. | | contentType | Content type identifier, evaluated against integer constants in MessageType . | | status | Message delivery status. | | sendTime / createTime | Server timestamp when sent and local timestamp when created. | | isRead | Read receipt state for the message. | | textElem , pictureElem , soundElem , videoElem , fileElem | Payload objects for standard media content types. | | atTextElem , quoteElem , mergeElem , customElem | Payload objects for mentions, quotes, merged chats, and custom data. | | offlinePush | Push notification configuration for the message. | | ex / localEx | Server synchronized extension and device local extension. | In the Dart SDK model, clientMsgID , sendID , recvID , groupID , and sessionType are nullable. Verify required fields before indexing records; do not use bang operators on untrusted message payloads. Message lifecycle and conversation routing 1. Initialize a local Message instance using dedicated factory methods. Constructing a message does not invoke network requests or trigger new message callbacks. 2. Call Send a message /sdk/flutter/message/sending messages/send message for standard delivery, or call Send a message without OSS /sdk/flutter/message/sending messages/send message not oss for pre uploaded media. 3. Upon Future resolution, update the sender UI using the returned Message object. Other participants receive the message via their message listeners. 4. Historical loading, local search, and ID queries return local database snapshots without triggering new message callbacks. When a message is sent or received within an active conversation with a known conversationID , merge the record directly into that conversation. For global receive events lacking context, resolve sourceID : for group conversations, use groupID ; for direct conversations, compare sendID with the current user ID to select the counterparty ID from recvID or sendID . Then provide sourceID and sessionType to the conversation ID helper. Skip messages with incomplete routing identifiers. Never substitute list indices, display names, or array lengths for stable conversation and message keys. Navigation by task Send messages Construct a message object, then dispatch it to a user or group. Set userID for direct messages or groupID for group messages, leaving the alternative target empty. When uploading media through the SDK, use path based or byte based creation methods alongside Send a message /sdk/flutter/message/sending messages/send message . When media is pre uploaded, use URL based creation methods with Send a message without OSS /sdk/flutter/message/sending messages/send message not oss . Both flows return the updated Message through a Future , which must be merged by clientMsgID . For parameter descriptions and delivery boundaries, see Send a message /sdk/flutter/message/sending messages/send message . Receive messages Handle standard real time messages, offline synchronized messages, and online only messages through onRecvNewMessage , onRecvOfflineNewMessage , and onRecvOnlineOnlyMessage . Global listeners must resolve the message's conversation first, then merge items idempotently using conversationID:clientMsgID . Online only messages are not persisted to local database storage. For callback parameters and error handling, see Receive messages /sdk/flutter/message/receiving messages/receive messages . Retrieve messages Retrieve historical messages in paginated batches by conversationID . Omit startMsg on the initial request, then pass the boundary message as the cursor for subsequent pages. Historical results and real time listeners may deliver identical records; deduplicate using clientMsgID . See Load older messages /sdk/flutter/message/retrieving messages/load older messages to paginate message history, and Locate messages by ID /sdk/flutter/message/retrieving messages/locate messages by id to fetch specific records. Search messages Search locally synchronized messages using keywords and filter parameters. When searching within a group, supply the group's conversationID rather than its groupID . The keywordListMatchType and senderUserIDList fields are currently reserved and do not filter local search results. See Search messages /sdk/flutter/message/searching messages/search messages for complete usage. Manage messages Manage existing messages by forwarding, merging, deleting, revoking, modifying, pinning, or inserting local placeholders, or send typing indicators. Revoke, delete, and modify events should update matching records by conversationID:clientMsgID . Replace pinned message lists by conversationID , then deduplicate by clientMsgID . See Create a forward message /sdk/flutter/message/creating messages/create forward message , Create a merger message /sdk/flutter/message/creating messages/create merger message , Delete saved messages /sdk/flutter/message/managing messages/delete saved message , Revoke a message /sdk/flutter/message/managing messages/revoke a message , Modify a message /sdk/flutter/message/managing messages/modify a message , Pin or unpin a message /sdk/flutter/message/managing messages/set message pinned , Insert a local single chat message /sdk/flutter/message/managing messages/insert local single message , Clear all local messages /sdk/flutter/message/managing messages/clear all local messages , and Update typing status /sdk/flutter/message/composing messages/update typing status . Mark messages as read Clear conversation unread counts using the mark as read API. The Flutter SDK receives single chat read receipts, but does not provide group member read receipt reporting, group read/unread queries, or group receipt listeners. A conversation's unread counter does not reflect which group members have read a message. For single chat read receipt flows, see Mark conversation as read /sdk/flutter/conversation/managing conversations/mark conversation read . Mention other users Create group @ messages using Create an @ mention message /sdk/flutter/message/creating messages/create text at message , then send them to the group via Send a message /sdk/flutter/message/sending messages/send message . Target users using their stable userID . Recipients parse mentions from atTextElem and render mention notifications using the conversation's groupAtType . Retrieve unread counts Conversation lists, total unread counts, and mention alerts are managed through conversation APIs and OnConversationListener . Merge changes by conversati

title: Create a text message
description: Create a text message with the OpenIM Flutter SDK.

content: Construct a plain text message object ready for delivery: Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | text | String | Yes | Body content of the text message. Once created, pass the Message instance to Send a message /sdk/flutter/message/sending messages/send message to deliver it to a direct or group conversation.

title: Receive messages
description: Handle standard real-time, offline-synchronized, and online-only message events in the OpenIM Flutter SDK.
keywords: sdk flutter v4 sdk flutter message receiving-messages receive-messages
content: Standard real time messages, offline messages synchronized upon login, and online only messages are received through onRecvNewMessage , onRecvOfflineNewMessage , and onRecvOnlineOnlyMessage callbacks respectively. Each Flutter callback delivers a single Message instance rather than an array of messages. Chat screens typically handle initial history snapshots upon opening, real time message arrivals, offline sync batches following reconnection, and transient online only notifications. Historical queries establish the base snapshot, while listeners apply incremental updates. Never treat listener delivery as the completion callback for a query or mark as read request. Message types Choose a renderer based on contentType and non null element payloads: textElem , atTextElem , and customElem represent text, mentions, and custom payloads; pictureElem , soundElem , videoElem , and fileElem contain download URLs, byte sizes, file names, durations, or thumbnail previews, requiring no re upload on the receiver. Render unsupported message placeholders for unrecognized types, and parse custom messages using your application's agreed data schema. If your product requires sending multiple files together, send consecutive file messages or encapsulate the file list in a single custom message. Regardless of presentation grouping, the application state layer must track each item by its stable clientMsgID . Parameters and fields Flutter's Message model does not contain a conversationID property. Global listeners must resolve conversation routing from message fields first, then request the conversation ID from the SDK. The following table details fields commonly used for routing, display, and state merging all declared nullable except exMap : | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | clientMsgID | String? | Yes | Client assigned unique ID. When non empty, serves as the stable merge key. | | serverMsgID | String? | No | Server assigned message ID. Does not replace clientMsgID for local merging. | | sessionType | int? | Yes | Conversation type from ConversationType , determining single or group routing. | | sendID | String? | Yes | Sender user ID. Combined with the current user ID to identify counterparties. | | recvID | String? | No | Recipient user ID, used to identify the peer when the current user is the sender. | | groupID | String? | No | Destination group ID in group chats. | | contentType | int? | Yes | Content type constant from MessageType , determining the active content element. | | sendTime | int? | No | Unix timestamp in milliseconds when sent, used for display ordering. | | status | int? | No | Delivery status from MessageStatus . | | isRead | bool? | No | Read status currently tracked by the SDK. | Text, image, audio, video, file, mention, custom, quote, and merged payloads reside in their corresponding nullable element properties. Practice defensive rendering by verifying both contentType and the element payload. If an expected element is missing, render a fallback placeholder instead of force unwrapping. Code example Future resolveMessageConversationID Message message, String currentUserID, async final sessionType = message.sessionType; if sessionType == null return null; final String? sourceID; if sessionType == ConversationType.single sourceID = message.sendID == currentUserID ? message.recvID : message.sendID; else sourceID = message.groupID; if sourceID == null || sourceID.isEmpty return null; final value = await OpenIM.iMManager.conversationManager .getConversationIDBySessionType sourceID: sourceID, sessionType: sessionType, ; final conversationID = value?.toString ; return conversationID == null || conversationID.isEmpty ? null : conversationID; Future mergeReceivedMessage Message message async final clientMsgID = message.clientMsgID; if clientMsgID == null || clientMsgID.isEmpty return; final conversationID = await resolveMessageConversationID message, currentUserID ; if conversationID == null return; upsertMessage conversationID, clientMsgID, message ; Future handleNewMessage Message message = mergeReceivedMessage message ; Future handleOfflineMessage Message message = mergeReceivedMessage message ; Future handleOnlineOnlyMessage Message message async final conversationID = await resolveMessageConversationID message, currentUserID ; if conversationID == null return; showEphemeralMessage conversationID, message ; State changes after the call Register these handlers within the application's single OnAdvancedMsgListener . For centralized listener setup, see Events overview /sdk/flutter/events/overview events . Attach the listener once during SDK initialization and authentication, dispatching received messages to active conversation stores via an application level event bus. Avoid reattaching listeners whenever opening chat screens, as subsequent registrations overwrite prior callbacks. Merge regular and offline messages idempotently using the resolved composite key conversationID:clientMsgID to prevent duplicate insertions across history pagination and sync intervals. If a specific chat view is active, compare the resolved conversation ID against the active conversation; route messages belonging to other chats to their background stores. Messages received via onRecvOnlineOnlyMessage sent with isOnlineOnly: true are not persisted to local databases and should not be stored as replayable history. Resolve the conversation routing to avoid displaying transient notifications from other conversations in the active screen. History snapshots and event increments When opening a conversation for the first time, load an initial history snapshot using the screen's conversationID . When scrolling upwards, use the earliest message as the boundary cursor. Because historical queries and event listeners may deliver identical records, deduplicate both using clientMsgID . For pagination details, see Load older messages /sdk/flutter/message/retrieving messages/load older messages . After the user opens and views the chat, call markConversationMessageAsRead conversationID: conversationID to clear conversation unread counts. This action is separate from group member read receipts. Future completion indicates that the mark as read request completed, but does not guarantee that conversation list events have reached all clients. Continue updating conversation unread counters and badge counts via conversation events, re querying when state reconciliation is needed. Pass null for the first page; pass the earliest loaded message for subsequent pages. | | count | int | Yes | Number of messages to retrieve in this batch. | | viewType | int? | No | History view type, defaulting to normal history GetHistoryViewType.history . | Code example final page = await OpenIM.iMManager.messageManager .getAdvancedHistoryMessageList conversationID: conversationID, startMsg: oldestMessage, count: 30, viewType: GetHistoryViewType.history, ; prependMessages page.messageList ?? const ; Return value Returns a Future resolving to an advanced message pagination object AdvancedMessage . description: Use the Flutter SDK to page from a message anchor toward newer message history.
keywords: sdk flutter v4 sdk flutter message retrieving-messages load-newer-messages
content: Page forward from a specific message anchor such as after searching or jumping to a quoted message toward newer message history: Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | conversationID | String | Yes | Target conversation ID. | | startMsg | Message? | No | Starting anchor message for reverse pagination. Loads messages created after this anchor. | | count | int | Yes | Number of messages to retrieve in this batch. | | viewType | int? | No | History view type, defaulting to normal history GetHistoryViewType.history . | Code example final page = await OpenIM.iMManager.messageManager .getAdvancedHistoryMessageListReverse conversationID: conversationID, startMsg: anchorMessage, count: 30, viewType: GetHistoryViewType.history, ; Avoid mixing forward and reverse cursor directions on the same scrolling boundary to prevent timeline rendering discontinuities. Return value Returns a Future resolving to an advanced message pagination object AdvancedMessage . Its messageList contains messages retrieved forward toward the newest timestamp. State changes after the call This query retrieves a point in time snapshot and does not trigger new message event callbacks. When merging into your UI list, constrain updates to the target conversationID and deduplicate records strictly by non empty clientMsgID . To load older historical messages while scrolling upward, see Load older messages /sdk/flutter/message/retrieving messages/load older messages .

title: Locate messages by ID
description: Locate one or more messages by conversationID and clientMsgID.
keywords: sdk flutter v4 sdk flutter message retrieving-messages locate-messages-by-id
content: When navigating to a chat screen from search results, quoted replies, or system notifications, retrieve locally synchronized message records using conversationID and clientMsgID : Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | conversationID | String | Yes | ID of the conversation containing the target messages. | | clientMsgIDList | List | Yes | List of client message IDs to locate. Pass a single element when locating one message. | Code example final result = await OpenIM.iMManager.messageManager.findMessageList searchParams: SearchParams conversationID: conversationID, clientMsgIDList: clientMsgID , , , ; final items = result.findResultItems ?? const ; final messages = items.isEmpty ? const : items.first.messageList ?? const ; final target = messages.isEmpty ? null : messages.first; Upon Future completion, matched messages are located in the messageList of SearchResult.findResultItems . If records have not synchronized locally, were deleted, or the IDs do not exist, the list may be empty; verify elements before accessing. clientMsgID is the stable primary key managed on the client side. Sending, receiving, searching, and history retrieval must all use it as the merge key, rather than list indices or display timestamps. Load surrounding messages After locating the target message, if you need to restore full conversation context before and after it, use the target message as a cursor. Call Load older message history /sdk/flutter/message/retrieving messages/load older messages to fetch earlier messages, and call Load newer message history /sdk/flutter/message/retrieving messages/load newer messages Enterprise to fetch later messages, assembling the full context using conversationID:clientMsgID : final older = await OpenIM.iMManager.messageManager .getAdvancedHistoryMessageList conversationID: conversationID, startMsg: target, count: 20, ; final newer = await OpenIM.iMManager.messageManager .getAdvancedHistoryMessageListReverse conversationID: conversationID, startMsg: target, count: 20, ; When combining older messages, the target, and newer messages, discard nullable or empty clientMsgID values and deduplicate strictly by conversationID:clientMsgID . Never rely on array indices to identify the target message. Locate requests can return empty results if local storage is not yet synchronized, or if the message was deleted or revoked. Retry the query after synchronization completes. Revocation and deletion updates are handled by global message listeners. Retrieve the latest group message If you only need to display the latest message in a group for example, in a chat list preview or group entry tile , retrieve the corresponding ConversationInfo : final conversation = await OpenIM.iMManager.conversationManager .getOneConversation sourceID: groupID, sessionType: ConversationType.superGroup, ; renderConversationPreview conversationID: conversation.conversationID, latestMessage: conversation.latestMsg, unreadCount: conversation.unreadCount, ; ConversationInfo.latestMsg is a nullable Message and does not require manual JSON parsing. When opening its surrounding context, verify that latestMsg and its clientMsgID are valid, then use the current conversationID to load messages in both directions. Return value Message queries, surrounding history pagination, and conversation lookups are read only operations. Future completion returns point in time data snapshots and does not trigger event callbacks. The UI can render the returned results directly. Subsequent new arrivals, revocations, and deletions must be handled through global listeners, merging updates idempotently using the composite key conversationID:clientMsgID . Related guides Load older message history /sdk/flutter/message/retrieving messages/load older messages Load newer message history /sdk/flutter/message/retrieving messages/load newer messages Search messages /sdk/flutter/message/searching messages/search messages Receive messages /sdk/flutter/message/receiving messages/receive messages

title: Search messages
description: Search locally synchronized messages by keyword and conversation criteria with the Flutter SDK.
keywords: sdk flutter v4 sdk flutter message searching-messages search-messages
content: Search through the locally synchronized message database on the current client by keywords, conversation, message types, and time ranges. When searching within a group chat, supply the corresponding conversationID rather than the groupID used during message sending. If you only hold a target user ID or group ID, first call Generate conversation ID /sdk/flutter/conversation/retrieving conversations/get conversation id to obtain the conversation ID. To perform a global search across all local conversations, pass null for conversationID . The search scope is limited to messages already synchronized to the SDK's local database. Global full text search across cloud history is an enterprise server capability; a backend search service can return matching conversation and message IDs for client navigation. Basic keyword search The keywordList parameter accepts a list of strings, but the search engine currently matches against the first non empty keyword. Trim whitespace and filter empty values before submitting: final keyword = input.trim ; if keyword.isNotEmpty final result = await OpenIM.iMManager.messageManager.searchLocalMessages conversationID: conversationID, keywordList: keyword , messageTypeList: MessageType.text, MessageType.atText , pageIndex: 1, count: 20, ; renderSearchResult result ; Advanced filtered search The search API also supports compound filtering by message type and time window: final result = await OpenIM.iMManager.messageManager.searchLocalMessages conversationID: conversationID, keywordList: 'release' , messageTypeList: MessageType.text , searchTimePosition: searchTimePosition, searchTimePeriod: searchTimePeriod, pageIndex: 1, count: 20, ; To include images, files, or custom messages in the search, add their corresponding MessageType integer constants to messageTypeList . Passing an empty list removes message type restrictions. Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | conversationID | String? | No | ID of the specific conversation to search. Pass null to search across all local conversations. | | keywordList | List | No | List of search keywords. The current implementation matches against the first non empty keyword. | | keywordListMatchType | int | No | Matching strategy for multiple keywords; defaults to 0 . | | senderUserIDList | List | No | Sender filter list; defaults to an empty list. | | messageTypeList | List | No | Filter list of MessageType integer constants such as MessageType.text . An empty list matches all types. | | searchTimePosition | int | No | Search start timestamp in seconds; defaults to 0 starts from the current time . | | searchTimePeriod | int | No | Number of seconds to search backward from searchTimePosition ; defaults to 0 unlimited . | | pageIndex | int | No | One based page number; defaults to 1 . | | count | int | No | Number of matching items per page; defaults to 40 . | Return value Returns a Future resolving to a search result object SearchResult . All fields may be nullable: | Field | Type | Description | | | | | | totalCount | int? | Total number of messages matching the search criteria. | | searchResultItems | List ? | Search results grouped by conversation. | | findResultItems | List ? | Exact match items; this method primarily populates searchResultItems . | Each SearchResultItems item aggregates matching messages for one conversation: | Field | Type | Description | | | | | | conversationID | String? | ID of the conversation containing matched messages. | | conversationType | int? | Conversation type. | | showName | String? | Display name of the conversation. | | faceURL | String? | Avatar URL of the conversation. | | messageCount | int? | Total number of matched messages in this conversation. | | messageList | List ? | Matched messages retrieved for the current page. | When paginating through results, keep all search filters identical and increment only pageIndex . When search keywords or filters change, clear previous results and reset pageIndex to 1 . Deduplicate search items using conversationID and non empty clientMsgID values. State changes after the call Local search queries retrieve a static snapshot of database records and do not trigger event callbacks. Messages matching search results may subsequently be revoked, deleted, or supplemented by background sync while the search view is open. Update result states using the centralized listeners described in Receive messages /sdk/flutter/message/receiving messages/receive messages , Delete saved messages /sdk/flutter/message/managing messages/delete saved message , and Revoke a message /sdk/flutter/message/managing messages/revoke a message . Avoid registering redundant message listeners in search components. To navigate to a matched message in chat, use the item's conversationID and clientMsgID . To load surrounding conversation context, follow Locate messages by ID /sdk/flutter/message/retrieving messages/locate messages by id to fetch older and newer records. Related guides Locate messages by ID /sdk/flutter/message/retrieving messages/locate messages by id Load older message history /sdk/flutter/message/retrieving messages/load older messages Receive messages /sdk/flutter/message/receiving messages/receive messages

title: Report typing status
description: Use the Flutter SDK to report the current user's typing status.
keywords: sdk flutter v4 sdk flutter message composing-messages update-typing-status
content: Report typing indicators when a user focuses on the input field or starts typing, and clear the state when losing focus or stopping input: Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | conversationID | String | Yes | Target conversation ID. | | focus | bool | Yes | Typing state: true indicates active typing; false indicates stopped typing or lost focus. | Code example await OpenIM.iMManager.conversationManager.changeInputStates conversationID: conversationID, focus: true, ; We recommend throttling and debouncing keystrokes on the client to avoid sending excessive network requests. Pass false promptly when sending a message, switching conversations, or blurring the input field. Return value Future completion indicates that the server accepted the typing status report, but does not guarantee the peer client received or rendered it. Typing status is transient signaling: it does not persist to database storage and does not create draft records. State changes after the call Typing notifications arrive via the onInputStatusChanged callback in OnConversationListener . When the counterparty's typing state updates, merge and replace the user's active platform array platformIDs keyed by conversationID:userID . For global listener registration and lifecycle management, see Events overview /sdk/flutter/events/overview events .

title: Retrieve typing status
description: Use the Flutter SDK to retrieve a member's current typing status.
keywords: sdk flutter v4 sdk flutter message composing-messages get-typing-status
content: Query whether a specific member in a conversation is currently in a "typing" state: Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | conversationID | String | Yes | Target conversation ID. | | userID | String | Yes | Target user ID to query. | Code example final platformIDs = await OpenIM.iMManager.conversationManager.getInputStates conversationID, otherUserID, ; setTyping otherUserID, platformIDs?.isNotEmpty == true ; Return value Returns a Future resolving to a nullable platform ID list List ? . A non empty list contains the platform IDs on which the user is actively typing. Returns null or an empty list if the user is not currently typing. State changes after the call This query returns a point in time snapshot and does not trigger event callbacks. In group chats, avoid polling all members frequently. You can query the counterparty when opening the chat screen or recovering from network reconnection; for continuous real time typing indicators, see the event listener in Update typing status /sdk/flutter/message/composing messages/update typing status .

title: Check speech recognition support
description: Use the Flutter SDK to check whether the current deployment supports speech recognition.
keywords: sdk flutter v4 sdk flutter message composing-messages check-speech-to-text
content: Check whether the current server deployment and environment support speech to text capabilities. This method takes no parameters and is ideal for verifying feature availability before displaying a speech transcription entry point in the UI: Code example try await OpenIM.iMManager.messageManager.speechToTextCapabilities ; setTranscriptionAvailable true ; catch error setTranscriptionAvailable false ; Return value Returns a Future . Success indicates that the server has speech recognition enabled. If the server does not support or has not enabled speech transcription, the call throws an error. This method does not return configuration details such as audio sample rate or duration limits. To perform speech to text transcription, see Transcribe audio /sdk/flutter/message/composing messages/transcribe audio . State changes after the call This capability check queries server feature availability and does not alter message state or trigger event notifications.

title: Transcribe audio
description: Use the Flutter SDK to transcribe text from a local audio file.
keywords: sdk flutter v4 sdk flutter message composing-messages transcribe-audio
content: Upload a local audio file to the speech recognition service and retrieve the transcribed text: Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | filename | String | Yes | Absolute local filesystem path to the audio file readable on the current device. | Code example final result = await OpenIM.iMManager.messageManager.speechToText filename: soundElem.soundPath , ; final transcript = result.text ?? ''; Return value Returns a Future resolving to a speech to text response SpeechToTextResp . Retrieve the transcribed string via its text field. State changes after the call This method only executes speech recognition; it does not modify the message object or trigger event callbacks. If a voice message only has a remote URL, download it to local application storage before transcribing. Before invoking transcription, verify service availability using Check speech recognition support /sdk/flutter/message/composing messages/check speech to text . To store the transcribed text in the local message, see Save a local transcript /sdk/flutter/message/composing messages/save local transcript .

title: Save a local transcript
description: Use the Flutter SDK to save a transcript to an audio message on the current device.
keywords: sdk flutter v4 sdk flutter message composing-messages save-local-transcript
content: Save transcribed audio text into a local voice message's soundElem.text field, ensuring the transcription remains visible when reopening the conversation. Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | conversationID | String | Yes | ID of the conversation containing the message. | | clientMsgID | String | Yes | Target client message ID. | | message | Message | Yes | The complete message object updated with the transcribed text. | Code example message.soundElem .text = SoundText text: transcript, translate: previousText?.translate ; await OpenIM.iMManager.messageManager.setMessageLocalContent conversationID: conversationID, clientMsgID: message.clientMsgID , message: message, ; Return value Future completion indicates that the transcription has been saved to the current device's local database. Update the local UI state using the client message identifier clientMsgID . State changes after the call This operation modifies only the local storage on the current device. It is not uploaded to the server, does not trigger message event notifications, and does not synchronize to remote devices. For the preceding speech recognition step, see Transcribe audio /sdk/flutter/message/composing messages/transcribe audio .

title: Delete a local message
description: Use the Flutter SDK to delete one message from the current device only.
keywords: sdk flutter v4 sdk flutter message managing-messages delete-local-message
content: Delete a single specified message from the local database on the current device only: Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | conversationID | String | Yes | ID of the conversation containing the message. | | clientMsgID | String | Yes | Target client message ID to delete. | Code example await OpenIM.iMManager.messageManager.deleteMessageFromLocalStorage conversationID: conversationID, clientMsgID: clientMsgID, ; Return value Future completion indicates that the target message has been removed from the current device's local database. Remove the record from your local state and UI list using the composite key conversationID:clientMsgID . State changes after the call This operation modifies only the local storage on the current device. It does not delete the server side roaming record, does not notify other devices or chat participants, and does not constitute a message recall. If you need to delete a message from both local storage and the server with cross device synchronization, see Delete saved messages /sdk/flutter/message/managing messages/delete saved message ; to recall a message and display a placeholder, see Revoke a message /sdk/flutter/message/managing messages/revoke a message .

title: Delete a message
description: Use the Flutter SDK to delete one message from a conversation for the current account.
keywords: sdk flutter v4 sdk flutter message managing-messages delete-saved-message
content: Delete a single historical message for the current account from both the local database and the server: Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | conversationID | String | Yes | ID of the conversation containing the message. | | clientMsgID | String | Yes | Target client message ID to delete. | Code example await OpenIM.iMManager.messageManager.deleteMessageFromLocalAndSvr conversationID: conversationID, clientMsgID: clientMsgID, ; Return value Future completion indicates that the message has been deleted from both the server and local storage for the current account. Remove the message from the UI list immediately using the composite key conversationID:clientMsgID . This operation removes message history only for the current user across logged in sessions; it does not delete copies stored on other conversation members' devices and does not constitute a message recall. State changes after the call Message deletion events are delivered through the onMsgDeleted callback in OnAdvancedMsgListener . When the current user deletes a message from another client, this callback notifies the active device. Because Flutter's Message model does not contain a conversationID property, resolve the conversation routing first, then remove the message idempotently using conversationID:clientMsgID . For global listener registration, see Events overview /sdk/flutter/events/overview events . To revoke a message for all members with a tombstone prompt, see Revoke a message /sdk/flutter/message/managing messages/revoke a message .

title: Revoke a message
description: Revoke a sent message and handle revocation notifications received by other clients.
keywords: sdk flutter v4 sdk flutter message managing-messages revoke-a-message
content: Revoking a message causes all conversation members to display the original message in a revoked state. OpenIM Server validates the message status, operator permissions, and the allowed revocation time window. If you only need to remove a message from the current account's view, use Delete saved messages /sdk/flutter/message/managing messages/delete saved message instead of revoking it. To change the content of an existing message, use Modify a message /sdk/flutter/message/managing messages/modify a message . Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | conversationID | String | Yes | ID of the conversation containing the message. Flutter's Message model does not contain this field. | | clientMsgID | String | Yes | Target client message ID to revoke. | Code example final clientMsgID = message.clientMsgID; if clientMsgID == null || clientMsgID.isEmpty throw StateError 'Message has no clientMsgID' ; await OpenIM.iMManager.messageManager.revokeMessage conversationID: conversationID, clientMsgID: clientMsgID, ; Flutter's Message model does not contain a conversationID field; the call site must supply the conversationID maintained by the current conversation context. If you only hold a message object from an event, resolve the route as shown in Receive messages /sdk/flutter/message/receiving messages/receive messages and obtain the conversation ID using the conversation ID helper. Return value Future completion indicates that the server has processed the revocation request. The active client should immediately update the matching message bubble in place to a "revoked" state using the composite key conversationID:clientMsgID . Future completion does not guarantee that event notifications have arrived at all clients. If server side validation indicates that the message does not exist or the revocation time limit has expired, the call throws an error. Show the error to the user and keep the original message visible; do not mark the message as revoked locally when the request fails. State changes after the call Message revocation events are handled through the onNewRecvMessageRevoked callback in OnAdvancedMsgListener . The callback provides a RevokedInfo payload. Update the local message bubble in place using the composite key conversationID:clientMsgID : void handleMessageRevoked RevokedInfo info final clientMsgID = info.clientMsgID; if clientMsgID == null || clientMsgID.isEmpty return; final conversationID = findConversationIDByClientMsgID clientMsgID ; if conversationID == null return; markMessageRevoked conversationID, clientMsgID, info ; We recommend transforming the revoked message into an in place tombstone notice such as "You revoked a message" or "A message was revoked" rather than deleting the item entirely from the UI list. This maintains chat timeline continuity and prevents UI layout jumps when subsequently fetching historical message batches. Register this handler in the application's single OnAdvancedMsgListener ; for global configuration, see Events overview /sdk/flutter/events/overview events . Related guides Delete saved messages /sdk/flutter/message/managing messages/delete saved message Modify a message /sdk/flutter/message/managing messages/modify a message Send a message /sdk/flutter/message/sending messages/send message Locate messages by ID /sdk/flutter/message/retrieving messages/locate messages by id Receive messages /sdk/flutter/message/receiving messages/receive messages

title: Modify a message
description: Use the OpenIM Flutter SDK to modify the content of a sent message.
keywords: sdk flutter v4 sdk flutter message managing-messages modify-a-message
content: Modify the content of a previously sent message in a conversation. Unlike Delete saved messages /sdk/flutter/message/managing messages/delete saved message , which affects whether the message remains visible to the current account, and Revoke a message /sdk/flutter/message/managing messages/revoke a message , which displays a revocation notice to all members, modifying a message replaces its body content and synchronizes updates to all conversation members. Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | conversationID | String | Yes | ID of the conversation containing the message. Flutter's Message model does not contain this field. | | message | Message | Yes | The complete modified message object; must preserve the original clientMsgID and routing fields. | Code example final clientMsgID = message.clientMsgID; final textElem = message.textElem; if clientMsgID == null || clientMsgID.isEmpty || textElem == null throw StateError 'Message cannot be edited' ; final previousText = textElem.content; textElem.content = editedText; try await OpenIM.iMManager.messageManager.modifyMessage conversationID: conversationID, message: message, ; replaceMessage conversationID, clientMsgID, message ; catch textElem.content = previousText; rethrow; This method is not a partial update. Start with the current complete message object, modify only the target element, and preserve clientMsgID , routing identifiers, sender, timestamps, and custom attributes. OpenIM Server validates the permitted sender, time window, and message types. If modification fails, revert local content or re query the message; do not retain uncommitted edits in local memory. Return value Returns a Future . Success indicates that the server accepted and persisted the message modification request. The local client may preview the submitted message using the composite key conversationID:clientMsgID , awaiting subsequent event delivery for final confirmation. Future resolution does not imply all participant clients have updated their screens. Events may also originate from other devices or authorized operators; never assume every event corresponds to the call just executed on the current screen. State changes after the call Message modification events are delivered through the onMessageModified callback in OnAdvancedMsgListener . The callback provides the single modified Message object. Because Flutter messages omit the conversationID attribute, resolve the conversation routing first, then replace the existing record by conversationID:clientMsgID : Future handleMessageModified Message message async final clientMsgID = message.clientMsgID; if clientMsgID == null || clientMsgID.isEmpty return; final conversationID = await resolveMessageConversationID message, currentUserID, ; if conversationID == null return; replaceMessage conversationID, clientMsgID, message ; The conversation ID resolution logic determines the message origin from sessionType , groupID , sendID , recvID , and the current user ID, then retrieves the conversation ID using the conversation ID helper. For complete helper implementation, see Receive messages /sdk/flutter/message/receiving messages/receive messages . Merge records strictly using conversationID:clientMsgID ; never match messages by array index, display text, or list length. Register this handler within the application's single OnAdvancedMsgListener . For centralized listener setup, see Events overview /sdk/flutter/events/overview events . When logging out or switching accounts, detach listeners from the prior account state and register the new account's listeners. Future completion, onMessageModified delivery, and historical re queries represent three distinct lifecycle stages. Re read messages when you must confirm final content; a failed query must not be misconstrued as a failed modification request. Related guides Delete saved messages /sdk/flutter/message/managing messages/delete saved message Revoke a message /sdk/flutter/message/managing messages/revoke a message Send a message /sdk/flutter/message/sending messages/send message Locate messages by ID /sdk/flutter/message/retrieving messages/locate messages by id Receive messages /sdk/flutter/message/receiving messages/receive messages

title: Retrieve pinned conversation messages
description: Use the Flutter SDK to retrieve the list of pinned messages in a conversation.
keywords: sdk flutter v4 sdk flutter message managing-messages get-pinned-messages
content: Retrieve a snapshot of all messages currently pinned in the specified conversation: Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | conversationID | String | Yes | Target conversation ID. | Code example final messages = await OpenIM.iMManager.messageManager .getConversationPinnedMsg conversationID: conversationID ; replacePinnedMessages conversationID, messages ; Return value Returns a Future resolving to a list of pinned messages List in the conversation. This response does not include pin metadata such as the operator ID or pinning timestamp. State changes after the call This query retrieves a point in time snapshot and does not trigger event callbacks. Replace the local pinned message state for the conversationID with the returned list, deduplicating items by non empty clientMsgID . For pinning operations and real time event updates, see Pin or unpin a message /sdk/flutter/message/managing messages/set message pinned .

title: Pin or unpin a message
description: Use the Flutter SDK to pin or unpin a message in a conversation.
keywords: sdk flutter v4 sdk flutter message managing-messages set-message-pinned
content: Pin a specific message to the top of a conversation, or unpin a previously pinned message: Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | conversationID | String | Yes | Target conversation ID. | | clientMsgID | String | Yes | Target client message ID to pin or unpin. | | pinned | bool | Yes | Pinning state: true to pin; false to unpin. | Code example await OpenIM.iMManager.messageManager.setConversationPinnedMsg conversationID: conversationID, clientMsgID: clientMsgID, pinned: true, ; Return value Future completion indicates that the server accepted the pin or unpin request. Future completion does not guarantee that event notifications have arrived at all clients. Update local conversation pin states optimistically if desired; to retrieve the complete current list of pinned messages, see Retrieve pinned conversation messages /sdk/flutter/message/managing messages/get pinned messages . State changes after the call Pinned message changes trigger the onChangedPinnedMsg callback in OnAdvancedMsgListener . When another client or an administrator updates pinned messages, participants in the conversation receive this callback. Locate the target conversation by conversationID and merge or replace the pinned message list deduplicating items by clientMsgID . For centralized listener registration, see Events overview /sdk/flutter/events/overview events .

title: Insert a local one-to-one message
description: Use the Flutter SDK to insert a local message into a one-to-one conversation.
keywords: sdk flutter v4 sdk flutter message managing-messages insert-local-single-message
content: Insert a local placeholder or private message into a one to one chat history on the current device only, without performing network delivery: Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | receiverID | String | Yes | Target user ID of the recipient in the direct chat. | | senderID | String | Yes | User ID of the message sender can be the current user or a virtual system user ID . | | message | Message | Yes | The complete message object to persist locally. | Code example final stored = await OpenIM.iMManager.messageManager .insertSingleMessageToLocalStorage receiverID: receiverUserID, senderID: senderUserID, message: localMessage, ; While parameters are marked nullable in the underlying SDK declaration, you must supply non empty values to guarantee correct conversation routing. Return value Returns a Future resolving to the persisted Message object. Merge it into your active one to one chat UI list using its non empty clientMsgID . State changes after the call This operation modifies only the local database on the current device. It does not synchronize to the server, is not sent to the peer user, and does not emit cross device event notifications. When real network delivery to the recipient is required, see Send a message /sdk/flutter/message/sending messages/send message ; to insert a local message in a group chat, see Insert a local group message /sdk/flutter/message/managing messages/insert local group message .

title: Insert a local group message
description: Use the Flutter SDK to insert a local message into a group conversation.
keywords: sdk flutter v4 sdk flutter message managing-messages insert-local-group-message
content: Insert a local placeholder or system notification message into the local group chat history on the current device only, without performing network delivery: Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | groupID | String | Yes | Target group ID. | | senderID | String | Yes | User ID of the message sender can be the current user or a virtual system user ID . | | message | Message | Yes | The complete message object to persist locally. | Code example final stored = await OpenIM.iMManager.messageManager .insertGroupMessageToLocalStorage groupID: groupID, senderID: senderUserID, message: localMessage, ; While parameters are marked nullable in the underlying SDK declaration, you must supply non empty values to guarantee correct local routing. Return value Returns a Future resolving to the persisted Message object. Merge it into your active group chat UI list using its clientMsgID . State changes after the call This operation modifies only the local database on the current device. It does not synchronize to server roaming history, is not sent to other group members, and does not emit cross device event notifications. When real network delivery to group members is required, see Send a message /sdk/flutter/message/sending messages/send message ; to insert a local message in a direct chat, see Insert a local single chat message /sdk/flutter/message/managing messages/insert local single message .

title: Clear all local messages
description: Use the Flutter SDK to clear all local messages for the current account.
keywords: sdk flutter v4 sdk flutter message managing-messages clear-all-local-messages
content: Clear all message records stored in the local database for the current logged in account on this device. This method takes no parameters and is suitable for releasing storage space or resetting local message cache: Code example await OpenIM.iMManager.messageManager.deleteAllMsgFromLocal ; clearLocalMessageState ; Return value Future completion indicates that all historical message records have been deleted from the current device's local database. State changes after the call This is a local only destructive operation that modifies solely the device's local storage. It does not delete messages stored on the server and does not emit cross device message deletion events. If the user subsequently fetches roaming history or logs in on another device, server side messages continue to synchronize normally. To delete all messages permanently from both local storage and the server, see Clear all messages /sdk/flutter/message/managing messages/clear all messages ; to delete a single local message, see Delete a local message /sdk/flutter/message/managing messages/delete local message .

title: Clear all messages
description: Use the Flutter SDK to clear all local and server-side messages for the current account.
keywords: sdk flutter v4 sdk flutter message managing-messages clear-all-messages
content: Permanently clear all historical messages for the current logged in user from both the local database and the server. This method takes no parameters and is used to wipe an account's message history completely: Code example await OpenIM.iMManager.messageManager.deleteAllMsgFromLocalAndSvr ; clearLocalMessageState ; Return value Future completion indicates that the deletion request has been processed on both the server and local storage for the current account. State changes after the call This is an irreversible account level operation. It removes message records from the current user's local database and server side roaming history; it does not delete message copies saved on other participants' devices. Once the Future completes, clear local in memory message caches and refresh your UI. Conversation summaries and unread counters subsequently update through conversation listeners, and you can reload the conversation list to reconcile state. If you only want to clear local storage while preserving server roaming history, see Clear all local messages /sdk/flutter/message/managing messages/clear all local messages ; to delete individual messages, see Delete saved messages /sdk/flutter/message/managing messages/delete saved message .

title: Set a message's local extension
description: Update a message's local extension field on the current Flutter device.
keywords: sdk flutter v4 sdk flutter message managing-messages set-message-local-ex
content: Set a device local custom extension string on a single message such as UI accordion toggle states or local parsing flags : Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | conversationID | String | Yes | ID of the conversation containing the message. | | clientMsgID | String | Yes | Target client message ID. | | localEx | String | Yes | Device local custom extension payload, typically encoded as a JSON string. | Code example await OpenIM.iMManager.messageManager.setMessageLocalEx conversationID: conversationID, clientMsgID: clientMsgID, localEx: jsonEncode 'expanded': true , ; The localEx payload replaces the entire string value; the SDK does not perform incremental merge operations. Ensure clientMsgID is non empty before calling. Return value Future completion indicates that the local extension string was successfully written to the local database on the current device. Update your UI state using the composite key conversationID:clientMsgID . State changes after the call This operation performs a device local data update only. It is not uploaded to the server, does not synchronize to other devices or chat participants, and does not trigger message event notifications.

title: Listen for file upload progress
description: Configure the standalone file upload listener in the OpenIM Flutter SDK.
keywords: sdk flutter v4 sdk flutter file-uploads set-upload-file-listener
content: Configure a standalone file upload listener centrally within your application upload management service: Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | listener | OnUploadFileListener | Yes | Upload listener instance providing file upload progress and completion callbacks. | OnUploadFileListener callback methods provide the following arguments: onUploadProgress id, fileSize, streamSize, storageSize : Task ID, total file size in bytes, stream bytes read, and bytes written to storage. onComplete id, size, url, type : Task ID, final file size in bytes, remote accessible URL, and storage type. Code example OpenIM.iMManager.setUploadFileListener OnUploadFileListener onUploadProgress: id, fileSize, streamSize, storageSize updateFileProgress id, streamSize, fileSize ; , onComplete: id, size, url, type completeFileUpload id, size, url, type ; , , ; State changes after the call The Flutter SDK maintains only a single OnUploadFileListener instance; setting a new listener replaces the previous one. Register this listener once in your application state layer, rather than inside individual UI widgets, to prevent callbacks from being inadvertently overwritten. Callbacks identify upload jobs by the task id . Do not rely on file names or array indexes to map upload progress to UI items. When switching accounts or destroying the upload manager, stop forwarding events to inactive views and clear the active task registry. To initiate file uploads, refer to Upload a file /sdk/flutter/file uploads/upload file .

title: Upload file
description: Upload a local file to storage using the OpenIM Flutter SDK.
keywords: sdk flutter v4 sdk flutter file-uploads upload-file
content: Upload a local file directly to object storage for user avatars, group avatars, or custom business attachments: Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | id | String | Yes | Unique task ID used to correlate progress and completion events in listener callbacks. | | filePath | String | Yes | Absolute local path of the file accessible by the client. | | fileName | String | Yes | Original file name, including its extension. | | contentType | String? | No | MIME type of the file for example, image/png . | | cause | String? | No | Business reason or description for the upload for example, user avatar . | Code example await OpenIM.iMManager.uploadFile id: 'upload task 001', filePath: filePath, fileName: fileName, contentType: contentType, cause: 'user avatar', ; Return value A successful Future returns void , indicating that the upload task was accepted and started. Upload progress and the resulting file URL are delivered through the global upload listener. Once the complete callback provides the remote URL, pass it to subsequent profile update or attachment storage APIs. Calling uploadFile does not automatically update user profiles or generate chat messages. For listener configuration and callback signatures, see Listen for file upload progress /sdk/flutter/file uploads/set upload file listener .

title: Audio and video calls overview
description: Understand VoIP calling signaling, room information, and event boundaries in the OpenIM Flutter SDK.
keywords: sdk flutter v4 sdk flutter calling overview-calling
content: The OpenIM Flutter SDK's SignalingManager provides signaling APIs for initiating, accepting, rejecting, cancelling, hanging up, querying rooms, and synchronizing call states. It coordinates participant entry into rooms and manages call session lifecycles; it does not capture camera video, play remote audio/video tracks, or render call UI components. Pass the roomID , token , and liveURL returned by the SDK to your chosen WebRTC/live media engine such as LiveKit . Your application manages device hardware permissions, audio/video track capture, network fallback policies, and UI views. The OpenIM Flutter SDK provides call signaling orchestration rather than standalone media streaming pipelines. Calling lifecycle workflow 1. Call Start a single call /sdk/flutter/calling/managing calls/start single call or Start a group call /sdk/flutter/calling/managing calls/start group call . 2. The invitee receives an invitation notification in Handle call events /sdk/flutter/calling/managing calls/handle call events , extracts SignalingInfo , and decides whether to accept or reject. 3. The callee calls Accept a call /sdk/flutter/calling/managing calls/accept call . Both parties connect to the media server using the returned room credentials. 4. Update local state as participants, media streams, and custom signals arrive via listeners during the call. 5. The initiator can cancel an unanswered invitation; any connected participant can hang up an active call. Core data structures | Structure | Description | | | | | InvitationInfo | Inviter, invitee list, group ID, room ID, media type, timeout, and session type. Fields are nullable in Dart; validate them when handling callbacks. | | SignalingInfo | Operator userID , the full invitation payload, and optional offlinePushInfo . | | SignalingCertificate | Room credentials returned by OpenIMServer, including roomID , token , liveURL , and busy user lists. | | RoomCallingInfo | Group call status including room details, invitations, active participants, and access credentials. | customData is not a property of the Flutter InvitationInfo model. For lightweight negotiation during a call, send custom signaling messages within the room. Custom signaling is intended for temporary in call coordination, not persistent data storage or file transfer. State synchronization and event boundaries State modifying operations initiating, accepting, rejecting, cancelling, and hanging up require handling both the Future and listener callbacks. Future completion signifies that the signaling request reached the server; listener events reflect asynchronous state transitions received across participants and other devices. Listen to invitation lifecycles, participant joins/leaves, hang ups, and stream changes in Handle call events /sdk/flutter/calling/managing calls/handle call events . For in room messaging, see Send a custom signal /sdk/flutter/calling/sending custom signals/send a custom signal . Room and token queries return snapshot data at invocation time via Futures and are documented under the call information guides. Manage call listeners centrally in Handle call events /sdk/flutter/calling/managing calls/handle call events . Use roomID as the primary merge key, qualified by participant userID . When rendering room membership, query fresh room status snapshots to reconcile UI state. Related guides Start a single call /sdk/flutter/calling/managing calls/start single call Handle call events /sdk/flutter/calling/managing calls/handle call events Restore pending invitations /sdk/flutter/calling/retrieving call information/restore pending invitation Send a custom signal /sdk/flutter/calling/sending custom signals/send a custom signal

title: Start a single call
description: Initiate a one-to-one audio or video call invitation to a specified user.
keywords: sdk flutter v4 sdk flutter calling managing-calls start-single-call
content: Initiate a one to one call invitation to an individual recipient. The OpenIM SDK manages the signaling channel and call lifecycle; your app connects to your RTC media engine using the returned credentials: Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | info | SignalingInfo | Yes | Call signaling initiation object containing the operator's userID , invitation , and optional offlinePushInfo . | Core fields of invitation : inviterUserID : Initiator user ID. inviteeUserIDList : List containing exactly one recipient user ID. groupID : Pass an empty string '' for single chat calls. roomID : Call room ID. Generate a globally unique ID per call session. timeout : Call timeout in seconds. mediaType : Media type for example, 'video' or 'audio' . sessionType : Session type; pass ConversationType.single for single chat calls. Code example final info = SignalingInfo userID: currentUserID, invitation: InvitationInfo inviterUserID: currentUserID, inviteeUserIDList: peerUserID , groupID: '', roomID: roomID, timeout: 30, mediaType: 'video', sessionType: ConversationType.single, platformID: Platform.isIOS ? IMPlatform.ios : IMPlatform.android, , offlinePushInfo: offlinePushInfo, ; final credentials = await OpenIM.iMManager.signalingManager .signalingInvite info: info ; Return value A successful Future returns a SignalingCertificate object containing credentials for entering the media room. | Field | Type | Description | | | | | | token | String? | Room authentication token required by the media engine. | | roomID | String? | Target call room ID. | | liveURL | String? | Live media streaming server URL. | | busyLineUserIDList | List ? | List of user IDs currently busy on another line. | State changes after the call A successful call indicates that the invitation signal has been dispatched. It does not mean the recipient has answered. The client creates a local calling state mapped to roomID and awaits acceptance, rejection, or timeout events see Handle call events /sdk/flutter/calling/managing calls/handle call events for complete event handling .

title: Start a group call
description: Invite specified group members to join a group audio or video call.
keywords: sdk flutter v4 sdk flutter calling managing-calls start-group-call
content: A group call invitation is sent only to the specific group members listed in inviteeUserIDList . Specifying a groupID does not automatically ring all members of the group: Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | info | SignalingInfo | Yes | Group call signaling initiation object containing the operator's userID and the complete invitation payload. | Core fields of invitation : inviterUserID : Initiator user ID. inviteeUserIDList : List of invited group member user IDs, excluding the caller. groupID : Target group ID; cannot be empty. roomID : Call room ID. If generated by the application, all participants must use the identical ID. timeout : Invitation expiration timeout in seconds. mediaType : Media stream type for example, 'video' or 'audio' . sessionType : Session type; pass ConversationType.group for group calls. Code example final info = SignalingInfo userID: currentUserID, invitation: InvitationInfo inviterUserID: currentUserID, inviteeUserIDList: selectedGroupMemberIDs, groupID: groupID, roomID: groupID, timeout: 30, mediaType: 'video', sessionType: ConversationType.group, platformID: Platform.isIOS ? IMPlatform.ios : IMPlatform.android, , ; final credentials = await OpenIM.iMManager.signalingManager .signalingInviteInGroup info: info ; Return value A successful Future returns a SignalingCertificate object containing the caller's room access credentials. | Field | Type | Description | | | | | | token | String? | Room authentication token required by the media engine. | | roomID | String? | Target call room ID. | | liveURL | String? | Live media streaming server URL. | | busyLineUserIDList | List ? | List of member user IDs currently busy on another line. Busy members do not prevent other invitees from receiving the call. | State changes after the call A successful call indicates that the group invitation has been dispatched by the server. It does not imply that invited members have answered. The client tracks the local call session via roomID . Member acceptances, rejections, and timeouts arrive asynchronously via events see Handle call events /sdk/flutter/calling/managing calls/handle call events for complete event handling .

title: Accept a call
description: Accept an incoming call invitation and retrieve room credentials using the OpenIM Flutter SDK.
keywords: sdk flutter v4 sdk flutter calling managing-calls accept-call
