content: When an invitee receives a call invitation in Handle call events /sdk/flutter/calling/managing calls/handle call events and obtains the raw SignalingInfo , call this method to accept the invitation: Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | info | SignalingInfo | Yes | The complete signaling object received in the invitation callback. Pass the original object rather than reconstructing one from roomID . | Code example final credentials = await OpenIM.iMManager.signalingManager .signalingAccept info: receivedInfo ; Return value A successful Future returns a SignalingCertificate object containing room connection credentials. | Field | Type | Description | | | | | | token | String? | Room authentication token required by the media engine. | | roomID | String? | Target call room ID. | | liveURL | String? | Live media streaming server URL. | | busyLineUserIDList | List ? | List of user IDs currently busy on another line. | State changes after the call A successful call indicates that the acceptance signal was accepted by the server and room credentials were issued. It does not imply that WebRTC media tracks are connected. Use roomID as the primary key to manage the active call session, and correlate participants with their user IDs. For complete event listening, see Handle call events /sdk/flutter/calling/managing calls/handle call events .

title: Reject a call
description: Decline an incoming call invitation before answering.
keywords: sdk flutter v4 sdk flutter calling managing-calls reject-call
content: When an invitee receives a call invitation and decides not to answer, call this method to decline the invitation: Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | info | SignalingInfo | Yes | The complete signaling object received in the invitation callback. Pass the original object rather than reconstructing one from roomID . | Code example await OpenIM.iMManager.signalingManager .signalingReject info: receivedInfo ; Return value A successful Future indicates that the rejection signaling request has been received by the server. State changes after the call The client should dismiss the incoming call dialog and release any unallocated media resources associated with roomID . The initiator updates its outgoing call UI upon receiving the rejection event see Handle call events /sdk/flutter/calling/managing calls/handle call events for complete event handling .

title: Cancel a call invitation
description: Cancel a pending call invitation as the initiator before it is answered.
keywords: sdk flutter v4 sdk flutter calling managing-calls cancel-call
content: Before an unanswered call is accepted, the initiator can cancel the invitation: Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | info | SignalingInfo | Yes | The complete signaling object saved when initiating the call invitation. | Code example await OpenIM.iMManager.signalingManager .signalingCancel info: activeInfo ; Return value A successful Future indicates that the cancellation signaling request has been received by the server. State changes after the call The client should terminate its outgoing call waiting UI and release local media resources using roomID . The invitee dismisses the incoming call notification upon receiving the cancellation event see Handle call events /sdk/flutter/calling/managing calls/handle call events for listener details . If the call has already been answered and established, invoke Hang up a call /sdk/flutter/calling/managing calls/hang up call instead.

title: Hang up a call
description: Terminate an active audio or video call session.
keywords: sdk flutter v4 sdk flutter calling managing-calls hang-up-call
content: Once a call is connected, any participant can terminate the call: Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | info | SignalingInfo | Yes | Active signaling object whose roomID matches the ongoing media room. | Code example await OpenIM.iMManager.signalingManager .signalingHungUp info: activeInfo ; Return value A successful Future indicates that the hang up signaling request has been received by the server. State changes after the call The client should terminate the local call session associated with roomID , stop local audio/video capture, disconnect from the media server, and release camera and microphone hardware resources. Other participants exit the call upon receiving the hang up event see Handle call events /sdk/flutter/calling/managing calls/handle call events for complete event handling . Implement local teardown logic idempotently using roomID .

title: Handle call events
description: Register the call signaling listener centrally in the OpenIM Flutter SDK.
keywords: sdk flutter v4 sdk flutter calling managing-calls handle-call-events
content: Register OnSignalingListener centrally when initializing your application's calling service: Code example Future registerCallListener return OpenIM.iMManager.signalingManager.setSignalingListener OnSignalingListener onReceiveNewInvitation: handleIncomingCall, onInviteeAccepted: handleInviteeAccepted, onInviteeRejected: handleInviteeRejected, onInvitationCancelled: handleInvitationCancelled, onInvitationTimeout: handleInvitationTimeout, onInviteeAcceptedByOtherDevice: handleAcceptedElsewhere, onInviteeRejectedByOtherDevice: handleRejectedElsewhere, onHangup: handleHangup, onRoomParticipantConnected: handleParticipantConnected, onRoomParticipantDisconnected: handleParticipantDisconnected, onStreamChange: handleStreamChange, , ; Call events encompass the full invitation lifecycle, participant joins and leaves, and media stream state transitions. Use roomID as the primary merge key for call state, and qualify participant states by their user IDs. For custom signaling events, see Send a custom signal /sdk/flutter/calling/sending custom signals/send a custom signal . SignalingManager stores only one listener instance; a subsequent invocation replaces previously registered callbacks. Because the SDK does not provide an unregister method, stop forwarding events to old state stores when logging out or switching accounts, and re register the complete listener instance upon the next user sign in.

title: Restore pending invitations
description: Restore unhandled call invitations upon app launch using the OpenIM Flutter SDK.
keywords: sdk flutter v4 sdk flutter calling retrieving-call-information restore-pending-invitation
content: When the app launches, re authenticates, or recovers from missed push notifications, call this method to retrieve any pending, still valid call invitations: Code example final info = await OpenIM.iMManager.signalingManager .getSignalingInvitationInfoStartApp ; if info.invitation?.roomID?.isNotEmpty == true restoreIncomingCall info.invitation , info.offlinePushInfo ; Return value A successful Future returns a SignalingInfo object containing pending call invitations and offline push metadata available at launch. | Field | Type | Description | | | | | | userID | String? | Operator user ID. | | invitation | InvitationInfo? | Pending invitation details. If roomID is empty, no recoverable call exists. | | offlinePushInfo | OfflinePushInfo? | Offline push notification payload. | This query returns only invitations that remain active when the application starts; if roomID is null or empty, dismiss any stale incoming call interfaces. After restoring an incoming call, continue monitoring timeout, cancellation, acceptance, and hang up callbacks in Handle call events /sdk/flutter/calling/managing calls/handle call events .

title: Query group call room
description: Query active ongoing call rooms by group ID using the OpenIM Flutter SDK.
keywords: sdk flutter v4 sdk flutter calling retrieving-call-information get-room-by-group-id
content: Query the active audio or video call room currently ongoing in a specified group: Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | groupID | String | Yes | Target group ID. | Code example final room = await OpenIM.iMManager.signalingManager .signalingGetRoomByGroupID groupID: groupID ; if room.roomID?.isNotEmpty == true renderParticipants room.participant ?? const ; Return value A successful Future returns a RoomCallingInfo object containing room metadata, invitation details, and participant lists. | Field | Type | Description | | | | | | roomID | String? | Active call room ID. Empty if no ongoing call exists in the group. | | invitation | InvitationInfo? | Invitation details of the active call. | | participant | List ? | List of participants currently connected in the room. | | token | String? | Room authentication token. | If roomID is non empty, use Get call room token /sdk/flutter/calling/retrieving call information/get token by room id to obtain media streaming credentials to join. If no active call is returned, treat the result as having no recoverable call and discard stale credentials.

title: Get call room token
description: Retrieve media room access credentials by room ID using the OpenIM Flutter SDK.
keywords: sdk flutter v4 sdk flutter calling retrieving-call-information get-token-by-room-id
content: When the roomID is already known, invoke this method to retrieve or refresh the access credentials required by the media engine: Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | roomID | String | Yes | Target call room ID. | Code example final credentials = await OpenIM.iMManager.signalingManager .signalingGetTokenByRoomID roomID: roomID ; if credentials.token?.isNotEmpty == true && credentials.roomID?.isNotEmpty == true await mediaEngine.join roomID: credentials.roomID , token: credentials.token , liveURL: credentials.liveURL, ; Return value A successful Future returns a SignalingCertificate object containing credentials for joining the call room. | Field | Type | Description | | | | | | token | String? | Room authentication token required by the media engine. | | roomID | String? | Call room ID. | | liveURL | String? | Live media streaming server URL. | | busyLineUserIDList | List ? | List of user IDs currently busy on another line. | Connect to the RTC media engine only after obtaining a non empty token and valid room credentials. If the token expires during a reconnection attempt, invoke this API again to acquire a refreshed credential.

title: Send a custom signal
description: Send and receive lightweight custom signaling payloads within a call room using the OpenIM Flutter SDK.
keywords: sdk flutter v4 sdk flutter calling sending-custom-signals send-a-custom-signal
content: Custom signals deliver lightweight business coordination payloads—such as raising hands, requesting layout changes, or syncing transient presentation state—to participants in an active call room. Custom signaling is not a chat messaging API and does not replace RTC media data channels. Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | roomID | String | Yes | Target call room ID. | | customInfo | String | Yes | Custom business signaling payload, typically a JSON serialized string. | Code example final signal = jsonEncode 'version': 1, 'eventID': eventID, 'type': 'hand raised', 'userID': currentUserID, 'sentAt': DateTime.now .millisecondsSinceEpoch, ; await OpenIM.iMManager.signalingManager.signalingSendCustomSignal roomID: roomID, customInfo: signal, ; Return value A successful Future indicates that the server accepted the signaling payload for dispatch. It does not guarantee that other participants have processed it. Custom signaling is designed for lightweight, ephemeral in call coordination; do not use it to transfer large files or persist long term state. Receive custom signals Receive custom signals through the onReceiveCustomSignal callback on OnSignalingListener : void handleCustomSignal CustomSignaling info final signalRoomID = info.roomID; final customInfo = info.customInfo; if signalRoomID = activeRoomID || customInfo == null return; final signal = parseAndValidateCallSignal customInfo ; if hasAppliedSignal signalRoomID , signal.eventID return; applyCallSignal signal ; Future registerCustomSignalListener return OpenIM.iMManager.signalingManager.setSignalingListener OnSignalingListener onReceiveCustomSignal: handleCustomSignal , ; Include a protocol version and an idempotency key eventID within the custom business payload. Deduplicate actions using roomID:eventID to prevent duplicate processing or out of order execution from corrupting UI state. Because the SDK does not provide an unregister method, stop dispatching events to old state stores when logging out or switching accounts, and overwrite the listener with a fresh instance upon the next login. For general call event handling, see Handle call events /sdk/flutter/calling/managing calls/handle call events .

title: Events overview
description: Register OpenIM Flutter SDK listeners centrally and dispatch real-time events across application domains.
keywords: sdk flutter v4 sdk flutter events overview-events
content: The OpenIM Flutter SDK delivers real time notifications for connection state, background data synchronization, users, friendships, conversations, conversation groups, groups, messages, and VoIP calling via listeners. Each manager maintains only one active listener instance; invoking a setter again overwrites the previously registered instance in the Dart layer. Therefore, register all callbacks once within a centralized application state service during startup, and avoid re registering listeners inside Widget build methods or individual page routes. Centralized listener registration The following entry point consolidates application wide listener registrations. The full incremental merge logic for each handle callback is documented in the dedicated topic pages listed in the table below. Code example Future registerOpenIMListeners async await OpenIM.iMManager.userManager.setUserListener OnUserListener onSelfInfoUpdated: handleSelfInfoUpdated, onUserStatusChanged: handleUserStatusChanged, , ; await OpenIM.iMManager.friendshipManager.setFriendshipListener OnFriendshipListener onBlackAdded: handleBlackAdded, onBlackDeleted: handleBlackDeleted, onFriendAdded: handleFriendChanged, onFriendDeleted: handleFriendDeleted, onFriendInfoChanged: handleFriendChanged, onFriendApplicationAdded: handleFriendApplicationChanged, onFriendApplicationAccepted: handleFriendApplicationChanged, onFriendApplicationRejected: handleFriendApplicationChanged, onFriendApplicationDeleted: handleFriendApplicationDeleted, , ; await OpenIM.iMManager.conversationManager.setConversationListener OnConversationListener onNewConversation: handleNewConversations, onConversationChanged: handleConversationsChanged, onTotalUnreadMessageCountChanged: handleTotalUnreadChanged, onInputStatusChanged: handleInputStatusChanged, onSyncServerStart: handleSyncStart, onSyncServerProgress: handleSyncProgress, onSyncServerFinish: handleSyncFinish, onSyncServerFailed: handleSyncFailed, , ; await OpenIM.iMManager.groupManager.setGroupListener OnGroupListener onJoinedGroupAdded: handleJoinedGroupAdded, onJoinedGroupDeleted: handleJoinedGroupDeleted, onGroupInfoChanged: handleGroupInfoChanged, onGroupDismissed: handleGroupDismissed, onGroupMemberAdded: handleGroupMemberAdded, onGroupMemberDeleted: handleGroupMemberDeleted, onGroupMemberInfoChanged: handleGroupMemberInfoChanged, onGroupApplicationAdded: handleGroupApplicationChanged, onGroupApplicationAccepted: handleGroupApplicationChanged, onGroupApplicationRejected: handleGroupApplicationChanged, onGroupApplicationDeleted: handleGroupApplicationDeleted, , ; await OpenIM.iMManager.messageManager.setAdvancedMsgListener OnAdvancedMsgListener onRecvNewMessage: handleNewMessage, onRecvOfflineNewMessage: handleOfflineMessage, onRecvOnlineOnlyMessage: handleOnlineOnlyMessage, onMsgDeleted: handleMessageDeleted, onNewRecvMessageRevoked: handleMessageRevoked, onRecvC2CReadReceipt: handleC2CReadReceipts, onMessageModified: handleMessageModified, onChangedPinnedMsg: handlePinnedMessagesChanged, , ; await OpenIM.iMManager.messageManager.setCustomBusinessListener OnCustomBusinessListener onRecvCustomBusinessMessage: handleCustomBusinessMessage, , ; await OpenIM.iMManager.signalingManager.setSignalingListener OnSignalingListener onReceiveNewInvitation: handleIncomingCall, onInviteeAccepted: handleInviteeAccepted, onInviteeRejected: handleInviteeRejected, onInvitationCancelled: handleInvitationCancelled, onInvitationTimeout: handleInvitationTimeout, onInviteeAcceptedByOtherDevice: handleAcceptedElsewhere, onInviteeRejectedByOtherDevice: handleRejectedElsewhere, onHangup: handleHangup, onRoomParticipantConnected: handleParticipantConnected, onRoomParticipantDisconnected: handleParticipantDisconnected, onStreamChange: handleStreamChange, onReceiveCustomSignal: handleCustomSignal, , ; The conversation group listener is maintained separately by ConversationGroupManager and is omitted from the consolidated entry point above. See Conversation groups overview /sdk/flutter/conversation/managing conversation groups/overview conversation groups for its registration, five callback types, and state merge rules. The SDK does not provide explicit remove or unset APIs. When signing out, switching accounts, or destroying state layers, cease dispatching events to old user stores or unmounted widgets. When logging in with a new account, overwrite the active listeners with new callbacks. Event domain mapping | Domain | Entity Merge Key | Dedicated Documentation Page | | | | | | User profile & online status | userID | Users overview /sdk/flutter/user/overview user | | Friends & blocklist | userID | Get friend list with pagination /sdk/flutter/user/friends/get friend list page | | Conversation list | conversationID | Retrieve conversation list /sdk/flutter/conversation/retrieving conversations/retrieve conversation list | | Conversation groups | conversationGroupID | Conversation groups overview /sdk/flutter/conversation/managing conversation groups/overview conversation groups | | Total unread message count | Current user | Get total unread count /sdk/flutter/conversation/managing conversations/get total unread count | | Typing status | conversationID:userID | Update typing status /sdk/flutter/message/composing messages/update typing status | | Groups | groupID | Groups overview /sdk/flutter/group/overview group | | Group members | groupID:userID | Retrieving group members overview /sdk/flutter/group/retrieving group members/overview retrieving group members | | Group join applications | groupID:userID | Group applications overview /sdk/flutter/group/group applications/overview group applications | | New incoming messages | conversationID:clientMsgID | Receive messages /sdk/flutter/message/receiving messages/receive messages | | Message deletion | conversationID:clientMsgID | Delete saved message /sdk/flutter/message/managing messages/delete saved message | | Message revocation | conversationID:clientMsgID | Revoke a message /sdk/flutter/message/managing messages/revoke a message | | Message modification | conversationID:clientMsgID | Modify a message /sdk/flutter/message/managing messages/modify a message | | Pinned messages | conversationID messages by clientMsgID | Pin or unpin message /sdk/flutter/message/managing messages/set message pinned | | C2C read receipts | conversationID:clientMsgID | Mark conversation as read /sdk/flutter/conversation/managing conversations/mark conversation read | | Custom business notifications | Payload business ID or idempotency key | Custom business listener /sdk/flutter/message/receiving messages/custom business listener | | VoIP calls | roomID participants by userID | Handle call events /sdk/flutter/calling/managing calls/handle call events | | Custom call signaling | roomID:eventID | Send a custom signal /sdk/flutter/calling/sending custom signals/send a custom signal | Listen to initial synchronization Synchronization callbacks belong to OnConversationListener . They describe background database synchronization progress with the server and are separate from query Future completions. Code example void handleSyncStart bool? reinstalled setSyncState status: 'syncing', progress: 0, reinstalled: reinstalled == true ; void handleSyncProgress int? progress setSyncState status: 'syncing', progress: progress ?? 0 ; void handleSyncFinish bool? reinstalled setSyncState status: 'ready', progress: 100, reinstalled: reinstalled == true ; reloadVisibleSnapshots ; void handleSyncFailed bool? reinstalled setSyncState status: 'failed', reinstalled: reinstalled == true ; Use onSyncServerStart to transition into a syncing state, and onSyncServerProgress to render progress bars. When onSyncServerFinish fires, reload the snapshots required by currently visible screens. If onSyncServerFailed triggers, record the failure and wait for connection recovery. Always handle asynchronous events, query results, and Future completions as distinct operational stages.

title: Logger
description: Configure OpenIM Flutter SDK logging, write diagnostic entries, and upload logs to the server.
keywords: sdk flutter v4 sdk flutter logger
content: The OpenIM Flutter SDK logging system assists in diagnosing SDK initialization issues, WebSocket connection errors, and business API failures. Configure the log level, standard output, and custom log file path during SDK initialization. You can also write application diagnostic entries into the SDK log buffer and upload local logs to the server on demand. Initialize logging configuration Configure the logging strategy during SDK initialization rather than at sign in time. Parameters Specify the following logging parameters when calling initSDK : | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | logLevel | int | No | Numeric SDK logging level. Lower numbers generate more detailed logs. Defaults to 6 . | | isLogStandardOutput | bool | No | Whether to print logs synchronously to the system console or debug terminal. | | logFilePath | String? | No | Custom local file path for storing logs. Must reside in a writable application sandbox directory on the target platform. | Code example import 'dart:io'; final platformID = Platform.isIOS ? IMPlatform.ios : IMPlatform.android; await OpenIM.iMManager.initSDK platformID: platformID, apiAddr: apiAddr, wsAddr: wsAddr, dataDir: dataDir, listener: connectListener, logLevel: 5, isLogStandardOutput: true, logFilePath: logFilePath, ; Pass IMPlatform.android when running on Android and IMPlatform.ios on iOS. Write custom diagnostic logs Record critical business exceptions or debug traces directly into the SDK's local log system so that application events correlate with underlying SDK diagnostics: Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | logLevel | int | No | Numeric log level for this entry. | | file | String | Yes | File name or module identifier where the log is generated. | | line | int | Yes | Source line number triggering the log. | | msgs | String | Yes | Main descriptive log message. | | err | String? | No | Caught error string or stack trace. | | keyAndValues | List ? | No | Structured key value pairs arranged alternately for example, 'key1', 'val1' . | Code example await OpenIM.iMManager.logs logLevel: 5, file: 'chat repository.dart', line: 120, msgs: 'load conversation page failed', err: error.toString , keyAndValues: 'conversationID', conversationID , ; Return value A successful Future returns void , indicating that the log entry has been written to the local log buffer. Listen and upload logs When a user initiates feedback or when remote troubleshooting is required, upload the local log files to the server: Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | ex | String? | No | Reason for uploading or supplementary business diagnostic remarks. | Code example OpenIM.iMManager.setUploadLogsListener OnUploadLogsListener onUploadProgress: current, size updateLogUploadProgress current, size ; , , ; await OpenIM.iMManager.uploadLogs ex: 'user initiated diagnostics' ; Return value A successful Future returns void , indicating that the log upload operation was initiated and completed the transfer. The SDK maintains a single OnUploadLogsListener instance; setting a new listener overwrites the previous one. Register this listener once within a centralized diagnostics service and dispatch progress to UI components. Clear pending upload tasks when switching accounts.

title: OpenIM SDK for uni-app / uni-app x
description: Integrate OpenIMClientSDK into Android, iOS, and HarmonyOS apps built with uni-app and uni-app x.
keywords: sdk uniapp v4 sdk uniapp overview
content: The OpenIM uni app / uni app x SDK is delivered as a UTS native plugin that exposes OpenIMClientSDK capabilities to both standard uni app Vue 2 / Vue 3 and uni app x projects. The SDK provides native client features across Android, iOS, and HarmonyOS apps, covering user identity, relationships, conversations, groups, messaging, audio/video call signaling, real time events, and local SQLite data persistence. Applicable scenarios Use this SDK when developing multi platform native mobile applications in HBuilderX and requiring full featured instant messaging within uni app Vue 2 / Vue 3 or uni app x. The plugin wraps underlying native SDKs directly, providing client capabilities including SQLite database storage, conversation caching, and offline message synchronization. This SDK does not support Web browsers or Mini Programs. For Web applications, refer to the OpenIM WASM SDK Overview /sdk/wasm/overview . For Mini Programs and lightweight Web scenarios without local SQLite message storage, refer to the OpenIM Mini Program SDK Overview /sdk/miniprogram/overview . Supported platforms | Project type and platform | Support status | Minimum OS version | | | | | | uni app App Android Vue 2 / Vue 3 | Supported | Android 5.0 / API 21 | | uni app App iOS Vue 2 / Vue 3 | Supported | iOS 14 | | uni app App HarmonyOS Vue 2 / Vue 3 | Commercial license required | HarmonyOS API 24 | | uni app x App Android | Supported | Android 5.0 / API 21 | | uni app x App iOS | Supported | iOS 14 | | uni app x App HarmonyOS | Commercial license required | HarmonyOS API 24 | | Web / Mini Programs | Not supported | — | HarmonyOS platform availability and commercial capabilities depend on the delivered SDK package and licensing agreement. When accessing photos, the camera, microphone, or local files, declare and request the appropriate system permissions within the host app manifest and runtime flow. Integration workflow The SDK is delivered in the uni modules/unix openim sdk directory. Place this folder into your project root and import API functions directly from the plugin package: import initSDK, login, createTextMessage, sendMessage, from '@/uni modules/unix openim sdk' Native dependencies are not included in the standard HBuilderX run base. Before debugging SDK initialization, user authentication, messaging, or event listeners, build and run a custom debugging base containing this plugin, or compile a formal native application package. Conventions and usage guidelines Promises : Methods return Promises for business results. When an operation fails, the Promise rejects with an error containing errCode and errMsg . Event subscriptions : Event registration methods prefixed with on return an OpenIMSDKEventSubscription . Call off subscription with that reference when unmounting components, logging out, or resetting the SDK lifecycle. Query snapshot vs. real time sync : Query methods retrieve point in time local snapshots, whereas real time event listeners stream incremental updates. A successful Promise indicates the local request completed; cross device state propagation occurs through subsequent events. File paths : File and media operations accept either POSIX absolute paths readable by the app sandbox or unifile:// URI paths generated from uni.env.USER DATA PATH . Next steps 1. Read Before you start /sdk/uniapp/getting started/before you start to set up OpenIMServer, prepare test credentials, and configure your native build environment. 2. Follow Integrate by project and platform /sdk/uniapp/getting started/environment specific implementation to install the plugin and configure platform settings for Android, iOS, and HarmonyOS. 3. Review Authenticate and manage a session /sdk/uniapp/getting started/authenticate and manage session to register connection listeners, initialize the SDK, and log in. 4. Follow Send your first message /sdk/uniapp/getting started/send first message to verify one on one and group messaging flows. Subsequent documentation is organized across user profiles, relationships, conversations, groups, messaging, file uploads, audio/video call signaling, and events, strictly adhering to public UTS types and methods exported by the uni app / uni app x plugin.

title: Before you start
description: Prepare OpenIMServer endpoints, user credentials, the UTS plugin, and your native app build environment.
keywords: sdk uniapp v4 sdk uniapp getting-started before-you-start
content: Before integrating OpenIMClientSDK into a uni app or uni app x project, ensure you have an accessible OpenIMServer deployment, user authentication credentials, the complete UTS native plugin package, and a native build environment capable of compiling native mobile dependencies. These prerequisites support both Authenticate and manage a session /sdk/uniapp/getting started/authenticate and manage session and Send your first message /sdk/uniapp/getting started/send first message . Prepare OpenIMServer endpoints If you do not have an operational OpenIMServer deployment, complete the Docker Deployment Guide /docs/guides/quick deployment/docker first. Confirm that your target Android, iOS, or HarmonyOS devices can reach the following endpoints: | Endpoint | Description | | | | | apiAddr | The HTTP API base address for OpenIMServer, used for login, data synchronization, and server resource queries. Use HTTPS in production. | | wsAddr | The WebSocket gateway address for OpenIMServer, used for maintaining persistent connections and streaming real time events. Use WSS in production. | Do not verify these URLs exclusively from your development workstation or localhost. Test connectivity from physical devices or emulators to ensure proper DNS resolution, valid TLS certificates, permissive firewall rules, WebSocket handshake upgrades, and media storage asset routing. Prepare user identities and tokens A userID uniquely identifies an OpenIM user, while an authentication token validates that user session. Your business backend creates or links users, generates tokens, and verifies application permissions. The client app then consumes the credentials returned by your server. Before setting up your server, review Preparation /platform api/prepare to use api and Get user token /platform api/auth/tokens/get user token . If your product already manages an account system, your backend service should authenticate the user and return their corresponding userID , token , apiAddr , and wsAddr . Each token must match its corresponding userID . Never attempt to generate or assemble OpenIM tokens directly within client side application code. Prepare the plugin and HBuilderX Ensure your workspace meets the following setup requirements: Obtain the unix openim sdk distribution package matching your licensing agreement and target mobile operating systems. Use an HBuilderX and uni app / uni app x version compatible with the delivered UTS plugin. Place the entire uni modules/unix openim sdk folder into the uni modules/ directory of your project. Do not copy only the inner utssdk subfolder. Avoid installing multiple versions of unix openim sdk . Do not manually link standalone OpenIM Android AARs, iOS XCFrameworks, CocoaPods pods, or HarmonyOS HARs, as doing so leads to duplicate symbols and mismatched native dependencies. Always import SDK functions from the package root: import initSDK, login from '@/uni modules/unix openim sdk' Do not import directly from internal platform directories such as utssdk/app android , utssdk/app ios , or utssdk/app harmony . Prepare your native runtime environment The standard HBuilderX debugging base does not package native OpenIM binary libraries, so it cannot validate SDK initialization, login, message transmission, or real time event callbacks. During development, package a custom debugging base containing this plugin. Before releasing to production, perform physical device validation using formally compiled application builds. The SDK supports the following native platforms: Android : Supports Android 5.0 API level 21 and later. iOS : Supports iOS 14.0 and later. HarmonyOS : Supports API 24 and later, requiring the corresponding commercial release package. Web and Mini Programs : Not supported by this native UTS SDK. When your application requires access to the photo library, camera, microphone, local files, or push notifications, declare and request the appropriate system permissions in your host app manifest and runtime handlers. The SDK does not request permissions on behalf of unused application features. Pre production checklist Before releasing your application, verify that: The custom debugging base or release build contains the compiled OpenIM native binaries for your target platforms. Physical devices can reach apiAddr , wsAddr , and media upload/download domain endpoints. Your backend service returns matching userID and token pairs for each authenticating user. Your client architecture accounts for background/foreground transitions, network reconnections, token expirations, multi device sessions, and user logout/switch operations. The SDK stores SQLite data inside a writable sandbox directory rather than a temporary folder, shared external volume, or virtual web path. Next steps Once you satisfy these prerequisites, proceed to Integrate by project and platform /sdk/uniapp/getting started/environment specific implementation to install and configure the plugin. Next, complete Authenticate and manage a session /sdk/uniapp/getting started/authenticate and manage session . After confirming connectivity, verify the messaging flow with Send your first message /sdk/uniapp/getting started/send first message .

title: Integrate by project and platform
description: Install the UTS plugin in uni-app and uni-app x projects, and initialize Android, iOS, and HarmonyOS runtimes.
keywords: sdk uniapp v4 sdk uniapp getting-started environment-specific-implementation
content: Standard uni app Vue 2 / Vue 3 and uni app x share the same unix openim sdk plugin directory structure, root import path, and API declarations. Differences across target platforms are confined to native binary packages, build bases, platform identifiers, system runtime permissions, and specific HarmonyOS boundary behaviors. The underlying data models for users, relationships, conversations, groups, and messages remain identical. Before proceeding, complete the server, user credential, and environment preparations outlined in Before you start /sdk/uniapp/getting started/before you start . Platform compatibility matrix | Project type | Android | iOS | HarmonyOS | Web / Mini Programs | | | | | | | | uni app Vue 2 / Vue 3 | Supported | Supported | Commercial license required | Not supported | | uni app x | Supported | Supported | Commercial license required | Not supported | When targeting multiple platforms from a shared codebase, verify plugin installation, initialization, authentication, and core API calls within an Android custom debugging base first. Next, validate platform specific configurations and permissions using iOS and HarmonyOS custom bases or formal release builds. Always test against actual compiled binaries rather than relying on standard debugging bases or behavior observed on another platform. Install the UTS plugin Copy the delivered plugin directory into the uni modules/ folder of your host application: your project/ └── uni modules/ └── unix openim sdk/ ├── package.json └── utssdk/ If your project already contains an older version of the plugin, verify the version and source origin before overwriting files. Do not merge separate distribution versions. The delivered package already includes platform locked native binaries, so do not link secondary OpenIM Core libraries via Maven, CocoaPods, or OHPM. After copying the plugin files, compile a custom debugging base or generate a formal build. The standard HBuilderX base does not package native UTS libraries. Import APIs from the plugin root In both JavaScript/TypeScript pages in traditional uni app and UTS pages in uni app x, import public SDK symbols from the plugin root: import OpenIMLogLevelWarn, OpenIMPlatformAndroid, OpenIMPlatformHarmony, OpenIMPlatformIOS, initSDK, from '@/uni modules/unix openim sdk' Code examples throughout this documentation use UTS syntax. Traditional uni app pages use the exact same exported symbol names and signatures. Never import internal platform implementation files such as index.uts , Kotlin, Swift, or ArkTS files directly. Initialize the SDK Pass the exported platform constant matching your target operating system instead of a numeric literal: | Target platform | Platform constant | | | | | Android App | OpenIMPlatformAndroid | | iOS App | OpenIMPlatformIOS | | HarmonyOS App | OpenIMPlatformHarmony | The following example initializes the SDK for Android. For iOS or HarmonyOS, substitute the corresponding platform constant and run against that platform's custom debugging base or release build: Code example const initialized = await initSDK platformID: OpenIMPlatformAndroid, apiAddr: 'https://api.example.com', wsAddr: 'wss://ws.example.com', dataDir: '', logFilePath: '', logLevel: OpenIMLogLevelWarn, isLogStandardOutput: false, systemType: 'your app', if initialized throw new Error 'OpenIMClientSDK failed to initialize' Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | platformID | OpenIMPlatform | Yes | The current application platform identifier. Supply the exported constant. | | apiAddr | string | Yes | The OpenIMServer HTTP API endpoint. In production, provide an HTTPS address accessible from physical devices. | | wsAddr | string | Yes | The OpenIMServer WebSocket endpoint. In production, provide a WSS address accessible from physical devices. | | dataDir | string | No | Base directory for SDK local database storage. Pass an empty string to use the default writable application sandbox directory. | | logFilePath | string | No | Native file path for SDK logs. Pass an empty string if local log file persistence is not needed. | | logLevel | OpenIMLogLevel | Yes | SDK logging verbosity. For production environments, use OpenIMLogLevelWarn or OpenIMLogLevelError . | | isLogStandardOutput | boolean | Yes | Whether the native Core prints log output to standard out. Typically set to false in production. | | systemType | string | Yes | A stable application identifier string defined by your project conventions. | Return value The Promise resolves with a boolean value true indicating that the native initialization completed successfully. Initializing the SDK and authenticating a user are distinct steps: after calling initSDK , register connection event listeners and proceed with Authenticate and manage a session /sdk/uniapp/getting started/authenticate and manage session . Initializing successfully does not mean the client is connected to OpenIMServer. Manage storage and file paths Leave dataDir as an empty string under normal circumstances so the SDK automatically selects the default writable sandbox directory. Do not pass the uni.env.USER DATA PATH literal string, unifile:// URI schemas, component relative paths, temporary cache directories, or read only locations as the Core database path. File, image, audio, and video messaging APIs follow different file path rules: they accept both POSIX absolute paths readable within the app sandbox and unifile:// URIs generated from uni.env.USER DATA PATH . The UTS plugin normalizes these paths before passing them to the native Core. Ensure the target file exists on disk and that your application has granted file read permissions before calling media APIs. Platform specific considerations Android and iOS support all standard UTS APIs and event streams documented here. HarmonyOS capabilities depend on the licensed commercial distribution. HarmonyOS does not support updating FCM device tokens, and omits the three message extension events, the streaming media status change event Commercial , and message key value update events. Photo, camera, microphone, file system, and push notification permissions must be declared and requested by the host application. Installing the plugin does not automatically grant runtime permissions. Whenever you modify native build configurations or update plugin binaries, rebuild your custom debugging base. Older debugging bases will not automatically pick up native library updates. Release the SDK Invoke unInitSDK only when your application is shutting down or needs to completely release the active SDK instance. Do not initialize and tear down the SDK repeatedly across page lifecycles. When a user logs out, perform a logout flow and clean up event subscriptions as described in Authenticate and manage a session /sdk/uniapp/getting started/authenticate and manage session . import unInitSDK from '@/uni modules/unix openim sdk' unInitSDK Next steps Authenticate and manage a session /sdk/uniapp/getting started/authenticate and manage session Send your first message /sdk/uniapp/getting started/send first message

title: Authenticate and manage a session
description: Initialize the UTS plugin, log in as the current user, handle connection events, refresh tokens, and log out.
keywords: sdk uniapp v4 sdk uniapp getting-started authenticate-and-manage-session
content: The uni app / uni app x SDK initializes its native Core before establishing an active user session. Complete the prerequisites and plugin installation in Before you start /sdk/uniapp/getting started/before you start and Integrate by project and platform /sdk/uniapp/getting started/environment specific implementation before proceeding. The standard authentication lifecycle follows these steps: 1. Initialize the SDK for the target platform. 2. Register connection, token expiration, and kick out event listeners before attempting login. 3. Retrieve the current user's userID and token securely from your business backend. 4. Invoke login , wait for the Promise to resolve, and await onConnectSuccess to verify WebSocket connectivity. 5. Query user profiles, relationships, conversations, groups, and message history once the connection is established. 6. When logging out or switching accounts, call logout and clean up application state and event subscriptions. Initialize the SDK The following snippet illustrates SDK initialization for the login flow. Refer to Integrate by project and platform /sdk/uniapp/getting started/environment specific implementation for parameter details and directory rules: import OpenIMLogLevelWarn, OpenIMPlatformAndroid, initSDK, from '@/uni modules/unix openim sdk' await initSDK platformID: OpenIMPlatformAndroid, apiAddr, wsAddr, dataDir: '', logFilePath: '', logLevel: OpenIMLogLevelWarn, isLogStandardOutput: false, systemType: 'your app', A resolved initSDK Promise indicates that the native Core has initialized. It does not establish a user session or verify WebSocket connectivity. Register connection listeners before login Register listeners for connection lifecycle changes, token invalidations, and kick out events before calling login . Each registration method returns an OpenIMSDKEventSubscription reference for precise unsubscription: import off, onConnectFailed, onConnectSuccess, onConnecting, onKickedOffline, onUserTokenExpired, onUserTokenInvalid, from '@/uni modules/unix openim sdk' const handleConnecting = = setConnectionState 'connecting' const handleConnectSuccess = = setConnectionState 'connected' const handleConnectFailed = errCode: number, errMsg: string = setConnectionState 'failed' console.error 'OpenIMClientSDK connection failed:', errCode, errMsg const handleKickedOffline = = clearCurrentSession showSignedInElsewhereDialog const handleUserTokenExpired = = void refreshOpenIMToken const handleUserTokenInvalid = errCode: number, errMsg: string = console.error 'OpenIMClientSDK token invalid:', errCode, errMsg redirectToSignIn const connectingSubscription = onConnecting handleConnecting const connectSuccessSubscription = onConnectSuccess handleConnectSuccess const connectFailedSubscription = onConnectFailed handleConnectFailed const kickedOfflineSubscription = onKickedOffline handleKickedOffline const tokenExpiredSubscription = onUserTokenExpired handleUserTokenExpired const tokenInvalidSubscription = onUserTokenInvalid handleUserTokenInvalid The callback handlers for onConnectFailed and onUserTokenInvalid accept two arguments: a numeric errCode and a string errMsg . Other connection event handlers accept no parameters. Log in as the current user Pass the current user's userID and authentication token to login . Endpoint addresses and platform constants were already configured during initialization and do not need to be provided again: Code example import login from '@/uni modules/unix openim sdk' await login userID, token Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | userID | string | Yes | The unique identifier of the user logging in. | | token | string | Yes | The authentication token issued by your business backend for this user. | Return value The returned Promise resolves with void upon successful authentication verification. A resolved Promise indicates that the login request was authenticated by OpenIMServer. Once the client receives the onConnectSuccess event, the WebSocket channel is fully established, allowing you to invoke business APIs. Treat authentication success and connection availability as distinct lifecycle phases. If a user triggers login multiple times, reuse the active login task instead of launching concurrent requests. When switching accounts, await completion of logout before calling login with the new credentials. Handle Promise results and errors Async APIs in the UTS plugin return domain data directly without wrapper response envelopes. When an invocation fails, the returned Promise rejects with an error containing errCode and errMsg : import OpenIMError, getSelfUserInfo, from '@/uni modules/unix openim sdk' try const currentUser = await getSelfUserInfo useCurrentUser currentUser catch error const sdkError = error as OpenIMError console.error 'Failed to retrieve user profile:', sdkError.errCode, sdkError.errMsg A resolved query Promise returns a point in time snapshot. For state changing operations, resolution confirms completion of the specific action; update your UI in response to event notifications and query re calibration. Check login status Query the client's current authentication state and active user ID without passing parameters: import OpenIMLoginStatusLogged, getLoginStatus, getLoginUserID, from '@/uni modules/unix openim sdk' const status = await getLoginStatus if status == OpenIMLoginStatusLogged const currentUserID = await getLoginUserID restoreSessionFor currentUserID | Status | Description | | | | | OpenIMLoginStatusLogout | The SDK is currently logged out. | | OpenIMLoginStatusLogging | Login is currently in progress; avoid triggering parallel login attempts. | | OpenIMLoginStatusLogged | The user is authenticated; verify connection events before assuming network readiness. | getLoginUserID returns the user ID associated with the active session. This helper lets you ensure consistency between your application state and the SDK session, though it should not replace server side authentication. These queries do not trigger connection events. Update the authentication token When an existing token approaches expiration or your backend issues a refreshed credential, invoke updateToken : Code example import updateToken from '@/uni modules/unix openim sdk' const nextToken = await requestOpenIMTokenFromBackend await updateToken token: nextToken Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | token | string | Yes | The refreshed authentication token issued by your business backend. | Return value The Promise resolves with void once the SDK adopts the updated token. If the session has been kicked offline or the credential is fundamentally invalid, terminate the local session and prompt the user to sign in again. Log out When a user logs out or switches accounts, invoke logout . Reset local conversation lists, unread counters, and cached message state once the Promise resolves: import logout from '@/uni modules/unix openim sdk' await logout clearCurrentSession When an onKickedOffline event arrives, the SDK automatically terminates the active session. In that scenario, clean up application UI state and notify the user; do not invoke logout again. Clean up event subscriptions When unmounting components, switching accounts, or tearing down the SDK scope, cancel event listeners using the subscription references captured during registration: function removeSessionListeners off connectingSubscription off connectSuccessSubscription off connectFailedSubscription off kickedOfflineSubscription off tokenExpiredSubscription off tokenInvalidSubscription While offAll eventName unsubscribes all handlers for a given event, prefer off subscription within individual views to avoid inadvertently removing listeners managed by other modules. Next steps Send your first message /sdk/uniapp/getting started/send first message Integrate by project and platform /sdk/uniapp/getting started/environment specific implementation

title: Send your first message
description: Verify sending and receiving one-on-one and group text messages in uni-app and uni-app x.
keywords: sdk uniapp v4 sdk uniapp getting-started send-first-message
content: Send your first text message in a uni app or uni app x application to verify direct and group messaging pipelines. Before proceeding, complete the environment setup in Before you start /sdk/uniapp/getting started/before you start and authenticate following Authenticate and manage a session /sdk/uniapp/getting started/authenticate and manage session . OpenIM messages can be sent to individual users or groups. Direct messages specify the recipient user via recvID , while group messages specify the target group via groupID . Prepare target identifiers | Conversation type | Target identifier requirements | | | | | Direct one on one | An existing recipient user ID passed as recvID , with groupID set to an empty string. | | Group | An existing group ID passed as groupID , with recvID set to an empty string. | Sending your first message validates your complete integration pipeline. Before sending: Ensure the direct chat recipient user exists and server permissions permit communication. Ensure the target group exists, the current user is an active member, and group speaking privileges are not muted. Verify that your client received onConnectSuccess , rather than relying solely on the resolved login Promise. Import messaging APIs Import messaging methods from the plugin root: import createTextMessage, sendMessage, from '@/uni modules/unix openim sdk' Send a direct message Sending a message involves two steps: construct an unsent OpenIMMessageItem with Create a text message /sdk/uniapp/message/creating messages/create text message , then pass that item and the target identifier to Send a message /sdk/uniapp/message/sending messages/send message : async function sendFirstDirectMessage const message = await createTextMessage 'Hello, OpenIM' if message == null return const sentMessage = await sendMessage message, recvID: 'user b', groupID: '', offlinePushInfo: null, isOnlineOnly: false, appendOutgoingMessage sentMessage Replace user b with a valid recipient user ID. Do not pass user nicknames, phone numbers, or the current user's own userID as recvID . Send a group message When sending to a group, set groupID and leave recvID empty: async function sendFirstGroupMessage const message = await createTextMessage 'Hello everyone' if message == null return const sentMessage = await sendMessage message, recvID: '', groupID: 'group 123', offlinePushInfo: null, isOnlineOnly: false, appendOutgoingMessage sentMessage Replace group 123 with a valid OpenIM group ID. You can reuse an existing group or create one via the admin console, backend APIs, or SDK group methods. Understand send results Create a text message /sdk/uniapp/message/creating messages/create text message returns an uncommitted message object locally. If it returns null , do not call sendMessage . Creating a message does not transmit data over the network or trigger message events. Send a message /sdk/uniapp/message/sending messages/send message returns the updated OpenIMMessageItem . Resolution indicates the message has been committed and persisted by OpenIMServer. The sender can locate the message in local state using clientMsgID and mark its status as sent. The recipient client receives the message through real time message events. Verify both sending and receiving sides during integration. If sending fails, the Promise rejects with an error containing errCode and errMsg . Inspect the error details alongside OpenIMServer logs to troubleshoot. Verification checklist 1. Confirm the return status and clientMsgID on the sending client. 2. Verify receipt of the message event on a second logged in client. Determine the conversationID from the message payload and merge it into your active conversation view. 3. Test both direct and group conversations. 4. Simulate network disconnections and reconnections to verify automatic recovery and message replay. For event registration, listener cleanup, and conversation merging rules, see Receive messages /sdk/uniapp/message/receiving messages/receive messages . Next steps Authenticate and manage a session /sdk/uniapp/getting started/authenticate and manage session Integrate by project and platform /sdk/uniapp/getting started/environment specific implementation

title: User overview
description: Understand user profiles, account-level preferences, and online status in the UniApp SDK.
keywords: sdk uniapp v4 sdk uniapp user overview-user
content: The UniApp SDK identifies users using a unique userID . The user domain manages the authenticated account's profile, public user cards for other contacts, account wide message reception options, friend request permissions, and real time online presence. Relationships friends, applications, and blacklists belong to the separate relationship domain, while group nicknames and roles reside within the group domain. User data models The UTS plugin exports the following primary user data structures: | Type | Intended context | How to obtain | | | | | | OpenIMUserInfo | The currently logged in user profile; also serves as the base structure for public cards | Get your profile /sdk/uniapp/user/profile/get self user info , Get user profiles /sdk/uniapp/user/profile/get users info | | OpenIMPublicUserItem | Public profile for other application users alias of OpenIMUserInfo | Get user profiles /sdk/uniapp/user/profile/get users info | | OpenIMFriendUserItem | Friend profile including friend remarks, pinned status, and custom extension strings | Friend query APIs in the relationships domain | | OpenIMBlackUserItem | Blocked user profile stored within the current account's blacklist | Blacklist query APIs in the relationships domain | | OpenIMUserStatusItem | Aggregated online connectivity status and active client platforms for a user | Online status subscription and query APIs | A single userID can exist simultaneously as a public user, friend contact, blacklisted user, and group member. Render stranger profiles using OpenIMPublicUserItem ; render contact rosters using OpenIMFriendUserItem ; render group rosters using OpenIMGroupMemberItem ; and display conversation headers using showName from the conversation object. Do not overwrite fields across distinct domains. User profile APIs Get user profiles /sdk/uniapp/user/profile/get users info : Batch query public profile records for other users by userID . Get your profile /sdk/uniapp/user/profile/get self user info : Retrieve nickname, avatar URL, extension data, and global message reception options for the active session. Update your profile /sdk/uniapp/user/profile/set self info : Update nickname, avatar URL, or custom extension attributes for the authenticated user. Set global message reception /sdk/uniapp/user/profile/set global message reception : Configure account level notification and reception behaviors. Set friend request permissions /sdk/uniapp/user/profile/set friend add permission : Choose how your account responds to incoming friend requests. Online status APIs Subscribe to online status /sdk/uniapp/user/online status/subscribe users status : Subscribe to presence updates for targeted users and monitor status events. Get subscribed user status /sdk/uniapp/user/online status/get subscribe users status : Query current presence snapshots for actively subscribed users. Unsubscribe from online status /sdk/uniapp/user/online status/unsubscribe users status : Stop tracking presence for users no longer visible in the UI. Online presence indicates whether a user maintains an active WebSocket session with OpenIMServer; it does not indicate whether they are viewing the app, a specific conversation, or a particular message. For typing indicators or business presence such as "in a meeting" , use dedicated business signals rather than inferring state from WebSocket connectivity. State synchronization principles Load baseline snapshots via query APIs when initializing screens, then merge incoming updates through domain events. Merge current user profiles by matching userID . When online status events arrive with multiple OpenIMUserStatusItem records, iterate and merge each item into your state by userID . Promise resolution, event delivery, and re queries represent three distinct phases. After a mutation Promise resolves, update UI state via the corresponding event, or call the query API to re calibrate immediately.

title: Get user profiles
description: Batch query public account-level profiles for application users by userID.
keywords: sdk uniapp v4 sdk uniapp user profile get-users-info
content: Invoke getUsersInfo to batch retrieve public account level profiles for specified userID values. This method is ideal for rendering stranger profile cards, contact search results, or message sender information. If your application supports searching users by nickname, phone number, organization, or email address, execute that search on your business backend first, then pass the resolved candidate userID array to the SDK. The SDK queries public profiles strictly by user ID. Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | userIDs | string | Yes | An array of OpenIM user IDs to retrieve. | Deduplicate and filter out empty strings before calling this method, and paginate or chunk requests based on your UI requirements. Code example import getUsersInfo from '@/uni modules/unix openim sdk' const userIDs = 'user a', 'user b' const result = await getUsersInfo userIDs const users = result?.users ?? users.forEach user = usersByID.set user.userID, user Return value The Promise resolves with an OpenIMUserListResult | null object. When non null, the users array contains OpenIMUserInfo objects OpenIMPublicUserItem is a type alias for this structure . | Property | Type | Description | | | | | | userID | string | OpenIM user ID. | | nickname | string | Public account level display nickname. | | faceURL | string | Public avatar image URL. | | ex | string | Custom extension string formatted according to your application rules. | | createTime | number \| null | Account creation timestamp in Unix milliseconds. | | attachedInfo | string \| null | Additional SDK internal metadata. | | globalRecvMsgOpt | OpenIMMessageReceiveOption \| null | Account level message reception option for this user. This is private to the user and should not be displayed on stranger profile cards. | | addFriendPermission Commercial | OpenIMAddFriendPermission \| null | Account level friend request policy. Consume only when relevant to business logic; do not display on general cards. | The returned array might not contain entries for all requested IDs if some users do not exist. Map results using the returned userID property rather than relying on array indices. Refresh user profiles Re invoke this API when opening profile dialogs, performing manual pull to refresh actions, reconnecting to the network, or receiving push notifications that user records have changed. The UTS plugin does not broadcast a universal profile change event for arbitrary public users. Updates to the authenticated user's profile are handled via Update your profile /sdk/uniapp/user/profile/set self info . In friend rosters, prefer OpenIMFriendUserItem returned by friend APIs, which includes friend remarks and relationship data. In group rosters, use OpenIMGroupMemberItem , which reflects group specific nicknames and member roles. Do not overwrite friend remarks or group nicknames with public account nicknames. Search and retrieve contacts A typical workflow searches via your backend before loading profiles through the SDK: async function loadFriendCandidates keyword: string const userIDs = await searchUserIDsFromBackend keyword if userIDs.length == 0 return const result = await getUsersInfo userIDs return result?.users ?? If your UI only supports exact user ID lookups, pass the user input directly as a userID . Perform fuzzy queries and attribute filtering on your server. Next steps Get your profile /sdk/uniapp/user/profile/get self user info Update your profile /sdk/uniapp/user/profile/set self info

title: Get your profile
description: Query the account-level profile and message reception settings of the authenticated user.
keywords: sdk uniapp v4 sdk uniapp user profile get-self-user-info
content: Invoke getSelfUserInfo to retrieve the account profile of the currently authenticated user. This method accepts no parameters. Code example import getSelfUserInfo from '@/uni modules/unix openim sdk' const currentUser = await getSelfUserInfo if currentUser = null setCurrentUser currentUser Return value The Promise resolves with an OpenIMUserInfo | null object: | Property | Type | Description | | | | | | userID | string | The authenticated user's OpenIM user ID. | | nickname | string | Account level display nickname. | | faceURL | string | Account level avatar URL. | | ex | string | Custom extension string agreed upon by application conventions. | | createTime | number \| null | Account creation timestamp in Unix milliseconds. | | attachedInfo | string \| null | Additional internal SDK metadata. | | globalRecvMsgOpt | OpenIMMessageReceiveOption \| null | Account level message reception option. See Set global message reception /sdk/uniapp/user/profile/set global message reception for valid values. | | addFriendPermission Commercial | OpenIMAddFriendPermission \| null | Friend request handling policy. See Set friend request permissions /sdk/uniapp/user/profile/set friend add permission for valid values. | Always compare options against exported SDK constants rather than checking raw numeric literals. State changes after the call This is a read only query that retrieves a local snapshot without modifying data or triggering events. When profile updates occur across sessions or devices, the SDK emits onSelfInfoUpdated . For event registration and unregistration patterns, see Update your profile /sdk/uniapp/user/profile/set self info . When switching user accounts, clear the active user profile from your application store before retrieving data for the new account.

title: Update your profile
description: Update the nickname, avatar URL, or account-level extension string of the authenticated user.
keywords: sdk uniapp v4 sdk uniapp user profile set-self-info
content: Invoke setSelfInfo to update display attributes for the currently logged in user. Pass only the properties being modified nickname , faceURL , or ex ; avoid accidentally overriding account level policy fields when saving a nickname or avatar. Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | nickname | string \| null | No | New account level display nickname. | | faceURL | string \| null | No | New account level avatar URL. | | ex | string \| null | No | New custom extension string; completely overwrites the previous value. | Supply at least one field to update. Code example import setSelfInfo from '@/uni modules/unix openim sdk' await setSelfInfo nickname: nickname.trim , faceURL, ex: mergedExtra, The ex property stores an opaque string. The SDK does not perform JSON patching. When multiple application modules share this attribute, read the current profile, merge changes into your application namespace, and submit the entire serialized string. Account level policy fields are documented in dedicated guides: refer to Set global message reception /sdk/uniapp/user/profile/set global message reception for notification preferences and Set friend request permissions /sdk/uniapp/user/profile/set friend add permission for friend authorization policies. Submit these settings from their dedicated preference screens. Return value The Promise resolves with void once OpenIMServer accepts the profile modification request. State changes after the call A resolved Promise confirms that the profile update was accepted by OpenIMServer. It does not indicate that the profile update event has propagated to other devices or clients. To synchronize state immediately, await the event callback or call Get your profile /sdk/uniapp/user/profile/get self user info to re calibrate. Monitor profile updates Register the onSelfInfoUpdated event to observe profile changes for the active account. The callback delivers an updated OpenIMUserInfo | null object. When non null, replace the cached profile matching userID : import OpenIMUserInfo, off, onSelfInfoUpdated, from '@/uni modules/unix openim sdk' const handleSelfInfoUpdated = user: OpenIMUserInfo | null = if user == null return setCurrentUser user const selfInfoSubscription = onSelfInfoUpdated handleSelfInfoUpdated function removeSelfInfoListener off selfInfoSubscription Unsubscribe from this listener when logging out, switching accounts, or tearing down the user store to prevent duplicate event execution.

title: Set global message reception
description: Configure account-level default message reception and notification options across all conversations.
keywords: sdk uniapp v4 sdk uniapp user profile set-global-message-reception
content: The globalRecvMsgOpt property defines the account level default message notification policy across all conversations. Because this preference is separate from display attributes like nicknames and avatars, update it independently from a dedicated settings screen. Parameters The globalRecvMsgOpt parameter accepts values of type OpenIMMessageReceiveOption . For account level configuration, use the following options: | Enum constant | Numeric value | Description | | | | | | OpenIMMessageReceiveOptionReceive | 0 | Normal message reception; notifications and offline push alerts are permitted. | | OpenIMMessageReceiveOptionReceiveWithoutNotification | 2 | Messages are received silently without offline push or local notification alerts Do Not Disturb . | Pass OpenIMMessageReceiveOptionReceive to disable account wide Do Not Disturb, or OpenIMMessageReceiveOptionReceiveWithoutNotification to enable it. Note that OpenIMMessageReceiveOptionDoNotReceive is reserved for specific conversation overrides and should not be offered as an account level setting. Code example import OpenIMMessageReceiveOptionReceiveWithoutNotification, setSelfInfo, from '@/uni modules/unix openim sdk' await setSelfInfo globalRecvMsgOpt: OpenIMMessageReceiveOptionReceiveWithoutNotification, Conversation level recvMsgOpt settings provide finer grained overrides. When both account level and conversation level settings are present, the SDK evaluates them hierarchically; always display the computed state returned by the SDK or server. Return value The Promise resolves with void once OpenIMServer updates the account preference. State changes after the call A resolved Promise confirms that the server accepted the setting. It does not indicate that the profile update event has completed across all local stores. For event registration and userID state merging, see Update your profile /sdk/uniapp/user/profile/set self info . To re verify current settings immediately, invoke Get your profile /sdk/uniapp/user/profile/get self user info .

title: Set friend request permissions
description: Configure approval policies for incoming friend requests directed to the authenticated user.
keywords: sdk uniapp v4 sdk uniapp user profile set-friend-add-permission
content: The addFriendPermission property configures whether other users can add the current account directly, require approval, or are blocked from sending friend requests. This account level setting is a commercial feature and should be configured through a dedicated privacy preference interface. Parameters The addFriendPermission parameter accepts values of type OpenIMAddFriendPermission : | Enum constant | Numeric value | Description | | | | | | OpenIMAddFriendPermissionAllowed | 0 | Other users may submit friend requests, which require manual review by the current user. | | OpenIMAddFriendPermissionAllowedNoReview | 1 | Other users can add this account as a friend immediately without manual approval. | | OpenIMAddFriendPermissionDenied | 2 | Other users are blocked from submitting friend requests to this account. | Code example import OpenIMAddFriendPermissionAllowed, setSelfInfo, from '@/uni modules/unix openim sdk' await setSelfInfo addFriendPermission: OpenIMAddFriendPermissionAllowed, This configuration applies exclusively to subsequent friend requests. It does not alter existing friendships or auto accept, reject, or purge pending friend applications. Return value The Promise resolves with void once OpenIMServer updates the account permission. State changes after the call A resolved Promise confirms that the policy has been updated on OpenIMServer. It does not mean the user profile update event has finished propagating to other active clients. For event registration and userID cache updating, see Update your profile /sdk/uniapp/user/profile/set self info . To verify the active policy immediately, invoke Get your profile /sdk/uniapp/user/profile/get self user info and inspect addFriendPermission .

title: Subscribe to online status
description: Subscribe to presence updates for targeted users and monitor subsequent status transitions.
keywords: sdk uniapp v4 sdk uniapp user online-status subscribe-users-status
content: Online presence indicates whether a user maintains an active connection to OpenIMServer; it does not indicate whether they are viewing the application, reading a conversation, or interacting with a specific message. Subscribe only to users currently visible on screen or strictly required by active views. An account can subscribe to a maximum of 3,000 users simultaneously. Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | userIDs | string | Yes | An array of user IDs to subscribe to. | Filter out empty strings and duplicates before calling subscribeUsersStatus . Never attempt to subscribe to an entire enterprise user directory at once. Code example import getSubscribeUsersStatus, subscribeUsersStatus, from '@/uni modules/unix openim sdk' const visibleUserIDs = 'user a', 'user b' await subscribeUsersStatus visibleUserIDs const current = await getSubscribeUsersStatus const states = current?.statuses ?? states.forEach state = presenceByUserID.set state.userID, state Return value The Promise resolves with a string operation confirmation rather than the immediate presence list. After subscribing, invoke Get subscribed user status /sdk/uniapp/user/online status/get subscribe users status to establish baseline presence records, then update your cache as events arrive. Presence data structure The OpenIMUserStatusItem object contains the following properties: | Property | Type | Description | | | | | | userID | string | The user ID associated with this status record; use this as the primary cache key. | | status | OpenIMOnlineState | Aggregated connectivity state. Check against OpenIMOnlineStateOnline or OpenIMOnlineStateOffline . | | platformIDs | OpenIMPlatform | List of platform identifiers where this user currently maintains active sessions. | The status field represents aggregated connectivity across all devices. When displaying per platform indicators such as mobile or desktop icons , inspect platformIDs and compare values against SDK constants like OpenIMPlatformAndroid , OpenIMPlatformIOS , or OpenIMPlatformHarmony . Monitor presence changes Register onUserStatusChanged to observe real time presence changes. The callback receives an OpenIMUserStatusListResult | null object containing one or more user status entries. Iterate through statuses and merge each record by userID : import OpenIMUserStatusListResult, off, onUserStatusChanged, from '@/uni modules/unix openim sdk' const handleUserStatusChanged = result: OpenIMUserStatusListResult | null, = if result == null return result.statuses.forEach state = presenceByUserID.set state.userID, state const userStatusSubscription = onUserStatusChanged handleUserStatusChanged, function removeUserStatusListener off userStatusSubscription Unsubscribe from this listener when logging out, switching accounts, or tearing down the presence manager. When pagination changes or contacts leave the viewport, unsubscribe those users to prevent your subscription set from growing unboundedly. Next steps Get subscribed user status /sdk/uniapp/user/online status/get subscribe users status Unsubscribe from online status /sdk/uniapp/user/online status/unsubscribe users status

title: Get subscribed user status
description: Retrieve presence snapshots for users currently subscribed to by the active account.
keywords: sdk uniapp v4 sdk uniapp user online-status get-subscribe-users-status
content: Invoke getSubscribeUsersStatus to retrieve a presence snapshot of all users currently subscribed to by the active session. This method accepts no parameters. Code example import getSubscribeUsersStatus from '@/uni modules/unix openim sdk' const result = await getSubscribeUsersStatus const states = result?.statuses ?? states.forEach state = presenceByUserID.set state.userID, state Return value The Promise resolves with an OpenIMUserStatusListResult | null object. The statuses array contains OpenIMUserStatusItem elements, each containing userID , aggregated status , and active platformIDs . For data property details, see Subscribe to online status /sdk/uniapp/user/online status/subscribe users status . State changes after the call This is a read only query that retrieves a local snapshot without modifying data or triggering presence events. If a user has not yet been subscribed to, call Subscribe to online status /sdk/uniapp/user/online status/subscribe users status first. Do not assume an omitted user is offline; verify that a subscription exists for their ID. Re query this method when initializing presence views, recovering from network disconnection, or re synchronizing application state. Real time incremental transitions are streamed via onUserStatusChanged as detailed in Subscribe to online status /sdk/uniapp/user/online status/subscribe users status .

title: Unsubscribe from online status
description: Stop receiving presence updates for targeted users.
keywords: sdk uniapp v4 sdk uniapp user online-status unsubscribe-users-status
content: Invoke unsubscribeUsersStatus to stop tracking presence updates for specific users. When contacts paginate out of view, search queries change, or user views unmount, unsubscribe from those IDs promptly to keep the active subscription set bounded. Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | userIDs | string | Yes | An array of user IDs to unsubscribe from. | Deduplicate array entries and remove empty values before calling this method. Code example import unsubscribeUsersStatus from '@/uni modules/unix openim sdk' const userIDs = 'user a', 'user b' await unsubscribeUsersStatus userIDs userIDs.forEach userID = presenceByUserID.delete userID Return value The Promise resolves with a string operation confirmation upon successful deregistration. It does not return updated status payloads. State changes after the call A resolved Promise confirms that OpenIMServer removed the specified users from the active subscription set. The application should immediately remove those userID keys from its local tracking set and presence state without waiting for events to confirm the removal. Unsubscribing from presence updates does not affect user profiles, friendship records, or conversation history. To resume tracking these users in the future, call Subscribe to online status /sdk/uniapp/user/online status/subscribe users status . When logging out or destroying the global presence manager, invoke off subscription to remove the event listener entirely. Unsubscribing individual users and tearing down the global listener are distinct operations.

title: Get the friend list
description: Query the authenticated user’s friends and relationship profiles with pagination.
keywords: sdk uniapp v4 sdk uniapp user friends get-friend-list-page
content: Invoke getFriendListPage to retrieve a paginated snapshot of the authenticated user's friend list. Start with offset: 0 for the first page, and increment the offset by the number of received records for subsequent pages. Reset pagination and re query after additions or deletions occur. Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | offset | number | Yes | Pagination offset index; pass 0 for the initial page. | | count | number | Yes | Number of friend records to retrieve in this page. | The UTS pagination parameters do not include filterBlack . Friends and blacklisted contacts are maintained as distinct data sets; determine whether a friend is blacklisted by matching their userID against the list returned by Get the blacklist /sdk/uniapp/user/blacklist/get black list .
