Treat this signal as an invalidation trigger to reload current group history rather than relying on unexposed payload fields. import off, onDeleteUserAllMsgsInConv, from '@/uni modules/unix openim sdk' const handleUserMessagesDeleted = payload: string = reloadCurrentGroupHistory const userMessagesDeletedSubscription = onDeleteUserAllMsgsInConv handleUserMessagesDeleted function removeUserMessagesDeletedListener off userMessagesDeletedSubscription Promise resolution, event delivery, and re querying the conversation history are three decoupled phases. Unregister the listener when unmounting views or switching accounts.

title: Clear all messages
description: Clear all messages stored both locally and on the server for the authenticated account.
keywords: sdk uniapp v4 sdk uniapp message managing-messages clear-all-messages
content: Invoke deleteAllMsgFromLocalAndSvr to purge all message records both from local device storage and from the server for the authenticated user across all conversations. This method accepts no parameters. Code example import deleteAllMsgFromLocalAndSvr from '@/uni modules/unix openim sdk' await deleteAllMsgFromLocalAndSvr resetAllMessageState Return value The Promise resolves with void upon successful completion. State changes after the call This is an irreversible, account wide operation. When the Promise resolves, clear all cached messages, search indices, pagination cursors, and message summaries across all conversations conversationID . This operation does not delete message copies held by other conversation participants, nor does it guarantee that other devices logged into the same account have completed UI updates. Subsequent conversation events will deliver updated conversation summaries keyed by conversationID . Re query conversation lists if necessary to calibrate state.

title: Delete a local message
description: Delete a single message exclusively from local device storage.
keywords: sdk uniapp v4 sdk uniapp message managing-messages delete-local-message
content: Invoke deleteMessageFromLocalStorage to remove a single message record exclusively from the local device database without affecting server side storage or other chat participants. Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | conversationID | string | Yes | Identifier of the conversation containing the message. | | clientMsgID | string | Yes | The clientMsgID of the message to delete. | Code example import deleteMessageFromLocalStorage from '@/uni modules/unix openim sdk' const clientMsgID = message.clientMsgID if clientMsgID == null return await deleteMessageFromLocalStorage conversationID, clientMsgID, removeMessage conversationID, clientMsgID Both parameters must originate from verified conversation and message structures. Ensure clientMsgID is non null before invoking the method. Return value The Promise resolves with void upon successful local deletion. State changes after the call Promise resolution indicates that the message record was purged from the local database. Immediately remove the message from your UI model using conversationID:clientMsgID . Because the server copy remains intact, clearing app data or switching devices may cause the message to re synchronize. This call does not trigger notifications to other participants. To retract a message for everyone, see Revoke a message /sdk/uniapp/message/managing messages/revoke a message .

title: Clear all local messages
description: Clear all messages stored on the local device for the authenticated account.
keywords: sdk uniapp v4 sdk uniapp message managing-messages clear-all-local-messages
content: Invoke deleteAllMsgFromLocal to clear all cached message records across all conversations stored on the local device for the currently authenticated account. This method accepts no parameters. Code example import deleteAllMsgFromLocal from '@/uni modules/unix openim sdk' await deleteAllMsgFromLocal resetAllMessageState Return value The Promise resolves with void upon successful local deletion. State changes after the call This is an irreversible, account level local database operation. After the Promise resolves, empty all in memory message lists, search indexes, pagination cursors, and unread counters across all conversations conversationID . This call does not notify other devices, affect other chat members, or trigger message deletion events. Because server copies may remain intact, re logging in or resynchronizing after clearing data may repopulate history. To wipe messages for a single specific conversation only, use Clear conversation messages /sdk/uniapp/conversation/managing conversations/clear conversation messages instead.

title: Insert a local single-chat message
description: Insert a message record directly into the local database for a single-chat conversation.
keywords: sdk uniapp v4 sdk uniapp message managing-messages insert-local-single-message
content: Invoke insertSingleMessageToLocalStorage to write a message item directly into the local device database for a single chat, suitable for device local system prompts, security reminders, or legacy data migration. Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | message | OpenIMMessageItem | Yes | Fully constructed message object created via a message creation method. | | recvID | string | Yes | Recipient user ID for the single chat. | | sendID | string | Yes | Sender user ID for the single chat. | Code example import createTextMessage, insertSingleMessageToLocalStorage, from '@/uni modules/unix openim sdk' const message = await createTextMessage 'Local notice' if message == null return await insertSingleMessageToLocalStorage message, recvID: targetUserID, sendID: currentUserID, The sendID and recvID parameters must match the participants of the target single chat session. Return value The Promise resolves with void upon successful insertion into the local database. State changes after the call Promise resolution indicates that the message record was written to the local database. Update your local list state using conversationID:clientMsgID . This call does not send network packets, trigger push notifications, or emit new message events. To transmit messages to remote peers, use Send a message /sdk/uniapp/message/sending messages/send message .

title: Insert a local group message
description: Insert a message record directly into the local database for a group chat.
keywords: sdk uniapp v4 sdk uniapp message managing-messages insert-local-group-message
content: Invoke insertGroupMessageToLocalStorage to inject a message directly into the local database for a group conversation. This is suitable for device local administrative notices, system hints, or data migration records. Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | message | OpenIMMessageItem | Yes | Fully constructed message object created via a message creation method. | | groupID | string | Yes | Identifier of the target group. | | sendID | string | Yes | Sender user ID for the message. | Code example import insertGroupMessageToLocalStorage from '@/uni modules/unix openim sdk' await insertGroupMessageToLocalStorage message, groupID, sendID: currentUserID, The groupID and sendID must match the target group conversation and sender identity accurately. Return value The Promise resolves with void upon successful insertion into the local database. State changes after the call Promise resolution indicates that the message was saved to local storage. Update your local view model using groupID:clientMsgID . This call does not deliver messages to fellow group members, trigger push alerts, or emit new message events. To transmit messages to group members across the network, use Send a message /sdk/uniapp/message/sending messages/send message .

title: Set message local extension
description: Store custom device-local extension strings on a message without synchronizing across devices.
keywords: sdk uniapp v4 sdk uniapp message managing-messages set-message-local-ex
content: The localEx property persists data exclusively on the local device, making it ideal for UI state such as folded states, selection checkboxes, local origin tags, or cached voice transcription text. It is never transmitted across the network or synchronized to other devices. Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | conversationID | string | Yes | Identifier of the conversation containing the message. | | clientMsgID | string | Yes | The clientMsgID of the target message. | | localEx | string | Yes | Complete serialized local extension string to store. | The SDK does not merge JSON properties automatically. If multiple application components use localEx , parse the existing string, update the relevant properties, and serialize the complete payload back into localEx to avoid clobbering existing data. Code example import setMessageLocalEx from '@/uni modules/unix openim sdk' const clientMsgID = message.clientMsgID if clientMsgID == null return const nextLocalEx = JSON.stringify selected: true, transcript: 'Transcribed text', await setMessageLocalEx conversationID, clientMsgID, localEx: nextLocalEx, Return value The Promise resolves with void upon successful local database persistence. State changes after the call Promise resolution indicates that the local database record was updated. Update the localEx property in your active message list item keyed by conversationID:clientMsgID . This operation does not emit shared network message events.

title: Get pinned messages
description: Retrieve the list of pinned messages for a specific conversation.
keywords: sdk uniapp v4 sdk uniapp message managing-messages get-pinned-messages
content: Retrieving pinned messages is a Commercial Edition capability. Query the pinned messages currently active in a conversation by supplying its conversationID . Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | conversationID | string | Yes | Identifier of the target conversation. | Code example import getConversationPinnedMsg from '@/uni modules/unix openim sdk' const result = await getConversationPinnedMsg conversationID const messages = result?.message ?? replacePinnedMessages conversationID, messages Return value The Promise resolves with an OpenIMGetConversationPinnedMsgResult | null object. Notice that the array of pinned message items is named message OpenIMMessageItem . Deduplicate and merge items into your banner models using clientMsgID . State changes after the call This call returns a point in time snapshot and does not emit events. To track live pin and unpin actions, listen for pinned message change events as described in Pin or unpin a message /sdk/uniapp/message/managing messages/set message pinned .

title: Pin or unpin a message
description: Pin or unpin a specific message to the top of a conversation and handle pinned message events.
keywords: sdk uniapp v4 sdk uniapp message managing-messages set-message-pinned
content: Pinning messages is a Commercial Edition capability. Invoke setConversationPinnedMsg with pinned: true to pin a message to the top banner of a conversation, or pinned: false to unpin it. Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | conversationID | string | Yes | Identifier of the conversation containing the message. | | clientMsgID | string | Yes | The clientMsgID of the message to pin or unpin. | | pinned | boolean | Yes | Pass true to pin the message, or false to unpin it. | Caller permissions, supported message types, and maximum pin counts are strictly verified by OpenIMServer. Code example import setConversationPinnedMsg from '@/uni modules/unix openim sdk' const clientMsgID = message.clientMsgID if clientMsgID == null return await setConversationPinnedMsg conversationID, clientMsgID, pinned: true, Return value The Promise resolves with void upon successful server processing. Listen for pinned message changes Centrally register onChangedPinnedMsg to observe changes in pinned messages. The event delivers an opaque string notification signal. Treat this signal as an invalidation trigger to re query the pinned messages for the active conversation rather than parsing undocumented properties. import off, onChangedPinnedMsg from '@/uni modules/unix openim sdk' const handlePinnedMessagesChanged = payload: string = reloadPinnedMessagesForCurrentConversation const pinnedMessagesSubscription = onChangedPinnedMsg handlePinnedMessagesChanged function removePinnedMessagesListener off pinnedMessagesSubscription For query implementation details, see Get pinned messages /sdk/uniapp/message/managing messages/get pinned messages . Unregister the listener when unmounting the view, logging out, or switching accounts.

title: Send group read receipts
description: Report member-level read receipts for group messages and listen for group read status changes.
keywords: sdk uniapp v4 sdk uniapp message managing-read-status send-group-read-receipts
content: Member level group read receipts are a Commercial Edition capability. All messages submitted in a single batch must belong strictly to the specified group conversation. Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | conversationID | string | Yes | Target group conversation ID. | | clientMsgIDs | string | Yes | Array of clientMsgID values marking visible read messages. | Code example import sendGroupMessageReadReceipt from '@/uni modules/unix openim sdk' await sendGroupMessageReadReceipt conversationID, clientMsgIDs: visibleUnreadMessageIDs, Do not mix message IDs from different conversations, and avoid sending receipts for messages that have not yet scrolled into visible view. Return value The Promise resolves with void upon successful server processing. State changes after the call Promise resolution indicates that the receipt report was processed by the server; it does not mean other client devices have finished rendering reader updates. Conversation unread counts are maintained separately by conversation level read operations; this method exclusively tracks member level reader details in groups. Listen for group read receipt changes Centrally register onRecvGroupReadReceipt to monitor group read receipts. The event provides an opaque string notification signal. Treat this signal as an invalidation trigger to re query the reader breakdown for currently visible group messages. import off, onRecvGroupReadReceipt from '@/uni modules/unix openim sdk' const handleGroupReadReceipt = payload: string = reloadVisibleGroupMessageReaders const groupReadReceiptSubscription = onRecvGroupReadReceipt handleGroupReadReceipt function removeGroupReadReceiptListener off groupReadReceiptSubscription Reporting receipts, receipt event arrival, and querying readers via Get group message readers /sdk/uniapp/message/managing read status/get group message readers represent three decoupled stages. Unregister the listener when leaving the conversation or switching accounts.

title: Get group message readers
description: Query paginated lists of group members who have read or not read a specific message.
keywords: sdk uniapp v4 sdk uniapp message managing-read-status get-group-message-readers
content: Tracking member level group read status is a Commercial Edition capability. Query group members who have either read or not read a specific message using pagination. Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | conversationID | string | Yes | Target group conversation ID. | | clientMsgID | string | Yes | The clientMsgID of the message being queried. | | filter | OpenIMGroupMessageReaderFilter | Yes | Use OpenIMGroupMessageReaderFilterRead for readers, or OpenIMGroupMessageReaderFilterUnread for unread members. | | offset | number | Yes | Pagination offset; supply 0 for the first page. | | count | number | Yes | Maximum number of members to fetch in this page. | Code example import OpenIMGroupMessageReaderFilterRead, getGroupMessageReaderList, from '@/uni modules/unix openim sdk' const clientMsgID = message.clientMsgID if clientMsgID == null return const result = await getGroupMessageReaderList conversationID, clientMsgID, filter: OpenIMGroupMessageReaderFilterRead, offset: 0, count: 50, const readers = result?.readers ?? Return value The Promise resolves with an OpenIMGetGroupMessageReaderListResult | null object. Retrieved member records are available in readers OpenIMGroupMemberItem . Deduplicate and merge members using groupID:userID . When the returned array contains fewer items than count , the end of the member list has been reached. State changes after the call This call retrieves a point in time snapshot and does not emit receipt events. To stay updated with incoming read receipts, listen to the read receipt events documented in Send group read receipts /sdk/uniapp/message/managing read status/send group read receipts .

title: Upload a file
description: Upload local files independently with the UniApp SDK and retrieve remote resource URLs.
keywords: sdk uniapp v4 sdk uniapp file-uploads upload-file
content: The file upload capability functions as an independent asset uploader for user avatars, group icons, profile attachments, or general application assets. It operates independently of the messaging pipeline and does not automatically construct or transmit messages. Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | filepath | string | Yes | Local file path readable by the native SDK. | | name | string | Yes | Filename including file extension. | | contentType | string | Yes | The MIME type of the file. | | uuid | string | Yes | A unique task identifier generated by the client for this upload. | | cancelID | string \| null | No | Identifier used to abort the upload; generate and store this before invoking the upload if cancellation is required. | | cause | string \| null | No | Optional business context or reason for the upload. | Temporary file paths obtained from the photo picker, document picker, or audio recorder can be uploaded directly, but the OS may purge temporary directories at any time. When implementing retry logic or requiring local persistence, move the file into uni.env.USER DATA PATH via uni.getFileSystemManager before persisting the path. Code example import uploadFile from '@/uni modules/unix openim sdk' const uploadTaskID = avatar $ Date.now const cancelID = cancel $ uploadTaskID const result = await uploadFile filepath: selectedImagePath, name: 'avatar.jpg', contentType: 'image/jpeg', uuid: uploadTaskID, cancelID, if result?.url = null await updateProfileAvatar result.url Return value The Promise resolves with an OpenIMUploadFileResult | null object: | Property | Type | Description | | | | | | url | string \| null | Public remote URL for the uploaded resource. | | uri | string \| null | Internal storage identifier or path returned by the server. | | uuid | string \| null | Task identifier matching the upload request. | | size | number \| null | File size reported by the storage backend. | | typ | number \| null | Storage resource type integer. | | mediaID | string \| null | Storage media identifier. | Only consume non null properties required by your application. A resolved Promise confirms that the binary upload succeeded; it does not update a user profile or create a message. Trigger subsequent operations explicitly. Monitor upload progress The onUploadFileProgress event provides an OpenIMUploadFileProgressEvent | null object containing only progress without a task identifier. Because the event payload does not include a task ID, avoid concurrent uploads if you need to track individual file percentages accurately. For multi file flows, serialize uploads or limit concurrency. import OpenIMUploadFileProgressEvent, off, onUploadFileProgress, from '@/uni modules/unix openim sdk' const handleUploadProgress = event: OpenIMUploadFileProgressEvent | null, = if event == null return setCurrentUploadProgress event.progress const uploadProgressSubscription = onUploadFileProgress handleUploadProgress // Clean up when destroying view models or switching sessions: off uploadProgressSubscription To abort an in flight upload task, pass the saved cancelID to Cancel a file upload /sdk/uniapp/file uploads/cancel upload .

title: Cancel a file upload
description: Abort an active file upload task using its cancellation identifier.
keywords: sdk uniapp v4 sdk uniapp file-uploads cancel-upload
content: When initiating an upload with Upload a file /sdk/uniapp/file uploads/upload file , supply a unique cancelID . You can subsequently invoke cancelUpload with that same identifier to abort the in flight transfer. The client runtime uses cancelID to target and terminate the specific upload task. Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | cancelID | string | Yes | The unique cancellation identifier provided when the upload was initiated. | Code example import cancelUpload from '@/uni modules/unix openim sdk' await cancelUpload cancelID Generate cancelID prior to calling uploadFile , and associate it with your local task state. Do not use filenames or array indices as task identifiers. For concurrent uploads, assign an independent cancelID to each file. Return value The Promise resolves with void once the SDK submits the cancellation signal to the native layer. If the upload has already finished, the cancelID does not exist, or the remote server has already processed the entire payload, outcome depends on the current transfer state. Rely on the rejection of the original upload Promise to update your UI, and avoid persisting partial avatars or attachments once cancelled. State changes after the call Aborting an upload terminates data transmission; it does not delete previously saved remote resources on the storage server or recall already transmitted messages. For full upload parameters and progress tracking, see Upload a file /sdk/uniapp/file uploads/upload file .

title: Calling overview
description: Understand call signaling, room credentials, and event boundaries in the UniApp SDK.
keywords: sdk uniapp v4 sdk uniapp calling overview-calling
content: The UniApp SDK provides signaling APIs to initiate, accept, reject, cancel, and hang up audio and video calls. It also enables querying active group rooms, retrieving room access credentials, and restoring pending call invitations. The SDK manages signaling metadata and room authentication credentials; it does not capture camera frames, process microphone audio, or render call UI components. Pass the returned roomID , token , and liveURL to your chosen real time audio/video RTC engine, and manage hardware permissions, media tracks, network adaptation, and UI rendering within your application layer. Calling lifecycle 1. Initiate a one on one call using Start a single call /sdk/uniapp/calling/managing calls/start single call , or launch a conference call using Start a group call /sdk/uniapp/calling/managing calls/start group call . 2. When invited clients receive incoming signaling events, invoke Restore pending call invitations /sdk/uniapp/calling/retrieving call information/restore pending invitation to reconstruct pending invitation state, then accept or reject. 3. The callee joins by calling Accept a call /sdk/uniapp/calling/managing calls/accept call and passing the returned room credentials to their RTC engine. 4. Update UI displays based on signaling events; RTC media tracks are maintained directly by the media engine. 5. The caller can abort an unanswered invitation using Cancel a call invitation /sdk/uniapp/calling/managing calls/cancel call , while any active participant can terminate their session using Hang up a call /sdk/uniapp/calling/managing calls/hang up call . Core data structures | Structure | Description | | | | | OpenIMSignalingInvitationInfo | Metadata containing inviter, invitees, group ID, room ID, media type, timeout, and session type. | | OpenIMSignalingInviteResult | Contains invitation details, RTC credentials, and busy user IDs returned when initiating a call. | | OpenIMSignalingAcceptResult | Room connection credentials returned upon accepting an invitation. | | OpenIMSignalingGetRoomByGroupIDResult | Active group call room ID and associated invitation payload. | Promise resolution, event delivery, and state re queries represent three distinct phases: A resolved Promise confirms that the signaling request reached OpenIMServer. Real time signaling events inform other devices of the transition. Re query APIs allow the app to synchronize state after returning to the foreground or reconnecting. Calling events deliver raw payload strings without exposed internal schemas. Use events as invalidation signals to re query strongly typed call data through the retrieval APIs. Identify call sessions using roomID , and track individual participants by combining roomID with user IDs. For event handling, see Handle call events /sdk/uniapp/calling/managing calls/handle call events . Quick reference | Task | Guide | | | | | Initiate a call | Start a single call /sdk/uniapp/calling/managing calls/start single call , Start a group call /sdk/uniapp/calling/managing calls/start group call | | Respond to an invitation | Accept a call /sdk/uniapp/calling/managing calls/accept call , Reject a call /sdk/uniapp/calling/managing calls/reject call | | Terminate a session | Cancel a call invitation /sdk/uniapp/calling/managing calls/cancel call , Hang up a call /sdk/uniapp/calling/managing calls/hang up call | | Restore call credentials | Restore pending call invitations /sdk/uniapp/calling/retrieving call information/restore pending invitation , Get room by group ID /sdk/uniapp/calling/retrieving call information/get room by group id , Get token by room ID /sdk/uniapp/calling/retrieving call information/get token by room id | | In call signaling | Send a custom signal /sdk/uniapp/calling/sending custom signals/send a custom signal |

title: Start a single call
description: Initiate a one-on-one audio or video call invitation to a specific user.
keywords: sdk uniapp v4 sdk uniapp calling managing-calls start-single-call
content: Invoke signalingInvite to initiate a direct one on one audio or video call to a target user. Generate a unique roomID for each call session, and retain the invitation payload in local state for subsequent cancellation or hang up operations. Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | invitation | OpenIMSignalingInvitationInfo | Yes | The signaling invitation configuration object. | | invitation.inviterUserID | string | Recommended | The user ID of the caller initiating the invitation. | | invitation.inviteeUserIDList | string | Yes | An array containing exactly one recipient user ID for direct calls. | | invitation.groupID | string | Recommended | An empty string for direct calls. | | invitation.roomID | string | Yes | A unique room identifier generated for this call session. | | invitation.timeout | number | Yes | Ringing timeout duration in seconds. | | invitation.mediaType | string | Yes | Media type agreed upon by your application, such as 'audio' or 'video' . | | invitation.sessionType | OpenIMSessionType | Yes | Supply OpenIMSessionTypeSingle for one on one calls. | | invitation.platformID | OpenIMPlatform | Recommended | Current platform constant matching the one used during initSDK . | | invitation.customData | string | No | Optional business payload string attached to the invitation. | | offlinePushInfo | OpenIMSignalingOfflinePushInfo | No | Offline push notification configuration for offline invitees. | Code example import OpenIMSessionTypeSingle, signalingInvite, from '@/uni modules/unix openim sdk' const invitation = inviterUserID: currentUserID, inviteeUserIDList: peerUserID , customData: JSON.stringify source: 'contact card' , groupID: '', roomID: createCallRoomID , timeout: 30, mediaType: 'video', sessionType: OpenIMSessionTypeSingle, platformID: currentOpenIMPlatform, const result = await signalingInvite invitation, offlinePushInfo: title: 'Video call', desc: 'You received a video call invitation', ex: '', iOSPushSound: 'default', iOSBadgeCount: true, , Return value The Promise resolves with an OpenIMSignalingInviteResult | null object. A non null result provides invitation , roomID , token , liveURL , and busyLineUserIDList . Join your media engine room only after receiving valid roomID and token credentials. State changes after the call A resolved Promise indicates that the signaling invitation was delivered to OpenIMServer and room credentials were generated; it does not mean the callee has answered. Track the call session state using roomID as the primary key. For incoming callee responses and participant lifecycle updates, see Handle call events /sdk/uniapp/calling/managing calls/handle call events .

title: Start a group call
description: Invite specified group members to join an audio or video group call.
keywords: sdk uniapp v4 sdk uniapp calling managing-calls start-group-call
content: Invoke signalingInviteInGroup to invite specific group members to an audio or video call. This API delivers invitations strictly to the members listed in inviteeUserIDList ; specifying groupID does not automatically invite all members of the group. Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | invitation | OpenIMSignalingInvitationInfo | Yes | The signaling invitation configuration object. | | invitation.inviterUserID | string | Recommended | The user ID of the caller initiating the invitation. | | invitation.inviteeUserIDList | string | Yes | An array of user IDs of the group members being invited. | | invitation.groupID | string | Yes | The target group identifier. | | invitation.roomID | string | Yes | A unique room identifier generated for this group call session. | | invitation.timeout | number | Yes | Ringing timeout duration in seconds. | | invitation.mediaType | string | Yes | Media type agreed upon by your application, such as 'audio' or 'video' . | | invitation.sessionType | OpenIMSessionType | Yes | Use the session type matching the group conversation typically OpenIMSessionTypeWriteGroup for working groups . | | invitation.platformID | OpenIMPlatform | Recommended | Current platform constant matching the one used during initSDK . | | invitation.customData | string | No | Optional business payload string attached to the invitation. | | offlinePushInfo | OpenIMSignalingOfflinePushInfo | No | Push notification configuration for offline group members. | Keep these group specific guidelines in mind: Pass the valid groupID of an active group. Filter inviteeUserIDList to exclude the inviter's own user ID, empty values, and duplicate entries. Generate a new, unique roomID for every call session rather than reusing groupID . Code example import OpenIMSessionTypeWriteGroup, signalingInviteInGroup, from '@/uni modules/unix openim sdk' const invitation = inviterUserID: currentUserID, inviteeUserIDList: selectedGroupMemberIDs, customData: JSON.stringify source: 'group call' , groupID, roomID: createCallRoomID , timeout: 30, mediaType: 'video', sessionType: OpenIMSessionTypeWriteGroup, platformID: currentOpenIMPlatform, const result = await signalingInviteInGroup invitation, offlinePushInfo, Return value The Promise resolves with an OpenIMSignalingInviteResult | null object containing room credentials and busyLineUserIDList . Users listed in busyLineUserIDList were busy on other calls; this does not invalidate invitations sent to other available group members. State changes after the call A resolved Promise confirms that invitation requests were dispatched to OpenIMServer and that room credentials were created. It does not indicate that any group member has accepted. Merge call session state by roomID , and track individual member statuses by combining roomID with each member's userID . For ongoing participation updates, see Handle call events /sdk/uniapp/calling/managing calls/handle call events .

title: Accept a call
description: Accept an incoming call invitation and retrieve room access credentials.
keywords: sdk uniapp v4 sdk uniapp calling managing-calls accept-call
content: After receiving or restoring a complete OpenIMSignalingInvitationInfo object, invoke signalingAccept to accept the incoming call invitation and obtain RTC room access credentials. Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | invitation | OpenIMSignalingInvitationInfo | Yes | The complete invitation object received via signaling events or recovered from queries. | Pass the complete invitation payload as received. Do not reconstruct an incomplete payload containing only roomID . If your application resumed from the background or restarted, retrieve the active invitation using Restore pending call invitations /sdk/uniapp/calling/retrieving call information/restore pending invitation . Code example import signalingAccept from '@/uni modules/unix openim sdk' const result = await signalingAccept invitation if result?.roomID = null && result?.token = null await mediaEngineJoin result.roomID , result.token , result.liveURL Return value The Promise resolves with an OpenIMSignalingAcceptResult | null object containing invitation , roomID , token , and liveURL . Connect your media engine to the RTC channel using the returned room ID and token. State changes after the call A resolved Promise confirms that the acceptance signal was submitted to OpenIMServer; it does not indicate that the media engine channel has connected or that other participants have received the update. Track calling session state using roomID . For multi party participant events and disconnection handling, see Handle call events /sdk/uniapp/calling/managing calls/handle call events .

title: Reject a call
description: Decline an unanswered incoming call invitation.
keywords: sdk uniapp v4 sdk uniapp calling managing-calls reject-call
content: When a user declines an incoming call, pass the complete OpenIMSignalingInvitationInfo object to signalingReject . Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | invitation | OpenIMSignalingInvitationInfo | Yes | The complete invitation object received via signaling events or recovered from queries. | Do not attempt to construct a simplified invitation using only roomID or the caller ID. Code example import signalingReject from '@/uni modules/unix openim sdk' await signalingReject invitation Return value The Promise resolves with void upon successful submission of the rejection signal. State changes after the call A resolved Promise confirms that the rejection request was accepted by OpenIMServer. The callee client should immediately tear down the incoming call UI, remove the pending invitation state indexed by roomID , and release any reserved audio/video hardware resources. Promise resolution does not guarantee that the caller has already processed the event; for caller side signaling synchronization, see Handle call events /sdk/uniapp/calling/managing calls/handle call events .

title: Cancel a call invitation
description: Cancel an unanswered call invitation as the caller.
keywords: sdk uniapp v4 sdk uniapp calling managing-calls cancel-call
content: While an outgoing invitation remains unanswered, the caller can abort the attempt by calling signalingCancel . Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | invitation | OpenIMSignalingInvitationInfo | Yes | The complete invitation object preserved from when the call was initiated. | Supply the original invitation retained during call initiation. Ensure roomID matches the active outgoing invitation. Code example import signalingCancel from '@/uni modules/unix openim sdk' await signalingCancel invitation Return value The Promise resolves with void once the cancellation signal is submitted to OpenIMServer. State changes after the call A resolved Promise indicates that the cancellation request completed successfully. The caller client should immediately terminate the outgoing ringing view indexed by roomID and release any reserved audio/video resources. Promise resolution does not guarantee that callee devices have processed the cancellation; for handling incoming cancellation events on callee devices, see Handle call events /sdk/uniapp/calling/managing calls/handle call events . Cancellation applies strictly to unanswered invitations. Once a call is answered and active, invoke Hang up a call /sdk/uniapp/calling/managing calls/hang up call instead.

title: Hang up a call
description: Terminate an active audio or video call session.
keywords: sdk uniapp v4 sdk uniapp calling managing-calls hang-up-call
content: Once a call is connected, any active participant can invoke signalingHungUp to hang up and terminate their participation. Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | invitation | OpenIMSignalingInvitationInfo | Yes | The complete invitation object associated with the active call. | Supply the complete invitation payload corresponding to the active call session. Ensure roomID matches the active media channel. Code example import signalingHungUp from '@/uni modules/unix openim sdk' await signalingHungUp invitation Return value The Promise resolves with void once the hang up signal is submitted to OpenIMServer. State changes after the call A resolved Promise confirms that the hang up signaling completed. The client must still stop local audio/video capture, exit the media engine room, and release hardware resources camera and microphone . Identify and clean up session state across components using roomID . For handling remote hang up notifications, see Handle call events /sdk/uniapp/calling/managing calls/handle call events .

title: Handle call events
description: Centrally listen for call invitations, acceptances, participants, and hang-up lifecycle changes.
keywords: sdk uniapp v4 sdk uniapp calling managing-calls handle-call-events
content: Your calling state layer should centrally register listeners for invitation lifecycles and participant changes. These event callbacks deliver a raw string payload without exposed internal schemas. Use these events as invalidation signals to re query strongly typed invitation or room details through dedicated retrieval APIs. | Event | Recommended handling | | | | | onReceiveNewInvitation | Query and restore the active pending invitation, then display the incoming call UI. | | onInviteeAccepted | Refresh call state and proceed with the RTC media connection. | | onInviteeAcceptedByOtherDevice | Terminate the incoming call UI on this device to avoid duplicate answering. | | onInviteeRejected | Update participant status; end the invitation if all invitees have rejected. | | onInviteeRejectedByOtherDevice | Dismiss the incoming call UI on this device. | | onInvitationCancelled , onInvitationTimeout | Dismiss ringing state and release pre allocated media resources. | | onHangUp | Leave the media channel and terminate the call. | | onRoomParticipantConnected , onRoomParticipantDisconnected | Re query the room or notify the media engine to update the participant list. | | onStreamChange | Supported on Android and iOS as a media state change notification; omitted on HarmonyOS. | Code example The following example treats signaling callbacks as trigger notifications. When onReceiveNewInvitation fires, it calls Restore pending call invitations /sdk/uniapp/calling/retrieving call information/restore pending invitation to fetch strongly typed invitation data. For group calls, query Get room by group ID /sdk/uniapp/calling/retrieving call information/get room by group id to synchronize room metadata: import off, onHangUp, onInvitationCancelled, onInvitationTimeout, onInviteeAccepted, onInviteeAcceptedByOtherDevice, onInviteeRejected, onInviteeRejectedByOtherDevice, onReceiveNewInvitation, onRoomParticipantConnected, onRoomParticipantDisconnected, onStreamChange, signalingGetInvitationInfoStartApp, from '@/uni modules/unix openim sdk' const restoreIncomingInvitation = async = const result = await signalingGetInvitationInfoStartApp userID: currentUserID, if result?.invitation?.roomID = null showIncomingCall result.invitation const handleIncomingInvitation = payload: string = void restoreIncomingInvitation const refreshCall = payload: string = void refreshCurrentCall const finishCurrentCall = payload: string = closeCallAndReleaseMedia const incomingSubscription = onReceiveNewInvitation handleIncomingInvitation const acceptedSubscription = onInviteeAccepted refreshCall const acceptedElsewhereSubscription = onInviteeAcceptedByOtherDevice finishCurrentCall const rejectedSubscription = onInviteeRejected refreshCall const rejectedElsewhereSubscription = onInviteeRejectedByOtherDevice finishCurrentCall const cancelledSubscription = onInvitationCancelled finishCurrentCall const timeoutSubscription = onInvitationTimeout finishCurrentCall const hangUpSubscription = onHangUp finishCurrentCall const participantConnectedSubscription = onRoomParticipantConnected refreshCall const participantDisconnectedSubscription = onRoomParticipantDisconnected refreshCall const streamChangeSubscription = onStreamChange refreshCall function removeCallListeners off incomingSubscription off acceptedSubscription off acceptedElsewhereSubscription off rejectedSubscription off rejectedElsewhereSubscription off cancelledSubscription off timeoutSubscription off hangUpSubscription off participantConnectedSubscription off participantDisconnectedSubscription off streamChangeSubscription If your application relies on an agreed string serialization format within the event payloads, parse them in a dedicated adapter layer. Validate payload fields and protocol versions, merge items using roomID as the primary key, and fall back to query APIs if parsing fails. Unsubscribe from all call listeners when logging out, switching user accounts, or dismantling the global calling manager. For custom signaling events, refer to Send a custom signal /sdk/uniapp/calling/sending custom signals/send a custom signal .

title: Restore pending call invitations
description: Query active, pending call invitations when your app launches or returns to the foreground.
keywords: sdk uniapp v4 sdk uniapp calling retrieving-call-information restore-pending-invitation
content: Query whether the current account has any active, pending audio or video call invitations. This method provides strongly typed, complete invitation records upon cold start, when returning from the background, or following receipt of an incoming call notification. Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | userID | string | No | The current logged in user ID. | The parameter object can be omitted. When providing userID , pass the currently authenticated user's ID. Do not query invitations on behalf of other users. Code example import signalingGetInvitationInfoStartApp, from '@/uni modules/unix openim sdk' const result = await signalingGetInvitationInfoStartApp userID: currentUserID, if result?.invitation?.roomID = null restoreIncomingCall result.invitation Return value The Promise resolves with an OpenIMSignalingGetInvitationInfoStartAppResult | null object containing an invitation property of type OpenIMSignalingInvitationInfo | null . If no valid invitation is returned, clear any stale incoming call views indexed by roomID to prevent reuse of outdated room state. State changes after the call This is a read only query that checks current invitation state without accepting, rejecting, or generating events. After restoring incoming call UI, continue listening for cancellations, timeouts, remote answers, and hang up notifications as described in Handle call events /sdk/uniapp/calling/managing calls/handle call events .

title: Get room by group ID
description: Query the active calling room information for a specific group.
keywords: sdk uniapp v4 sdk uniapp calling retrieving-call-information get-room-by-group-id
content: Query active calling room details for a given group using its groupID . Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | groupID | string | Yes | The target group identifier. | Code example import signalingGetRoomByGroupID, from '@/uni modules/unix openim sdk' const result = await signalingGetRoomByGroupID groupID if result?.roomID = null restoreGroupCall result.roomID , result.invitation else clearStaleGroupCall groupID Return value The Promise resolves with an OpenIMSignalingGetRoomByGroupIDResult | null object: | Property | Type | Description | | | | | | roomID | string \| null | The active group call room identifier. | | invitation | OpenIMSignalingInvitationInfo \| null | The invitation payload associated with the active room. | If the result is null or does not contain a valid roomID , no call is currently active in that group; clean up any cached group call UI accordingly. A rejected Promise indicates a query error; do not mistake network timeouts or authentication errors for an absent call unless the server specifically reports that no room exists. State changes after the call This is a read only query that retrieves point in time room metadata without altering server side state or triggering events. For real time updates on active calls, see Handle call events /sdk/uniapp/calling/managing calls/handle call events .

title: Get token by room ID
description: Retrieve media room connection credentials using a room identifier.
keywords: sdk uniapp v4 sdk uniapp calling retrieving-call-information get-token-by-room-id
content: When the application already possesses a roomID but needs to obtain or refresh its RTC authentication credentials, invoke signalingGetTokenByRoomID . Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | roomID | string | Yes | The target calling room identifier. | Code example import signalingGetTokenByRoomID, from '@/uni modules/unix openim sdk' const result = await signalingGetTokenByRoomID roomID if result?.token = null await mediaEngineJoin roomID, result.token , result.liveURL Return value The Promise resolves with an OpenIMSignalingGetTokenByRoomIDResult | null object containing nullable token and liveURL properties. The result object does not repeat roomID ; retain the roomID supplied to the query when configuring your media engine connection. If token is missing or null, do not attempt to join the media room. Re query after network recovery or session re authentication. State changes after the call This is a point in time credential query that does not modify call status or trigger events. For overall call session tracking and remote event streams, see Handle call events /sdk/uniapp/calling/managing calls/handle call events .

title: Send a custom signal
description: Transmit lightweight in-call business signaling data within a specified calling room.
keywords: sdk uniapp v4 sdk uniapp calling sending-custom-signals send-a-custom-signal
content: Transmit lightweight application specific signaling data within an active calling room—such as raise hand requests, video layout switch triggers, or custom interaction states. This API is not a chat messaging interface and does not replace the binary data channels of an RTC engine. Code example import signalingSendCustomSignaling, from '@/uni modules/unix openim sdk' const signal = version: 1, eventID: createBusinessEventID , type: 'hand raised', userID: currentUserID, sentAt: Date.now , await signalingSendCustomSignaling roomID, customInfo: JSON.stringify signal , Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | roomID | string | Yes | The active calling room identifier. | | customInfo | string | Yes | Custom payload string. When passing JSON, include a schema version and a unique event ID. | Return value The Promise resolves with void once OpenIMServer accepts the dispatch request; it does not indicate that remote participants have processed the payload. Custom signals are suited for ephemeral, lightweight coordination. Do not use this method for large files, chat history persistence, or long lived synchronized state. Receive custom signals The onReceiveCustomSignal event delivers a raw string payload. Identify the call session using roomID , and validate JSON schemas, protocol versions, and deduplication IDs within an adapter layer before applying changes to the view: import off, onReceiveCustomSignal, from '@/uni modules/unix openim sdk' const handleCustomSignal = payload: string = const signal = parseAndValidateCallSignal payload if signal == null return if hasAppliedSignal signal.eventID return applyCallSignal signal const customSignalSubscription = onReceiveCustomSignal handleCustomSignal // Clean up when leaving call screens or switching accounts: off customSignalSubscription If the incoming string wraps the payload within an SDK container structure, extract customInfo in your adapter layer to normalize payload representations across client platforms. State changes after the call A resolved Promise confirms transmission across OpenIMServer. Recipient clients process the payload asynchronously via onReceiveCustomSignal . Because custom signaling is ephemeral, it does not alter server persisted calling records.

title: Events overview
description: Register, consume, and clean up UniApp SDK events across application and session lifecycles.
keywords: sdk uniapp v4 sdk uniapp events overview-events
content: The UniApp SDK provides dedicated listener registration functions for connection lifecycles, background data synchronization, user profiles, relationships, conversations, groups, messages, file uploads, and audio/video calling. Each registration call returns an OpenIMSDKEventSubscription reference, which you pass to off to unregister that specific listener. Always register stable function references rather than inline closures within re rendering components to prevent memory leaks and duplicate handler execution. Global connection, messaging, and call listeners should reside in application or session level stores, while listeners scoped to a specific view should be unsubscribed when that page unmounts. Recommended registration lifecycles | Event domain | Recommended lifecycle | Detailed documentation | | | | | | Connection, token, and kick out | Register before login; clean up when switching accounts | Authenticate and manage a session /sdk/uniapp/getting started/authenticate and manage session | | User profile, friends, and blacklist | Register when initializing the contact state layer | User overview /sdk/uniapp/user/overview user | | Conversation list and unread counts | Register when initializing the conversation state layer | Get the conversation list /sdk/uniapp/conversation/retrieving conversations/retrieve conversation list , Get total unread count /sdk/uniapp/conversation/managing conversations/get total unread count | | Groups and group members | Register when initializing the group state layer | Group overview /sdk/uniapp/group/overview group | | Group join applications | Register when initializing group application management | Get received group applications /sdk/uniapp/group/group applications/get group application list as recipient | | Messages and receipts | Register when initializing the message store | Receive messages /sdk/uniapp/message/receiving messages/receive messages | | File uploads | Register before initiating upload tasks | Upload a file /sdk/uniapp/file uploads/upload file | | Audio/video calls | Register when initializing calling services | Handle call events /sdk/uniapp/calling/managing calls/handle call events | Monitor server data synchronization After successful login, the SDK synchronizes historical records and offline changes from OpenIMServer. Use these four events to track synchronization progress: | Event | Callback parameter | Description | | | | | | onSyncServerStart | boolean | Emitted when a synchronization cycle begins. | | onSyncServerProgress | number | The current synchronization percentage 0 to 100 . | | onSyncServerFinish | boolean | Emitted when synchronization completes successfully. | | onSyncServerFailed | boolean | Emitted when synchronization fails. | The callback parameters for onSyncServerStart , onSyncServerFinish , and onSyncServerFailed are booleans without specific payload properties. Determine the sync phase by the event name itself rather than attempting to interpret the boolean payload. Code example import off, onSyncServerFailed, onSyncServerFinish, onSyncServerProgress, onSyncServerStart, from '@/uni modules/unix openim sdk' const handleSyncStart = value: boolean = setSyncState 'syncing', 0 const handleSyncProgress = progress: number = setSyncState 'syncing', progress const handleSyncFinish = value: boolean = setSyncState 'ready', 100 void reloadVisibleData const handleSyncFailed = value: boolean = setSyncState 'failed', 0 const syncStartSubscription = onSyncServerStart handleSyncStart const syncProgressSubscription = onSyncServerProgress handleSyncProgress const syncFinishSubscription = onSyncServerFinish handleSyncFinish const syncFailedSubscription = onSyncServerFailed handleSyncFailed function removeSyncListeners off syncStartSubscription off syncProgressSubscription off syncFinishSubscription off syncFailedSubscription Synchronization events describe the SDK's background sync lifecycle rather than a specific query API. Once synchronization completes, refresh view models for active screens, and rely on domain specific events for subsequent real time updates. Because events can arrive out of order during network transitions, merge items into your state using stable keys: userID , conversationID , groupID , groupID:userID , or clientMsgID .

title: Logging and diagnostics
description: Configure UniApp SDK log levels and upload native diagnostic logs.
keywords: sdk uniapp v4 sdk uniapp logger
content: UniApp SDK logs help trace native mobile app initialization, connection lifecycles, and API execution. You can configure log levels, enable standard output logging, and designate native storage directories to accommodate diagnostics across development and production environments. Configure log levels Log settings are configured through initialization parameters when calling initSDK : import OpenIMLogLevelDebug, initSDK, from '@/uni modules/unix openim sdk' await initSDK platformID: currentOpenIMPlatform, apiAddr, wsAddr, dataDir: '', logFilePath: '', logLevel: OpenIMLogLevelDebug, isLogStandardOutput: true, systemType: 'your app', | Enum value | Numeric value | Description | | | | | | OpenIMLogLevelPanic | 0 | Catastrophic failures only; terminates the runtime. | | OpenIMLogLevelFatal | 1 | Fatal crashes and non recoverable internal errors. | | OpenIMLogLevelError | 2 | Errors affecting operations; recommended for production troubleshooting. | | OpenIMLogLevelWarn | 3 | Non critical warnings; standard for production environments. | | OpenIMLogLevelInfo | 4 | General lifecycle milestones and connectivity updates. | | OpenIMLogLevelDebug | 5 | Detailed logs for local development and integration debugging. | | OpenIMLogLevelVerbose | 6 | Deep diagnostic tracing; avoid leaving enabled long term in production. | Set isLogStandardOutput to control whether the SDK prints logs to standard output. Use logFilePath to designate the local directory where native logs are written. Ensure this path points to a writable application directory rather than a read only bundle directory. Refer to Integrate by project and platform /sdk/uniapp/getting started/environment specific implementation for full initialization options. Upload diagnostic logs Invoke uploadLogs to package and transmit locally stored native SDK logs to the log collection service configured for your OpenIM deployment. Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | line | number | Yes | The number of recent log lines to collect and upload. | | ex | string | Yes | Additional diagnostic context or metadata formatted according to your server deployment conventions. | Code example import OpenIMUploadLogsProgressEvent, off, onUploadLogsProgress, uploadLogs, from '@/uni modules/unix openim sdk' const handleLogUploadProgress = event: OpenIMUploadLogsProgressEvent | null, = if event == null return setDiagnosticUploadProgress event.progress const logUploadSubscription = onUploadLogsProgress handleLogUploadProgress await uploadLogs line: 2000, ex: 'connection diagnostic session', off logUploadSubscription Return value The returned Promise resolves with a string confirming that the log upload completed successfully. This call does not modify user records, conversations, or messages, nor does it trigger domain events. If the upload fails, the Promise rejects with an error containing errCode and errMsg . Except for this diagnostics guide, API methods in this SDK do not require client code to generate or pass an operationID . When tracing specific request traces against OpenIMServer logs, diagnostic tools parse the internal identifiers managed by the SDK.

title: OpenIM HarmonyOS SDK overview
description: Integrate OpenIMClientSDK into HarmonyOS phones, tablets, and 2in1 devices.
keywords: sdk harmony v4 sdk harmony overview
content: The OpenIM HarmonyOS SDK is designed specifically for the HarmonyOS ecosystem, providing type safe native ArkTS APIs powered by a high performance cross platform core engine via N API. By adding the HAR package, you can implement user profiles, relationship chains, conversation lists, group management, message transmission, local persistence storage, audio and video call signaling, and real time event listeners. Scope and support The HarmonyOS SDK supports the following device categories and native architectures: | Device type | Support status | Native architecture | | | | | | Phone | Supported | arm64 v8a | | Tablet | Supported | arm64 v8a | | 2in1 | Supported | x86 64 , arm64 v8a | All three device categories share Platform.HarmonyOS , eliminating the need to maintain different business APIs across form factors. Multi window 2in1 applications should maintain the SDK instance and database directory at the application process level; closing an individual window does not destroy the SDK instance. The HarmonyOS SDK is a commercial delivery feature. Consult your commercial agreement and provided HAR package for specific distribution artifacts, license scopes, and enterprise capabilities. SDK entry point The SDK exports a default process level instance: import sdk, OpenIMSDKEvent from '@openimsdk/imsdk'; Asynchronous APIs return Promises that resolve directly to the declared response object without an extra data wrapper. When an API call fails, the Promise rejects with an error object containing errCode and errMsg to differentiate parameter, network, and server side errors. sdk.on returns an unsubscribe function. Query APIs fetch initial data snapshots, while event listeners merge incremental updates in real time. During weak network reconnection or unexpected state drift, query again to reconcile local data. Local databases, logs, and media files must use valid, writable or readable paths within the application sandbox. Recommended integration workflow 1. Review Before you start /sdk/harmony/getting started/before you start to set up OpenIMServer, prepare login credentials, and configure DevEco Studio. 2. Follow Environment specific implementation /sdk/harmony/getting started/environment specific implementation to install the HAR, declare required permissions, and initialize the SDK. 3. Register connection and synchronization listeners before logging in, then follow Authenticate and manage session /sdk/harmony/getting started/authenticate and manage session to log in. 4. Wait for the connection to succeed and server data synchronization to finish, then follow Send your first message /sdk/harmony/getting started/send first message to verify message transmission. The recommended lifecycle order is: Initialize the SDK Environment specific implementation /sdk/harmony/getting started/environment specific implementation Register event listeners Log in Authenticate and manage session /sdk/harmony/getting started/authenticate and manage session Await connection success and server synchronization Invoke business APIs.

title: Before you start
description: Prepare your OpenIMServer instance, user credentials, HarmonyOS development environment, and SDK HAR.
keywords: sdk harmony v4 sdk harmony getting-started before-you-start
content: Before integrating the OpenIM HarmonyOS SDK, ensure you have an accessible OpenIMServer deployment, a valid userID and matching token, the commercially distributed SDK HAR, and a development environment configured to build HarmonyOS native modules. Service endpoints | Field | Description | | | | | apiAddr | OpenIMServer HTTP API endpoint, such as https://api.example.com . | | wsAddr | OpenIMServer WebSocket endpoint, such as wss://ws.example.com . | Verify DNS resolution, TLS certificates, firewall rules, reverse proxy settings, and WebSocket upgrade handshakes directly on target physical phones, tablets, and 2in1 devices. Do not test these endpoints solely on your development workstation. User credentials and token Your business server must generate a userID and an authentication token, then provide both credentials to your HarmonyOS application for sign in. For backend integration details, see API preparation /platform api/prepare to use api and Get user token /platform api/auth/tokens/get user token . Development environment DevEco Studio configured to build your target HarmonyOS application. The HarmonyOS SDK matching your target device and API level, along with matching Hvigor and OHPM toolchains. The commercially delivered OpenIM SDK HAR package. An application module targeting phone , tablet , or 2in1 . Do not import multiple versions of the OpenIM HAR or manually extract and copy .so shared libraries into your project. Doing so causes duplicate native modules, ABI mismatches, or runtime errors between ArkTS declarations and compiled binaries. Permissions and storage directories The SDK requires ohos.permission.INTERNET . The SDK wrapper automatically monitors app foreground/background transitions and network connectivity changes; do not register redundant low level lifecycle listeners or manual state APIs in application pages. Configure persistent sandbox directories before initializing the SDK: dataDir and dbPath store local SQLite databases and synchronized metadata. logFilePath stores SDK execution logs. All paths must point to stable, writable locations within the application's internal files directory. Do not use temporary cache directories or shared external paths. Pre flight checklist Verify that the HAR package contains the required ABI architectures arm64 v8a , x86 64 for your target devices. Confirm physical devices can reach the API, WebSocket, and media object storage domains. Ensure the userID matches the subject in the token before attempting sign in. Implement token expiration handling, account switching logic, and multi device kick out events, and verify that synchronization resumes smoothly when the app returns to the foreground or network connectivity recovers. Treat logging out and process level SDK termination as separate phases. Do not destroy the SDK instance when unmounting individual pages or closing single windows. Next, proceed to Environment specific implementation /sdk/harmony/getting started/environment specific implementation .

title: Get SDK version
description: Retrieve the OpenIMClientSDK version bundled inside the current HarmonyOS HAR package.
keywords: sdk harmony v4 sdk harmony getting-started get-sdk-version
content: After completing Environment specific implementation /sdk/harmony/getting started/environment specific implementation and adding the HAR package, call version to inspect the runtime version of the embedded OpenIMClientSDK core. This is useful for diagnostics, startup telemetry, and platform compatibility checks. Code example import sdk, VersionResp from '@openimsdk/imsdk'; const response: VersionResp = await sdk.version ; console.info OpenIMClientSDK version: $ response.version ; Return value Returns a Promise that resolves to a VersionResp object: | Property | Type | Description | | | | | | version | string | The underlying OpenIMClientSDK semantic version string. | Use this value to verify that the loaded binary matches expectations. Do not substitute this version string for your application's product version or use it as a server authentication credential. If multiple components require version information, cache the result at the application layer rather than re querying the SDK during view rendering. Once your environment is verified, proceed to Authenticate and manage session /sdk/harmony/getting started/authenticate and manage session .

title: Environment-specific implementation
description: Install the HAR package, declare permissions, and initialize OpenIMClientSDK in a HarmonyOS project.
keywords: sdk harmony v4 sdk harmony getting-started environment-specific-implementation
content: The OpenIM HarmonyOS SDK uses a single HAR package to support phones, tablets, and 2in1 devices. Before proceeding, complete the server, credential, and development environment setup described in Before you start /sdk/harmony/getting started/before you start . Install the HAR package Copy the delivered HAR package into your application module and declare the local file dependency in the module's oh package.json5 . Replace .har with the actual file name: dependencies: '@openimsdk/imsdk': 'file:./libs/ .har', , Declare the internet permission in src/main/module.json5 : module: requestPermissions: name: 'ohos.permission.INTERNET' , , After modifying the HAR package or permission declarations, resync OHPM dependencies and trigger a full project build instead of relying on stale incremental artifacts. Initialize the SDK Call initSDK with your configuration before performing any chat operations: Code example import sdk, AppFramework, HttpClientMode, InitSDKReq, LogLevel, Platform, from '@openimsdk/imsdk'; const request: InitSDKReq = config: apiAddr: 'https://api.example.com', wsAddr: 'wss://ws.example.com', dataDir: $ filesDir /openim/data , dbPath: $ filesDir /openim/data , logFilePath: $ filesDir /openim/logs , appFramework: AppFramework.Native, platform: Platform.HarmonyOS, logLevel: LogLevel.LevelWarn, isLogStandardOutput: false, StopGoroutineOnBackground: true, LogRemainCount: 3, diagnoseHashSalt: 'your app specific diagnose salt', httpClientMode: HttpClientMode.ConnFirst, , ; await sdk.initSDK request ; Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | apiAddr | string | Yes | OpenIMServer HTTP API endpoint. | | wsAddr | string | Yes | OpenIMServer WebSocket endpoint. | | dataDir , dbPath | string | Yes | Persistent, writable internal sandbox directories for databases and cached metadata. Must remain consistent across windows in the same process. | | logFilePath | string | No | Directory for SDK execution logs. Defaults to the distribution's built in log path if omitted. | | appFramework | AppFramework | No | Use AppFramework.Native for native ArkTS applications. | | platform | Platform | No | Use Platform.HarmonyOS for HarmonyOS applications. | | logLevel | LogLevel | No | SDK logging verbosity level. | | isLogStandardOutput | boolean | Yes | Whether to redirect native core logs to standard system output hilog . | | StopGoroutineOnBackground | boolean | Yes | Pause internal background goroutines when the application enters the background. Typically true on phones and tablets; can be false on long running 2in1 daemon processes. | | LogRemainCount | number | Yes | Number of rotated log files to retain locally. | | diagnoseHashSalt | string | Yes | Application specific salt string used for diagnostic hashing. | | httpClientMode | HttpClientMode | Yes | HTTP connection strategy. Typically HttpClientMode.ConnFirst . | Return value Returns a Promise that resolves to void upon successful initialization. Promise resolution indicates only that the native engine and database structures are ready. It does not indicate that a user is logged in or that server synchronization is complete. After initialization, verify the engine runtime via Get SDK version /sdk/harmony/getting started/get sdk version , register connection and sync event listeners, and proceed to Authenticate and manage session /sdk/harmony/getting started/authenticate and manage session . Terminate the SDK Call unInitSDK only when the application process is shutting down permanently and all concurrent operations, event listeners, and active user sessions have terminated: await sdk.logout ; await sdk.unInitSDK ; Page navigation, component unmounting, or closing an individual 2in1 window must not destroy the global SDK instance. If you need to re initialize the SDK, always await the completion of the previous unInitSDK call.

title: Authenticate and manage session
description: Sign in the current user, handle connection and token lifecycle events, update tokens, and sign out.
keywords: sdk harmony v4 sdk harmony getting-started authenticate-and-manage-session
content: After initializing the SDK, register connection and account lifecycle listeners before signing in. Sign in using matching userID and token credentials. The login Promise resolution, the WebSocket long connection establishment, and the server data synchronization completion represent three distinct stages. Register connection and account events Register connection lifecycle and token status callbacks using stable handler functions before logging in: Code example import sdk, EventOnConnectFailedData, EventOnKickedOfflineData, EventOnUserTokenInvalidData, OpenIMSDKEmptyPayload, OpenIMSDKEvent, from '@openimsdk/imsdk'; const handleConnecting = data: OpenIMSDKEmptyPayload : void = setConnectionState 'connecting' ; ; const handleConnected = data: OpenIMSDKEmptyPayload : void = setConnectionState 'connected' ; ; const handleConnectFailed = data: EventOnConnectFailedData : void = console.error OpenIM connection failed: $ data.errCode $ data.errMsg ; ; const handleKickedOffline = data: EventOnKickedOfflineData : void = clearCurrentSession ; showSignedInElsewhereDialog data.reason ; ; const handleTokenExpired = data: OpenIMSDKEmptyPayload : void = refreshOpenIMToken ; ; const handleTokenInvalid = data: EventOnUserTokenInvalidData : void = clearCurrentSession ; showTokenInvalidMessage data.errMsg ; ; const unsubscribeConnecting = sdk.on OpenIMSDKEvent.EventOnConnecting, handleConnecting ; const unsubscribeConnected = sdk.on OpenIMSDKEvent.EventOnConnectSuccess, handleConnected ; const unsubscribeConnectFailed = sdk.on OpenIMSDKEvent.EventOnConnectFailed, handleConnectFailed ; const unsubscribeKickedOffline = sdk.on OpenIMSDKEvent.EventOnKickedOffline, handleKickedOffline ; const unsubscribeTokenExpired = sdk.on OpenIMSDKEvent.EventOnUserTokenExpired, handleTokenExpired ; const unsubscribeTokenInvalid = sdk.on OpenIMSDKEvent.EventOnUserTokenInvalid, handleTokenInvalid ; When multiple devices sign into the same account simultaneously under single device concurrency policies, the earlier session receives EventOnKickedOffline . Upon receiving this event, clear active user state, terminate the local session, and navigate back to your sign in view. Sign in the current user Pass the userID and matching token to login : import sdk, LoginReq from '@openimsdk/imsdk'; const request: LoginReq = userID: currentUserID, token: currentToken, ; await sdk.login request ; Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | userID | string | Yes | The user identifier matching the token subject. | | token | string | Yes | Authentication token issued by your business backend. | Return value Returns a Promise that resolves to void when the login request is accepted by the native SDK runtime. State changes after the call Resolving the login Promise indicates that the SDK has accepted the credentials and initiated the connection. Wait for EventOnConnectSuccess to confirm socket connection, followed by EventOnSyncServerFinish detailed in Event listener overview /sdk/harmony/events/overview events to confirm server data synchronization. Only after both events arrive should you query conversation lists, group directories, relationship chains, or historical messages. Query login status Check the current authentication status before triggering business actions or restoring user interfaces: import sdk, GetLoginStatusResp, LoginStatus from '@openimsdk/imsdk'; const response: GetLoginStatusResp = await sdk.getLoginStatus ; if response.status === LoginStatus.Logged restoreSignedInInterface ; Response The returned GetLoginStatusResp object provides the following status values: | Status | Description | | | | | LoginStatus.LoggedOut | No user is currently signed in. | | LoginStatus.Logging | A sign in operation is currently in progress; avoid redundant concurrent login calls. | | LoginStatus.Logged | The user session is active; check connection and synchronization events to determine data availability. | | LoginStatus.LoggingOut | A sign out operation is currently in progress. | Update the authentication token When the token nears expiration, supply a newly generated token using updateToken : import sdk, UpdateTokenReq from '@openimsdk/imsdk'; const request: UpdateTokenReq = token: await requestOpenIMTokenFromBackend , ; await sdk.updateToken request ; Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | token | string | Yes | The freshly issued authentication token. | Return value Returns a Promise that resolves to void once the SDK updates its internal session credentials. If the previous token has already expired and the socket closed, or if the user was kicked offline, perform a clean login sequence instead. Sign out and clean up listeners Call logout to terminate the session and invoke the retained unsubscribe callbacks: await sdk.logout ; unsubscribeConnecting ; unsubscribeConnected ; unsubscribeConnectFailed ; unsubscribeKickedOffline ; unsubscribeTokenExpired ; unsubscribeTokenInvalid ; After logout resolves, clear in memory user caches and reset UI state. Only invoke unInitSDK when terminating the application process entirely; switching accounts does not require tearing down the native runtime.

title: Send your first message
description: Create and send your first one-to-one or group text message using the OpenIM HarmonyOS SDK.
keywords: sdk harmony v4 sdk harmony getting-started send-first-message
content: Before sending messages, complete SDK initialization, sign in the user, and wait for connection establishment and server synchronization. Sending a message consists of two separate phases: creating the message object locally and transmitting it over the network. Send a one to one message Create a text message object using createTextMessage and send it to a recipient with sendMessage : Code example import sdk, CreateTextMessageResp, SendMessageReq, SendMessageResp from '@openimsdk/imsdk'; const created: CreateTextMessageResp = await sdk.createTextMessage text: 'Hello, OpenIM ', ; const request: SendMessageReq = message: created.message, recvID: 'user b', groupID: '', isOnlineOnly: false, ; const sent: SendMessageResp = await sdk.sendMessage request ; appendOutgoingMessage sent.message ; The recvID must be a valid user identifier; do not use nicknames, phone numbers, or UI display labels. Create text message /sdk/harmony/message/creating messages/create text message only constructs the message object in memory without network transmission. Send a group message To send a message to a group, specify the groupID and leave recvID empty: const created: CreateTextMessageResp = await sdk.createTextMessage text: 'Hello everyone ', ; const request: SendMessageReq = message: created.message, recvID: '', groupID: 'group 123', isOnlineOnly: false, ; const sent: SendMessageResp = await sdk.sendMessage request ; appendOutgoingMessage sent.message ; The current user must be an active member of the target group with permission to send messages. Specify only recvID for direct messages and only groupID for group messages; never provide both destinations simultaneously. Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | message | MessageItem | Yes | The message object returned by a creation method such as createTextMessage . | | recvID | string | No | Target user ID for one to one messages. Leave empty for group messages. | | groupID | string | No | Target group ID for group messages. Leave empty for one to one messages. | | isOnlineOnly | boolean | No | Whether the message is delivered only to currently online clients without persisting to history. Default is false . | Return value Returns a Promise that resolves to a SendMessageResp containing the updated message item with delivery status and timestamps. State changes after the call Once the Promise resolves, update or replace your local optimistic pending message in the UI using the stable identifier clientMsgID . Message receipt on the remote peer is an asynchronous stage handled via incoming message events. See Receive messages /sdk/harmony/message/receiving messages/receive messages for complete event listener examples.

title: User overview
description: Understand user profiles, account-level preferences, and online presence in the OpenIM HarmonyOS SDK.
keywords: sdk harmony v4 sdk harmony user overview-user
content: OpenIMClientSDK uses userID as the unique user identifier. The user domain manages personal profiles, public profiles of other users, global notification settings, friend application permissions, and online presence. Friendships, friend applications, and blocklists belong to the relationship domain, whereas group specific nicknames and role levels belong to the group domain. Data models | Model | Purpose | | | | | IMUser | Account level and public profile information for self and other users. | | IMFriend | Friend relationship record, including private remarks and relationship extensions. | | IMBlack | Blocklist entry maintained by the current account. | | IMGroupMember | Group specific nickname, avatar, role level, and mute status. | | UserOnlinePlatform | Platform presence details for online users. | A single user can appear simultaneously across multiple data sources. Contact lists should prioritize friend remarks, group rosters should display group member nicknames, and conversation headers should use showName . Never overwrite context specific display labels with public nicknames. Common operations Retrieve user profiles /sdk/harmony/user/profile/get users info Retrieve current user profile /sdk/harmony/user/profile/get self user info Update current user profile /sdk/harmony/user/profile/set self info Set global message reception /sdk/harmony/user/profile/set global message reception Set friend request permission /sdk/harmony/user/profile/set friend add permission Subscribe to user online status /sdk/harmony/user/online status/subscribe users status Query APIs establish initial data snapshots, while event listeners merge incremental updates in real time. Remember that API Promise resolution, asynchronous event arrival, and post reconnection reconciliation represent three distinct stages.

title: Retrieve user profiles
description: Batch query public account profiles for a list of user IDs.
keywords: sdk harmony v4 sdk harmony user profile get-users-info
content: Batch querying user profiles is ideal for stranger profile cards, contact recommendations, or message sender headers.
