description: Delete all message history stored locally and on the server for the current account.
keywords: sdk harmony v4 sdk harmony message managing-messages clear-all-messages
content: This operation affects all conversations belonging to the current account and is not intended as an action for individual messages or single conversations. Code example import sdk from '@openimsdk/imsdk'; await sdk.deleteAllMsgFromLocalAndServer ; resetAllMessageState ; Parameters This method does not take any parameters. Return value Returns a Promise that resolves to void upon server acceptance and local database completion. State changes after the call This is an irreversible account wide operation. When the Promise resolves, clear all in memory message feeds, search results, pagination states, and related caches for the current account. It does not delete copies held by other conversation participants, nor does it guarantee that other active devices of the current user have already refreshed their UI. To clear only local database records, see Clear all local messages /sdk/harmony/message/managing messages/clear all local messages ; to clear messages within a specific conversation, see Clear conversation messages /sdk/harmony/conversation/managing conversations/clear conversation messages .

title: Delete local message
description: Delete a single message from the current device only.
keywords: sdk harmony v4 sdk harmony message managing-messages delete-local-message
content: Deletes a single message record from the local device database without affecting server records or other clients. Code example import sdk, DeleteMessageFromLocalReq from '@openimsdk/imsdk'; const request: DeleteMessageFromLocalReq = conversationID: conversationID, clientMsgID: message.clientMsgID, ; await sdk.deleteMessageFromLocal request ; removeMessage conversationID, message.clientMsgID ; Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | conversationID | string | Yes | Target conversation identifier. | | clientMsgID | string | Yes | Client message identifier of the target message. | Return value Returns a Promise that resolves to void when the local message record is deleted. State changes after the call Both IDs should come from the active conversation context and the target message object. Remove the item from UI state by matching clientMsgID qualified by conversationID if needed . Promise resolution indicates only that the message was removed from the local device database; server records may still exist and could re synchronize after full database rebuilds. This action does not broadcast events to other devices or conversation participants. For multi device synchronized deletion, see Batch delete messages /sdk/harmony/message/managing messages/delete saved messages ; for message revocation, see Revoke message /sdk/harmony/message/managing messages/revoke a message .

title: Clear all local messages
description: Delete all cached messages for the current account on the local device.
keywords: sdk harmony v4 sdk harmony message managing-messages clear-all-local-messages
content: Deletes all message history stored in local database storage on the current device for the signed in account. Code example import sdk from '@openimsdk/imsdk'; await sdk.deleteAllMessageFromLocal ; resetAllMessageState ; Parameters This method does not take any parameters. Return value Returns a Promise that resolves to void when the local database operation completes. State changes after the call This is an irreversible account wide local operation. After the Promise resolves, immediately reset in memory message lists, search indices, pagination cursors, and related caches for the current account. This action does not notify other devices or conversation participants; messages may still exist on the server and could reappear after full synchronization. To purge messages from both the local database and the server, see Clear all local and remote messages /sdk/harmony/message/managing messages/clear all messages ; to clear messages for a single conversation, see Clear conversation messages /sdk/harmony/conversation/managing conversations/clear conversation messages .

title: Insert local single chat message
description: Insert a local-only message into the single chat history on the current device.
keywords: sdk harmony v4 sdk harmony message managing-messages insert-local-single-message
content: Local insertion is intended for device local system prompts, notices, or migration data that should not be transmitted to the peer. Code example import sdk, InsertSingleMessageToLocalReq, InsertSingleMessageToLocalResp, from '@openimsdk/imsdk'; const request: InsertSingleMessageToLocalReq = msg: message, recvID: targetUserID, sendID: currentUserID, ; const response: InsertSingleMessageToLocalResp = await sdk.insertSingleMessageToLocal request ; insertMessage response.msg ; Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | msg | IMMessage | Yes | Message object to insert into the local database. | | recvID | string | Yes | Recipient user ID in the single chat. | | sendID | string | Yes | Sender user ID. | Return value Returns a Promise resolving to InsertSingleMessageToLocalResp : | Property | Type | Description | | | | | | msg | IMMessage | The inserted message object. | State changes after the call sendID and recvID must match the destination single chat conversation. Clients merge inserted records into local feeds using clientMsgID qualified by conversationID as needed . Resolving the Promise affects only the current device without sending network messages, triggering offline push notifications, or firing new message events. To insert local messages in group chats, see Insert local group message /sdk/harmony/message/managing messages/insert local group message .

title: Insert local group message
description: Insert a local-only message into the group chat history on the current device.
keywords: sdk harmony v4 sdk harmony message managing-messages insert-local-group-message
content: Inserts a synthetic or migrated message directly into the local device database for a group chat. Code example import sdk, InsertGroupMessageToLocalReq, InsertGroupMessageToLocalResp from '@openimsdk/imsdk'; const request: InsertGroupMessageToLocalReq = msg: message, groupID: groupID, sendID: currentUserID, ; const response: InsertGroupMessageToLocalResp = await sdk.insertGroupMessageToLocal request ; insertMessage response.msg ; Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | msg | IMMessage | Yes | Message object to insert into the local database. | | groupID | string | Yes | Target group identifier. | | sendID | string | Yes | Sender user ID shown on the message bubble. | Return value Returns a Promise resolving to InsertGroupMessageToLocalResp : | Property | Type | Description | | | | | | msg | IMMessage | The inserted message object with initialized database state. | State changes after the call groupID and sendID must match the message routing and display context. Merge the inserted item into UI feeds using clientMsgID qualified by conversationID as needed . Resolving the Promise modifies only the local database of the current device; it does not dispatch messages to group members or trigger shared message arrival events. To insert a local message in single chat, see Insert local single message /sdk/harmony/message/managing messages/insert local single message .

title: Set message local extension
description: Update the device-local extension field of a message on the current client.
keywords: sdk harmony v4 sdk harmony message managing-messages set-message-local-ex
content: localEx is stored exclusively on the current device, making it ideal for UI folding, selection flags, local source tags, or application specific audio transcription text. Code example import sdk, SetMessageLocalExReq from '@openimsdk/imsdk'; const request: SetMessageLocalExReq = conversationID: conversationID, clientMsgID: message.clientMsgID, localEx: JSON.stringify selected: true, transcript: 'Transcribed speech text' , ; await sdk.setMessageLocalEx request ; Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | conversationID | string | Yes | Target conversation identifier. | | clientMsgID | string | Yes | Client message identifier of the target message. | | localEx | string | Yes | Device local extension string. | Return value Returns a Promise that resolves to void when the local database write completes. State changes after the call This method does not automatically merge previous JSON fields. When multiple application modules share this property, read and validate existing values first, merge attributes in your business layer, and write back the entire string. Clients locate the record using clientMsgID qualified by conversationID as needed . Resolving the Promise confirms the local database update without triggering shared message events.

title: Get pinned messages in conversation
description: Query all currently pinned messages within a conversation.
keywords: sdk harmony v4 sdk harmony message managing-messages get-pinned-messages
content: Retrieves all pinned messages for a specific conversation by conversationID . Code example import sdk, GetConversationPinnedMsgReq, GetConversationPinnedMsgResp from '@openimsdk/imsdk'; const request: GetConversationPinnedMsgReq = conversationID: conversationID ; const response: GetConversationPinnedMsgResp = await sdk.getConversationPinnedMsg request ; replacePinnedMessages conversationID, response.message ; Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | conversationID | string | Yes | Target conversation identifier. | Return value Returns a Promise resolving to GetConversationPinnedMsgResp : | Property | Type | Description | | | | | | message | IMMessage | Array of currently pinned messages within the conversation. | State changes after the call In the response payload, message is an array of IMMessage objects. When rendering pinned messages, deduplicate by clientMsgID and reconcile against recent deletion, revocation, or edit events. This query does not fire pin change events; for real time synchronization, see Pin or unpin a message /sdk/harmony/message/managing messages/set message pinned .

title: Pin or unpin message
description: Pin or unpin a message within a conversation.
keywords: sdk harmony v4 sdk harmony message managing-messages set-message-pinned
content: Use pinned to toggle the pinned status of a message. Code example import sdk, EventOnChangedPinnedMsgData, OpenIMSDKEvent, SetConversationPinnedMsgReq, from '@openimsdk/imsdk'; const request: SetConversationPinnedMsgReq = conversationID: conversationID, clientMsgID: message.clientMsgID, pinned: true, ; await sdk.setConversationPinnedMsg request ; const handlePinnedMessagesChanged = data: EventOnChangedPinnedMsgData : void = replacePinnedMessageRecords data.conversationID, data.msgs ; ; const unsubscribePinnedMessages = sdk.on OpenIMSDKEvent.EventOnChangedPinnedMsg, handlePinnedMessagesChanged, ; export function removePinnedMessageListener : void unsubscribePinnedMessages ; Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | conversationID | string | Yes | Target conversation identifier. | | clientMsgID | string | Yes | Client message identifier of the target message. | | pinned | boolean | Yes | Pass true to pin the message; pass false to unpin it. | Return value Returns a Promise that resolves to void upon server acceptance. State changes after the call Permissions, eligible message types, and maximum pin count limits are verified by OpenIMServer. Resolving the Promise confirms server processing, but does not indicate that the change event has arrived. The msgs property in the event delivers records containing pinner identity, timestamps, and message details. Clients reconcile pinned states using conversationID and clientMsgID . To load initial pinned messages, see Get pinned messages in conversation /sdk/harmony/message/managing messages/get pinned messages . Remove listeners when disposing of the state layer.

title: Send group message read receipts
description: Report member-level read receipts for group messages and listen for read detail updates.
keywords: sdk harmony v4 sdk harmony message managing-read-status send-group-read-receipts
content: All messages within a single batch must belong to the target group chat conversation. Code example import sdk, EventOnRecvGroupReadReceiptData, OpenIMSDKEvent, SendGroupMessageReadReceiptReq, from '@openimsdk/imsdk'; const request: SendGroupMessageReadReceiptReq = conversationID: conversationID, clientMsgIDs: visibleUnreadMessageIDs, ; await sdk.sendGroupMessageReadReceipt request ; const handleGroupReadReceipt = data: EventOnRecvGroupReadReceiptData : void = mergeGroupMessageReadInfo data.groupMessageReceipt.conversationID, data.groupMessageReceipt.groupMessageReadInfo, ; ; const unsubscribeGroupReadReceipt = sdk.on OpenIMSDKEvent.EventOnRecvGroupReadReceipt, handleGroupReadReceipt, ; export function removeGroupReadReceiptListener : void unsubscribeGroupReadReceipt ; Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | conversationID | string | Yes | Target group conversation identifier. | | clientMsgIDs | string | Yes | Array of client message IDs marked as read. | Return value Returns a Promise that resolves to void upon server acceptance. State changes after the call Do not include messages from other conversations or messages that have not yet been rendered to the user. Clients reconcile message read status using clientMsgID qualified by conversationID as needed . Promise resolution, receipt event delivery, and reader list queries represent three distinct stages. To query which members have read a message, see Get group message readers /sdk/harmony/message/managing read status/get group message readers ; conversation unread counters are maintained independently by conversation level read APIs. Remove the listener when disposing of the state layer.

title: Get group message readers
description: Paginate read or unread member status for a specific group message.
keywords: sdk harmony v4 sdk harmony message managing-read-status get-group-message-readers
content: Locates the target group message using conversationID and clientMsgID . Code example import sdk, GetGroupMessageReaderListReq, GetGroupMessageReaderListResp from '@openimsdk/imsdk'; const request: GetGroupMessageReaderListReq = conversationID: conversationID, clientMsgID: message.clientMsgID, filter: 0, offset: 0, count: 50, ; const response: GetGroupMessageReaderListResp = await sdk.getGroupMessageReaderList request ; const readers = response.readers; Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | conversationID | string | Yes | Target conversation identifier. | | clientMsgID | string | Yes | Client message identifier of the target group message. | | filter | number | Yes | 0 for read members; 1 for unread members. | | offset | number | Yes | Starting offset index for pagination. | | count | number | Yes | Number of records to return. | Return value Returns a Promise resolving to GetGroupMessageReaderListResp : | Property | Type | Description | | | | | | readers | GroupMessageReader | Array of member items matching the filter. | State changes after the call Pass filter: 0 to query members who have read the message, or 1 for unread members. Clients deduplicate items by groupID:userID . This method uses offset based pagination; when the returned item count is less than count , the end of the list has been reached. This is a read only query that does not fire receipt events. To report group message read receipts, see Send group message read receipts /sdk/harmony/message/managing read status/send group read receipts .

title: Upload file
description: Upload a local file to remote object storage and obtain its remote URL.
keywords: sdk harmony v4 sdk harmony file-uploads upload-file
content: File upload is an independent infrastructure utility used for user avatars, group icons, profile attachments, or arbitrary business assets. This method operates independently of messages and does not automatically create or send a chat message. Code example import sdk, EventOnUploadFileProgressData, OpenIMSDKEvent, UploadFileReq, UploadFileResp, from '@openimsdk/imsdk'; const cancelID = avatar $ Date.now ; const handleUploadProgress = data: EventOnUploadFileProgressData : void = setCurrentUploadProgress data.progress ; ; const unsubscribeUploadProgress = sdk.on OpenIMSDKEvent.EventOnUploadFileProgress, handleUploadProgress, ; const request: UploadFileReq = filepath: selectedImagePath, name: 'avatar.jpg', mimeType: 'image/jpeg', fileCategory: 'image', cancelID: cancelID, data: '', ; const response: UploadFileResp = await sdk.uploadFile request ; await updateProfileAvatar response.url ; export function removeUploadProgressListener : void unsubscribeUploadProgress ; Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | filepath | string | Yes | Local filesystem path readable by the native engine. | | name | string | Yes | The file name including a valid extension. | | mimeType | string | Yes | Standard MIME type representing the file format. | | fileCategory | string | Yes | Storage bucket category defined by the backend server. | | cancelID | string | Yes | Unique string identifier generated by the application to track or cancel the task. | | data | string | Yes | Pass an empty string when uploading by path; reserved for specific backend payload extensions. | Return value Returns a Promise that resolves to an UploadFileResp object: | Property | Type | Description | | | | | | url | string | The publicly accessible remote URL of the uploaded file. | State changes after the call The EventOnUploadFileProgress callback reports only the integer progress value without an associated task identifier. If running multiple concurrent uploads, serialize them or track active jobs at the application layer to avoid progress ambiguity. Resolving the Promise indicates only that the file has uploaded successfully to remote storage; applying the URL to a user profile, group avatar, or chat message requires invoking the corresponding domain API. To abort an in flight upload, see Cancel file upload /sdk/harmony/file uploads/cancel upload . Call removeUploadProgressListener to detach the event callback when the task completes.

title: Cancel file upload
description: Terminate an in-progress file upload task using its cancellation identifier.
keywords: sdk harmony v4 sdk harmony file-uploads cancel-upload
content: Generate a unique cancellation identifier before initiating an upload and store it alongside your application upload task. Concurrent uploads must use distinct IDs. Code example import sdk, CancelUploadReq from '@openimsdk/imsdk'; const request: CancelUploadReq = cancelID: cancelID ; await sdk.cancelUpload request ; Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | cancelID | string | Yes | The cancellation identifier originally assigned in the UploadFileReq . | Return value Returns a Promise that resolves to void when the cancellation instruction has been issued to the network pipeline. State changes after the call If the upload task has already concluded, the cancelID does not exist, or the server already received the entire payload, the final outcome depends on the current pipeline state. Application logic should handle rejection on the original uploadFile Promise and prevent subsequent profile or message updates. For initiating uploads and tracking progress, see Upload file /sdk/harmony/file uploads/upload file . Cancelling an upload does not delete remote files that were already committed to storage, nor does it revoke any previously dispatched messages.

title: Audio and video calling overview
description: Understand call signaling, room credentials, and RTC lifecycle boundaries in the OpenIM HarmonyOS SDK.
keywords: sdk harmony v4 sdk harmony calling overview-calling
content: The OpenIM HarmonyOS SDK provides call signaling APIs to initiate, accept, reject, cancel, and hang up calls, as well as query active group rooms, refresh room credentials, and restore unhandled incoming invitations. The SDK manages signaling channels and room session metadata; it does not handle camera capture, microphone input, remote media rendering, or calling UI components. Pass the provided roomID , token , and liveURL to your selected WebRTC or third party real time media engine, and manage hardware permissions, media tracks, quality monitoring, and UI presentation in application code. Lifecycle workflow 1. The caller constructs a complete SignalingInvitationInfo payload and initiates an invitation via Start single call /sdk/harmony/calling/managing calls/start single call or Start group call /sdk/harmony/calling/managing calls/start group call . 2. The invitee listens for incoming calls in Handle call events /sdk/harmony/calling/managing calls/handle call events , or retrieves pending invitations during application cold starts via Restore pending call invitation /sdk/harmony/calling/retrieving call information/restore pending invitation . 3. The callee calls Accept call /sdk/harmony/calling/managing calls/accept call to obtain room credentials and join the media engine session, or dismisses the call UI via Reject call /sdk/harmony/calling/managing calls/reject call . 4. During an active call, synchronize room status using the unique roomID , and track individual participant presence using each participant's userID . 5. The caller can cancel an unanswered call using Cancel call /sdk/harmony/calling/managing calls/cancel call , while connected participants end active sessions using Hang up call /sdk/harmony/calling/managing calls/hang up call . The SignalingParticipantMetaData object contains the participant's IMUser profile, while OfflinePushInfo defines push notification payloads delivered when invitees are offline. Room tokens are time sensitive; always use the token returned by the active invitation or re fetch valid tokens before joining media channels. Resolving a signaling Promise, receiving signaling events, and executing room status queries represent three separate stages. Resolving a signaling API call does not imply that remote RTC channels are connected or that remote peers have rendered updated UI views.

title: Start single call
description: Initiate a 1-on-1 audio or video call invitation to a specific user.
keywords: sdk harmony v4 sdk harmony calling managing-calls start-single-call
content: Generate a unique roomID for each call attempt and preserve the full invitation structure locally to support cancellation, hangup, and UI state restoration. Code example import sdk, OfflinePushInfo, Platform, SessionType, SignalingInvitationInfo, SignalingInviteReq, SignalingInviteResp, SignalingMediaType, SignalingParticipantMetaData, from '@openimsdk/imsdk'; const invitation: SignalingInvitationInfo = inviterUserID: currentUserID, inviteeUserIDList: peerUserID , customData: JSON.stringify source: 'contact card' , groupID: '', roomID: createCallRoomID , timeout: 30, mediaType: SignalingMediaType.SignalingMediaTypeVideo, platformID: Platform.HarmonyOS, sessionType: SessionType.Single, initiateTime: Date.now , busyLineUserIDList: , ; const offlinePush: OfflinePushInfo = title: 'Video call', desc: 'You have an incoming video call invitation', ex: '', iOSPushSound: 'default', iOSBadgeCount: true, SignalingInfo: '', ; const participant: SignalingParticipantMetaData = user: selfUser ; const request: SignalingInviteReq = invitation: invitation, offlinePush: offlinePush, participant: participant, userID: peerUserID, ; const response: SignalingInviteResp = await sdk.signalingInvite request ; Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | invitation | SignalingInvitationInfo | Yes | Call invitation payload containing room ID, media type, timeout, and participants. | | offlinePush | OfflinePushInfo | Yes | Push notification details delivered when the recipient is offline. | | participant | SignalingParticipantMetaData | Yes | Profile metadata of the calling user. | | userID | string | Yes | The target user ID. Must match the element in inviteeUserIDList . | Return value Returns a Promise that resolves to a SignalingInviteResp object: | Property | Type | Description | | | | | | roomID | string | The active room identifier. | | token | string | Dynamic authentication token required to enter the media room. | | liveURL | string | Streaming gateway or media server address. | | busyLineUserIDList | string | List of invitees who are currently busy in another call. | State changes after the call Pass the returned roomID , token , and liveURL to your media engine. Resolving the Promise confirms only that the signaling invite was dispatched to the server; it does not indicate that the callee has answered. Track local outgoing call state using roomID , and listen for accept, reject, cancel, or timeout events via Handle call events /sdk/harmony/calling/managing calls/handle call events .

title: Start group call
description: Invite designated group members to join an audio or video call.
keywords: sdk harmony v4 sdk harmony calling managing-calls start-group-call
content: A group call invitation targets only the explicit user IDs listed in inviteeUserIDList ; specifying groupID does not automatically invite all members in the group. Always generate a unique roomID for each call rather than reusing the group identifier. Code example import sdk, Platform, SessionType, SignalingInvitationInfo, SignalingInviteInGroupReq, SignalingInviteInGroupResp, SignalingMediaType, from '@openimsdk/imsdk'; const invitation: SignalingInvitationInfo = inviterUserID: currentUserID, inviteeUserIDList: selectedMemberIDs, customData: JSON.stringify source: 'group call' , groupID: groupID, roomID: createCallRoomID , timeout: 30, mediaType: SignalingMediaType.SignalingMediaTypeVideo, platformID: Platform.HarmonyOS, sessionType: SessionType.WriteGroup, initiateTime: Date.now , busyLineUserIDList: , ; const request: SignalingInviteInGroupReq = userID: primaryInviteeUserID, invitation: invitation, offlinePush: offlinePush, participant: participant, ; const response: SignalingInviteInGroupResp = await sdk.signalingInviteInGroup request ; Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | userID | string | Yes | Primary invitee user ID. Must also appear in inviteeUserIDList . | | invitation | SignalingInvitationInfo | Yes | Invitation object containing room ID, group ID, media type, timeout, and the invitee ID list. | | offlinePush | OfflinePushInfo | Yes | Offline push configuration for offline recipients. | | participant | SignalingParticipantMetaData | Yes | Profile information of the calling participant. | Return value Returns a Promise that resolves to a SignalingInviteInGroupResp containing roomID , token , liveURL , and busyLineUserIDList . State changes after the call Exclude the initiator, empty strings, and duplicate IDs from inviteeUserIDList . Any invitees listed in busyLineUserIDList do not block invitations from reaching other members. Resolving the Promise indicates that signaling invites were delivered to the server; it does not indicate that any group members have joined the room. Track the active call session using roomID , and monitor participant joins, rejects, and timeouts via Handle call events /sdk/harmony/calling/managing calls/handle call events .

title: Accept call
description: Accept an incoming call invitation and retrieve room credentials.
keywords: sdk harmony v4 sdk harmony calling managing-calls accept-call
content: Pass the original, complete invitation object received in incoming events or recovered during cold starts. Do not construct a partial invitation payload with only roomID . Code example import sdk, Platform, SignalingAcceptReq, SignalingAcceptResp from '@openimsdk/imsdk'; const request: SignalingAcceptReq = invitation: invitation, offlinePush: offlinePush, participant: participant, opUserPlatformID: Platform.HarmonyOS, userID: invitation.inviterUserID, ; const response: SignalingAcceptResp = await sdk.signalingAccept request ; await mediaEngineJoin response.roomID, response.token, response.liveURL ; Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | invitation | SignalingInvitationInfo | Yes | Complete invitation object originally delivered by incoming call events. | | offlinePush | OfflinePushInfo | Yes | Push notification configuration for offline participants. | | participant | SignalingParticipantMetaData | Yes | User metadata of the accepting participant. | | opUserPlatformID | Platform | Yes | Platform identifier of the accepting device Platform.HarmonyOS . | | userID | string | Yes | User ID of the inviter receiving the accept signal. | Return value Returns a Promise that resolves to a SignalingAcceptResp object: | Property | Type | Description | | | | | | roomID | string | The active room identifier. | | token | string | Authentication token for entering the RTC media room. | | liveURL | string | Media stream server address. | State changes after the call Resolving the Promise confirms that the acceptance signal was accepted by the server and returned room credentials. It does not establish media track connections; feed the credentials into your media engine to join the room. Track ongoing call and participant states using roomID and userID . For event handling across participants, see Handle call events /sdk/harmony/calling/managing calls/handle call events .

title: Reject call
description: Decline an unanswered incoming audio or video call invitation.
keywords: sdk harmony v4 sdk harmony calling managing-calls reject-call
content: Supply the complete invitation payload along with the callee's participant metadata to reject an incoming call: Code example import sdk, Platform, SignalingRejectReq from '@openimsdk/imsdk'; const request: SignalingRejectReq = invitation: invitation, offlinePush: offlinePush, participant: participant, opUserPlatformID: Platform.HarmonyOS, userID: invitation.inviterUserID, ; await sdk.signalingReject request ; Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | invitation | SignalingInvitationInfo | Yes | The complete call invitation object to reject. | | offlinePush | OfflinePushInfo | Yes | Push notification options for offline participants. | | participant | SignalingParticipantMetaData | Yes | User metadata of the rejecting participant. | | opUserPlatformID | Platform | Yes | Platform identifier of the rejecting device Platform.HarmonyOS . | | userID | string | Yes | User ID of the inviter receiving the rejection signal. | Return value Returns a Promise that resolves to void when the rejection signal is transmitted. State changes after the call Once the Promise resolves, dismiss the incoming call interface locally identified by roomID and release any reserved audio resources. The caller receives an invitation rejection event and updates UI accordingly. For remote event handling, see Handle call events /sdk/harmony/calling/managing calls/handle call events .

title: Cancel call
description: Cancel an unanswered call invitation by the calling initiator.
keywords: sdk harmony v4 sdk harmony calling managing-calls cancel-call
content: Use signalingCancel to cancel an outgoing call invitation before the callee answers: Code example import sdk, SignalingCancelReq from '@openimsdk/imsdk'; const request: SignalingCancelReq = invitation: invitation, offlinePush: offlinePush, participant: participant, userID: peerUserID, ; await sdk.signalingCancel request ; Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | invitation | SignalingInvitationInfo | Yes | The complete invitation object originally sent by the caller. | | offlinePush | OfflinePushInfo | Yes | Push notification payload delivered to offline devices. | | participant | SignalingParticipantMetaData | Yes | User metadata of the caller. | | userID | string | Yes | User ID of the invitee receiving the cancellation signal. | Return value Returns a Promise that resolves to void upon cancellation delivery. State changes after the call Once the Promise resolves, terminate the outgoing ringing view identified by roomID and release calling media resources. The callee receives an invitation cancelled event and dismisses their incoming call screen. For active calls that are already connected, use Hang up call /sdk/harmony/calling/managing calls/hang up call instead. To handle remote cancellation notifications, see Handle call events /sdk/harmony/calling/managing calls/handle call events .

title: Hang up call
description: Terminate an active audio or video call session.
keywords: sdk harmony v4 sdk harmony calling managing-calls hang-up-call
content: End an active call session by sending a hangup signal to the remote participant: Code example import sdk, SignalingHungUpReq from '@openimsdk/imsdk'; const request: SignalingHungUpReq = invitation: invitation, offlinePush: offlinePush, userID: peerUserID, ; await sdk.signalingHungUp request ; Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | invitation | SignalingInvitationInfo | Yes | Complete call invitation object representing the current active room. | | offlinePush | OfflinePushInfo | Yes | Push notification configuration for offline participants. | | userID | string | Yes | User ID of the participant receiving the hangup signal. | Return value Returns a Promise that resolves to void when the hangup signal is sent. State changes after the call The roomID inside invitation must match the active media session. Once the Promise resolves, terminate the local call session identified by roomID , stop camera/microphone capture, depart the RTC room, and release media hardware. Remote peers receive a hangup event and exit their media channels. We recommend implementing an idempotent cleanup helper shared across cancel, reject, timeout, and hangup flows. For peer event listeners, see Handle call events /sdk/harmony/calling/managing calls/handle call events .

title: Handle call events
description: Centrally listen for call invitations, acceptances, participant changes, cancellations, and hangup events.
keywords: sdk harmony v4 sdk harmony calling managing-calls handle-call-events
content: Register signaling lifecycle and participant status listeners within a centralized application calling controller. Every signaling event carries a typed payload correlated by invitation.roomID . Code example import sdk, EventOnHangUpData, EventOnInvitationCancelledData, EventOnInvitationTimeoutData, EventOnInviteeAcceptedByOtherDeviceData, EventOnInviteeAcceptedData, EventOnInviteeRejectedByOtherDeviceData, EventOnInviteeRejectedData, EventOnReceiveNewInvitationData, EventOnRoomParticipantConnectedData, EventOnRoomParticipantDisconnectedData, OpenIMSDKEvent, from '@openimsdk/imsdk'; const handleIncoming = data: EventOnReceiveNewInvitationData : void = showIncomingCall data.invitation, data.offlinePush, data.participant ; ; const handleAccepted = data: EventOnInviteeAcceptedData : void = markInviteeAccepted data.invitation.roomID, data.userID ; ; const handleAcceptedElsewhere = data: EventOnInviteeAcceptedByOtherDeviceData : void = finishLocalIncomingState data.invitation.roomID ; ; const handleRejected = data: EventOnInviteeRejectedData : void = markInviteeRejected data.invitation.roomID, data.userID ; ; const handleRejectedElsewhere = data: EventOnInviteeRejectedByOtherDeviceData : void = finishLocalIncomingState data.invitation.roomID ; ; const handleCancelled = data: EventOnInvitationCancelledData : void = closeCallAndReleaseMedia data.invitation.roomID ; ; const handleTimeout = data: EventOnInvitationTimeoutData : void = closeCallAndReleaseMedia data.invitation.roomID ; ; const handleHangUp = data: EventOnHangUpData : void = closeCallAndReleaseMedia data.invitation.roomID ; ; const handleParticipantConnected = data: EventOnRoomParticipantConnectedData : void = replaceCallParticipants data.invitation.roomID, data.participants ; ; const handleParticipantDisconnected = data: EventOnRoomParticipantDisconnectedData : void = replaceCallParticipants data.invitation.roomID, data.participants ; ; const unsubscribeIncoming = sdk.on OpenIMSDKEvent.EventOnReceiveNewInvitation, handleIncoming ; const unsubscribeAccepted = sdk.on OpenIMSDKEvent.EventOnInviteeAccepted, handleAccepted ; const unsubscribeAcceptedElsewhere = sdk.on OpenIMSDKEvent.EventOnInviteeAcceptedByOtherDevice, handleAcceptedElsewhere, ; const unsubscribeRejected = sdk.on OpenIMSDKEvent.EventOnInviteeRejected, handleRejected ; const unsubscribeRejectedElsewhere = sdk.on OpenIMSDKEvent.EventOnInviteeRejectedByOtherDevice, handleRejectedElsewhere, ; const unsubscribeCancelled = sdk.on OpenIMSDKEvent.EventOnInvitationCancelled, handleCancelled ; const unsubscribeTimeout = sdk.on OpenIMSDKEvent.EventOnInvitationTimeout, handleTimeout ; const unsubscribeHangUp = sdk.on OpenIMSDKEvent.EventOnHangUp, handleHangUp ; const unsubscribeParticipantConnected = sdk.on OpenIMSDKEvent.EventOnRoomParticipantConnected, handleParticipantConnected, ; const unsubscribeParticipantDisconnected = sdk.on OpenIMSDKEvent.EventOnRoomParticipantDisconnected, handleParticipantDisconnected, ; export function removeCallListeners : void unsubscribeIncoming ; unsubscribeAccepted ; unsubscribeAcceptedElsewhere ; unsubscribeRejected ; unsubscribeRejectedElsewhere ; unsubscribeCancelled ; unsubscribeTimeout ; unsubscribeHangUp ; unsubscribeParticipantConnected ; unsubscribeParticipantDisconnected ; State changes after the call Multi device coordination : When another device signs into the same account and accepts or rejects the call, the current device receives EventOnInviteeAcceptedByOtherDevice or EventOnInviteeRejectedByOtherDevice and must dismiss its incoming call screen immediately. Idempotent teardown : Implement teardown handlers for EventOnInvitationCancelled , EventOnInvitationTimeout , and EventOnHangUp idempotently to handle out of order delivery gracefully. Participant roster : Participant connect and disconnect events report updated SignalingParticipantMetaData lists for the specified room; track actual audio/video stream publishing states via your RTC media engine callbacks. Cleanup : Invoke removeCallListeners when the user signs out or the application terminates the call manager.

title: Restore pending call invitation
description: Query unhandled call invitations still pending when the app launches or returns to the foreground.
keywords: sdk harmony v4 sdk harmony calling retrieving-call-information restore-pending-invitation
content: When the app cold starts, resumes from the background, or reconnects after missed incoming call events, check for unhandled call invitations targeted at the current account: Code example import sdk, SignalingGetInvitationInfoStartAppReq, SignalingGetInvitationInfoStartAppResp, from '@openimsdk/imsdk'; const request: SignalingGetInvitationInfoStartAppReq = userID: currentUserID ; const response: SignalingGetInvitationInfoStartAppResp = await sdk.signalingGetInvitationInfoStartApp request ; if response.invitation.roomID.length 0 restoreIncomingCall response.invitation, response.offlinePush ; Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | userID | string | Yes | The currently logged in user identifier. | Return value Returns a Promise that resolves to a SignalingGetInvitationInfoStartAppResp object: | Property | Type | Description | | | | | | invitation | SignalingInvitationInfo | The unhandled call invitation object. | | offlinePush | OfflinePushInfo | The push notification payload accompanying the invitation. | State changes after the call Specify only the currently signed in user's ID; do not query invitations for other accounts. If response.invitation.roomID is empty, dismiss any lingering incoming call dialogs and clear cached credentials. This query only checks invitation state; it does not automatically accept, reject, or re emit signaling events.

title: Query group call room
description: Retrieve the active calling room associated with a group ID.
keywords: sdk harmony v4 sdk harmony calling retrieving-call-information get-room-by-group-id
content: Query whether a specific group has an ongoing audio or video call session: Code example import sdk, SignalingGetRoomByGroupIDReq, SignalingGetRoomByGroupIDResp from '@openimsdk/imsdk'; const request: SignalingGetRoomByGroupIDReq = groupID: groupID ; const response: SignalingGetRoomByGroupIDResp = await sdk.signalingGetRoomByGroupID request ; if response.roomID.length 0 restoreGroupCall response.roomID, response.invitation, response.participants ; Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | groupID | string | Yes | Target group identifier. | Return value Returns a Promise that resolves to a SignalingGetRoomByGroupIDResp object: | Property | Type | Description | | | | | | roomID | string | Room identifier. An empty string indicates no call is currently active in this group. | | invitation | SignalingInvitationInfo | Complete call invitation object for the active session. | | participants | SignalingParticipantMetaData | List of participants currently present in the room. | State changes after the call An empty roomID confirms that there is no active call in the specified group. When a non empty roomID is returned, call Get call room credentials /sdk/harmony/calling/retrieving call information/get token by room id to obtain the credentials required to join the RTC channel. If the query rejects due to network failure, do not treat the error as an empty room state; retry when the network is restored.

title: Get call room credentials
description: Refresh or retrieve the media room token and gateway URL by room ID.
keywords: sdk harmony v4 sdk harmony calling retrieving-call-information get-token-by-room-id
content: Use signalingGetTokenByRoomID to refresh room credentials when joining an existing room or reconnecting to a session: Code example import sdk, SignalingGetTokenByRoomIDReq, SignalingGetTokenByRoomIDResp from '@openimsdk/imsdk'; const request: SignalingGetTokenByRoomIDReq = roomID: roomID, userID: currentUserID, participant: participant, ; const response: SignalingGetTokenByRoomIDResp = await sdk.signalingGetTokenByRoomID request ; await mediaEngineJoin roomID, response.token, response.liveURL ; Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | roomID | string | Yes | Target call room identifier. | | userID | string | Yes | Current user ID joining or reconnecting to the room. | | participant | SignalingParticipantMetaData | Yes | Current user participant metadata. | Return value Returns a Promise that resolves to a SignalingGetTokenByRoomIDResp object: | Property | Type | Description | | | | | | token | string | Fresh token for joining the RTC media session. | | liveURL | string | Media gateway server URL. | State changes after the call The response returns credentials for the requested room; reuse the existing roomID from the request when configuring your media client. Only proceed to connect your media engine once non empty token and liveURL values are obtained. If the query rejects, verify network connectivity and ensure the room has not already been dismantled.

title: Send custom signaling
description: Send lightweight business negotiation payloads within a designated call room.
keywords: sdk harmony v4 sdk harmony calling sending-custom-signals send-a-custom-signal
content: Custom signaling is designed for in call business events such as hand raising, layout switching notifications, or custom room status broadcasts. It is not an alternative to standard chat messages or high throughput RTC data channels. Code example import sdk, EventOnReceiveCustomSignalingData, OpenIMSDKEvent, SignalingSendCustomSignalingReq, from '@openimsdk/imsdk'; const request: SignalingSendCustomSignalingReq = roomID: roomID, customInfo: JSON.stringify version: 1, eventID: createBusinessEventID , type: 'hand raised', userID: currentUserID, , ; await sdk.signalingSendCustomSignaling request ; const handleCustomSignal = data: EventOnReceiveCustomSignalingData : void = const signal = parseAndValidateCallSignal data.customInfo ; applyCallSignal data.roomID, signal ; ; const unsubscribeCustomSignal = sdk.on OpenIMSDKEvent.EventOnReceiveCustomSignaling, handleCustomSignal, ; export function removeCustomSignalListener : void unsubscribeCustomSignal ; Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | roomID | string | Yes | Target call room identifier. | | customInfo | string | Yes | Application defined string payload typically JSON serialized . | Return value Returns a Promise that resolves to void when the signal has been submitted to the server. State changes after the call Promise resolution indicates that the server accepted the custom signal, not that remote participants have parsed or rendered it. Keep the customInfo payload concise, include a schema version and unique event ID, and avoid using signaling for persistent room state. Receivers correlate the payload by roomID . Detach the listener with removeCustomSignalListener when navigating away from the call view.

title: Event listener overview
description: Register, consume, and clean up OpenIM HarmonyOS SDK events across application and account lifecycles.
keywords: sdk harmony v4 sdk harmony events overview-events
content: The sdk.on method registers an event listener and returns a cancellation callback. Maintain stable function references for all event handlers; do not register anonymous closures inside reactive component render methods. Connection, message, and call signaling events should reside in global or account level state stores, whereas page scoped listeners should be unsubscribed when the view unmounts. | Event domain | Primary documentation page | | | | | Connection, token, and sign out | Authenticate and manage session /sdk/harmony/getting started/authenticate and manage session | | Conversation lists and unread badges | Retrieve conversation list /sdk/harmony/conversation/retrieving conversations/retrieve conversation list | | Users, relationships, groups, and members | User overview /sdk/harmony/user/overview user , Group overview /sdk/harmony/group/overview group | | Incoming messages | Receive messages /sdk/harmony/message/receiving messages/receive messages | | File uploads | Upload file /sdk/harmony/file uploads/upload file | | Audio and video calls | Handle call events /sdk/harmony/calling/managing calls/handle call events | Listen for server data synchronization After successful sign in, the SDK synchronizes state with OpenIMServer. The reinstalled flag indicates whether the sync occurred after a fresh installation or local database reset. Once synchronization finishes, reload visible UI snapshots from the local cache. Code example import sdk, EventOnSyncServerFailedData, EventOnSyncServerFinishData, EventOnSyncServerProgressData, EventOnSyncServerStartData, OpenIMSDKEvent, from '@openimsdk/imsdk'; const handleSyncStart = data: EventOnSyncServerStartData : void = setSyncState 'syncing', 0, data.reinstalled ; ; const handleSyncProgress = data: EventOnSyncServerProgressData : void = setSyncState 'syncing', data.progress, false ; ; const handleSyncFinish = data: EventOnSyncServerFinishData : void = setSyncState 'ready', 100, data.reinstalled ; reloadVisibleData ; ; const handleSyncFailed = data: EventOnSyncServerFailedData : void = setSyncState 'failed', 0, data.reinstalled ; ; const unsubscribeSyncStart = sdk.on OpenIMSDKEvent.EventOnSyncServerStart, handleSyncStart ; const unsubscribeSyncProgress = sdk.on OpenIMSDKEvent.EventOnSyncServerProgress, handleSyncProgress, ; const unsubscribeSyncFinish = sdk.on OpenIMSDKEvent.EventOnSyncServerFinish, handleSyncFinish ; const unsubscribeSyncFailed = sdk.on OpenIMSDKEvent.EventOnSyncServerFailed, handleSyncFailed ; export function removeSyncListeners : void unsubscribeSyncStart ; unsubscribeSyncProgress ; unsubscribeSyncFinish ; unsubscribeSyncFailed ; Listen for local database migration When upgrading the SDK or modifying local database schemas, the engine may initiate an automatic migration. Do not query or populate views from local stores while migration is active. import sdk, EventOnMigrationFailedData, EventOnMigrationProgressData, OpenIMSDKEmptyPayload, OpenIMSDKEvent, from '@openimsdk/imsdk'; const handleMigrationStart = data: OpenIMSDKEmptyPayload : void = setMigrationState 'running', 0, '' ; ; const handleMigrationProgress = data: EventOnMigrationProgressData : void = setMigrationState 'running', data.progress, data.message ; ; const handleMigrationFinished = data: OpenIMSDKEmptyPayload : void = setMigrationState 'finished', 100, '' ; ; const handleMigrationFailed = data: EventOnMigrationFailedData : void = setMigrationFailed data.errCode, data.errMsg ; ; const unsubscribeMigrationStart = sdk.on OpenIMSDKEvent.EventOnMigrationStart, handleMigrationStart, ; const unsubscribeMigrationProgress = sdk.on OpenIMSDKEvent.EventOnMigrationProgress, handleMigrationProgress, ; const unsubscribeMigrationFinished = sdk.on OpenIMSDKEvent.EventOnMigrationFinished, handleMigrationFinished, ; const unsubscribeMigrationFailed = sdk.on OpenIMSDKEvent.EventOnMigrationFailed, handleMigrationFailed, ; export function removeMigrationListeners : void unsubscribeMigrationStart ; unsubscribeMigrationProgress ; unsubscribeMigrationFinished ; unsubscribeMigrationFailed ; When signing out or disposing of application stores, call removeSyncListeners and removeMigrationListeners to release references. Because network notifications may arrive out of order, merge domain objects using stable unique keys: userID , conversationID , groupID , groupID:userID , and clientMsgID .

title: Logging and diagnostics
description: Configure OpenIM HarmonyOS SDK logging, record diagnostic telemetry, and upload diagnostics.
keywords: sdk harmony v4 sdk harmony logger
content: The OpenIM HarmonyOS SDK writes core engine logs to internal application directories or system logs, and provides capabilities to temporarily modify log verbosity levels, append custom diagnostic events, and upload diagnostic artifacts for troubleshooting. Initialize logging configuration Specify a writable application sandbox directory for logs during SDK initialization. Set isLogStandardOutput to control whether logs are also mirrored to system console output hilog . Code example import sdk, HttpClientMode, InitSDKReq, LogLevel from '@openimsdk/imsdk'; const request: InitSDKReq = config: apiAddr: apiAddress, wsAddr: websocketAddress, dataDir: context.filesDir, dbPath: context.databaseDir, logFilePath: context.filesDir + '/openim logs', logLevel: LogLevel.LevelInfo, isLogStandardOutput: false, StopGoroutineOnBackground: false, LogRemainCount: 7, diagnoseHashSalt: diagnoseHashSalt, httpClientMode: HttpClientMode.TCPFirst, , ; await sdk.initSDK request ; | Log level | Description | | | | | LevelFatal , LevelPanic | Critical fatal conditions that cause abnormal termination. | | LevelError , LevelWarn | Actionable runtime errors and operational warnings. | | LevelInfo | Informational events for standard execution flow and debugging. | | LevelDebug , LevelDebugWithSQL | Verbose troubleshooting details, including SQL execution statements. | Adjust log level temporarily Elevate the SDK logging level for a specific duration without permanently altering your baseline startup configuration: import sdk, LogLevel, SetTemporaryLogLevelReq from '@openimsdk/imsdk'; const request: SetTemporaryLogLevelReq = logLevel: LogLevel.LevelDebug, durationSeconds: 600, ; await sdk.setTemporaryLogLevel request ; Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | logLevel | LogLevel | Yes | Target temporary log level to activate. | | durationSeconds | number | Yes | Lifetime of the temporary level in seconds. Once expired, the SDK reverts to its initial level. | Return value Returns a Promise that resolves to void when the temporary log level is applied. Record application diagnostic logs Call log to write application level diagnostic records into the unified SDK log stream. Regular business APIs do not require an explicit operationID because the SDK generates one automatically; in logging and diagnostic contexts, you can supply a custom operationID to correlate operations across distributed traces: import sdk, LogLevel, LogReq from '@openimsdk/imsdk'; const request: LogReq = logLevel: LogLevel.LevelInfo, file: 'ConversationStore.ets', line: 120, msg: 'conversation reload requested', err: '', kvs: , ; const operationID = createDiagnosticOperationID ; await sdk.log request, operationID ; Register a process level log callback using setLogCallback to receive raw native core log strings. Submitting a new callback replaces any previous registration, so register from a centralized diagnostic manager: const handleNativeLog = message: string : void = appendSDKLog message ; ; sdk.setLogCallback handleNativeLog ; The internal debugging method emitLog is intended for native bridge test fixtures rather than production application logging. Upload diagnostic data Invoke uploadSDKData to upload logs, databases, or both depending on the selected mode . Monitor progress using the EventOnUploadSDKDataProgress event: import sdk, EventOnUploadSDKDataProgressData, OpenIMSDKEvent, UploadSDKDataMode, UploadSDKDataReq, from '@openimsdk/imsdk'; const handleDiagnosticProgress = data: EventOnUploadSDKDataProgressData : void = setDiagnosticUploadProgress data.progress ; ; const unsubscribeDiagnosticProgress = sdk.on OpenIMSDKEvent.EventOnUploadSDKDataProgress, handleDiagnosticProgress, ; const request: UploadSDKDataReq = line: 2000, ex: 'user approved diagnostic session', mode: UploadSDKDataMode.UploadLogs, cancelID: diagnostic $ Date.now , ; await sdk.uploadSDKData request ; unsubscribeDiagnosticProgress ; Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | line | number | Yes | Maximum number of log lines to extract for upload. | | ex | string | No | Custom diagnostic metadata attached to the upload request. | | mode | UploadSDKDataMode | Yes | Upload target type UploadLogs , UploadDatabase , or UploadAll . | | cancelID | string | Yes | Unique task identifier used to track or abort the upload operation. | Return value Returns a Promise that resolves to void upon successful completion of the upload task. If the operation fails, inspect the error code and message to determine network or storage causes.

title: OpenIM SDK for WASM
description: Integrate users, conversations, groups, messages, calling signals, realtime events, and local storage into browser applications with the OpenIM WASM SDK.
keywords: sdk wasm v4 sdk wasm overview

title: Before you start
description: Prepare OpenIMServer, user sign-in details, and the browser runtime before authenticating or sending messages.
keywords: sdk wasm v4 sdk wasm getting-started before-you-start
content: Before integrating the OpenIM WASM SDK into a browser application, prepare an accessible OpenIMServer deployment, the current user's sign in details, and the SDK runtime assets. These prerequisites apply to both authenticating and managing a session /sdk/wasm/getting started/authenticate and manage session and sending your first message /sdk/wasm/getting started/send first message . Prepare OpenIMServer If you do not yet have an OpenIMServer deployment, follow the Docker deployment guide /docs/guides/quick deployment/docker . Then verify that the browser can reach apiAddr and wsAddr , including HTTPS/WSS, reverse proxy, and cross origin settings. Browser sign in requires the following service addresses: | Field | Description | | | | | apiAddr | The OpenIMServer HTTP API address used for sign in, synchronization, and resource requests. Pages served over HTTPS must use an HTTPS address that the browser can reach. | | wsAddr | The OpenIMServer WebSocket address used to establish a persistent connection and receive realtime events. Pages served over HTTPS normally use a WSS address. | Do not only verify that the services are reachable from an internal network or the server itself. Test from the deployed application as well, and confirm that cross origin settings, HTTPS certificates, reverse proxy rules, and WebSocket upgrades all work correctly. Prepare the user and token userID identifies an OpenIMSDK user, while the token authenticates that user. The application backend creates or binds OpenIMSDK users, issues tokens, and enforces application permissions. The browser uses the user level sign in details returned by that backend. Before integrating your backend with the OpenIMServer REST API, see Prepare to use the Platform API /platform api/prepare to use api and Issue a session token /platform api/user/managing session tokens/issue a session token . If your product already has an account system, maintain a stable mapping between each application account and its OpenIMSDK userID , and make sure the returned token belongs to that userID . The application backend can expose a session endpoint that returns the information required by the SDK: type OpenIMSDKSession = userID: string; token: string; apiAddr: string; wsAddr: string; ; async function loadOpenIMSDKSession : Promise const response = await fetch '/api/openim/session' ; if response.ok throw new Error 'Failed to load OpenIMSDK session.' ; return response.json ; The application session endpoint returns the OpenIMSDK sign in details for the current application account. The userID and token must belong to the same user. Prepare the browser runtime The OpenIM WASM SDK depends on WebAssembly, WebSocket, and IndexedDB in the browser. Your project must also publish openIM.wasm , sql wasm.wasm , and wasm exec.js , and the page must be able to load them from the configured static asset paths. If your application uses a server rendering framework such as Next.js, Nuxt, or Remix, initialize the SDK, access the local database, and establish connections only in the browser. See Integrate by runtime /sdk/wasm/getting started/environment specific implementation for initialization locations and lifecycle handling in different environments. Before a production release, test the environments and networks your product actually supports: All three SDK assets load successfully, and their responses have not been replaced by a sign in page or error page. apiAddr accepts HTTP requests and wsAddr completes a WebSocket connection. IndexedDB can create and write to the local database. Private browsing, low storage conditions, and restoring the page after it enters the background behave as your product expects. Continue the integration After preparing these shared prerequisites, authenticate and manage the session /sdk/wasm/getting started/authenticate and manage session . Once the connection succeeds, send your first message /sdk/wasm/getting started/send first message to a prepared user or group and verify the messaging flow.

title: Environment-specific implementation
description: Choose the appropriate OpenIM SDK for browsers, SSR frameworks, Electron, and Mini Program runtimes, and understand the boundaries of each environment.
keywords: sdk wasm v4 sdk wasm getting-started environment-specific-implementation
content: Choose a runtime Before integrating an OpenIMSDK Web client, identify the target runtime. Browser pages, SSR frameworks, Electron applications, and Mini Program environments use the same user, conversation, message, group, and event models. However, their SDK distributions, asset loading methods, local storage capabilities, and runtime lifecycles differ. Select the appropriate SDK distribution for your target architecture and configure WASM assets, initialization options, and runtime boundaries. For message, conversation, group, and event capabilities, refer to their dedicated feature pages. Compare runtime environments | Runtime | Recommended SDK distribution | Intended use | | | | | | Web browser | WASM SDK | Browser applications that need a local cache, conversation list, message history, and the full Web client feature set. | | SSR framework | WASM SDK, initialized only on the client | Browser pages built with Next.js, Nuxt, Remix, and similar frameworks. The server supplies only the credentials and service addresses required for sign in. | | Electron Web or renderer layer | Electron SDK, WASM distribution | Electron renderer processes, WebViews, and other browser style pages. Integration is similar to the Web. | | Electron native desktop layer | Electron SDK, FFI distribution | Desktop packaging, native runtime capabilities, and integration with the desktop native runtime layer. | | Hybrid Web and Electron product | WASM and FFI | Products that support both a Web client and a packaged Electron application. Plan for both distributions and expose a unified application layer adapter. | | Mini Program or lightweight Web | Mini Program SDK | Mini Programs and lightweight Web scenarios. It does not provide local message storage and is suitable when local caching is unnecessary. | | React Native | React Native SDK | React Native is not a WASM runtime. Use the React Native SDK or a native bridge. | Prerequisites See Before you start /sdk/wasm/getting started/before you start for shared prerequisites such as service addresses, user tokens, and browser assets. Before publishing assets and initializing the SDK, confirm that: The OpenIMServer HTTP API address, apiAddr , and WebSocket address, wsAddr , are reachable from the target client. The current user has been bound to an OpenIMSDK user by your application backend and has a valid userID and token. The Web application or Electron renderer can access openIM.wasm , sql wasm.wasm , and wasm exec.js . Then check the requirements specific to the target runtime: SSR frameworks: initialize the SDK from a client component, browser lifecycle, or dynamic import. Electron: separate the responsibilities of the Web or renderer layer from the native desktop layer. Products that support both Web and packaged desktop clients normally need both WASM and FFI distributions. Mini Program SDK: make sure the product can operate without local message storage. Publish the runtime assets Install the browser WASM SDK with pnpm and copy its runtime assets during your build or deployment. The following example publishes them at the root of the site's static assets: pnpm add @openim/wasm client sdk cp R node modules/@openim/wasm client sdk/assets/ public/ Commit the dependency lockfile for team projects. When pinning the SDK, select a version verified by your team in testing. If the application is deployed behind a CDN, under a subpath, or inside an Electron package, replace the example paths with URLs that are actually accessible in that runtime. Initialize the browser SDK A browser application normally creates one SDK instance and reuses it throughout the session. Register connection and token lifecycle listeners as shown in Authenticate and manage a session /sdk/wasm/getting started/authenticate and manage session before invoking login . import getSDK, Platform from '@openim/wasm client sdk'; const openimsdk = getSDK coreWasmPath: '/openIM.wasm', sqlWasmPath: '/sql wasm.wasm', ; await openimsdk.login userID, token, platformID: Platform.Web, apiAddr, wsAddr, ; The login Promise succeeding and OnConnectSuccess arriving are separate stages. The former means that the sign in request has completed; the latter means that the connection is ready for subsequent business APIs. The authentication page provides the complete handlers, error callback data, and cleanup code. Use Platform.Web for browser sign in instead of entering a numeric platform value directly. If Electron or Mini Program clients participate in multi device session eviction, online status, or client type statistics, choose the appropriate Platform value according to the product's client types and the server's multi device sign in policy. Implement each runtime Web browsers For browsers, focus on assets, connectivity, and the local cache: wasm exec.js , openIM.wasm , and sql wasm.wasm must be accessible from production paths, not only from the local development server. The OpenIMServer HTTP API and WebSocket addresses must allow access from the current page and correctly handle HTTPS/WSS mixed content restrictions. The SDK local cache depends on browser storage. Do not read or write the SDK's IndexedDB or sql.js internals directly. Synchronize data into your application state through SDK APIs and events. Network changes, page foreground/background transitions, and focus recovery should be handled centrally by the SDK wrapper. Business components should not register duplicate low level runtime listeners. SSR frameworks Next.js, Nuxt, Remix, and similar frameworks execute some code on the server. Initialize the OpenIM WASM SDK only in a browser context. We recommend wrapping SDK creation in a client side function and loading the package through a dynamic import: import type getSDK as createOpenIMClientSDK from '@openim/wasm client sdk'; let openimsdk: ReturnType | undefined; export async function getOpenIMClientSDK if typeof window === 'undefined' throw new Error 'OpenIM WASM SDK must be initialized in the browser.' ; if openimsdk const getSDK = await import '@openim/wasm client sdk' ; openimsdk = getSDK coreWasmPath: '/openIM.wasm', sqlWasmPath: '/sql wasm.wasm', ; return openimsdk; Do not import and create an SDK instance in a React Server Component or server side API route. The server is responsible only for creating users, issuing tokens, and returning sign in parameters such as apiAddr and wsAddr . Electron The Electron SDK has WASM and FFI distributions. Use WASM in an Electron renderer process, WebView, or browser style page. Use FFI in the native desktop runtime layer. Choose the distribution based on the responsibilities of each runtime layer; use both when necessary. If one product supports both a Web client and a packaged Electron application, you normally need to plan for both WASM and FFI and expose a common business interface through an application layer adapter. When implementing Electron, verify that: With the WASM distribution, publish the WASM assets as you would for a browser and make sure the renderer can load scripts, WASM, WebSocket, HTTP API, and any Worker resources. With the FFI distribution, do not reuse browser WASM asset paths. Follow the installation, packaging, permission, and runtime requirements of the Electron FFI SDK. When using WASM and FFI together, decide which runtime layer owns sign in, connectivity, message events, and local state so that multiple SDK instances do not compete for the same user session. Desktop platform IDs may need to distinguish Windows, macOS, Linux, or Web clients. Follow the server's multi device sign in policy. Mini Programs The Mini Program SDK can also be used in lightweight Web scenarios. It does not provide local message storage, making it suitable for customer service entry points, campaign pages, admin pages, temporary conversations, and other lightweight experiences that do not depend on a local history cache. Before integrating it, confirm that: Request, WebSocket, and upload domains are configured on the target Mini Program platform. The application does not depend on the SDK's local message database, offline history cache, or local conversation persistence. File messages use the target platform's supported file picker, temporary file paths, and upload APIs. After a network change, entering the background, or process reclamation by the platform, restore the connection and synchronize data according to the platform lifecycle. When method level APIs match the WASM documentation, you can continue to consult the WASM feature pages. Follow the Mini Program SDK implementation for initialization, network adapters, and file uploads. Unsupported environments React Native is not a browser WASM runtime. It does not provide the standard browser DOM, IndexedDB, or wasm exec.js loading model, so do not use @openim/wasm client sdk directly as a mobile SDK. For a React Native client, start with the React Native SDK overview /sdk/react native/overview and use a mobile SDK or native bridge. Connection keepalive, push notifications, local caching, photo library files, and background lifecycle handling require separate implementation. Validate and troubleshoot After a production build, the browser or Electron renderer can access /wasm exec.js , /openIM.wasm , and /sql wasm.wasm directly. login succeeds, and SdkEvent.OnConnectSuccess has fired before you call message, conversation, or group APIs. The connection state and conversation list recover after a page reload, network interruption and recovery, or tab foreground/background transition. Test a packaged Electron installer, not only development mode. For the Mini Program SDK, test requests, WebSocket connections, uploads, and background recovery, and confirm that the product does not depend on local message storage. Common issues | Symptom | Possible cause | Resolution | | | | | | WASM assets return 404 | The assets directory was not copied to the production static directory, or a CDN/subpath rewrote the URL. | Copy the entire assets directory and use the browser Network panel to confirm that all three required assets are accessible. | | SSR reports window is not defined | The SDK was imported or instantiated during server rendering. | Move SDK initialization to a client component, browser lifecycle, or dynamically imported function. | | No successful connection after login | apiAddr , wsAddr , the token, the platform ID, or network policy is incorrect. | Register connection events first, then use errCode , errMsg , and server logs to locate the cause. | | Electron works in development but fails after packaging | Production asset paths, CSP, or the WASM/FFI runtime boundary differs from development mode. | Inspect the packaged application's SDK distribution, asset paths, protocol, CSP, WebSocket, IPC boundary, and API permissions. | | Mini Program cannot connect or upload | The platform's allowed domains are not configured, or its file API differs from browser APIs. | Configure request, WebSocket, and upload domains in the platform console, and adapt file messages to the Mini Program's native file capabilities. | | Mini Program has no history after reload | The Mini Program SDK does not provide local message storage. | Reload the required data through the server or SDK queries, or use a client SDK that supports a local cache. | | Local cache behaves unexpectedly | Browser storage was cleared, private browsing restricts storage, or the application directly modified SDK internals. | Do not manipulate the SDK IndexedDB/sql.js data directly. Restore the UI through SDK APIs, events, and application state. | Next steps Send your first message /sdk/wasm/getting started/send first message User authentication /sdk/wasm/getting started/authenticate and manage session Receive messages /sdk/wasm/message/receiving messages/receive messages Electron SDK overview /sdk/electron/overview Mini Program SDK overview /sdk/miniprogram/overview React Native SDK overview /sdk/react native/overview

title: Authenticate and manage a session
description: Sign in with the WASM SDK, inspect the sign-in state, handle connection events, and sign out the current user.
keywords: sdk wasm v4 sdk wasm getting-started authenticate-and-manage-session
content: The WASM SDK uses login to establish a session for the current user. Before authenticating, complete the prerequisites in Before you start /sdk/wasm/getting started/before you start : OpenIMServer, user sign in details, browser accessible service addresses, and SDK runtime assets. Follow this sequence for a complete sign in flow: 1. Publish the WASM assets and create an SDK instance with getSDK . 2. Register connection, token, and account sign out events so that no state changes are missed during sign in. 3. Obtain the userID , token, apiAddr , and wsAddr described in “Before you start” from the application backend. 4. Call login , wait for its Promise to succeed, and then wait for OnConnectSuccess to confirm that the connection is ready. 5. Query user, friend, conversation, group, and message data only after the connection succeeds. 6. When the user signs out or switches accounts, call logout , then clear application state and event listeners for the current account. Initialize the SDK with application configuration Publish the WASM assets required by the browser SDK before creating the SDK instance. coreWasmPath and sqlWasmPath must point to assets the browser can access. import getSDK, SdkEvent from '@openim/wasm client sdk'; const openimsdk = getSDK coreWasmPath: '/openIM.wasm', sqlWasmPath: '/sql wasm.wasm', ; Parameters getSDK accepts the following configuration fields: | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | coreWasmPath | string | No | Browser accessible URL for openIM.wasm . Defaults to /openIM.wasm when omitted. | | sqlWasmPath | string | No | Browser accessible URL for sql wasm.wasm . Set it explicitly when the project changes its static asset directory or uses a CDN. | | debug | boolean | No | Controls diagnostic output from the JavaScript wrapper and local database bridge. It is enabled by default. | Understand the browser package @openim/wasm client sdk is the browser WASM package. getSDK reuses an SDK instance within the same page runtime, so application components should not create separate instances. Do not initialize it during server side rendering, in a Node.js API route, or in the Electron main process. The OpenIMSDK application configuration has two parts: WASM asset paths are passed to getSDK , while the OpenIMServer addresses and user credentials are passed to login . Obtain sign in details for the current user Call an endpoint on your application backend to obtain the current user's userID , token, and OpenIMServer addresses. See Before you start /sdk/wasm/getting started/before you start for the endpoint's responsibilities and response shape. const userID, token, apiAddr, wsAddr = await loadOpenIMSDKSession ; userID identifies the current OpenIMSDK user; it is not an authentication credential. It must match the token. The browser consumes the sign in details returned by the backend and must not create users or issue tokens. Register connection events before signing in Register connection events before calling login . This lets the application capture errors caused by network access, service addresses, tokens, or server conditions during sign in and update its connection state. const handleConnecting = = setConnectionState 'connecting' ; ; const handleConnectSuccess = = setConnectionState 'connected' ; ; const handleConnectFailed = errCode, errMsg = setConnectionState 'failed' ; handleOpenIMError errCode, errMsg ; ; openimsdk.on SdkEvent.OnConnecting, handleConnecting ; openimsdk.on SdkEvent.OnConnectSuccess, handleConnectSuccess ; openimsdk.on SdkEvent.OnConnectFailed, handleConnectFailed ; Sign in the current user Pass a LoginParams object to login . The following example uses Platform.Web instead of placing a numeric platform value in application code: import LogLevel, Platform from '@openim/wasm client sdk'; try await openimsdk.login userID, token, platformID: Platform.Web, apiAddr, wsAddr, logLevel: LogLevel.Warn, isLogStandardOutput: false, ; catch errCode, errMsg handleOpenIMError errCode, errMsg ; throw new Error OpenIMClientSDK login failed: $ errCode $ errMsg ; Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | | | | | | userID | string | Yes | The current OpenIMSDK user ID, which must match the token. It is not a nickname, phone number, or temporary application session ID. | | token | string | Yes | The current user's OpenIMSDK token returned by the application backend. It must correspond to userID . | | platformID | number | Yes | The current client platform. Use Platform.Web in a browser. Desktop and mobile clients should select the appropriate enum according to their runtime and the server's multi device sign in policy. | | apiAddr | string | Yes | The OpenIMServer HTTP API address, which must be reachable from the current browser. Use an HTTPS address on an HTTPS page. | | wsAddr | string | Yes | The OpenIMServer WebSocket address, which must accept connections from the current browser. An HTTPS page normally uses WSS. | | logLevel | LogLevel | No | The SDK log level. See Logging /sdk/wasm/logger for enum values. | | isLogStandardOutput | boolean | No | Whether to send core SDK logs to the browser console. Disabling this option does not disable JavaScript wrapper logs controlled by getSDK debug . | | isExternalExtensions | boolean | No | Whether to enable external message extensions. Set it to true only when the server and application implement the corresponding extension contract. | | tryParse | boolean | No | Whether the SDK should try to parse JSON response strings into objects. It defaults to true ; when disabled, the application must parse response data itself. | A successful login Promise means that the sign in request has completed. OnConnectSuccess means that the SDK connection is ready. These are separate stages: do not call message, conversation, group, or user APIs that depend on the connection solely because the Promise succeeded. If the user clicks the sign in button repeatedly, reuse the in progress sign in request and its Promise instead of invoking login concurrently. Handle API results Asynchronous WASM SDK APIs return Promises. On success, read business data from the response's data field. On failure, the Promise rejects with an error containing errCode and errMsg . The “Return value” section on each API page describes only the business shape of data and does not repeat this shared response envelope. try const data = await openimsdk.getSelfUserInfo ; useCurrentUser data ; catch errCode, errMsg handleOpenIMError errCode, errMsg ; For a query API, data contains the business data available at the time of the call. When a state changing API has no business data with which to refresh the UI, await the Promise and then process the relevant event or query again as described on that API page. Do not treat Promise completion, event delivery, and the final UI state as the same stage. Complex objects have a complete field reference on one primary query page. Other API pages explain the fields used by that operation and link to the shared object reference, avoiding inconsistent field tables for the same type. Inspect the current sign in state Neither getLoginStatus nor getLoginUserID accepts business parameters: import LoginStatus from '@openim/wasm client sdk'; const data: loginStatus = await openimsdk.getLoginStatus ; if loginStatus === LoginStatus.LoggedIn const data: currentUserID = await openimsdk.getLoginUserID ; restoreSessionFor currentUserID ; LoginStatus has three values: | Value | Description | | | | | LoginStatus.LoggedOut | The current SDK instance is signed out. | | LoginStatus.LoggingIn | Sign in is in progress. Do not start another sign in concurrently. | | LoginStatus.LoggedIn | The SDK is signed in. Continue to use connection events to determine whether the network connection is currently available. | getLoginUserID returns the user ID currently signed in to the SDK. Use it to verify that the application account and SDK account match; it does not replace application authentication.
